_objectcallmethod.name: _ObjectCallMethod
_objectcallmethod.doc: Calls a specific method for an ActiveX object. (See the documentation for your ActiveX object for details on methods and properties.)
_objectcallmethod.returns: The return value from the method - if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hObject: The handle for the object (as returned by the ObjectByName function).
paramDocs.vParameters: A variable length parameter list of method arguments. The variables will be passed however you enter them, and will then be coerced into appropriate automation types. Likewise, any values modified by the automation call will be written back - with appropriate coercion - into the passed Cicode variable.

_objectgetproperty.name: _ObjectGetProperty
_objectgetproperty.doc: Gets a specific property of an ActiveX object.
_objectgetproperty.returns: The value of the property - if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hObject: The handle for the object (as returned by the ObjectByName function).
paramDocs.sProperty: The name of the property you want to get.

_objectsetproperty.name: _ObjectSetProperty
_objectsetproperty.doc: Sets a specific property of an ActiveX object.
_objectsetproperty.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hObject: The handle for the object (as returned by the ObjectByName function).
paramDocs.sProperty: The name of the property you want to set.
paramDocs.vValue: The value to which the property will be set. This value can be of any data type. Appropriate coercion will take place when creating the equivalent automation parameter.

abs.name: Abs
abs.doc: Calculates the absolute (positive) value of a number. The absolute value of a number is the number without its sign.

acccontrol.name: AccControl
acccontrol.doc: Controls accumulators, for example, motor run hours. You can reset the values of Run Time, Totalizer Inc, and No. of Starts (defined in the Accumulator database), re-read these values from the I/O device, or flush pending writes of these values to the I/O device.
acccontrol.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the accumulator or a mask for the names of accumulators. You can use the following wildcards:
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the control:
paramDocs.sClusterName: Name of the cluster in which the accumulator resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the reports server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

accumbrowseclose.name: AccumBrowseClose
accumbrowseclose.doc: The AccumBrowseClose function terminates an active data browse session and cleans up all resources associated with the session.
accumbrowseclose.returns: 0 (zero) if the accumulator browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by an AccumBrowseOpen call.

accumbrowsefirst.name: AccumBrowseFirst
accumbrowsefirst.doc: The AccumBrowseFirst function places the data browse cursor at the first record.
accumbrowsefirst.returns: 0 (zero) if the accumulator browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AccumBrowseOpen call.

accumbrowsegetfield.name: AccumBrowseGetField
accumbrowsegetfield.doc: The AccumBrowseGetField function retrieves the value of the specified field from the record the data browse cursor is currently referencing.
accumbrowsegetfield.returns: The value of the specified field as a string. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. The last error should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AccumBrowseOpen call.
paramDocs.FieldName: The name of the field that references the value to be returned. Supported fields are:

accumbrowsenext.name: AccumBrowseNext
accumbrowsenext.doc: The AccumBrowseNext function moves the data browse cursor forward one record. If you call this function after you have reached the end of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
accumbrowsenext.returns: 0 (zero) if the accumulator browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AccumBrowseOpen call.

accumbrowsenumrecords.name: AccumBrowseNumRecords
accumbrowsenumrecords.doc: The AccumBrowseNumRecords function returns the number of records that match the filter criteria.
accumbrowsenumrecords.returns: The number of records that have matched the filter criteria. A value of 0 denotes that no records have matched. A value of -1 denotes that the browse session is unable to provide a fixed number. This may be the case if the data being browsed changed during the browse session.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AccumBrowseOpen call.

accumbrowseopen.name: AccumBrowseOpen
accumbrowseopen.doc: The AccumBrowseOpen function initiates a new browse session and returns a handle to the new session that can be used in subsequent data browse function calls.
accumbrowseopen.returns: Returns an integer handle to the browse session. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.Filter: A filter expression specifying the records to return during the browse. An empty string indicates that all records will be returned. Where a fieldname is not specified in the filter, it is assumed to be tagname. For example, the filter "AAA" is equivalent to "name=AAA".
paramDocs.Fields: Specifies via a comma delimited string the columns to be returned during the browse. An empty string indicates that the server will return all available columns. Supported fields are:
paramDocs.Clusters: An optional parameter that specifies via a comma delimited string the subset of the clusters to browse. An empty string indicates that the connected clusters will be browsed.

accumbrowseprev.name: AccumBrowsePrev
accumbrowseprev.doc: The AccumBrowsePrev function moves the data browse cursor back one record. If you call this function after you have reached the beginning of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
accumbrowseprev.returns: 0 (zero) if the accumulator browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AccumBrowseOpen call.

alarmack.name: AlarmAck
alarmack.doc: Acknowledges alarms. You can acknowledge the alarm where the cursor is positioned, one or more alarm lists on the active page, a whole category of alarms, or alarms of a particular priority.
alarmack.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code will return

paramDocs.Value: Used with Mode 1 and 2 to specify which alarms to acknowledge.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Used with Mode 2 or 3 to specify the name of the cluster in which the alarms being acknowledged reside. This argument is optional if the client is connected to only one cluster containing an alarm server or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context.

alarmackrec.name: AlarmAckRec
alarmackrec.doc: Acknowledges alarms by record number on both the primary and standby alarm servers. This function can be called from alarm server or client and should not be used with a MsgRPC() call to the alarm server.
alarmackrec.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmacktag.name: AlarmAckTag
alarmacktag.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code will return.

paramDocs.Tag: A string that identifies the alarm to acknowledge. It can be one of the following:
paramDocs.ClusterName: The cluster where the tag resides

alarmactive.name: AlarmActive
alarmactive.doc: Determines if any alarms are active in the user's area. Call this function from the Page Strings database, to display an alarm message at a specified AN on a graphics page. You can specify the type of alarms, for example, active hardware alarms or disabled non-hardware alarms.

paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to check:
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to check for active alarms. If this argument is blank or empty, the function will check the connected clusters.

alarmcatgetformat.name: AlarmCatGetFormat
alarmcatgetformat.doc: Returns the display format string of the specified alarm category.
alarmcatgetformat.returns: The display format string of the specified category. If the alarm category is not specifically defined or it has no format string specified in your project, the format string of category 0 will be returned.

paramDocs.Type: The type of display format string:

alarmclear.name: AlarmClear
alarmclear.doc: Clears an acknowledged (and off) alarm from the active alarm list. You can clear the alarm where the cursor is positioned, one or more alarm lists on the active page, a whole category of alarms, or alarms of a particular priority.
alarmclear.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Value: Used with Mode 1 or 2 to specify which alarms to clear.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Used with Mode 2 or 3 to specify the name of the cluster in which the alarms being cleared reside. This argument is optional if the client is connected to only one cluster containing an Alarm Server or you are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context.

alarmclearrec.name: AlarmClearRec
alarmclearrec.doc: Clears an alarm by its record number on both the Primary and Standby Alarms Servers. This function can be called from Alarm Server or Client.
alarmclearrec.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmcleartag.name: AlarmClearTag
alarmcleartag.doc: Clears alarms by Tag on both the Primary and Standby Alarms Servers.
alarmcleartag.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: A string that identifies the alarm to acknowledge. It can be one of the following:
paramDocs.ClusterName: The cluster where the tag resides.

alarmcomment.name: AlarmComment
alarmcomment.doc: Allows an operator to add a comment to a selected alarm summary or SOE entry during runtime. You would normally call this function from a keyboard command.
alarmcomment.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Comment: The comment to add to the alarm summary entry or SOE entry. Currently for the Alarm summary page the maximum length of a comment is 128 characters. The maximum length for a comment on the SOE page is 244 characters. If you exceed the maximum length it will be truncated and an ellipsis appended.
paramDocs.AN: An animation identifier. Enter the value of the AN where the alarm is displayed. If AN is not specified, the default value will be 0, which means the current cursor position will be used.

alarmcommentrecid.name: AlarmCommentRecID
alarmcommentrecid.doc: Allows an operator to add a comment to a selected alarm summary or SOE entry during runtime. You would normally call this function from a keyboard command.
alarmcommentrecid.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Comment: The comment to add to the alarm summary entry or SOE entry. Currently for the Alarm summary page the maximum length of a comment is 128 characters. The maximum length for a comment on the SOE page is 244 characters. If you exceed the maximum length it will be truncated and an ellipsis appended.
paramDocs.nListType: Following are the nListType values for SOE or Alarm Summary lists.
paramDocs.sCluster: Specifies the cluster context for the alarms displayed in the list.

alarmcount.name: AlarmCount
alarmcount.doc: Counts the available alarms for the selected filter criteria.
alarmcount.returns: Returns counted alarms for the selected filter criteria. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.FilterCriteria: A filter name OR filter text.
paramDocs.KeepAliveSeconds: Optional length of time (in seconds) that the count will remain in memory. Default is 30 seconds.
paramDocs.CachedMode: Optional flag that causes the current cached value to be supplied even when the value is being refreshed. This makes the function non-blocking. If the property has not yet been cached, an error is set.

alarmcountequipment.name: AlarmCountEquipment
alarmcountequipment.doc: Counts the available alarms for specified equipment and referenced equipment in conjunction with the selected filter criteria.
alarmcountequipment.returns: Returns counted alarms for the selected filter criteria. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.EquipmentFilter: A comma-separated list of equipment names or categories (RefCat) to filter alarms prior to applying the other filter specified on the FilterCriteria argument. This field has been extended to support wildcards, and hence accept partial filter strings.
paramDocs.FilterCriteria: A filter name OR filter text.
paramDocs.KeepAliveSeconds: Optional length of time (in seconds) that the count will remain in memory. Default is 30 seconds.
paramDocs.CachedMode: 1 - Force cached read. Cicode is non-blocking
paramDocs.IncludingReference: 1 - Include alarms belonging to referenced equipment in Alarm Count for current equipment. This is set by default.

alarmcountlist.name: AlarmCountList
alarmcountlist.doc: Counts the available alarms for the selected filter criteria.
alarmcountlist.returns: Returns counted alarms for the selected filter criteria. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.AN: An animation identifier of an alarm list.

alarmdelete.name: AlarmDelete
alarmdelete.doc: Deletes alarm summary entries that are currently displayed. You can delete the alarm where the cursor is positioned, one or more alarm lists on the active page, a whole category of alarms, or alarms of a particular priority.
alarmdelete.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Value: Used with Mode 1 or 2 to specify which alarms to delete.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Used with Mode 2 or 3 to specify the name of the cluster in which the alarms being deleted reside. This argument is optional if the client is connected to only one cluster containing an Alarm Server or you are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. This argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmdisable.name: AlarmDisable
alarmdisable.doc: Disables alarms. You can disable the alarm where the cursor is positioned, one or more alarm lists on the active page, a whole category of alarms, or alarms of a particular priority.
alarmdisable.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Value: Used with Mode 1 and 2 to specify which alarms to disable.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Used with Mode 2 or 3 to specify the name of the cluster where the alarms being disabled reside in. This argument is optional if the client is connected to only one cluster containing an alarm server, or if the alarm server is resolved via the current cluster context.
paramDocs.EndTime: A date/time variable that indicates when the alarm will no longer be disabled. If this parameter is omitted or set to 0, the alarm will be disabled indefinitely.
paramDocs.Comment: An optional comment limited to 200 characters explaining why the alarm is disabled. If the comment exceeds 200 characters, hardware error 274 ("Invalid argument passed") will be displayed.

alarmdisablerec.name: AlarmDisableRec
alarmdisablerec.doc: Disables alarms by record number on both the Primary and Standby Alarms Servers. This function can be called from alarm server or client and should not be used with a MsgRPC call to the alarm server.
alarmdisablerec.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.EndTime: A date/time variable that indicates when the alarm will no longer be disabled. If this parameter is omitted or set to 0, the alarm will be disabled indefinitely.
paramDocs.Comment: An optional comment limited to 200 characters explaining why the alarm is disabled. If the comment exceeds 200 characters, hardware error 274 ("Invalid argument passed") will be displayed.

alarmdisabletag.name: AlarmDisableTag
alarmdisabletag.doc: Disables alarms by Tag on both the Primary and Standby Alarms Servers.
alarmdisabletag.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: A string that identifies the alarm to acknowledge. It can be one of the following:
paramDocs.ClusterName: The cluster where the tag resides.
paramDocs.EndTime: A date/time variable that indicates when the alarm will no longer be disabled. If this parameter is omitted or set to 0, the alarm will be disabled indefinitely.
paramDocs.Comment: An optional comment limited to 200 characters explaining why the alarm is disabled. If the comment exceeds 200 characters, hardware error 274 ("Invalid argument passed") will be displayed.

alarmdsp.name: AlarmDsp
alarmdsp.doc: Displays an alarm list, starting at a specified AN and then on subsequent ANs. You specify the number of alarms to display, the type of alarms and the name of the cluster the alarms belong to, for example, active hardware alarms or disabled non-hardware alarms in cluster XYZ. Before you call this function, you need to first add animation points to the graphics page for each alarm to be displayed.
alarmdsp.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Count: The number of alarms to display.
paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.ClusterName: The cluster name to which the alarms belong. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.NoDraw: Makes call to alarm server to update the ALMCB but does not automatically perform the animation of the data when the result is returned.
paramDocs.CallbackFunc: Callback function to associate with the return of the ALMCB data from the Alarm Server.

alarmdspclusteradd.name: AlarmDspClusterAdd
alarmdspclusteradd.doc: Adds a cluster to a client's alarm list. Alarms in the specified cluster (that correspond to the mode set in AlarmDsp) will be added to the alarm list at the AN number.
alarmdspclusteradd.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN used in the original AlarmDsp call.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to be used for this alarm list. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks ("").

alarmdspclusterinuse.name: AlarmDspClusterInUse
alarmdspclusterinuse.doc: Determines if a cluster is included in a client's alarm list.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN used in the original AlarmDsp call.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to query an alarm list for to determine if it's included. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks ("").

alarmdspclusterremove.name: AlarmDspClusterRemove
alarmdspclusterremove.doc: Removes a cluster from a client's alarms list. Alarms for the specified cluster will be removed from the alarms list at the AN number.
alarmdspclusterremove.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN used in the original AlarmDsp call.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to remove from this alarm list. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks ("").

alarmdsplast.name: AlarmDspLast
alarmdsplast.doc: Displays the latest alarms, at a specified AN with the cluster name. Use this function to display the last alarms. You can specify the number of alarms to display of a specified type, for example, active hardware alarms or disabled non-hardware alarms.
alarmdsplast.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the last alarms are to be displayed.
paramDocs.Count: The number of alarms to display. If you omit the Count, the default is 1.
paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.sClusterName: The cluster name to which the alarms belong. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks " ".
paramDocs.iNoDraw: Makes call to alarm server to update the ALMCB but does not automatically perform the animation of the data when the result is returned.
paramDocs.sCallbackFunc: Callback function to associate with the return of the ALMCB data from the Alarm Server.

alarmdspnext.name: AlarmDspNext
alarmdspnext.doc: Displays the next page of alarms. This function pages down (scrolls) the alarms displayed by the AlarmDsp function. You would normally call this function from a keyboard command.
alarmdspnext.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the alarm list is displayed, or:

alarmdspprev.name: AlarmDspPrev
alarmdspprev.doc: Displays the previous page of alarms. This function pages up (scrolls) the alarms displayed by the AlarmDsp function. You would normally call this function from a keyboard command.
alarmdspprev.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the alarm list is displayed, or:

alarmenable.name: AlarmEnable
alarmenable.doc: Enables an alarm on the active alarm list. You can enable the alarm where the cursor is positioned, one or more alarm lists on the active page, a whole category of alarms, or alarms of a particular priority.
alarmenable.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Value: Used with Mode 0, 1 and 2 to specify which alarms to enable.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Used with Mode 2 or 3 to specify the name of the cluster where the alarms being enabled reside in. This argument is optional if the client is connected to only one cluster containing an Alarm Server or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context.
paramDocs.bAcknowledge: Forces acknowledgment of an alarm after it is enabled. The accepted values are:

alarmenablerec.name: AlarmEnableRec
alarmenablerec.doc: Enables alarms by record number on both the primary and standby alarms servers. This function can be called from an alarm server or client and should not be used with a MsgRPC call to the alarm server.
alarmenablerec.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks " ".
paramDocs.bAcknowledge: Forces acknowledgment of an alarm after it is enabled. The accepted values are:

alarmenabletag.name: AlarmEnableTag
alarmenabletag.doc: Enables alarms by Tag on both the Primary and Standby Alarms Servers.
alarmenabletag.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: A string that identifies the alarm to acknowledge. It can be one of the following:
paramDocs.ClusterName: The cluster where the tag resides.
paramDocs.bAcknowledge: Forces acknowledgment of an alarm after it is enabled. The accepted values are:

alarmeventque.name: AlarmEventQue
alarmeventque.doc: Opens the alarm event queue. The Alarms Server writes events into this queue as they are processed. These events include activated, reset, acknowledged, enabled and disabled alarms.
alarmeventque.returns: The handle of the alarm event queue, or -1 if the queue cannot be opened.

alarmfilterclose.name: AlarmFilterClose
alarmfilterclose.doc: This function removes the named filter from memory.
alarmfilterclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

alarmfiltereditappend.name: AlarmFilterEditAppend
alarmfiltereditappend.doc: The AlarmFilterEditAppend function takes a session handle and a filter expression as parameters. It appends the provided expression to the current filter session content without any validation. This does not apply to all filters on the list (see AlarmFilterEditCommit).
alarmfiltereditappend.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm filter session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hSession: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.
paramDocs.FilterCriteria: Filter expression as a string. For example:"(Tag=A) OR (TAG=B)"

alarmfiltereditappendequipment.name: AlarmFilterEditAppendEquipment
alarmfiltereditappendequipment.doc: Appends the provided expression that can include equipment names to the current filter session content without validation.
alarmfiltereditappendequipment.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm filter session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hSession: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.
paramDocs.EquipmentFilter: A comma-separated list of equipment names to filter alarms prior to applying the other filter specified on the FilterCriteria argument. This field has been extended to support wildcards, and hence accept partial filter strings.
paramDocs.Ref: 1 - Include alarms belonging to referenced equipment in Filter

alarmfiltereditclose.name: AlarmFilterEditClose
alarmfiltereditclose.doc: The AlmFilterEditClose function removes the session from the memory. The filter is not reset and is valid until a new filter is created and applied.
alarmfiltereditclose.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm filter session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Session: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.

alarmfiltereditcommit.name: AlarmFilterEditCommit
alarmfiltereditcommit.doc: The AlarmFilterEditCommit function takes a session handle as parameter. It validate the filter created in this session and, if valid, applies this filter to the list associated with the session.
alarmfiltereditcommit.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm filter session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hSession: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.

alarmfiltereditfirst.name: AlarmFilterEditFirst
alarmfiltereditfirst.doc: This function takes a session handle parameter. It gets the first part of the filter. Each part is either:
alarmfiltereditfirst.returns: First part of filter or if does not exist an empty string "".

paramDocs.hSession: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.

alarmfilteredithasfield.name: AlarmFilterEditHasField
alarmfilteredithasfield.doc: The AlarmFilterEditHasField function checks whether an alarm field name or any field in a set of field names is used in the filter specified in an alarm filter edit session.
alarmfilteredithasfield.returns: 1 (TRUE) if the filter criteria is valid and alarm field name is used, otherwise 0 (FALSE) is returned.

paramDocs.Session: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.
paramDocs.sFieldName: The alarm field name or names separated by comma (no space) to be checked if it is used in filter criteria.

alarmfiltereditlast.name: AlarmFilterEditLast
alarmfiltereditlast.doc: This function takes a session handle parameter. It gets the last part of the filter. Each part is either:
alarmfiltereditlast.returns: First part of filter or if does not exist an empty string "".

paramDocs.hSession: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.

alarmfiltereditnext.name: AlarmFilterEditNext
alarmfiltereditnext.doc: This function takes a session handle parameter. It gets the next part of the filter. Each part is either:
alarmfiltereditnext.returns: Next part of filter or if does not exist an empty string "".

paramDocs.hSession: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.

alarmfiltereditopen.name: AlarmFilterEditOpen
params: STRING FilterName or INT AN or INT -1
alarmfiltereditopen.doc: The AlmFilterEditOpen function creates a session for the historical list (or lists) associated with the provided animation number (AN) or FilterName or all alarm lists displayed on the page via (-1) option. This session is initialised with the current filter applied on the lists.
alarmfiltereditopen.returns: Returns a session handle to the filter browse session. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.AN: Animation Number, for example 21 or 11
paramDocs.-1: Change the display parameters of all alarm lists displayed on the page
paramDocs.AutoCloseMode: Values for AutoCloseMode are bit flags.

alarmfiltereditprev.name: AlarmFilterEditPrev
alarmfiltereditprev.doc: This function takes a session handle parameter. It gets the previous part of the filter. Each part is either:
alarmfiltereditprev.returns: Previous part of filter or if does not exist an empty string "".

paramDocs.hSession: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.

alarmfiltereditset.name: AlarmFilterEditSet
alarmfiltereditset.doc: The AlarmFilterEditSet function takes a session handle and a filter expression as parameters. It replaces the current filter session content by the provided expression without any validation. This does not apply to all filters on the list (see AlarmFilterEditCommit).
alarmfiltereditset.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm filter session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hSession: Session handle for the historical list previously returned by the function AlarmFilterEditOpen.
paramDocs.FilterCriteria: Filter expression as a string. For example:"(Tag=A) OR (TAG=B)"

alarmfilterform.name: AlarmFilterForm
alarmfilterform.doc: Displays a form for specifying filtering criteria for either an alarm list or a named filter. This function uses the AlarmFilterEdit family of Cicode functions to set the filter.
alarmfilterform.returns: 1 if filter has been applied, 0 if filter has been cleared, or -1 if no change is made.

paramDocs.nMode: 1 is for form having datetime as droplets and shift interface;
paramDocs.nDebug: For debugging filter values; 1 will write filter parameters to file - filter.txt in the [run] folder
paramDocs.nFilterSrc: The source where the filter will be applied to. It can either be the Animation Number (AN) of an alarm list or the name of a filter created via the AlarmFilterOpen Cicode function. If it is not specified, it is defaulted to -1 which refers to all alarm lists on the current page.

alarmfilteropen.name: AlarmFilterOpen
alarmfilteropen.doc: This function creates a named filter. The filter is initialized with empty content (matches all alarms). If unable to open the named filter an error code is returned.
alarmfilteropen.returns: 0 (zero) if the filter was opened or created or an error if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.AutoCloseMode: Values for AutoCloseMode are bit flags.

alarmfirstcatrec.name: AlarmFirstCatRec
alarmfirstcatrec.doc: Searches for the first occurrence of an alarm category and type. You can search all areas, the current area only, or specify an area to limit the search.
alarmfirstcatrec.returns: The alarm record identifier or -1 if no match is found.

paramDocs.Category: The alarm category or group number to match. Set Category to 0 (zero) to match all alarm categories.
paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.Area: The area in which to search for alarms. If you do not specify an area, or if you set Area to -1, only the current area will be searched.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmfirstprirec.name: AlarmFirstPriRec
alarmfirstprirec.doc: Searches for the first occurrence of an alarm priority and type. You can search all areas, the current area only, or specify an area to limit the search.
alarmfirstprirec.returns: The alarm record identifier or -1 if no match is found. If you do not specify an area, only alarms in the current area on the alarms server are searched.

paramDocs.Priority: The alarm Priority or group handle of a group of alarm priorities. Set Priority to 0 (zero) to match all alarm priorities.
paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.Area: The area in which to search for alarms. If you do not specify an area, or if you set Area to -1, only the current area will be searched.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmfirsttagrec.name: AlarmFirstTagRec
alarmfirsttagrec.doc: Searches for the first occurrence of an alarm tag, name, and description.
alarmfirsttagrec.returns: The alarm record identifier or -1 if no match is found.

paramDocs.Tag: A string that identifies the tag to be matched. It can be one of the following:
paramDocs.Name: The alarm name to be matched. Specify an empty string (" ") to match all alarm names.
paramDocs.Description: The alarm description to be matched. Specify an empty string (" ") to match all alarm descriptions.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmgetdelay.name: AlarmGetDelay
alarmgetdelay.doc: Gets the delay setting for the alarm the cursor is currently positioned over.
alarmgetdelay.returns: The alarm delay if successful, otherwise -1 is returned. Use IsError() to retrieve extended error information.

paramDocs.nType: The type of delay:

alarmgetdelayrec.name: AlarmGetDelayRec
alarmgetdelayrec.doc: Gets the delay setting for an alarm via the alarm record number.
alarmgetdelayrec.returns: The alarm delay if successful, otherwise -1 is returned. Use IsError() to retrieve extended error information.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmgetdsp.name: AlarmGetDsp
alarmgetdsp.doc: Gets field data from the alarm record that is displayed at the specified AN. You can use this function for Alarm Pages, Sequence of Events pages, and Alarm Summary pages (an Alarm Page, SOE Page, and Alarm Summary needs to be displayed before this function can be used).
alarmgetdsp.returns: The alarm field data (as a string) or empty string "".

paramDocs.AN: AN number of an ALMCB Alarm record. Equal to AN where actual ALMCB resides + Offset into the list of ALMCB records.
paramDocs.Field: The name of the field from which the data is retrieved. The contents of the following fields can be retrieved when the alarm page is displayed.

alarmgetfieldrec.name: AlarmGetFieldRec
alarmgetfieldrec.doc: Gets the contents of the specified field in the specified alarm record.
alarmgetfieldrec.returns: The alarm field data (as a string) or empty string "".

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.Field: The name of the field from which the data is retrieved.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmgetfiltername.name: AlarmGetFilterName
alarmgetfiltername.doc: Retrieves the name of the linked named filter for the supplied An. If empty text, there is currently no linked named filter.

alarmgetinfo.name: AlarmGetInfo
alarmgetinfo.doc: Gets data on the alarm list displayed at a specified AN. Use this function to display the current alarm list information on an alarm page. If only one alarm list has been configured on an alarm page, modes 2 and 3 of this function return the current alarm page information.
alarmgetinfo.returns: Alarm list data as a numeric value.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the alarm list (with the required information) is displayed. Set the AN to 0 (zero) to get information on the alarm list where the cursor is positioned.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is only required for type 14. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks " ".

alarmgetorderbykey.name: AlarmGetOrderbyKey
alarmgetorderbykey.doc: Retrieves the list of key(s) that are used to determine the order of the alarm list. These keys can be set by the AlarmSetInfo function.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the alarm list (with the required information) is displayed.

alarmgetthreshold.name: AlarmGetThreshold
alarmgetthreshold.doc: Gets the threshold of the analog alarm where the cursor is positioned.

paramDocs.nType: The type of threshold:

alarmgetthresholdrec.name: AlarmGetThresholdRec
alarmgetthresholdrec.doc: Gets the threshold of analog alarms by the alarm record number.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmhelp.name: AlarmHelp
alarmhelp.doc: Displays the alarm help page (associated with the alarm) where the cursor is positioned. You can assign a help page to each alarm when you define it (using the Digital Alarms or the Analog Alarms database, depending on the type of alarm). You need to also define the help page in the pages database.
alarmhelp.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

alarmhighestpriority.name: AlarmHighestPriority
alarmhighestpriority.doc: Returns the alarm priority and/or state of the current highest priority alarm for the given equipment in conjunction with the selected filter criteria.
alarmhighestpriority.returns: For Mode 0, return the priority ID of the current highest priority alarm.

paramDocs.Mode: 1 - return the alarm state of the highest priority alarm.
paramDocs.EquipmentFilter: A comma-separated list of equipment names to filter alarms prior to applying the filter specified in the FilterCriteria argument. Each equipment name may be a part of full equipment name from the root. For example, "Region.Plant" will count alarms with equipment names literally starting with "Region.Plant" that includes "Region.PlantA" and "Region.Plant.AreaB". If it is needed to count children of a particular equipment tree only, the equipment name should end with a period('.'). A comma in between equipment expressions is regarded as an OR operator. If an empty string is specified, return Highest Priority for all Alarms.
paramDocs.FilterCriteria: A filter name OR filter text. See the topic Implementing Alarm Filters Using Cicode for more information about filter syntax.
paramDocs.KeepAliveSeconds: Optional length of time (in seconds) for which the count will remain in memory. Default is 30 seconds.
paramDocs.CachedMode: Optional flag that causes the current cached value to be supplied even when the value is being refreshed. This makes the function non-blocking. If the property has not yet been cached, an error is set.
paramDocs.IncludingReference: 1 - Include alarms belonging to referenced equipment in AlarmHighestPriority for current equipment.
paramDocs.Type: The rule used to determine the relative priority of alarms (currently fixed to 0).

alarmlistcreate.name: AlarmListCreate
alarmlistcreate.doc: Creates an alarms list at a specified AN.
alarmlistcreate.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN number to associate with the alarms list.
paramDocs.alarm_type: The type of alarms to display in the alarms list:
paramDocs.width: The width of the area in which the alarms list will display (in pixels).
paramDocs.height: The height of the area in which the alarms list will display (in pixels).
paramDocs.rowheight: The height of each row in the alarms list (in pixels).
paramDocs.drawheader: Determines if the alarms list includes a header row. You need to enter a value; there is no default.
paramDocs.sCluster: Specifies the cluster context for the alarms displayed in the list. This value is optional. If not specified, it defaults to all clusters.
paramDocs.sFormat: The name of the display format applied to the alarms list. This determines the arrangement of columns that are presented. A customized name can be defined for a display format using the parameter [Format]FormatName.
paramDocs.hFontRow: The handle for the font you would like to use in the alarm list rows. This value is optional. If not specified, it defaults to –1 (the default font).
paramDocs.hFontHeader: The handle for the font you would like to use in the alarm list header row. This value is optional. If not specified, it defaults to –1 (the default font).

alarmlistdestroy.name: AlarmListDestroy
alarmlistdestroy.doc: Destroys an alarms list at a specified AN.
alarmlistdestroy.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN number associated with the alarms list you want to destroy.

alarmlistdisplay.name: AlarmListDisplay
alarmlistdisplay.doc: Displays an alarms list at a specified AN.
alarmlistdisplay.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN number associated with the alarms list you want to display.

alarmlistfill.name: AlarmListFill
alarmlistfill.doc: Fills an alarms list at a specified AN to be used by another routine (for example, the interlocks processing routine).
alarmlistfill.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN number associated with the alarms list you want to use.

alarmnextcatrec.name: AlarmNextCatRec
alarmnextcatrec.doc: Searches for the next occurrence of an alarm category and type, commencing with the specified alarm record identifier (returned from the previous search through the AlarmFirstCatRec function). You can search all areas, the current area only, or specify an area to limit the search.
alarmnextcatrec.returns: The alarm record identifier or -1 if no match is found.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.Category: The alarm category or group number to match. Set Category to 0 (zero) to match all alarm categories.
paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.Area: The area in which to search for alarms. If you choose to omit the area, or if you set Area to -1, only the current area will be searched.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmnextprirec.name: AlarmNextPriRec
alarmnextprirec.doc: Searches for the next occurrence of an alarm of a specified priority and type, commencing with the specified alarm record identifier (returned from the previous search through the AlarmFirstPriRec() function). You can search all areas, the current area only, or specify an area to limit the search.
alarmnextprirec.returns: The alarm record identifier or -1 if no match is found.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.Priority: The alarm Priority or group handle of a group of alarm priorities. Set Priority to 0 (zero) to match all alarm priorities.
paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.Area: The area in which to search for alarms. Set Area to -1 to search all areas. If you do not specify an area, only alarms in the current area on the Alarms Server are searched.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmnexttagrec.name: AlarmNextTagRec
alarmnexttagrec.doc: Searches for the next occurrence of an alarm tag, name, and description, starting with the alarm record identifier (returned from the previous search through the AlarmFirstTagRec function).
alarmnexttagrec.returns: The alarm record identifier or -1 if no match is found.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.Tag: A string that identifies the tag to be matched. It can be one of the following:
paramDocs.Name: The alarm name to be matched. Specify an empty string (" ") to match all alarm names.
paramDocs.Description: The alarm description to be matched. Specify an empty string (" ") to match all alarm descriptions.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks " ".

alarmnotifyvarchange.name: AlarmNotifyVarChange
alarmnotifyvarchange.doc: This function is used to provide time-stamped digital and time-stamped analog alarms with data. When called, it notifies the alarm server that the specified variable tag has changed.
alarmnotifyvarchange.returns: For synchronous mode, the return value will be the error that was detected when the function was called. For asynchronous mode, the return value will be 0, unless there was no server available.

paramDocs.Tag: Name of the variable tag that has changed as a string. This name may include the name of the tag's cluster in the form cluster.tagname. This cluster name may be different from the cluster of the alarm server indicated by ClusterName below.
paramDocs.Value: Value of the variable tag at the time of the change as a floating-point number
paramDocs.Timestamp: Time/date at which the variable tag changed in the standard Plant SCADA time/date variable format (Seconds since 1970).
paramDocs.TimestampMS: Millisecond portion of the time at which the variable tag changed.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Name of the cluster of the alarm server. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.bSync: An optional boolean argument that specifies whether the command is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous (non-blocking). If it is specified as synchronous (true) the function will wait until the notification has been recorded into the alarm database before further code execution. If it is specified as asynchronous (false) the function will only return an error if no alarm server is currently available.

alarmqueryfirstrec.name: AlarmQueryFirstRec
alarmqueryfirstrec.doc: Searches for the first occurrence of an alarm category (or priority) and type. This is a wrapper function of AlarmFirstCatRec and AlarmFirstPriRec.
alarmqueryfirstrec.returns: The alarm record identifier or -1 if no match is found.

paramDocs.Group: Alarm category if QueryType is 0 or alarm priority if QueryType is 1.
paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.Area: Area in which to search for alarms. Set Area to -1 to search all areas.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks " ".

alarmquerynextrec.name: AlarmQueryNextRec
alarmquerynextrec.doc: Searches for the next occurrence of an alarm category (or priority) and type, commencing with the specified alarm record identifier (returned from the previous search through the alarm query functions).
alarmquerynextrec.returns: The alarm record identifier or -1 if no match is found.

paramDocs.Group: Alarm Category if QueryType is 0 or alarm priority if QueryType is 1.
paramDocs.nType: The type of alarms to display:
paramDocs.Area: Area in which to search for alarms. Set Area to -1 to search all areas.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmresetquery.name: AlarmResetQuery
alarmresetquery.doc: Clears the filter of the specified filter source. Used to reset the filter set up by the Cicode function AlarmFilterForm. This function uses the AlarmFilterEdit family of Cicode functions, to reset the filter.

paramDocs.FilterSrc: The source where the filter will be applied to. It can either be the Animation Number (AN) of an alarm list or the name of a filter created via the AlarmFilterOpen Cicode function. If it is not specified, it is defaulted to -1 which refers to all alarm lists on the current page.

alarmsetdelay.name: AlarmSetDelay
alarmsetdelay.doc: Changes the delay setting for an alarm (that is Delay, High High Delay, Deviation Delay, etc.). This function acts on the alarm that the cursor is positioned over. Use this function during runtime to change the delay values that were specified in the alarms database. Delay changes made using this process are persistent (that is they are saved to the project).
alarmsetdelay.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nType: The type of delay:
paramDocs.Value: The new value for the delay. Enter a blank value " " to remove the delay setting.

alarmsetdelayrec.name: AlarmSetDelayRec
alarmsetdelayrec.doc: Changes the delay setting for an alarm (that is Delay, High High Delay, Deviation Delay, etc.) by the alarm record number. You can only call this function on an alarms server for local alarms, or on a redundant server if one has been configured.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.nType: The type of delay:
paramDocs.Value: The new value for the delay. Enter a blank value " " to remove the delay setting.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmsetinfo.name: AlarmSetInfo
alarmsetinfo.doc: Controls different aspects of the alarm list displayed at a specified AN. Currently applies only to non-hardware alarm lists.
alarmsetinfo.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the alarm list originally commenced. (AN alarm page can contain more than one alarm list). You can also specify:
paramDocs.Type: The type of data. The aspects and related types are listed below:
paramDocs.Value: The meaning of the Value argument depends on the data type specified in the Type argument.

alarmsetthreshold.name: AlarmSetThreshold
alarmsetthreshold.doc: Changes the thresholds (that is High High, Low etc.) of analog alarms. This function acts on the analog alarm where the cursor is positioned. Use this function to change (at run time) the threshold values that were specified in the Analog Alarms database. Threshold changes made using this function are permanent (that is they are saved to the project). The display format currently specified for the record (in the Analog Alarms settings) will be applied to these values.
alarmsetthreshold.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nType: The type of threshold:
paramDocs.Value: The new value of the threshold. Enter a blank value " " to remove the threshold.

alarmsetthresholdrec.name: AlarmSetThresholdRec
alarmsetthresholdrec.doc: Changes the threshold (that is High High, Low etc.) of analog alarms by the alarm record number. You can call this function only on an Alarms Server for alarms on that server, or on the redundant server (if a redundant server is configured).
alarmsetthresholdrec.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.Value: The new value of the threshold. Enter a blank value "" to remove the threshold.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmsplit.name: AlarmSplit
alarmsplit.doc: Splits an alarm summary entry which has no Off time. The current entry will be given an off time equal to the time when AlarmSplit is called, and the new entry will have the same On time, with empty Off time.
alarmsplit.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.AN: Animation Number where alarm is displayed. You can:

alarmsumappend.name: AlarmSumAppend
alarmsumappend.doc: Appends a new blank record to the alarm summary. Use this function to add new alarm summary entries, either for actual alarms or as special user summary entries.
alarmsumappend.returns: The index of the alarm summary entry, or -1 if the record could not be appended.

paramDocs.sTag: The alarm tag to append. Use an asterisk '*' as the first letter to append a user event to the alarm summary. Please be aware that the AlarmSumAppend function returns the alarm summary index - not the error code.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.OnTime: The alarm OnTime (if omitted or is equal to 0, will default to current time, i.e. the time the function was invoked).
paramDocs.OnMilli: Milliseconds part of the alarm's ON time

alarmsumcommit.name: AlarmSumCommit
alarmsumcommit.doc: Commits the alarm summary entry to the Summary Device specified in the alarm category of the entry. The same alarm summary entry is unable to be committed twice. The Cicode function returns an error code if the entry has been commited by timeout (referring to [Alarm]SummaryTimeout parameter), or if AlarmSumCommit() is called twice. An entry is not commited by timeout if AlarmSumCommit() is called on this entry.
alarmsumcommit.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Index: The alarm summary index (returned from the AlarmSumFirst(), AlarmSumNext(), AlarmSumLast(), AlarmSumPrev(), AlarmSumAppend(), or AlarmSumFind() function).
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmsumdelete.name: AlarmSumDelete
alarmsumdelete.doc: Deletes an alarm summary entry. You identify the alarm summary entry by the Index, returned by one of the alarm summary search functions.
alarmsumdelete.returns: 0 (zero) if the specified alarm entry exists, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Index: The alarm summary index (returned from the AlarmSumFirst(), AlarmSumNext(), AlarmSumLast(), AlarmSumPrev(), AlarmSumAppend(), or AlarmSumFind() function).
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmsumfind.name: AlarmSumFind
alarmsumfind.doc: Finds the alarm summary index for an alarm that you specify by the alarm record identifier and alarm activation time (OnTime). You can use this index in the AlarmSumGet() function to get field data from an alarm record, in the AlarmSumSet() function to change the existing data in that record, or in the AlarmSumDelete() function to delete the record. If calling this function from a remote client, use the MsgRPC() function.
alarmsumfind.returns: The index of the alarm summary entry, or -1 if no alarm summary entry is found.

paramDocs.Record: The alarm record number, returned from any of the following alarm functions:
paramDocs.OnTime: The ON time of the alarm associated with the Record, that is, the time that the alarm was activated.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmsumfirst.name: AlarmSumFirst
alarmsumfirst.doc: Gets the index of the oldest alarm summary entry. You can use this index in the AlarmSumGet() function to get field data from an alarm record, in the AlarmSumSet() function to change the existing data in that record, or in the AlarmSumDelete() function to delete the record.
alarmsumfirst.returns: The index of the oldest alarm summary entry, or -1 if no alarm summary entry is found.

paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmsumget.name: AlarmSumGet
alarmsumget.doc: Gets field data from an alarm summary entry. The data is returned as a string. You identify the alarm summary entry by the Index, returned by one of the alarm summary search functions. If calling this function from a remote client, use the MsgRPC function.
alarmsumget.returns: Field data from the alarm summary entry (as a string).

paramDocs.Index: The alarm summary index (returned from the AlarmSumFirst(), AlarmSumNext(), AlarmSumLast(), AlarmSumPrev(), AlarmSumAppend(), or AlarmSumFind() function).
paramDocs.sField: The name of the field from which to extract the data:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmsumlast.name: AlarmSumLast
alarmsumlast.doc: Gets the index of the most recent alarm summary entry. You can use this index in the AlarmSumGet() function to get field data from an alarm record, in the AlarmSumSet() function to change the existing data in that record, or in the AlarmSumDelete() function to delete the record.
alarmsumlast.returns: The index of the most recent alarm summary entry, or -1 if no alarm summary entry is found.

paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Alarm Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the alarm server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

alarmsumnext.name: AlarmSumNext
alarmsumnext.doc: Gets the index of the next alarm summary entry, that is, the entry that occurred later than the entry specified by Index. You can use this index in the AlarmSumGet() function to get field data from an alarm record, in the AlarmSumSet() function to change the existing data in that record, or in the AlarmSumDelete() function to delete the record.
alarmsumnext.returns: The index of the next alarm summary entry or -1 if no more alarm summary entries are found.

alarmsumprev.name: AlarmSumPrev
alarmsumprev.doc: Gets the index of the previous alarm summary entry, that is, the entry that occurred before the entry specified by Index. You can use this index in the AlarmSumGet function to get field data from an alarm record, in the AlarmSumSet function to change the existing data in that record, or in the AlarmSumDelete function to delete the record.
alarmsumprev.returns: The index of the previous alarm summary entry or -1 if no more alarm summary entries are found.

paramDocs.Index: The alarm summary index (returned from the AlarmSumFirst(), AlarmSumNext(), AlarmSumLast(), AlarmSumPrev(), or AlarmSumFind() function).

almbrowsegetfield.doc: The AlmBrowseGetField function retrieves the value of the specified field from the record the data browse cursor is currently referencing.
almbrowsegetfield.returns: The value of the specified field as a string. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. The last error should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred.

paramDocs.sFieldName: The name of the field that references the value to be returned. Supported fields are:

almbrowsenext.name: AlmBrowseNext
almbrowsenext.doc: The AlmBrowseNext function moves the data browse cursor forward one record. If you call this function after you have reached the end of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
almbrowsenext.returns: 0 (zero) if the browse has successfully been moved to the next record, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AlmBrowseOpen call.

almbrowsenumrecords.name: AlmBrowseNumRecords
almbrowsenumrecords.doc: The AlmBrowseNumRecords function returns the number of records that match the filter criteria.
almbrowsenumrecords.returns: The number of records that have matched the filter criteria. A value of 0 denotes that no records have matched. A value of -1 denotes that the browse session is unable to provide a fixed number. This may be the case if the data being browsed changed during the browse session.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AlmBrowseOpen call.

almbrowseopen.name: AlmBrowseOpen
almbrowseopen.doc: The AlmBrowseOpen function initiates a new browse session and returns a handle to the new session that can be used in subsequent data browse function calls. Use this function to browse all configured alarms.
almbrowseopen.returns: Returns an integer handle to the browse session. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.Filter: A filter expression specifying the records to return during the browse. An empty string indicates that all records will be returned. Where a fieldname is not specified in the filter, it is assumed to be tagname. For example, the filter "AAA" is equivalent to "Tag=AAA". Multiple filters separated by semicolons are supported.
paramDocs.Fields: Specifies via a comma delimited string the columns to be returned during the browse. An empty string indicates that the server will return all available columns. Supported fields are:
paramDocs.Clusters: An optional parameter that specifies via a comma delimited string the subset of the clusters to browse. An empty string indicates that the connected clusters will be browsed.
paramDocs.AutoCloseMode: An optional parameter to automatically close the browsing session at page navigation.

almbrowseprev.name: AlmBrowsePrev
almbrowseprev.doc: The AlmBrowsePrev function moves the data browse cursor back one record. If you call this function after you have reached the beginning of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
almbrowseprev.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AlmBrowseOpen call.

almsummaryack.name: AlmSummaryAck
almsummaryack.doc: The AlmSummaryAck function acknowledges the alarm in the active alarm list which is linked to the current entry of the alarm summary browse session.
almsummaryack.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AlmSummaryOpen call.

almsummaryclear.name: AlmSummaryClear
almsummaryclear.doc: The AlmSummaryClear function clears the latched alarm at the current cursor position in an active data browse session. A latched alarm is an alarm which is OFF and acknowledged when [Alarm]AckHold is set to 1. The function does nothing if the alarm summary entry at the cursor is not linked to a latched alarm.
almsummaryclear.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AlmSummaryOpen call.

almsummaryclose.name: AlmSummaryClose
almsummaryclose.doc: The AlmSummaryClose function terminates an active data browse session and cleans up all resources associated with the session.
almsummaryclose.returns: 0 (zero) if the alarm browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AlmSummaryOpen call.

almsummarycommit.doc: The AlmSummaryCommit function triggers the actual write of the value for the field previously specified by AlmSummarySetFieldValue.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a AlmSummaryOpen call.

almsummarydelete.name: AlmSummaryDelete
almsummarydelete.doc: The AlmSummaryDelete function deletes the record in the filtered list that the cursor is currently referencing. The cursor moves to the next available entry in the data browse session after the current alarm summary is deleted.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a filtered list previously returned by a AlmSummaryOpen call.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a filtered list previously returned by a AlmSummaryOpen call.

arraycopy.name: ArrayCopy
arraycopy.doc: Makes a copy of an array.

paramDocs.hArray: The handle of the array you want to copy.

arraycreate.name: ArrayCreate
arraycreate.doc: Creates an array. An array can include up to 2,097,153 elements, but each dimension needs to have less than 32765.
arraycreate.returns: The handle of the array. If unsuccessful, –1 is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.x: The size of the array's x–dimension (from 1 to 32765).
paramDocs.y: The size of the array's y–dimension (from 1 to 32765). This value is optional. If not specified, it defaults to 1.
paramDocs.z: The size of the array's z–dimension (from 1 to 32765). This value is optional. If not specified, it defaults to 1.

arraycreatebyan.name: ArrayCreateByAn
arraycreatebyan.doc: Creates an array at a specified AN. An array can include up to 2,097,153 elements, but each dimension needs to have less than 32765.
arraycreatebyan.returns: The handle of the array. If unsuccessful, –1 is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN number to associate with the array.

paramDocs.y: The size of the array's y–dimension (from 1 to 32765). This value is optional. If not specified, it defaults to 1.
paramDocs.z: The size of the array's z–dimension (from 1 to 32765). This value is optional. If not specified, it defaults to 1.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN associated with array.

arrayisdirty.name: ArrayIsDirty
arrayisdirty.doc: Determines if an array is ‘dirty’ (information in the array has changed). When any array element is changed, the ‘Dirty’ flag of the array is set to be TRUE.
arrayisdirty.returns: 1 if true (is dirty), or 0 if false (is not dirty). An error is not returned by this function.

arraysetint.name: ArraySetInt
arraysetint.doc: Sets an integer value within an array.
arraysetint.returns: If unsuccessful, an error code will be returned by the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.nValue: The value you would like to set.

arraysetintbyan.name: ArraySetIntByAn
arraysetintbyan.doc: Sets an integer value in an array associated with a specified AN.
arraysetintbyan.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN associated with the array.
paramDocs.nValue: The value you would like to set.

arraysetisdirty.name: ArraySetIsDirty
arraysetisdirty.doc: Allows you to indicate that an array is dirty (meaning the information in the array has changed), or not dirty (the information in the array has not been changed).
arraysetisdirty.returns: If unsuccessful, an error code will be returned by the IsError Cicode function.

arraysetstring.name: ArraySetString
arraysetstring.doc: Sets a string value in an array.
arraysetstring.returns: If unsuccessful, an error code will be returned by the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.sValue: The string value you would like to set.

arraysetstringbyan.name: ArraySetStringByAn
arraysetstringbyan.doc: Sets a string value in an array associated with a specified AN.
arraysetstringbyan.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN associated with the array.
paramDocs.sValue: The string value you would like to set.

arrayswap.name: ArraySwap
arrayswap.doc: Swaps the contents of two arrays.
arrayswap.returns: If unsuccessful, an error code will be returned by the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.hArray1: The handle of the array that you would like to swap with hArray2.
paramDocs.hArray2: The handle of the array that you would like to swap with hArray1.

ass.name: Ass
ass.doc: Associates a variable tag or equipment with a Super Genie. This association is only made for the next Super Genie you display (either in the current window or in a new window). You cannot create an association for a Super Genie that is already displayed. You need to call this function once for every Super Genie substitution string in the Super Genie, otherwise the variable (substitution string) will remain uninitialized and it will be displayed as #ASC.
ass.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.When using partial associations, an error 274 or 289 may be returned even though the association is successful, and can be ignored.

paramDocs.hWin: The association will be created for the next Super Genie to display in the window specified here; enter the window number or:
paramDocs.nArg: The argument number or name (substitution string number or name) of the Super Genie string to be replaced by sTag. For example, to replace ?INT 3? with sTag, set nArg to 3 ,or ?Level? set nArg to Level.
paramDocs.sTag: Variable tag, or equipment and item name reference of a variable tag (using equipment.item notation) that will replace the Super Genie association. Partial tag names or equipment.item tag references can also be used.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the association. Set to 0.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Variable Tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the tag via the page's current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

asschain.name: AssChain
asschain.doc: Chains the associations from the current Super Genie to a new Super Genie. Use this function to display a new Super Genie when you already have one displayed. The new Super Genie will inherit the associations of the first Super Genie.
asschain.returns: Returns the number of associations copied.

paramDocs.hDest: The next Super Genie to display in the window specified here will inherit the associations of the current Super Genie - enter the window number, or:
paramDocs.hSource: The number of the window containing the source Super Genie (that is the Super Genie from which the associations will be inherited).
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the association. Set to 0.

asschainpage.name: AssChainPage
asschainpage.doc: Chains the associations from the current Super Genie to a new Super Genie, and displays the new Super Genie (in the current window). Use this function to display a new Super Genie when you already have one displayed. The new Super Genie will inherit the associations of the first Super Genie.
asschainpage.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The page name of the Super Genie. If you prefixed your Super Genie page name with an exclamation mark (!), remember to include it here.

asschainpopup.name: AssChainPopUp
asschainpopup.doc: Chains the associations from the current Super Genie to a new Super Genie, and displays the new Super Genie in a new popup window. Use this function to display a new Super Genie in a new popup window when a Super Genie is already displayed. The new Super Genie will inherit the associations of the first.
asschainpopup.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The page name of the Super Genie. If you prefixed your Super Genie page name with an exclamation mark (!), remember to include it here.

asschainwin.name: AssChainWin
asschainwin.doc: Chains the associations from the current Super Genie to a new Super Genie, and displays the new Super Genie in a new window. The new window will be of the same type as the current window. Use this function to display a new Super Genie in a new window when a Super Genie is already displayed. The new Super Genie will inherit the associations of the first.
asschainwin.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The page name of the Super Genie. If you prefixed your Super Genie page name with an exclamation mark (!), remember to include it here.
paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.

asschainwinfree.name: AssChainWinFree
asschainwinfree.doc: Stores the associations on an existing Super Genie, closes it, then assigns the tags to a new window. This allows a Super Genie popup window to call another popup window, and close the parent popup.
asschainwinfree.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The page name of the Super Genie. If you prefixed your Super Genie page name with an exclamation mark (!), remember to include it here.
paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.

assequipparameters.name: AssEquipParameters
assequipparameters.doc: Associates a set of equipment parameters defined in Plant SCADA Studio System Model | Equipment | Runtime Parameters with a page. This association is only made for the next page you display (either in the current window or in a new window). You cannot create an association for a page that is already displayed.
assequipparameters.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.When using partial associations, an error 274 or 289 may be returned even though the association is successful, and can be ignored.

paramDocs.hWin: The association will be created for the next page to display in the window specified here; enter the window number or:
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the equipment resides. The cluster name is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the tag via the page's current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

assequipreferences.name: AssEquipReferences
assequipreferences.doc: Creates Super Genie associations for each piece of equipment referenced by the specified equipment.

paramDocs.hWin: The association will be created for the next Super Genie to display in the window specified here; enter the window number or:
paramDocs.sClusterAndEquipment: The cluster and prefixed equipment name
paramDocs.sCategory: The category of reference to create associations for.

assert.name: Assert
assert.doc: Verifies that the specified expression is TRUE. If then expression is FALSE, the current task will be halted. This is useful to help prevent the execution of code you do not want to run in the event an error has been detected.
assert.returns: None. However, if the assertion tests as FALSE, error 347 is generated.

paramDocs.bCondition: The boolean expression. This expression needs to evaluate to TRUE (1) or FALSE (0).

assgetproperty.name: AssGetProperty
assgetproperty.doc: This function gets association information about the current Super Genie from the data source (that is, information about a variable tag that has been substituted into the Super Genie). You can only call this function on a Super Genie after the associations are completed.
assgetproperty.returns: String representation of the property of the referenced tag. On detection of an error, an empty string and an error are set.

paramDocs.sArg: The argument number or name (integer or string) of the association from which to get information.
paramDocs.sProperty: The property to read. Property names are case sensitive. Supported properties are:
paramDocs.iCachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.

assgetscale.name: AssGetScale
assgetscale.doc: Gets scale information about the tag references for the current Super Genie from the datasource (that is scale information about a variable tag that has been substituted into the Super Genie). You can only call this function on a Super Genie after the associations are completed.
assgetscale.returns: The scale of the referenced tag (as a string).

paramDocs.sArg: The argument number or name of the association from which to get information.
paramDocs.iPercent: The percentage of full scale of the returned value.
paramDocs.iEngUnits: Flag to determine if the value is returned with engineering units:
paramDocs.iCached: Optional flag to attempt to retrieve the cached value for the property rather than the current value. This makes the function non-blocking. If the property has not yet been cached, an error is set.

assinfo.name: AssInfo
assinfo.doc: Gets association information about the current Super Genie (that is information about a variable tag that has been substituted into the Super Genie). You can only call this function on a Super Genie after the associations are completed.
