assinfo.returns: The value of the information as a string.

paramDocs.sArg: When you associate variable tags (can use equipment.item to reference the variable tag) with Super Genies, the Super Genie substitution strings are replaced by variable tags. The sArg argument allows you to get information about one of those variable tags. What you need to know is which substitution string it replaced when the association was performed.
paramDocs.nType: The type of information to get:
paramDocs.iCachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.

assinfoex.name: AssInfoEx
assinfoex.doc: Gets association information about the current Super Genie (that is information about a variable tag that has been substituted into the Super Genie). You can only call this function on a Super Genie after the associations are completed.
assinfoex.returns: The value of the information as a string. If an error is detected an empty string is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.sArg: When you associate variable tags with super Genies, the Super Genie substitution strings are replaced by variable tags. The sArg argument allows you to get information about one of those variable tags. What you need to know is which substitution string it replaced when the association was performed.
paramDocs.nType: The type of information to get:
paramDocs.iCachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.

assmetadata.name: AssMetadata
assmetadata.doc: This non-blocking function performs Super Genie associations using the "Name" and "Value" fields defined on the Object Properties - Metadata tab, and matches it to the 'Name' field in the page associations table. While performing associations any additional metadata entries are ignored.
assmetadata.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.When using partial associations, an error 274 may be returned even though the association is successful, and can be ignored.

paramDocs.hWin: The associations will be created for the next Super Genie to display in the window specified. Enter the window number or:
paramDocs.nAN: An animation number that uniquely identifies an object. This object contains the list of metadata definitions that will be used to perform the association operations.This parameter is optional with -2 being the default value.When -2 is specified, it is equivalent to DspGetAnCur() which returns the animation number of the current active command cursor, please refer DspGetAnCur() for usage and limitations.

assmetadatapage.name: AssMetadataPage
assmetadatapage.doc: Uses the metadata information from the current object for the page associations for a new Super Genie page, and displays the new Super Genie (in the current page).
assmetadatapage.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the Super Genie page to open.
paramDocs.nAN: An animation number that uniquely identifies an object. This object contains the list of metadata definitions that will be used to perform the association operations.This parameter is optional with -2 being the default value. When -2 is specified, it is equivalent to DspGetAnCur() which returns the animation number of the current active command cursor, please refer DspGetAnCur() for usage and limitations.

assmetadatapopup.name: AssMetadataPopUp
assmetadatapopup.doc: Uses the metadata information from the current animation point for the associations for a new Super Genie page, and displays the new Super Genie in a pop up window.
assmetadatapopup.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the Super Genie page to open.
paramDocs.nAN: An animation number that uniquely identifies an object. This object contains the list of metadata definitions that will be used to perform the association operations.This parameter is optional with -2 being the default value. When -2 is specified, it is equivalent to DspGetAnCur() which returns the animation number of the current active command cursor, please refer DspGetAnCur() for usage and limitations.

assmetadatawin.name: AssMetadataWin
assmetadatawin.doc: Uses the metadata information from the current animation-point for the associations for a new Super Genie page, and displays the new Super Genie in a new window.
assmetadatawin.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the Super Genie page to open.
paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window. Default value is 0.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window. Default value is 0.
paramDocs.nAN: An animation number that uniquely identifies an object. This object contains the list of metadata definitions that will be used to perform the association operations.This parameter is optional with -2 being the default value.When -2 is specified, it is equivalent to DspGetAnCur() which returns the animation number of the current active command cursor, please refer DspGetAnCur() for usage and limitations.

asspage.name: AssPage
asspage.doc: Associates up to eight variable tags or equipment.item tag references with a Super Genie and displays the Super Genie in the current window. Partial tag names and equipment.item tag references can also be used. The first variable tag (sTag1) replaces Super Genie substitution string 1. The second variable tag (sTag2) replaces substitution string 2, and so on.
asspage.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The page name of the Super Genie. If you prefixed your Super Genie page name with an exclamation mark (!), remember to include it here.
paramDocs.sTag1..sTag8: The first eight physical tags to be associated with the Super Genie. For any given Super Genie, the variable tags will replace the Super Genie substitution strings as follows:

asspopup.name: AssPopUp
asspopup.doc: Associates up to eight variable tags or equipment.item tag references with a Super Genie and displays the Super Genie in a popup window. Partial tag names or equipment.item tag references can also be used. The first variable tag (sTag1) replaces Super Genie substitution string 1. The second variable tag (sTag2) replaces substitution string 2, and so on.
asspopup.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The page name of the Super Genie. If you prefixed your Super Genie page name with an exclamation mark (!), remember to include it here.
paramDocs.sTag1..sTag8: The first 8 physical tags to be associated with the Super Genie. For any given Super Genie, the variable tags will replace the Super Genie substitution strings as follows:

assscalestr.name: AssScaleStr
assscalestr.doc: Gets scale information about the associations of the current Super Genie (that is scale information about a variable tag that has been substituted into the Super Genie). You can only call this function on a Super Genie after the associations are completed.
assscalestr.returns: The scale of the referenced tag(as a string).

paramDocs.sArg: When you associate variable tags with Super Genies, the Super Genie substitution strings are replaced by variable tags. The nArg argument allows you to get scale information about a particular variable tag. You need to know which substitution string the tag replaced when the association was performed.
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of full scale of the returned value.
paramDocs.EngUnits: Determines if the value is returned with engineering units:
paramDocs.CachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.

asstag.name: AssTag
asstag.doc: Associates a variable tag or equipment.item tag reference with a Super Genie. The association will only be created for the next Super Genie you display in the current window, and will only come into effect after you re-display the Super Genie. You need to call this function once for every substitution string in the current Super Genie, or the super-genie variable (substitution string) will remain uninitialized and it will display as #ASC. You cannot use this function to create associations for variables that will display in new windows.
asstag.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.When using partial associations, an error 274, or 289 may be returned even though the association is successful, and can be ignored.

paramDocs.nArg: The argument name (substitution string name) of the Super Genie string to be replaced by sTag. For example, to replace ?INT equip? with sTag, set nArg to equip.
paramDocs.sTag: The variable tag or equipment.item tag reference that will replace the Super Genie substitution string.Partial tag names or equipment.item tag references can also be used.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Variable Tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the tag via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

asstitle.name: AssTitle
asstitle.doc: Sets the runtime window title to the tag name of the first variable substituted into the Super Genie.
asstitle.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Mask: The number of characters to mask (hide) from the right of the title string (optional).
paramDocs.Prefix: A string to add to the beginning of the title string (optional).
paramDocs.Suffix: A string to add to the end of the title string (optional).

assvartags.name: AssVarTags
assvartags.doc: Associates up to eight variable tags or equipment.item tag references with a Super Genie. Partial tag names or equipment.item tag references can also be used. This association is only made for the next Super Genie you display (either in the current window or in a new window). This function has an offset that allows you to specify which substitution string the first variable tag will replace. This means that if you have a Super Genie with more than 8 substitution strings, you can use this function repeatedly (while increasing the offset), until you have associated the necessary variable tags.

paramDocs.hWin: The association will be created for the next Super Genie to display in the window specified here - enter the window number or:
paramDocs.nOffset: By default, the first variable tag (sTag1) will replace substitution string 1, and sTag2 will replace substitution string 2, and so on. Enter an offset to change this so that sTag1 replaces a substitution string other than the first. For example, an offset of 8 means that sTag1 replaces string 9 instead of the default string 1 (8+1=9), and sTag2 replaces string 10 instead of string 2 (8+2=10) etc. This means that you can use this function repeatedly to associate more than eight variables.
paramDocs.sTag1..8: The physical variable tags (up to eight) to be associated with the Super Genie. For any given Super Genie, the variable tags will replace the Super Genie substitution strings as follows:

asswin.name: AssWin
asswin.doc: Associates up to eight variable tags or equipment.item tag references with a Super Genie, and displays the Super Genie in a new window. This function has the same effect as calling the Ass() or AssTag() function eight times, and then calling the WinNewAt() function. The AssWin() function is a quick way of associating eight Super Genie variables and creating a new window - at the same time.
asswin.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The page name of the Super Genie. If you prefixed your Super Genie page name with an exclamation mark (!), remember to include it here.
paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.sTag1..8: The first eight physical tags to be associated with the Super Genie. For any given Super Genie, the variable tags will replace the Super Genie substitution strings as follows:

asswinreplace.name: AssWinReplace
asswinreplace.doc: This function removes the associations on a specified Super Genie window and applies any pending associations. This may be a useful alternative to calling PageDisplay or WinNewAt to update associations, as a full page reload is not required.
asswinreplace.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nTargetWindow: The number of the window where associations will be replaced.

beep.name: Beep
beep.doc: Beeps the internal speaker or sound card (installed in the computer). If you use the internal speaker on your computer, the function does not return until the sound has completed. If you use a sound card, the function returns immediately and the sound plays in the background.
beep.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

callevent.name: CallEvent
callevent.doc: Simulates an event, triggering any OnEvent() function that has the same Type argument specified.
callevent.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is set. To view the error, use the IsError() function.

paramDocs.Window: The number of the window, returned from the WinNew(), WinNewAt(), or WinNumber() function.
paramDocs.nType: The type of event:

chainevent.name: ChainEvent
chainevent.doc: Calls an event function using the function handle. This creates a chain of event handlers from a single event. Use the GetEvent() function to get the function number of the current event handler.
chainevent.returns: The return value of the called event function.

paramDocs.hFn: The function handle, as returned from the GetEvent() function.

chartostr.name: CharToStr
chartostr.doc: Converts an ASCII code into a string.
chartostr.returns: A string containing the converted ASCII code.

citectcolourtopackedrgb.name: CitectColourToPackedRGB
citectcolourtopackedrgb.doc: Converts a Plant SCADA color value into a packed RGB color value that can be understood by an ActiveX object.
citectcolourtopackedrgb.returns: The packed RGB color value - if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nCitectColor: The Plant SCADA color value to be converted into a packed RGB color. Plant SCADA colors are defined in the labels database, or calculated by the function MakeColour.

citectinfo.name: CitectInfo
citectinfo.doc: Gets information about a Plant SCADA variable. This function returns internal statistics and other information about the Plant SCADAruntime system.
citectinfo.returns: The type of information (as an integer).

paramDocs.sGroup: The name of the group to which the variable belongs. Valid group names are: "General", "Port", "IODevice", "Network", "Stats", "Memory", "Disk" or "Queue".
paramDocs.sName: The name of the variable. This name depends on sGroup:
paramDocs.sType: The type of information to get, depending on sGroup:

clipcopy.name: ClipCopy
clipcopy.doc: Copies a string to the Windows clipboard. When the string is in the clipboard, you can paste it to any Windows program.
clipcopy.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sText: The string to copy to the clipboard.

clippaste.name: ClipPaste
clippaste.doc: Pastes a string from the Windows clipboard.
clippaste.returns: The contents of the clipboard (as a string). If the clipboard is empty, an empty string is returned.

clipreadln.name: ClipReadLn
clipreadln.doc: Reads a single line of text from the Windows clipboard. With this function, you can read a block of text from the clipboard - line by line. Call the function once to read each line of text from the clipboard. When the end of the clipboard is reached, an empty string is returned.
clipreadln.returns: One line of text from the clipboard (as a string). If the clipboard is empty, an empty string is returned.

clipsetmode.name: ClipSetMode
clipsetmode.doc: Sets the format of data sent to the Windows clipboard.
clipsetmode.returns: The value of the previous mode.

paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the data:

clipwriteln.name: ClipWriteLn
clipwriteln.doc: Writes a line of text to the Windows clipboard. With this function, you can write any amount of text to the clipboard. Call this function once for each line of text. To terminate the block of text, call this function and pass an empty string.
clipwriteln.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sText: The line of text to write to the clipboard, or an empty string (" ") to end the write operation.

clusteractivate.name: ClusterActivate
clusteractivate.doc: This function allows the user to activate an inactive cluster. When a cluster is made active, all data associated with that cluster is available to the client, and hardware alarms will occur if no connections can be made to the servers in the cluster.
clusteractivate.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to activate enclosed in quotation marks "".

clusterdeactivate.name: ClusterDeactivate
clusterdeactivate.doc: This function allows the user to deactivate an active cluster. When a cluster is made inactive, no data associated with that cluster is available to the client, and hardware alarms will not occur if no connections can be made to the servers in the cluster.
clusterdeactivate.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to deactivate enclosed in quotation marks "".

clusterfirst.name: ClusterFirst
clusterfirst.doc: This function allows the user to retrieve the first configured cluster in the project.
clusterfirst.returns: The name of the first configured cluster.

clustergetname.name: ClusterGetName
clustergetname.doc: ClusterGetName is deprecated in this version of Plant SCADA.
clustergetname.returns: The status of the get name.

paramDocs.sPrimary: The name of the cluster's primary server (that is that which was set as sPrimary using the ClusterSetName() function). Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.sStandby: The name of the cluster's standby server (that is that which was set as sStandby using the ClusterSetName() function). Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode is for future expansion of the function - set to 0 (zero).

clusterisactive.name: ClusterIsActive
clusterisactive.doc: This function allows the user to determine if a cluster is active.
clusterisactive.returns: TRUE if active, FALSE otherwise. If the cluster name was invalid, this function will return FALSE and a hardware alarm will be generated.

paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to query enclosed in quotation marks " ".

clusternext.name: ClusterNext
clusternext.doc: This function allows the user to retrieve the next configured cluster in the project.
clusternext.returns: The name of the next configured cluster or an empty string if there is no more clusters.

paramDocs.sClusterName: Any configured cluster name enclosed in quotation marks "", this will usually be the name of the previous cluster as returned from ClusterFirst, or a previous call to ClusterNext.

clusterservertypes.name: ClusterServerTypes
clusterservertypes.doc: This function allows the user to determine which servers are defined for a given cluster.
clusterservertypes.returns: Logical OR of the following server flags:

paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to query enclosed in quotation marks "".

clustersetname.name: ClusterSetName
clustersetname.doc: ClusterSetName is deprecated in this version of Plant SCADA.
clustersetname.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPrimary: The name of the cluster's primary server (Reports Server, Alarms Server etc.), as defined using the Computer Setup Wizard. When the ClusterSetName() function is used, Plant SCADA will attempt to connect to this server.
paramDocs.sStandby: The name of the cluster's standby server (Reports Server, Alarms Server etc.), as defined using the Computer Setup Wizard. If the sPrimary server is unavailable when the ClusterSetName() function is used, Plant SCADA will attempt to connect to this server.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the connection:

clusterstatus.name: ClusterStatus
clusterstatus.doc: This function allows the user to determine the connection status from the client to a server on a cluster.

paramDocs.clusterName: The name of the cluster to query enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.serverType: The type of server (not a bit mask):

clusterswapactive.name: ClusterSwapActive
clusterswapactive.doc: This function allows the user to deactivate an active cluster at the same time as activating an inactive cluster. The arguments may be passed in any order, but one cluster needs to be active and the other needs to be inactive.
clusterswapactive.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.clusterNameA: The name of the cluster to activate or deactivate enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.clusterNameB: The name of the cluster to activate or deactivate enclosed in quotation marks "".

codesetmode.name: CodeSetMode
codesetmode.doc: Sets various execution modes for Cicode tasks in the current thread. Using this function, you can specify whether to:
codesetmode.returns: -1 if there is an error, otherwise the last value of the mode.

paramDocs.nType: Type of mode:
paramDocs.Value: The value of the mode:

codetrace.name: CodeTrace
codetrace.doc: Traces Cicode into the Kernel and the SYSLOG.DAT file. Use this function for finding bugs in your Cicode. It will trace the functions called, the arguments to those functions, and their return values. It will also trace any errors, writes to the I/O devices, and task state changes.
codetrace.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hTask: The Cicode task handle as returned from TaskHnd() function or any of the following special values:
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the trace:

comclose.name: ComClose
comclose.doc: This function flags a port for close and reopen when the next ComOpen (Port mode 0) or driver open occurs. It does not actually close the port when called. Any Cicode tasks that are waiting for a read or write operation to complete (or that are retrying to read or write) return with a range error.
comclose.returns: 0 if the port is successfully closed, or an error if the port is already closed or if the port number is invalid.

paramDocs.hPort: The communication port handle, returned from the ComOpen function. This handle identifies the table where all data on the associated communication port is stored.

comopen.name: ComOpen
comopen.doc: Opens a communication port for access. The board and port need to both be defined in the database (using the Boards and Ports settings).
comopen.returns: A communication port handle if the communication system is opened successfully, otherwise -1 is returned. The handle identifies the table where all data on the associated port is stored. You can use the handle in the other communication functions, to send and receive characters from the port.

paramDocs.sPort: The port name as specified in the Ports database.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the open:

comread.name: ComRead
comread.doc: Reads characters from a communication port. The characters are read from the communication port into a string buffer. If no characters have arrived after the specified timeout, the function returns with a timeout error. If the timeout is 0, the function gets any characters that have arrived from the last call, and returns immediately.
comread.returns: 0 (zero) if the read is successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hPort: The communication port handle, returned from the ComOpen() function. This handle identifies the table where the data on the associated communication port is stored.
paramDocs.sBuffer: The buffer into which to put the characters. The actual number of characters read is returned in iLength. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.iLength: The number of characters to read into the buffer. The maximum length you may read in one call is 128 characters. When the function returns, this variable is set to the actual number of characters read. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.iTimeOut: The timeout for the read to complete in seconds:

comreset.name: ComReset
comreset.doc: Resets the communication port. This function can only be called from an I/O Server.
comreset.returns: 0 (zero) if the write is successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hPort: The communication port handle, returned from the ComOpen function. This handle identifies the table where all data on the associated communication port is stored.

comwrite.name: ComWrite
comwrite.doc: Writes characters to a communication port. The characters are written from the string buffer to the port. If the characters have not been transmitted after the specified timeout, the function returns with a timeout error. If the timeout is 0, the function returns immediately and the characters are transmitted in the background.
comwrite.returns: 0 (zero) if the write is successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hPort: The communication port handle, returned from the ComOpen() function. This handle identifies the table where all data on the associated communication port is stored.
paramDocs.sBuffer: The buffer from which to write the characters. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.iLength: The number of characters to write from the buffer. The maximum number of characters you can write is 128. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.iTimeOut: The timeout for the write to complete in seconds.

cos.name: Cos
cos.doc: Calculates the trigonometric cosine of an angle.

createcontrolobject.name: CreateControlObject
createcontrolobject.doc: Creates a new instance of an ActiveX object.
createcontrolobject.returns: The newly created object, if successful, otherwise an error is generated.

paramDocs.sClass: The class of the object. You can use the object's human readable name, its program ID, or its GUID. If the class does not exist, the function will return an error message.
paramDocs.sName: The name for the object in the form of "AN" followed by its AN number, for example, "AN35". This name is used to access the object.
paramDocs.x1: The x coordinate of the object's top left hand corner as it will appear in your Plant SCADA window.
paramDocs.y1: The y coordinate of the object's top left hand corner as it will appear in your Plant SCADA window.
paramDocs.x2: The x coordinate of the object's bottom right hand corner as it will appear in your Plant SCADA window.
paramDocs.y2: The y coordinate of the object's bottom right hand corner as it will appear in your Plant SCADA window.
paramDocs.sEventClass: The string you would like to use as the event class for the object.

createobject.name: CreateObject
createobject.doc: Creates a new instance of an ActiveX object. If you use this function to create an ActiveX object, it will have no visual component (only the automation component will be created).
createobject.returns: The newly created object, if successful, otherwise an error is generated.

paramDocs.sClass: The class of the object. You can use the object's human readable name, its program ID, or its GUID. If the class does not exist, the function will return an error.

date.name: Date
date.doc: Gets the current date in string format.

dateadd.name: DateAdd
dateadd.doc: Adds time (in seconds) to a time/date value. The return value is in time/date variable format. Use this function for time and date calculations.
dateadd.returns: The date as a time/date variable.

paramDocs.Time: The time/date to which the AddTime will be added.
paramDocs.AddTime: The time to add, in seconds.

dateday.name: DateDay
dateday.doc: Gets the day of the month from a time/date variable.
dateday.returns: The day of the month as an integer.

dateinfo.name: DateInfo
dateinfo.doc: Returns the date format currently used on the Plant SCADA Server.
dateinfo.returns: A string containing one of the following:

paramDocs.nInfo: Determines the contents of the string returned by the DateInfo() function. Valid values and resulting strings are:
paramDocs.nExtra: When an nInfo argument of 6 or 7 is specified, the nExtra argument determines which weekday (1-7) is returned by the DateInfo() function.

datemonth.name: DateMonth
datemonth.doc: Gets the month from a time/date variable.
datemonth.returns: The month of the year as an integer.

datesub.name: DateSub
datesub.doc: Subtracts time (in seconds) from a time/date value. The return value is in time/date variable format. Use this function for time and date calculations.
datesub.returns: The time difference (in seconds) as an integer.

paramDocs.Time: The time/date from which the SubTime will be subtracted.
paramDocs.SubTime: The time to subtract, in seconds.

dateweekday.name: DateWeekDay
dateweekday.doc: Gets the day of the week from a time/date variable.
dateweekday.returns: An integer representing the day of the week as follows:

dateyear.name: DateYear
dateyear.doc: Gets the year from a time/date variable.

ddeexec.name: DDEExec
ddeexec.doc: Executes a command in an external Windows application running on the same computer. With this function, you can control other applications that support DDE. Refer to the documentation provided with the external Windows application to determine if DDE is supported and what functions can be called.
ddeexec.returns: 1 (one) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sCommand: The command that the application will execute.

ddehexecute.name: DDEhExecute
ddehexecute.doc: Executes a command in an external Windows application. You need to first start a conversation with the DDEhInitiate function, and use the handle returned by that function to identify the conversation.
ddehexecute.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Handle: The integer handle that identifies the DDE conversation, returned from the DDEhInitiate function.
paramDocs.sCommand: The command that the application will execute.

ddehgetlasterror.name: DDEhGetLastError
ddehgetlasterror.doc: Gets the latest error code issued from Windows for the conversation identified by the handle.
ddehgetlasterror.returns: The error code last issued from Windows DDEML (for that conversation):

ddehinitiate.name: DDEhInitiate
ddehinitiate.doc: Starts a conversation with an external Windows application. When the data exchange is complete, you should terminate the conversation to free system resources.
ddehinitiate.returns: An integer handle for the conversation between Plant SCADA and the other application, or -1 if the conversation is not started successfully. The handle is used by the other DDEh... functions, to identify the conversation.

paramDocs.sApplication: The application name (.EXE filename), for example, "WinWord".
paramDocs.sDocument: The document, topic, or file name.

ddehpoke.name: DDEhPoke
ddehpoke.doc: Writes a value to an external Windows application, for example, an Excel spreadsheet. The value is written once to the application. (To write the value dynamically, you need to call this function at the rate at which the data needs to be updated.)
ddehpoke.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Handle: The integer handle that identifies the DDE conversation, returned from the DDEhInitiate function.
paramDocs.sItem: A unique name for the item; for example, the variable name, field name, or spreadsheet cell position.

ddehreadln.name: DDEhReadLn
ddehreadln.doc: Reads a line of text from a DDE Conversion, for example, from an Excel spreadsheet. You need to first start a conversation with the DDEhInitiate function, and use the handle returned by that function to identify the conversation. This function allows you to read a large amount of data via DDE. Keep calling the function until an empty string is returned to verify that all the data has been read.
ddehreadln.returns: A line of data, or an empty string when all data has been read.

paramDocs.Handle: The integer handle that identifies the DDE conversation, returned from the DDEhInitiate function.
paramDocs.sTopic: A unique topic name for the item; for example, the variable name, field name, or spreadsheet cell position.

ddehrequest.name: DDEhRequest
ddehrequest.doc: Reads a value from an external Windows application, for example, from an Excel spreadsheet. You need to first start a conversation with the DDEhInitiate function, and use the handle returned by that function to identify the conversation.
ddehrequest.returns: A string of data, or an empty string if the function cannot read the value.

paramDocs.Handle: The integer handle that identifies the DDE conversation, returned from the DDEhInitiate function.
paramDocs.sItem: A unique name for the item; for example, the variable name, field name, or spreadsheet cell position.

ddehsetmode.name: DDEhSetMode
ddehsetmode.doc: Set the mode of the DDE conversation. The default mode of a DDE conversation is to use TEXT data format - a simple string of data. This function allows you to set the mode to CSV (Comma Separated Values). Some Windows applications support this mode of data as it helps them to separate the data. For example, when you send CSV format to Excel, each value will be placed into a unique cell. If you use TEXT mode all the data will be placed into the same cell.

paramDocs.Handle: The integer handle that identifies the DDE conversation, returned from the DDEhInitiate function.
paramDocs.sMode: The mode of the DDE conversation:

ddehterminate.name: DDEhTerminate
ddehterminate.doc: Closes the conversation identified by the handle, and frees the resources associated with that conversation. After you call this function, the handle is no longer valid.
ddehterminate.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Handle: The integer handle that identifies the DDE conversation, returned from the DDEhInitiate function.

ddehwriteln.name: DDEhWriteLn
ddehwriteln.doc: Writes a line of text to the DDE conversation. With this function, you can write any amount of text to the DDE conversation. Call this function once for each line of text. To terminate the block of text, call this function and pass an empty string.
ddehwriteln.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Handle: The integer handle that identifies the DDE conversation, returned from the DDEhInitiate function.
paramDocs.sTopic: A unique name for the topic the data will be written to; for example, the spreadsheet cell position. The topic is only used when you complete the write by passing an empty string for data.
paramDocs.sData: The line of data to write. To terminate the data and make Plant SCADA send the data, set the data to an empty string.

ddepost.name: DDEPost
ddepost.doc: Makes a Plant SCADA variable value available for DDE linking (which means it posts a DDE link so that it can be read by other DDE compliant applications running on the same computer). This sets up Plant SCADA to behave as a DDE Server for this DDE channel.
ddepost.returns: The value that is posted, or empty string if the function does not succeed in posting the link.

paramDocs.sItem: A unique name for the item; for example, the variable name, field name, or spreadsheet cell position.

dderead.name: DDERead
dderead.doc: Reads values from an external DDE compliant Windows application running on the same computer, (for example, from an Excel spreadsheet cell or a Word document).
dderead.returns: The value (from the external application) as a string, or an empty string if the function cannot read the desired values.

paramDocs.sApplication: The application name (.EXE filename), for example, "WinWord".
paramDocs.sDocument: The document, topic, or file name.
paramDocs.sItem: A unique name for the item; for example, the variable name, field name, or spreadsheet cell position.
paramDocs.Mode: A flag that tells the application whether or not to set up an advise loop:

ddewrite.name: DDEWrite
ddewrite.doc: Writes a value to an external Windows application, for example, to an Excel spreadsheet. The value is written once to the application. To write the value dynamically, you need to call this function at the rate at which the data needs to be updated.
ddewrite.returns: The value that is sent to the other application, or an empty string if the function does not successfully write the value.

paramDocs.sApplication: The application name (.EXE filename), for example, "WinWord".
paramDocs.sDocument: The document, topic, or file name.
paramDocs.sItem: A unique name for the item; for example, the variable name, field name, or spreadsheet cell position.

debugbreak.name: DebugBreak
debugbreak.doc: Causes a breakpoint exception error to occur (error number 342). This allows programmers to trap invalid states in their Cicode. If the Cicode Editor is not running, and the Plant SCADA Runtime will start debugger on hardware errors option is set (Debug menu - Options), the Debugger will be started. When the debugger starts, the correct Cicode file, function, and line will be displayed.

debugmsg.name: DebugMsg
debugmsg.doc: Provides in-line debug messages of user Cicode, to the Kernel, Debugger Debug window, and the SysLog.DAT file. This function can be enabled or disabled with the [Code]DebugMessage parameter or DebugMsgSet() function at runtime.

paramDocs.sMessage: The debugging message to log. Be sure to enclose this message in double quotes (" ").

debugmsgset.name: DebugMsgSet
debugmsgset.doc: Enables/disables the DebugMsg() logging functionality. It also controls whether logging is enabled for the Assert() function. This function also sets the [Code]DebugMessage parameter appropriately.
debugmsgset.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nMode: The logging mode:

degtorad.name: DegToRad
degtorad.doc: Converts an angle from degrees to radians.

delayshutdown.name: DelayShutdown
delayshutdown.doc: Terminates Plant SCADA's operation after the specified delay period (in milliseconds). This function is suitable to be called by the CTAPI. The delay period enables the user to close the connection between the CTAPI and third-party applications before Plant SCADA shuts down.

paramDocs.Delay: The period (in milliseconds) after whichPlant SCADA will shut down.

devappend.name: DevAppend
devappend.doc: Appends a blank record to the end of a device. After the record is appended, you can use the DevSetField function to add data to fields in the record.
devappend.returns: 0 (zero) if the record is successfully appended, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devclose.name: DevClose
devclose.doc: Closes a device. Any data in the buffer is flushed to the device before it is closed. After a device is closed, its device handle becomes invalid and cannot be used.
devclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where data on the associated device is stored.

devcontrol.name: DevControl
devcontrol.doc: Controls a dBASE or SQL device. You can pack a dBASE device to physically remove deleted records, or re-index a dBASE device to regenerate the keys. You can issue queries to an SQL device, or get the error status of the last SQL query.
devcontrol.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.nType: The type of command:
paramDocs.sData: The command data, that is the SQL query to be issued. Used only for Type 2 commands.

devcurr.name: DevCurr
devcurr.doc: Gets the current device handle. You can only call this function in a report, to get the handle of the device where the report is logging. You can then use the other device functions (for example, DevPrint) to access that logging device. (To get the handle of a device other than a logging device, you need to use the DevOpen function.)
devcurr.returns: The current device handle or group handle.

devdelete.name: DevDelete
devdelete.doc: Deletes the current record in a dBASE database device. The record is not physically deleted, but is marked for deletion. You can physically delete the record by packing the database with the DevControl function.
devdelete.returns: 0 (zero) if the record is successfully deleted, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devdisable.name: DevDisable
devdisable.doc: Disables (and re-enables) a device from all access, and discards any data written to the device. When a device is disabled, it cannot be opened, and data cannot be read from the device. Use this function to disable logging to a database or printer.
devdisable.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The device name, or * (asterisk) for all devices.

deveof.name: DevEOF
deveof.doc: Gets the status of the end of file (EOF) flag for a device. When you use the DevPrev, DevNext, or DevSeek function, the start or end of the device will eventually be reached, and the EOF flag will be set. Use this function to test the EOF flag.
deveof.returns: 1 if the EOF flag has been set, otherwise 0 (zero).

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen() function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devfind.name: DevFind
devfind.doc: Searches a device for a record that contains specified data in a specified field. The search starts at the current record and continues forward until the matched data is found or the end of the database is reached. If the file has a keyed index, an indexed search is used.
devfind.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen() function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.sFind: The data to find in sField, as a string.

devfirst.name: DevFirst
devfirst.doc: Finds the first record in a device.
devfirst.returns: The first indexed record (if the device is an indexed database), otherwise the first record in the device.

devflush.name: DevFlush
devflush.doc: Flushes buffered data to the physical device. Plant SCADA normally optimizes the writing of data for maximum performance, so use this function only if it is really necessary.
devflush.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where data on the associated device is stored.

devgetfield.name: DevGetField
devgetfield.doc: Gets field data from the current record in a device.
devgetfield.returns: The field data (as a string). If the field is not found an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.sField: The field name, as a string of up to 10 characters. (The dBASE file format limits all field names to a maximum of 10 characters.)

devhistory.name: DevHistory
devhistory.doc: Renames a device file and any subsequent history files. The current device is closed and renamed as the first history file. For example, the device file 'Templog.txt' is renamed as 'Templog.001'. If a history file 'Templog.001' already exists, it is renamed as 'Templog.002', and so on. The next time data is written to the device, a new device file is created.
devhistory.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devinfo.name: DevInfo
devinfo.returns: The device information as a string if successful, otherwise an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.nType: Type of information:

devmodify.name: DevModify
devmodify.doc: Modifies the attributes of a device. The device needs to be closed before you can modify a device.
devmodify.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the device.
paramDocs.Format: A new format for the device or "*" to use the existing format.See Format Templates for more information.
paramDocs.Header: A new header for the device or "*" to use the existing header.
paramDocs.FileName: A new file name for the device or "*" (asterisk) to use the existing filename.
paramDocs.nType: A new device type, or -1 to use the existing device type.

devnext.name: DevNext
devnext.doc: Gets the next record in a device. If the end of the database is reached, the EOF flag is set and an error code is returned.
devnext.returns: 0 if the next record is read, or an error if the end of the database is reached.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devopen.name: DevOpen
devopen.doc: Opens a device and returns the device handle. The device needs to be defined in the Plant SCADA database. If the device cannot be opened, and user error checking is not enabled, the current Cicode task is halted.
devopen.returns: The device handle. If the device cannot be opened, -1 is returned. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the device.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the open:

devprev.name: DevPrev
devprev.doc: Gets the previous record in a device. If the start of the database is reached, the EOF flag is set and an error code is returned.
devprev.returns: 0 if the record is read successfully, or an error code if the start of the database is reached.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devprint.name: DevPrint
devprint.doc: Prints free-format data to groups of devices. Using this function, you can write data to many devices at the same time. You would normally use this function in a report.
devprint.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hGrp: The device handle, or the group handle for a group of devices.
paramDocs.sData: The data to print to the group of devices.

devread.name: DevRead
devread.doc: Reads characters from a device. If the device is record-based, the current field is read. If the device is free-format, the specified number of characters is read. If the number of characters specified is greater than the number of characters remaining in the device, only the remaining characters are read.
devread.returns: The data (in string format). If the end of the device is found, an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.Length: The number of characters to read.

devreadln.name: DevReadLn
devreadln.doc: Reads data from the current record of a device until the end of the line, or end of the record. If the device is record-based, the record number is incremented. The carriage return and newline characters are not returned.
devreadln.returns: The data (in string format). If the end of the device is found, an empty string is returned and the EOF flag is set.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devrecno.name: DevRecNo
devrecno.doc: Gets the current record number of a device. If the device is record-based, the record number ranges from 1 to the maximum size of the file. If the device is free-format, the record number ranges from 0 to the maximum byte size -1.
devrecno.returns: The record number. If an error is detected while getting the record number, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devseek.name: DevSeek
devseek.doc: Moves the device pointer to a specified position in the device. If the device is a database, and it is opened in indexed mode, DevSeek will seek to the record number - not through the index. To locate the first record in an indexed device, call the DevFirst function.
devseek.returns: 0 (zero) if the seek was successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen() function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.Offset: The offset in the device. If the device is a database device, the offset is the record number. If the device is a binary device, the offset is in bytes (from 0 to the maximum file size -1).

devsetfield.name: DevSetField
devsetfield.doc: Sets new field data in the current record in a device.
devsetfield.returns: 0 (zero) if the data is successfully set, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.sField: The field name, as a string of up to 10 characters. (The dBASE file format limits all field names to a maximum of 10 characters.)
paramDocs.sData: New field data, in string format. Plant SCADA converts any other data type into a string before setting the data.

devsize.name: DevSize
devsize.doc: Gets the size of a physical device.
devsize.returns: If the device is a database device, the number of records is returned. If the device is a binary device, the number of bytes in the file is returned. If an error is detected, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

devwrite.name: DevWrite
devwrite.doc: Writes a string to a device. If the device is free-format, the data is written to the device as specified. If the device is record-based, the data is written to the current field, and the field pointer is moved to the next field.
devwrite.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.sData: The data to write, as a string.

devwriteln.name: DevWriteLn
devwriteln.doc: Writes a string to a device. If the device is free-format, the data is written to the device, followed by a newline character. If the device is record-based, a new record is appended to the device and the data is written to this record. The record pointer is then moved to the next record.
devwriteln.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.
paramDocs.sData: The data to write, as a string.

devzap.name: DevZap
devzap.doc: Zaps a device. If a database device is zapped, all records are deleted. If an ASCII file is zapped, the file is truncated to 0 (zero) length. Use this function when you want to delete all records in a database or file without deleting the actual file.
devzap.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hDev: The device handle, returned from the DevOpen function. The device handle identifies the table where all data on the associated device is stored.

displayruntimemanager.name: DisplayRuntimeManager
displayruntimemanager.doc: This function will start the Plant SCADA Runtime Manager if it is not already running, otherwise it will just bring the Plant SCADA Runtime Manager to the foreground.
displayruntimemanager.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

dllcall.name: DLLCall
dllcall.doc: Calls a DLL function, and passes a string of arguments to that function. Plant SCADA converts these arguments (where required) into the type specified in the DLLOpen call. If an argument cannot be converted, it is set to zero (0) or an empty string "".
dllcall.returns: The result of the function, as a string.

paramDocs.hFunction: The DLL function handle, returned from DLLOpen.
paramDocs.sArgs: The string of arguments to pass to the DLL function. The argument string contains all the arguments for the function, separated by commas (,). Enclose string arguments in quote marks "", and use the string escape character (^) to put a string delimiter within a string. This syntax is the same as the syntax for the TaskNew() function

dllcallex.name: DLLCallEx
dllcallex.doc: Calls a DLL function, and passes the specified arguments to that function.

paramDocs.hFunction: The DLL function handle, returned from DLLOpen().
paramDocs.vParameters: A variable length parameter list of method arguments. The parameters will be passed to the function in the order that you enter them.

dllclasscallmethod.name: DllClassCallMethod
dllclasscallmethod.doc: Use this function to call a method of a .Net object, passing in the method name and any arguments required for the matching prototype of the method.
dllclasscallmethod.returns: Var if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

dllclasscreate.name: DllClassCreate
dllclasscreate.doc: Use this function to instantiate a new .Net object by specifying the path, class and arguments required for the matching constructor of the class.
dllclasscreate.returns: .Net object if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

dllclassdispose.name: DllClassDispose
dllclassdispose.doc: Use this function to clean up resources used by the .Net object and any other objects created via the use of the object.
dllclassdispose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

dllclassgetproperty.name: DllClassGetProperty
dllclassgetproperty.doc: Use this function to get a property of the .Net object.
dllclassgetproperty.returns: Var if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

dllclassisvalid.name: DllClassIsValid
dllclassisvalid.doc: Use this function to validate the handle for the class returned from DllClassCreate.

dllclasssetproperty.name: DllClassSetProperty
dllclasssetproperty.doc: Use this function to set a property of the .Net object. The property may be of any type or an object itself.
dllclasssetproperty.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sProperty: The name of the property of the .Net object.
paramDocs.Value: The value to which the property of the .Net object will be set to.

dllclose.name: DLLClose
dllclose.doc: Closes the link to a DLL function, and frees the memory allocated for that function link. When the link is closed, you cannot call the function. Plant SCADA automatically closes all function links at shutdown.
dllclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hFunction: The DLL function handle, returned from DLLOpen().

dllopen.name: DLLOpen
dllopen.doc: Opens a link to a DLL function, by loading the specified DLL library into memory and attaching it to the named function. After you open the function link, you can call the function with the DLLCall function. You pass the function number returned from the DLLOpen function as an argument in the DLLCall function.
dllopen.returns: The DLL function handle, or -1 if the library or function could not be found or loaded.

paramDocs.sName: The function name. An underscore (_) is required in the function name for a 'C' function, but not for a Pascal function. When you call a DLL from a Cicode function, sName needs to be the same as the name defined in the .DEF file used to link the DLL. The file extension is not required.
paramDocs.sArgs: The string specifying the function arguments. The first character in the string is the return value of the function.

driverinfo.name: DriverInfo
driverinfo.doc: Provides information about the driver for a specified I/O device. Select the device using the IODevice argument, and the information to be returned using the Type argument.
driverinfo.returns: The driver information as a string. In the case of an error the return value is an empty string.

paramDocs.IODevice: The name of the I/O device.
paramDocs.nType: The type of information returned about the driver. Specify one of the following:
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the I/O Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the I/O server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.ServerName: Specifies the name of the the I/O Server. This parameter is only required if you are running more than one I/O server process from the same cluster on the same computer and need to instruct the system which process to redirect to. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

dspancreatecontrolobject.name: DspAnCreateControlObject
dspancreatecontrolobject.doc: Creates a new instance of an ActiveX object. If the object already exists for the given Animation Point Number, then that object will be used, that is a new object will not be created, the existing object will merely be refreshed.
dspancreatecontrolobject.returns: The newly created object, if successful, otherwise an error is generated.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.sClass: The class of the object. You can use the object's human readable name, its program ID, or its GUID. If the class does not exist, the function will return an error.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the ActiveX object.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the ActiveX object.
paramDocs.sEventClass: The string you would like to use as the event class for the object.

dspanfree.name: DspAnFree
dspanfree.doc: Frees (removes) an AN from the current page. If an animation exists at the animation number, it is deleted before the AN is freed. Use this function to free existing ANs or ANs created with the DspAnNew() function. Please be aware that the ANs are only freed in memory - the change is not persistent. The next time the page is opened it will display the AN.
dspanfree.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspangetarea.name: DspAnGetArea
dspangetarea.doc: Gets the area configured for an object at a specific AN (animation-point number). The area is returned as an integer.
dspangetarea.returns: The area if successful, otherwise an error is returned. If the object is configured with 'Same area as page' checked, the area of the page will be returned. AN area of 0 (zero) means no areas are configured for the object.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspangetmetadata.name: DspAnGetMetadata
dspangetmetadata.doc: Retrieves the field value of the specified metadata entry.
dspangetmetadata.returns: Value for the specified metadata. Returns empty string if a matching metadata entry is not defined and error code if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.nAN: An animation number that uniquely identifies an object. This object contains the list of metadata definitions that will be used to perform the association operations. When -2 is specified, it is equivalent to using DspGetAnCur(). (See for usage and limitations.)
paramDocs.sMetaName: The name of the metadata entry for which to search.

dspangetmetadataat.name: DspAnGetMetadataAt
dspangetmetadataat.doc: Retrieves metadata information at the specified index.
dspangetmetadataat.returns: The field value string. If there is an error, an empty string is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.nAn: An animation number that uniquely identifies an object. This object contains the list of metadata definitions that will be used to perform the association operations. When -2 is specified, it is equivalent to using DspGetAnCur. (See DspGetAnCur for usage and limitations.)
paramDocs.nIndex: The index of the metadata in the animation point. The index is 0-based; i.e. the first metadata entry has an index of 0, the next 1, and so on.
paramDocs.sField: The name of the field from which to retrieve the information for the metadata. Supported fields are:

dspangetpos.name: DspAnGetPos
dspangetpos.doc: Gets the x and y coordinates of an AN, in pixels, relative to the top-left corner of the window.
dspangetpos.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned. The X and Y variables are set to the AN's position if successful, or to -1 if an error has been detected.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.nMode: 1 – Gets coordinates of an AN from its configuration. i.e. page coordinates at which the object was originally inserted in Graphics Builder is returned from calling the function.

dspangetprivilege.name: DspAnGetPrivilege
dspangetprivilege.doc: Gets the privileges configured for an object at a specific AN (animation-point number). The privilege is returned as an integer.
dspangetprivilege.returns: The privilege if successful, otherwise an error is returned. A privilege of 0 (zero) means no privileges are configured for the object.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspaninfo.name: DspAnInfo
dspaninfo.doc: Gets information on an AN - the type or state of the animation that is currently displayed.
dspaninfo.returns: The animation information, which depends on the type passed argument, as described above, as a string.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.nType: The type of information:

dspaninrgn.name: DspAnInRgn
dspaninrgn.doc: Checks if an AN is within a region bounded by two ANs.
dspaninrgn.returns: 1 if the AN is within the region, or 0 (zero) if it is not.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspanmove.name: DspAnMove
dspanmove.doc: Moves an AN to a new position. Any animation at this AN is also moved.
dspanmove.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinates of the new position.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinates of the new position.

dspanmoverel.name: DspAnMoveRel
dspanmoverel.doc: Moves an AN relative to its current position. Any animation at this AN is also moved.
dspanmoverel.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.X: The number of pixels to move the AN in the x plane.
paramDocs.Y: The number of pixels to move the AN in the y plane.

dspannew.name: DspAnNew
dspannew.doc: Creates an AN at the specified x and y coordinates.
dspannew.returns: If successful, the new AN is returned. If the AN cannot be created, -1 is returned. If an AN already exists at this location, that AN is returned.

paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinate where the new AN is created.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinate where the new AN is created.

dspannewrel.name: DspAnNewRel
dspannewrel.doc: Creates an AN at a distance of x,y pixels from a specified AN.
dspannewrel.returns: If successful, the new AN is returned. If the AN cannot be created, -1 is returned. If an AN already exists at this location, that AN is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN used as a reference for the new AN.
paramDocs.X: The distance in the x plane (in pixels) from the reference AN to the new AN.
paramDocs.Y: The distance in the y plane (in pixels) from the reference AN to the new AN.

dspansetmetadata.name: DspAnSetMetadata
dspansetmetadata.doc: Non-blocking function, that sets the value of the specified metadata entry.
dspansetmetadata.returns: 0 if successful, error code if unsuccessful

paramDocs.nAn: An animation number that uniquely identifies an object. This object contains the list of metadata definitions that will be used to perform the association operations. When -2 is specified, it is equivalent to using DspGetAnCur(). (See DspGetAnCur for usage and limitations.)
paramDocs.sMetaName: The name of metadata entry for which to search.
paramDocs.sValue: The value for the metadata to be set.

dspansetmetadataat.name: DspAnSetMetadataAt
dspansetmetadataat.doc: Non-blocking function, that sets the value of a metadata entry.
dspansetmetadataat.returns: 0 if successful, error code if unsuccessful

paramDocs.nAn: An animation number that uniquely identifies an object. This object contains the list of metadata definitions that will be used to perform the association operations. When -2 is specified, it is equivalent to using DspGetAnCur(). (See DspGetAnCur for usage and limitations.)
paramDocs.nIndex: The index of the metadata in the animation point.
paramDocs.sField: The name of the field in which to set the information for the metadata. Supported fields are:
paramDocs.sFieldValue: The value to set in the specified field of the metadata entry.

dspansetname.name: DspAnSetName
dspansetname.doc: Using a valid AN set the name of an animation object.
dspansetname.returns: Returns an error if given name is already in use.

paramDocs.hAN: The AN used as a reference for the new Animation Name.
paramDocs.sName: Animation Name to be set

dsparraybyan.name: DspArrayByAn
dsparraybyan.doc: Displays an alarm list associated with a specified AN at the location of that AN. The array associated with the AN contains the alarm data. It is typically used as part of an alarm list or generic list Genie.
dsparraybyan.returns: 0 (zero). If there is an error, the error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN associated the array that contains alarm data.

dspbar.name: DspBar
dspbar.doc: Displays a bar graph (on a graphics page) at a specified AN. To scale a tag into the correct range, use the EngToGeneric() function.
dspbar.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the bar graph will be displayed.
paramDocs.Bar: The name of the bar graph to display in the format <[LibName.]BarName>. If you do not specify the library name, a bar graph from the Global library displays (if it exists). To display a Version 1.xx bar graph, specify the bar definition (1 to 255). For example, if you specify bar 1, Plant SCADA displays the bar graph Global.Bar001.
paramDocs.Value: The value to display on the bar graph. The value needs to be from 0 to 32000 to give 0 to full-scale range on the bar.

dspbmp.name: DspBmp
dspbmp.doc: Displays a bitmap at a specified AN. This function allows you to display any bitmap file at run time. (You can get a new bitmap file from operator input or from the plant, and display it dynamically.)
dspbmp.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.sFile: The name of the bitmap (.BMP) file. The file needs to be in the user project path. (Only .bmp files are supported. Other image formats like .png or .jpg are not supported.)

dspbutton.name: DspButton
dspbutton.doc: Displays a button at a specified AN. When the button is selected, the key definition is put into the key command line. The font, width, height, and down and repeat keys of the button are optional. If you do not specify a width and height, the button adjusts to the size of the button sName.
dspbutton.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.UpKey: The key generated when the command button is selected (when the mouse button is released after being clicked down). This is the default operation for commands activated by a button.
paramDocs.Name: The name to display on the button.
paramDocs.hFont: The handle of the font used to display the button name. Use the DspFont() function to create a new font and return the font handle. Use the DspFontHnd() function to return the font handle of an existing font. The Windows button font is used if the font is omitted or is not defined in the database.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the button in pixels.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the button in pixels.
paramDocs.DownKey: The key generated when the mouse button is clicked down (over the command button). Normally this parameter is not used, because most buttons are configured to activate a command when the mouse button is released (returning to the `up' position).
paramDocs.RepeatKey: The key generated repetitively, while the mouse button is being held down (over the command button).
paramDocs.Style: A number indicating the visibility style of the button:

dspbuttonfn.name: DspButtonFn
dspbuttonfn.doc: Displays a button at a specified AN. When the button is selected, a user function is called. If the width and height are 0 (zero), then the button adjusts to the size of the button sName.
dspbuttonfn.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.UpFunction: The user function called when the command button is selected (when the mouse button is released after being clicked down). This is the default operation for commands activated by a button. This callback function can have no arguments, so specify the function with no parentheses (). The callback function needs to return INT as its return data type. You cannot specify a Plant SCADA built-in function for this argument.
paramDocs.Name: The name to display on the button.
paramDocs.hFont: The handle of the font used to display the button name. Use the DspFont() function to create a new font and return the font handle. Use the DspFontHnd() function to return the font handle of an existing font. The Windows button font is used if the font is omitted or is not defined in the database.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the button in pixels.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the buton in pixels.
paramDocs.DownFunction: The user function called when the mouse button is clicked down (over the command button). Normally this parameter is not used, because most buttons are configured to activate when the mouse button is released (returning to the `up' position). The callback function needs to have no arguments, so specify the function with no parentheses (). The callback function needs to return INT as its return data type. You cannot specify a Plant SCADA built-in function for this argument.
paramDocs.RepeatFunction: The user function called repetitively, while the mouse button is being held down (over the command button) The callback function needs to have no arguments, so specify the function with no parentheses (). The callback function needs to return INT as its return data type. You cannot specify a Plant SCADA built-in function for this argument.

dspchart.name: DspChart
dspchart.doc: Displays a chart at an AN. Charts are trend lines with markers on them. Values are plotted on the chart pens. You need to specify Value1, but Value2 to Value8 are optional.
dspchart.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the chart will be displayed.
paramDocs.Value1: The value to display on Pen 1 of the chart.
paramDocs.Value2 ... 8: The values to display on Pen 2...Pen 8 of the chart. These values are optional.

dspclearclip.name: DspClearClip
dspclearclip.doc: Clears the clipping rectangle surrounding the object or group of objects.
dspclearclip.returns: If nAN is invalid will return 0

paramDocs.nAn: The animation-point number of the object or groups within the clipping rectangle.

dspcol.name: DspCol
dspcol.doc: DspCol is deprecated in this version of Plant SCADA.
dspcol.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.Color: The color to display at the AN.

dspdel.name: DspDel
dspdel.doc: Deletes all objects from a specified AN.
dspdel.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspdelayrenderbegin.name: DspDelayRenderBegin
dspdelayrenderbegin.doc: Delays screen updating until DspDelayRenderEnd is called. This function should be used with DspDelayRenderEnd() to "sandwich" Cicode that will modify the appearance of a page. The code should be preceded by DspDelayRenderBegin(), and followed by DspDelayRenderEnd(). This will reduce screen update times, because the modifying code is given time to execute before the page is updated with the changes, and the changes are all made in a single re-draw.

dspdelayrenderend.name: DspDelayRenderEnd
dspdelayrenderend.doc: Ends the screen update delay set by DspDelayRenderBegin. This function should be used with DspDelayRenderBegin() to "sandwich" Cicode that will modify the appearance of a page. The code should be preceded by DspDelayRenderBegin(), and followed by DspDelayRenderEnd(). This will reduce screen update times, because the modifying code is given time to execute before the page is updated with the changes, and the changes are all made in a single re-draw.

dspdirty.name: DspDirty
dspdirty.doc: Forces Plant SCADA to update an AN. Normally, Plant SCADA updates the animation on the AN only if the data has changed. This function tells Plant SCADA to update the AN the next time it animates the AN - even if the data has not changed.
dspdirty.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dsperror.name: DspError
dsperror.doc: Displays an error message at the prompt AN on the operator's computer. You can disable the error message display (of this function) by setting the Cicode execution mode in the CodeSetMode() function.
dsperror.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

dspfile.name: DspFile
dspfile.doc: Defines the screen attributes for displaying a text file. This function defines a "window" where the file will be displayed. You should call this function before any file-to-screen function.
dspfile.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the file display window will be positioned.
paramDocs.hFont: The handle for the font that is used to display the file, returned from the DspFont() or DspFontHnd() function. The font handle identifies the table where data on the associated font is stored.
paramDocs.Height: The maximum number of lines to display on one page of the file display window.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the file display window, in characters.

dspfilegetinfo.name: DspFileGetInfo
dspfilegetinfo.doc: Gets the attributes of a file-to-screen display (used for displaying text files).
dspfilegetinfo.returns: The attributes of the "window" as an integer. If an incorrect AN is specified, an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the file display window will be located. This AN needs to be the same as the AN specified with the DspFile() function.
paramDocs.nType: The type of data required:

dspfilegetname.name: DspFileGetName
dspfilegetname.doc: Gets the name of the file being displayed in the display "window". You can use this function to display the file name on the screen.
dspfilegetname.returns: The name of the file (as a string). If an incorrect AN is specified, an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspfilescroll.name: DspFileScroll
dspfilescroll.doc: Scrolls a file (displayed in the display "window") by a number of characters.
dspfilescroll.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.Direction: The direction in which to scroll:
paramDocs.Characters: The number of characters to scroll. To page up or page down through the file, scroll by the height of the file-to-screen window (returned by DspFileGetInfo(AN, 1)).

dspfilesetname.name: DspFileSetName
dspfilesetname.doc: Sets the name of the file to display in the display "window". You should call the DspFile() function first (as the entry function for a graphics page) to define the attributes of the display. You can then use the DspFileSetName() function (as a keyboard command) to display a user-specified file. When you call this function, the specified file name is read from disk and displayed on the screen.
dspfilesetname.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.sName: The name of the file to display.

dspfont.name: DspFont
dspfont.doc: Creates a font and returns a font handle. If the requested font already exists, its font handle is returned. You can use this font handle in the functions that display text, buttons, and text files.
dspfont.returns: The font handle as an integer. If the font cannot be created, -1 is returned. The font handle identifies the table where all data on the associated font is stored.

paramDocs.PixelSize: The font size, as a positive number for pixels, or a negative number for points.
paramDocs.ForeOnColor: The foreground color used for the text. If implementing flashing color, this is the initial color that will be used. Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.BackOnColor: The color used for the background of text. If implementing flashing color, this is the initial color that will be used. Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.ForeOffColor: An optional argument only required if implementing flashing color for the font foreground. It represents the secondary color used. Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.BackOffColor: An optional argument only required if implementing flashing color for the font background. It represents the secondary color used. Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.

dspfonthnd.name: DspFontHnd
dspfonthnd.doc: Gets the font handle of a font that is defined in the Fonts database. You can use this font handle in the functions that display text, buttons, and text files.
dspfonthnd.returns: The font handle as an integer. If the font cannot be found, -1 is returned. The font handle identifies the table where the data on the associated font is stored.

paramDocs.Name: The font name in the fonts database.

dspfullscreen.name: DspFullScreen
dspfullscreen.doc: Disables or enables the fullscreen mode of the currently active window. This function does not resize the window when it is called; it merely sets the mode flag. The next time the window is displayed, its size (on screen) changes to reflect the setting of the flag. This function overrides the [Animator]FullScreen parameter setting.
dspfullscreen.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.
