dspgetanbottom.name: DspGetAnBottom
dspgetanbottom.doc: Gets the bottom extent of the object at the specified AN.
dspgetanbottom.returns: The y coordinate of the bottom extent of the object at the AN. If no object exists at the AN, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspgetancur.name: DspGetAnCur
dspgetancur.doc: Gets the AN of the current graphics object. This function should only be used by expressions or Cicode functions called from the condition fields of a graphics object, excluding input/command fields. If you need to know the AN that triggered the input/command, the KeyGetCursor function may be used as it returns the AN where the cursor is currently positioned.
dspgetancur.returns: The AN associated with the current graphics object. If this function is called outside the page animation system or from an input/command field, -1 will be returned.

dspgetanextent.name: DspGetAnExtent
dspgetanextent.doc: Gts the extent (the page co-ordinates) of the object at the specified AN.
dspgetanextent.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned. The Top, Left, Bottom, and Right arguments contain the extents of the object, in pixels.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN at which the object is positioned.
paramDocs.Top: A buffer that contains the top-most extent of the object.
paramDocs.Left: A buffer that contains the left-most extent of the object.
paramDocs.Bottom: A buffer that contains the bottom-most extent of the object.
paramDocs.Right: A buffer that contains the right-most extent of the object.

dspgetanfirst.name: DspGetAnFirst
dspgetanfirst.doc: Gets the first AN on the current page, based on the order in which the ANs were stored by Graphics Builder.
dspgetanfirst.returns: The value for the first AN, otherwise an error is returned.

dspgetanfromname.name: DspGetAnFromName
dspgetanfromname.doc: Name used to retrieve the AN of an object on the page. Use the following relative path syntax:
dspgetanfromname.returns: AN of object or -1 if not found.

paramDocs.sName: The Name of the object used as a reference for the AN.

dspgetanfromnamerelative.name: DspGetAnFromNameRelative
dspgetanfromnamerelative.doc: Name used to retrieve the animation number (AN) of an object on the page relative to a given Animation Number(AN). Use the following syntax:
dspgetanfromnamerelative.returns: AN of object or -1 if not found.

paramDocs.hAN: AN used as the starting point for the search.
paramDocs.sName: The Name used as a reference for the AN.

dspgetanfrompoint.name: DspGetAnFromPoint
dspgetanfrompoint.doc: Gets the AN of the object at a specified set of screen coordinates. If the X and Y coordinates given are within the extents of an object, then the AN number of the object will be returned.
dspgetanfrompoint.returns: The AN or 0 (zero) if no object exists at the point.

paramDocs.X: The x coordinate of the screen point.
paramDocs.Y: The y coordinate of the screen point.
paramDocs.PrevAN: Retrieves the previous AN (in z-order) in situations where a number of objects overlap at the specified point. The default of 0 (zero) specifies no previous AN. A non-zero value should only ever be passed if it is the result of a previous call to DspGetAnFromPoint.

dspgetanheight.name: DspGetAnHeight
dspgetanheight.doc: Gets the height of the object at a specified AN.
dspgetanheight.returns: The height of the object (in pixels). If no object exists at the AN, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspgetanleft.name: DspGetAnLeft
dspgetanleft.doc: Gets the left extent of the object at the specified AN.
dspgetanleft.returns: The x coordinate of the left extent of the object at the AN. If no object exists at the AN, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspgetannext.name: DspGetAnNext
dspgetannext.doc: Returns the AN that follows the specified AN, based on the order in which the ANs were stored on a page by Graphics Builder.
dspgetannext.returns: The value for the next AN. If -1 is returned, it means the specified AN is invalid or it is the last AN on the page.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspgetanrawextent.name: DspGetAnRawExtent
dspgetanrawextent.doc: Gets the extent of the object from the graphics page at the specified AN. The extent represents the page co-ordinates at which the object was originally inserted.
dspgetanrawextent.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned. The Top, Left, Bottom, and Right arguments contain the extents of the object, in pixels.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN at which the object is positioned.
paramDocs.Top: A buffer that contains the top-most extent of the object.
paramDocs.Left: A buffer that contains the left-most extent of the object.
paramDocs.Bottom: A buffer that contains the bottom-most extent of the object.
paramDocs.Right: A buffer that contains the right-most extent of the object.

dspgetanright.name: DspGetAnRight
dspgetanright.doc: Gets the right extent of the object at the specified AN.
dspgetanright.returns: The x coordinate of the right extent of the object at the AN. If no object exists at the AN, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspgetantop.name: DspGetAnTop
dspgetantop.doc: Gets the top extent of the object at the specified AN.
dspgetantop.returns: The y coordinate of the top extent of the object at the AN. If no object exists at the AN, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspgetanwidth.name: DspGetAnWidth
dspgetanwidth.doc: Gets the width of the object at a specified AN.
dspgetanwidth.returns: The width of the object (in pixels). If no object exists at the AN, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspgetenv.name: DspGetEnv
dspgetenv.returns: The value of the variable (as a string).

paramDocs.sName: The name of the variable (set using the page environment dialog).

dspgetmetadatafromname.name: DspGetMetadataFromName
dspgetmetadatafromname.doc: Name used to retrieve the metadata of an object on the page. Use the following relative path syntax:
dspgetmetadatafromname.returns: The value of the metadata or blank.

paramDocs.sName: The Name used as a reference for the object.
paramDocs.sMetaName: The name of the metadata to be returned.

dspgetmetadatafromnamerelative.name: DspGetMetadataFromNameRelative
dspgetmetadatafromnamerelative.doc: Name used to retrieve the metadata of an object on the page relative to a given Animation Number (AN). Use the following syntax:
dspgetmetadatafromnamerelative.returns: The value of the metadata or blank.

paramDocs.hAN: AN used as the starting point for the search.
paramDocs.sName: The name of the AN used as a reference for the object.
paramDocs.sMetaName: The name of the metadata to be returned.

dspgetmouse.name: DspGetMouse
dspgetmouse.doc: Gets the x and y coordinates of the mouse position, relative to the top left corner of the window.
dspgetmouse.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned. The X and Y variables are set to the mouse position.

paramDocs.X: A locally declared variable used to store the x pixel coordinate of the mouse position, returned from this function.
paramDocs.Y: A locally declared variable used to store the y pixel coordinate of the mouse position, returned from this function.

dspgetmouseover.name: DspGetMouseOver
dspgetmouseover.doc: Determines if the mouse is within the boundaries of a given AN.
dspgetmouseover.returns: 1 if within the specified AN, 0 if not.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the animation you wish to check, or -1 for the current AN. Defaults to -1.

dspgetnamefroman.name: DspGetNameFromAn
dspgetnamefroman.doc: Using a valid animation number (AN) the animation name of the object is returned.
dspgetnamefroman.returns: The animation name of the object, or blank

paramDocs.hAN: The AN used as a reference for the name of the object.

dspgetnearestan.name: DspGetNearestAn
dspgetnearestan.doc: Gets the AN nearest to a specified x,y pixel location.
dspgetnearestan.returns: The animation point number (AN). A value of -1 is returned if no AN is found.

dspgetparentan.name: DspGetParentAn
dspgetparentan.doc: Gets the parent animation number (if any), for the specified animation number. AN animation point will have a parent animation point if it corresponds to an object in a group.
dspgetparentan.returns: The parent animation point number (AN). If no parent animation exists or an invalid animation number is passed, 0 (zero) is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The animation-point number.

dspgetslider.name: DspGetSlider
dspgetslider.doc: Gets the current position (value) of a slider at an AN. You can call this function in the slider event to find the new position of the slider.
dspgetslider.returns: The value of the slider from 0 to 32000. If no animation exists at the AN, -1 is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.

dspgettip.name: DspGetTip
dspgettip.doc: Gets the tool tip text associated with an AN.
dspgettip.returns: The tool tip text (as a string). If no user tip is available, an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN from which to get the tool tip text. If no object is configured at the AN, the function will return an empty string.
paramDocs.Mode: 1 - The tool tip from the object configured at the AN.

dspgraybutton.name: DspGrayButton
dspgraybutton.doc: Grays and disables a button. If the button is a symbol, the symbol is overwritten with a gray mask. (When a button is grayed, it cannot be selected.) If the Disabled field in the Buttons database is blank, the button is enabled unless you use this function. If the Disabled field in the Buttons database contains an expression, this function will not override the expression.
dspgraybutton.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise, -1 (if no AN is found).

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the button is located.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the operation:

dspinfo.name: DspInfo
dspinfo.doc: Extracts individual pieces of object information from an AN. Each AN can have multiple expressions associated with it, and each expression can have multiple variables associated with it. You use an index to refer to each individual expressions or variables. Typically, you would query the number of expressions, then the number of variables in a given expression, then the details of a given variable tag.
dspinfo.returns: The object information (as a string). A blank string is returned if you specify a non-existent expression or variable.

paramDocs.hInfo: The object information block handle, as returned by DspInfoNew(). This handle identifies the table (or block) where all object data is stored.
paramDocs.nType: The type of data to extract:
paramDocs.Index: An index to the variable within the information block. The required index changes according to the Type as follows:

dspinfodestroy.name: DspInfoDestroy
dspinfodestroy.doc: Destroys an object information block created by DspInfoNew(). You should destroy an object information block when you no longer need it, to free Plant SCADA resources.
dspinfodestroy.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hInfo: The object information block handle, as returned by DspInfoNew(). This handle identifies the table (or block) where all object data is stored.

dspinfofield.name: DspInfoField
dspinfofield.doc: Obtains static and real-time data from a variable tag. You get static data from the Variable Tags database. The additional field "Eng_Value", returns dynamic real-time data for the variable tag. To get this real-time data, you need to first call the DspInfoNew() function to get the information block handle hInfo.

paramDocs.hInfo: The object information block handle, as returned by DspInfoNew(). This handle identifies the table (or block) where data on the object is stored. Set this handle to 0 (zero) if you do not require real-time data.
paramDocs.sTag: The name of the variable tag. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag". This argument does not support arrays. If array syntax is used, the information will be retrieved for only the tag name.
paramDocs.sField: The name of the field from which to extract the data:
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the tag via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

dspinfonew.name: DspInfoNew
dspinfonew.doc: Creates an object information block. Use this function with the associated low-level animation information functions to get and process object information on an AN.
dspinfonew.returns: The object information block handle. If no object data is available, then -1 is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN for which object information is provided.

dspinfovalid.name: DspInfoValid
dspinfovalid.doc: Checks if an object information block handle is valid. An object information block handle becomes invalid after it is destroyed, or if the user closes the page it is associated with. Use this function if background Cicode is using the object information block, and the operator closes the page.
dspinfovalid.returns: 1 if the information block handle is valid, otherwise 0 (zero).

paramDocs.hInfo: The object information block handle, as returned by DspInfoNew(). This handle identifies the table (or block) where all object data is stored.

dspisbuttongray.name: DspIsButtonGray
dspisbuttongray.doc: Gets the current status of a button.
dspisbuttongray.returns: The current mode of the button:

paramDocs.nAN: The AN for which object information is provided.

dspkernel.name: DspKernel
dspkernel.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nMode: The display mode of Kernel:

dspmarkermove.name: DspMarkerMove
dspmarkermove.doc: Moves a trend or chart marker to a specified position.
dspmarkermove.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend or chart is positioned.
paramDocs.hMarker: The marker handle, as returned from the DspMarkerNew() function. The marker handle identifies the table where all data on the associated marker is stored.
paramDocs.Offset: The offset by which to move the marker. Vertical markers have an offset from 0 (zero) to the maximum number of samples in the trend. Horizontal markers have a offset of 0 (zero) to 32000.

dspmarkernew.name: DspMarkerNew
dspmarkernew.doc: Creates a new trend marker. A trend marker is used to show cursor values or limits on a trend. You can use up to 10 markers on a single trend or chart.
dspmarkernew.returns: The marker handle, or -1 if the function is unsuccessful. The marker handle identifies the table where data on the associated marker is stored.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.Color: The color of the marker (flashing color not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB color using the function MakeColour.

dspmci.name: DspMCI
dspmci.doc: Controls a multimedia device. The Media Control Interface (MCI) is a high-level command interface to multimedia devices and resource files. MCI provides applications with device-independent capabilities for controlling audio and visual peripherals (for example, for playing multimedia devices and recording multimedia resource files).
dspmci.returns: A string message with the status of the MCI command.

paramDocs.sCommand: The MCI command. See Microsoft Windows documentation for details.

dspplaysound.name: DspPlaySound
dspplaysound.doc: Plays a waveform (sound). Wave form sound files *.wav are provided with Windows and by third-party developers, or you can record them yourself to play long (and complex) sound sequences.
dspplaysound.returns: TRUE if successful, otherwise FALSE (if an error is detected).

paramDocs.sSoundname: Sound File Path: Sound file to be played from the specified path.
paramDocs.nMode: • Mode 0: For use when the "sSoundname" is a sound file path.

dsppopupconfigmenu.name: DspPopupConfigMenu
dsppopupconfigmenu.doc: Displays the contents of a menu node as a pop-up (context) menu, and run the command associated with the selected menu item. You can specify the contents of a menu using the menu configuration dialog at design time, or using the Menu family of Cicode functions at runtime.
dsppopupconfigmenu.returns: 0 if the selected menu command is run or error code if menu command cannot run.

paramDocs.hParent: The parent node of the menu tree returned from any of the following functions:
paramDocs.bNonRecursive: Whether not to recursively transverse child tree nodes and list them as sub-menus in the pop-up menu. This parameter is optional. If it is left unspecified, its value will be defaulted to 0 (recursive). When it is set to 1, only the immediate child nodes of the specified menu handle will be listed. In this mode, tree nodes will be listed as normal menu items (instead of submenus) in the pop-up menu.
paramDocs.XPos: The x-coordinate (relative to the page) at which the menu will be displayed.This parameter is optional. If it is left unspecified, the menu will display at the cursor's current position.
paramDocs.YPos: The y-coordinate (relative to the page) at which the menu will be displayed.This parameter is optional. If it is left unspecified, the menu will display at the cursor's current position.

dsppopupmenu.name: DspPopupMenu
dsppopupmenu.doc: Creates a popup menu consisting of a number of menu items. Multiple calls to this function enable you to add new items and create sub menus, building a system of linked, Windows-style menus.
dsppopupmenu.returns: The selected menu item as an integer. This comprises the menu number (return value div 100), and the position of the item in the menu (return value mod 100). For example, a return value of 201 indicates that the first item in Menu 2 was selected, and a return value of 3 indicates that the third item in Menu 0 was selected.

paramDocs.iMenuNumber: An integer representing the menu you are adding items to. The first menu created is Menu 0. If left unspecified, this parameter defaults to -1, causing the menu to be displayed on the screen.
paramDocs.sMenuItems: A comma-separated string defining the items in each menu. The default value for this parameter is an empty string, which will get passed to the function in the call to display the menu.
paramDocs.XPos: The x-coordinate (relative to the page) at which the menu will be displayed. This parameter is optional. If it is left unspecified, the menu will display at the cursor's current position.
paramDocs.YPos: The y-coordinate (relative to the page) at which the menu will be displayed. This parameter is optional. If it is left unspecified, the menu will display at the cursor's current position.

dsprichtext.name: DspRichText
dsprichtext.doc: Creates a Rich Text object of the given dimensions at the animation point nAN. This object can then be used to display an RTF file (like an RTF report) called using the DspRichTextLoad function.
dsprichtext.returns: 0 if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN at which the rich text object will display when the DspRichText command is run.
paramDocs.iHeight: The height of the rich text object in pixels. The height is established by measuring down from the animation point.
paramDocs.iWidth: The width of the rich text object in pixels. The width is established by measuring across to the right from the animation point.
paramDocs.nMode: The display mode for the rich text object. The mode can be any combination of:

dsprichtextedit.name: DspRichTextEdit
dsprichtextedit.doc: Enables editing of the contents of the rich text object at nAN if nEdit = TRUE, and disables editing if nEdit = FALSE.
dsprichtextedit.returns: 0 if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The reference AN for the rich text object.
paramDocs.bEdit: The value of this argument determines whether you will be able to edit the contents of the rich text object at AN. Enter TRUE to enable editing, or enter FALSE to make the contents read-only.

dsprichtextenable.name: DspRichTextEnable
dsprichtextenable.doc: Enables the rich text object at nAN if nEnable = TRUE, and disables the object if nEnable = FALSE. When the object is disabled, its contents cannot be selected or copied etc.
dsprichtextenable.returns: 0 if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The reference AN for the rich text object.
paramDocs.bEnable: The value of this argument determines whether the rich text object at AN will be enabled or disabled. Enter TRUE to enable the object (that is you can select and copy the contents of the RTF object, but you can't make changes). Enter FALSE to disable the object (that is make it display only).

dsprichtextgetinfo.name: DspRichTextGetInfo
dsprichtextgetinfo.doc: Retrieves size information about the rich text object at animation point nAN.
dsprichtextgetinfo.returns: The requested information as a string (units = pixels).

paramDocs.nAN: The reference AN for the rich text object.
paramDocs.iType: The following size information (in pixels) can be returned about the specified rich text object:

dsprichtextload.name: DspRichTextLoad
dsprichtextload.doc: Loads a copy of the file Filename into the rich text object) at animation point nAN. (The rich text object may have been created using either the DspRichTextLoad function or the PageRichTextFile function.)
dsprichtextload.returns: 0 if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation point at which a copy of the rich text file (for example, an RTF report) will display. This AN needs to match that of a rich text object (created using either the DspRichText function, or the PageRichTextFile function), or the copy of the file will not be loaded into anything, and will not display.
paramDocs.sFilename: The name of the file to be copied and loaded into the rich text object at the specified animation point. The filename needs to be entered in quotation marks "".

dsprichtextpgscroll.name: DspRichTextPgScroll
dsprichtextpgscroll.doc: Scrolls the contents of the rich text object displayed at nAN, by one page length in the direction given in direction.
dsprichtextpgscroll.returns: 0 if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The reference AN for the rich text object.
paramDocs.iDirection: The direction in which you want to scroll each time this function is run. You can choose from the following:

dsprichtextprint.name: DspRichTextPrint
dsprichtextprint.doc: Prints the contents of the rich text object at animation point nAN, to the port PortName.
dsprichtextprint.returns: 0 if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The reference AN for the rich text object.
paramDocs.sPortName: The name of the printer port to which the contents of the rich text object will be printed. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks "". For example "LPT1", to print to the local printer, or "\\Pserver\canon1" using UNC to print to a network printer.

dsprichtextsave.name: DspRichTextSave
dsprichtextsave.doc: Saves the contents of the rich text object at animation point nAN, to the file Filename.
dsprichtextsave.returns: 0 if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The reference AN for the rich text object.
paramDocs.sFilename: The name under which the contents of the rich text object will be saved. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks "", and needs to include the destination path. For example "[Data]\saved.rtf".

dsprichtextscroll.name: DspRichTextScroll
dsprichtextscroll.doc: Scrolls the contents of the rich text object displayed at nAN, in the direction given in direction, by the number of lines/units given in amount. Remember that the height of a line varies according to the font used, therefore if you need to scroll absolute distances, it might be advisable to use the DspRichTextPgScroll function.
dsprichtextscroll.returns: 0 if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The reference AN for the rich text object.
paramDocs.iDirection: The direction in which you want to scroll each time this function is run. You can choose from the following:
paramDocs.iAmount: The amount by which you would like to scroll each time this function is run. Enter the number of lines (for a vertical direction) or units (for a horizontal direction) by which you would like to scroll.

dsprubend.name: DspRubEnd
dsprubend.doc: Ends the rubber band selection, and returns the coordinates of the rubber band selection. The meaning of the cx and cy values depend on the nMode you specify in the DspRubStart() function.
dsprubend.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

dsprubmove.name: DspRubMove
dsprubmove.doc: Moves the rubber band selection to the new position. You need to first have defined a rubber band selection using the DspRubStart() and DspRubEnd() functions.
dsprubmove.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

dsprubsetclip.name: DspRubSetClip
dsprubsetclip.doc: Sets the clipping region for the rubber band display. If you enable the clipping region, the rubber band will not move outside of the clip region. This allows you to restrict the rubber band to within some constrained region. (For example, to prevent an operator from dragging the rubber band outside of the trend display when zooming the trend.)
dsprubsetclip.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

dsprubsetcolor.name: DspRubSetColor
dsprubsetcolor.doc: Sets the color of the rubber band tool that is used to select a section within a trend object.
dsprubsetcolor.returns: The previous rubber band color as an integer.

paramDocs.Color: An integer representing the color to use for the rubber band. The default value is white (0x00FFFFFF).

dsprubstart.name: DspRubStart
dsprubstart.doc: Starts the rubber band selection. Call this function when the left mouse button is pressed - the rubber band is displayed at the starting position. Call the DspRubEnd() function to end the selection, when the mouse button is released. The DspRubMove() function moves the selection to the new position.
dsprubstart.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the rubber banding operation:

dspsetclip.name: DspSetClip
dspsetclip.doc: Sets the clip rectangle for the AN of an object or group of objects, defined by the top, left, right and bottom co- ordinates.
dspsetclip.returns: It returns an error if nAN is invalid, or the specified rectangle is invalid i.e. nLeft >= nRight or nTop >= nBottom.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number of the object or group of objects inside the clipping region.
paramDocs.nLeft: The x coordinate of the left side of the clipping boundary
paramDocs.nTop: The x coordinate of the top of the clipping boundary
paramDocs.nRight: The y co-ordinate of the right side of the clip rectangle.
paramDocs.nBottom: The y co-ordinate of the bottom of the clip rectangle.

dspsetcurcolor.name: DspSetCurColor
dspsetcurcolor.doc: Sets the color of the focus rectangle. The focus rectangle is used to highlight a selectable object, tab or list item as the mouse moves over it.
dspsetcurcolor.returns: The previous focus rectangle color as an integer.

paramDocs.Color: An integer representing the color to use for the focus rectangle. The default value is white (0x00FFFFFF).

dspsetmetadatafromname.name: DspSetMetadataFromName
dspsetmetadatafromname.doc: Name used to set the metadata of an object on the page. Use the following syntax:
dspsetmetadatafromname.returns: The value of the metadata or error code.

paramDocs.sName: The Name used as a reference for the object.
paramDocs.sMetaName: The Name of the metadata to be returned.
paramDocs.sValue: The value of the metadata to be returned.

dspsetmetadatafromnamerelative.name: DspSetMetadataFromNameRelative
dspsetmetadatafromnamerelative.doc: Name used to set the metadata of an object on the page relative to the given AN. Use the following syntax:
dspsetmetadatafromnamerelative.returns: The value of the metadata or error code

paramDocs.hAN: AN used as the starting point for the search of the object name.
paramDocs.sName: The Name used as a reference for the object.
paramDocs.sMetaName: The Name of the metadata to be returned.
paramDocs.sValue: The Name of the metadata to be returned.

dspsetpopupmenufont.name: DspSetPopupMenuFont
dspsetpopupmenufont.doc: Allows you to set the font and font size for text that appears in popup menus at runtime. For example, you can use this function to adjust the size of the text that appears in context menus to suit a particular screen resolution.

paramDocs.hFont: The handle of font to be used.

dspsetslider.name: DspSetSlider
dspsetslider.doc: Sets the current position of a slider at the specified AN. You can use this function to move a slider, and adjust the value of the variable associated with the slider.
dspsetslider.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.nPos: The position of the slider from 0 to 32000 where 0 is the zero position of the slider and 32000 if full position of the slider.

dspsettip.name: DspSetTip
dspsettip.doc: Sets tool tip text associated with an AN. Any existing text associated with the AN will be replaced with the new text.
dspsettip.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.sText: The tool tip text to set for the AN.

dspsettooltipfont.name: DspSetTooltipFont
dspsettooltipfont.doc: Sets the font for tool tip text.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the Windows font to be used, enclosed by quotation marks " ". A value for this parameter is required, however specifying an empty string "" will set the tooltip font to the default of MS Sans Serif.
paramDocs.nPointSize: The size of the font in points. If you do not specify a value, the point size defaults to 12.
paramDocs.sAttribs: A string specifying the format of the font. Use one or all of the following, enclosed by quotation marks " ":

dspstatus.name: DspStatus
dspstatus.doc: Determines whether the object at the specified AN will be grayed (hatch pattern) in the event communication attempts are unsuccessful.
dspstatus.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation-point number.
paramDocs.nMode: 1 - Gray the object (with a hatch pattern) when communication attempts are unsuccessful

dspstr.name: DspStr
dspstr.doc: Displays a string at a specified AN.
dspstr.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the text will be displayed.
paramDocs.sFont: The name of the font that is used to display the text. The Font Name needs to be defined in the Fonts database. If the font is not found, the default font is used.
paramDocs.iLength: Length of the text to display, either in characters or pixels depending on Mode (default -1, no truncation)
paramDocs.iAlignMode: The alignment of the text string:
paramDocs.iLengthMode: The length mode of the text string:
paramDocs.bTooltip: Determines if the original text is provided as tool tip when the displayed text becomes truncated.

dspsym.name: DspSym
dspsym.doc: Displays a symbol or a Genie at a specified AN. This dynamically displayed object will disappear at page navigation.
dspsym.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise one of the following errors will be returned. A hardware alarm is also raised against DspSym when there is an error message.

paramDocs.iAN: The AN where the symbol will be displayed.
paramDocs.sSymbol: The name of the symbol to display in the format <[LibName.]SymName>. If you do not specify the library name, a symbol from the Global library will display (if it exists).
paramDocs.iMode: Not used. The mode is always set to 1, which means do not erase the existing symbol, just draw the new symbol.

dspsymanm.name: DspSymAnm
dspsymanm.doc: Animates a series of symbols at an AN. Sym1 displays first, then Sym2, Sym3 . . . Sym8 and then Sym1 displays again, etc. When the next symbol in the sequence is displayed, the current symbol is not erased, but is overwritten to provide a smoother animation. The symbols should all be the same size.
dspsymanm.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the animation will occur.
paramDocs.Sym1: The name of the first symbol to animate in the format <[LibName.]SymName>. If you do not specify the library name, a symbol from the Global library will display (if it exists). Sym1 needs to be specified.
paramDocs.Sym2..Sym8: The names of the symbols to animate in frames 2 to 8 in the format <[LibName.]SymName>. If you do not specify the library name, a symbol from the Global library will display (if it exists).
paramDocs.iDisplayMode: Not used. Always set to -1, which means Soft animation. The background screen (a rectangular region beneath the symbol) is restored with the original image. Any objects that are within the rectangular region are destroyed when the background is restored. Use this mode when each animation symbol is a different size.
paramDocs.Sym9: Not all symbols have to be specified. If for example, only two symbols are to display, specify Sym1 and Sym2.

dspsymanmex.name: DspSymAnmEx
dspsymanmex.doc: Animates a series of symbols at an AN. Sym1 displays first, then Sym2, Sym3 . . . Sym9 and then Sym1 displays again, etc. When the next symbol in the sequence is displayed, the current symbol is not erased, but is overwritten to provide a smoother animation. The symbols should all be the same size.
dspsymanmex.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the animation will occur.
paramDocs.Mode: Not used. Always set to -1, which means Soft animation. The background screen (a rectangular region beneath the symbol) is restored with the original image. Any objects that are within the rectangular region are destroyed when the background is restored. Use this mode when each animation symbol is a different size.
paramDocs.Sym1: The name of the first symbol to animate in the format <[LibName.]SymName>. If you do not specify the library name, a symbol from the Global library will display (if it exists). Sym1 needs to be specified.
paramDocs.Sym2..Sym9: The names of the symbols to animate in frames 2 to 9 in the format <[LibName.]SymName>. If you do not specify the library name, a symbol from the Global library will display (if it exists).

dspsymatsize.name: DspSymAtSize
dspsymatsize.doc: Displays a symbol or a genie at the specified scale and offset from the AN position.
dspsymatsize.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the symbol will be animated.
paramDocs.sSym: The name of the symbol to display, move, or size. If sSym is 0 (zero), any existing symbol at the AN is erased.
paramDocs.PositionX: The horizontal offset position (from the AN) of the symbol (in pixels).
paramDocs.PositionY: The vertical offset position (from the AN) of the symbol (in pixels).

dsptext.name: DspText
dsptext.doc: Displays text at a specified AN location. This function does the same operation as DspStr(), however it uses a font number rather than a font name.
dsptext.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hAN: The AN where the text will be displayed.
paramDocs.iFont: The font number that is used to display the text. (To use the default font, set to -1.)
paramDocs.iLength: Length of the Text to display, either in characters or pixels depending on Mode (default -1, no truncation).
paramDocs.iAlignMode: The alignment of the text string:
paramDocs.iLengthMode: The length mode of the text string:
paramDocs.bTooltip: Determines if the original text is provided as tool tip when the displayed text becomes truncated.

dsptipmode.name: DspTipMode
dsptipmode.doc: Switches the display of tool tips on or off. This function overrides the setting in the [Page]TipHelp parameter.

paramDocs.nMode: The display mode:

dsptrend.name: DspTrend
dsptrend.doc: Displays a trend at an AN. Values are plotted on the trend pens. You need to specify Value1, but Value2 to Value8 are optional. If more values (than configured pens) are specified, the additional values are ignored. If fewer values (than configured pens) are specified, the pens that have no values are not displayed.
dsptrend.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend will be displayed.
paramDocs.Trend: The name of the trend to display in the format <[LibName.]TrnName>. If you do not specify the library name, a trend from the Global library will display (if it exists).
paramDocs.Value1: The value to display on Pen 1 of the trend.
paramDocs.Value2...8: The values to display on Pen 2...Pen 8 of the trend (optional).

dsptrendinfo.name: DspTrendInfo
dsptrendinfo.doc: Get information on a trend definition.
dsptrendinfo.returns: The trend information (as an integer). If Pen Color (Types 11 - 18) is requested from a bar trend, the return value is -1.

paramDocs.hTrend: The name of the trend in the format <[LibName.]TrnName>. If you do not specify the library name, a trend from the Global library is assumed.
paramDocs.nType: Type of trend info:
paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is displayed.

dspwebcontentgeturl.name: DspWebContentGetURL
dspwebcontentgeturl.doc: Gets the current URL for a Web Content control on a graphics page.
dspwebcontentgeturl.returns: The current URL of the specified Web Content control as a string.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the Web Content control is displayed.

dspwebcontentseturl.name: DspWebContentSetURL
dspwebcontentseturl.doc: Sets the URL for a Web Content control on a graphics page.
dspwebcontentseturl.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the Web Content control is displayed.

dumpkernel.name: DumpKernel
dumpkernel.doc: Dumps Kernel data to the KERNEL.DAT file. Instead of creating a new file subsequent calls to this function will append Kernel data to the KERNEL.DAT file.
dumpkernel.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The queue or table name (if "", returns data for all queues or tables). Only valid if iMode is 0x0020 and 0x0040.

engtogeneric.name: EngToGeneric
engtogeneric.doc: Gets a variable in the Plant SCADA generic scale format. Plant SCADA uses this scale to display trends. It calls this function automatically for trends defined in the project. If you want to display a trend using Cicode you need to call this function.

paramDocs.Value: The value to convert to the Plant SCADA generic scale format.

entercriticalsection.name: EnterCriticalSection
entercriticalsection.doc: Requests permission for the current thread to have access to a critical section (shared critical resource). If the critical section is already being accessed by another thread (using the EnterCriticalSection() function), the current thread will be granted access when the other thread relinquishes ownership using the LeaveCriticalSection() function.
entercriticalsection.returns: This function does not return a value.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the critical section. The name needs to be entered in quotation marks and follow the rules outlined in the topic Tag Name Syntax in the main help..

equipbrowseclose.name: EquipBrowseClose
equipbrowseclose.doc: The EquipBrowseClose function terminates an active data browse session and cleans up resources associated with the session.
equipbrowseclose.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment database browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipBrowseOpen call.

equipbrowsefirst.name: EquipBrowseFirst
equipbrowsefirst.doc: The EquipBrowseFirst function places the data browse cursor at the first record.
equipbrowsefirst.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment database browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipBrowseOpen call.

equipbrowsegetfield.name: EquipBrowseGetField
equipbrowsegetfield.doc: The EquipBrowseGetField function retrieves the value of the specified field from the record the data browse cursor is currently referencing.
equipbrowsegetfield.returns: The value of the specified field as a string. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. The last error should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipBrowseOpen call.
paramDocs.FieldName: The name of the field that references the value to be returned. Supported fields are:

equipbrowsenext.name: EquipBrowseNext
equipbrowsenext.doc: The EquipBrowseNext function moves the data browse cursor forward one record. If you call this function after you have reached the end of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
equipbrowsenext.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment database browse session exists, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipBrowseOpen call.

equipbrowsenumrecords.name: EquipBrowseNumRecords
equipbrowsenumrecords.doc: The EquipBrowseNumRecords function returns the number of records that match the filter criteria.
equipbrowsenumrecords.returns: The number of records that have matched the filter criteria. A value of 0 denotes that no records have matched. A value of -1 denotes that the browse session is unable to provide a fixed number. This may be the case if the data being browsed changed during the browse session.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipBrowseOpen call.

equipbrowseopen.name: EquipBrowseOpen
equipbrowseopen.doc: The EquipBrowseOpen function initiates a new browse session and returns a handle to the new session that can be used in subsequent data browse function calls.
equipbrowseopen.returns: Returns an integer handle to the browse session. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.Filter: A filter expression specifying the records to return during the browse. An empty string indicates that all records will be returned. Where a fieldname is not specified in the filter, it is assumed to be equipment name. For example, the filter "AAA" is equivalent to "name=AAA".
paramDocs.Fields: Specifies via a comma delimited string the columns to be returned during the browse. An empty string indicates that the server will return all available columns. Supported fields are:
paramDocs.Clusters: An optional parameter that specifies via a comma delimited string the subset of the clusters to browse. An empty string indicates that all connected clusters will be browsed.

equipbrowseprev.name: EquipBrowsePrev
equipbrowseprev.doc: The EquipBrowsePrev function moves the data browse cursor back one record. If you call this function after you have reached the beginning of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
equipbrowseprev.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment database browse session exists, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipBrowseOpen call.

equipcheckupdate.name: EquipCheckUpdate
equipcheckupdate.doc: The runtime environment will automatically check if the equipment database has been updated before each page open and before running an equipment browse open function (EquipBrowseOpen). It does this by checking the version of the database file. You may also update the database periodically in a background task to reload the database even if the page is not changed.
equipcheckupdate.returns: 0 (FALSE) if the equipment database has not changed, or 1 (TRUE) if it has been changed, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Reload: 0 (FALSE) checks the status of the database without reloading it.
paramDocs.Cluster: The cluster name to check and/or reload the equipment database for. All clusters will be checked if omitted or an empty string is set.

equipgetparameter.name: EquipGetParameter
equipgetparameter.doc: Reads a runtime parameter of an equipment database record from the EQPARAM.RDB database file.
equipgetparameter.returns: The value of the specified parameter as a string. If the parameter is a tag reference, the value of the tag shall be returned.

paramDocs.ClusterName: The name of the cluster (optional for a single cluster system)
paramDocs.EquipmentName: The name of the equipment from which to get information. The name of the equipment can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Equipment".
paramDocs.ParameterName: The name of the parameter for which to retrieve a value.

equipgetproperty.name: EquipGetProperty
equipgetproperty.doc: This function reads a property of an equipment database record from the EQUIP.RDB database file.
equipgetproperty.returns: The value of the specified field as a string. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. The last error should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the equipment from which to get information. The name of the equipment can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Equipment".
paramDocs.Field: The field to read. Supported fields are:
paramDocs.Mode: 1 Cache - values are first retrieved from local memory cache, if the property is missing from the memory cache, a request will be sent to the report server and the result will then be cached. If the property is missing from the memory cache or if a previous request is in progress, an empty string will be returned.
paramDocs.Cluster: The name of the cluster (optional for a single cluster system).

equiprefbrowseclose.name: EquipRefBrowseClose
equiprefbrowseclose.doc: The EquipRefBrowseClose function terminates an active data browse session and cleans up resources associated with the session.
equiprefbrowseclose.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment database browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipBrowseOpen call.

equiprefbrowsefirst.name: EquipRefBrowseFirst
equiprefbrowsefirst.doc: The EquipRefBrowseFirst function places the reference browse cursor at the first record.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipRefBrowseOpen call.

equiprefbrowsegetfield.name: EquipRefBrowseGetField
equiprefbrowsegetfield.doc: The EquipRefBrowseGetField function retrieves the value of the specified field from the record the data browse cursor is currently referencing.
equiprefbrowsegetfield.returns: The value of the specified field as a string. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. The last error should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipRefBrowseOpen call.

equiprefbrowsenext.name: EquipRefBrowseNext
equiprefbrowsenext.doc: The EquipRefBrowseNext function moves the data browse cursor forward one record. If you call this function after you have reached the end of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
equiprefbrowsenext.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment reference database browse session exists, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipRefBrowseNext call.

equiprefbrowsenumrecords.name: EquipRefBrowseNumRecords
equiprefbrowsenumrecords.doc: The EquipRefBrowseNumRecords function returns the number of records that match the filter criteria.
equiprefbrowsenumrecords.returns: The number of records that have matched the filter criteria. A value of 0 denotes that no records have matched. A value of -1 denotes that the browse session is unable to provide a fixed number. This may be the case if the data being browsed changed during the browse session.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipRefBrowseOpen call.

equiprefbrowseopen.name: EquipRefBrowseOpen
equiprefbrowseopen.doc: The EquipRefBrowseOpen function initiates a new browse session and returns a handle to the new session that can be used in subsequent equipment reference browse function calls.
equiprefbrowseopen.returns: Returns an integer handle to the browse session. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.Filter: A filter expression specifying the records to return during the browse. An empty string indicates that all records will be returned. Where a fieldname is not specified in the filter, it is assumed to be equipment name. For example, the filter "AAA" is equivalent to "name=AAA".
paramDocs.Fields: Specifies via a comma delimited string the columns to be returned during the browse. An empty string indicates that the server will return all available columns. Supported fields are:
paramDocs.Sort: Comma delimited list of record fields to be returned in order of sorting preferences. For example(GROUP:D, ORDER:A)

equiprefbrowseprev.name: EquipRefBrowsePrev
equiprefbrowseprev.doc: The EquipRefBrowsePrev function moves the data browse cursor back one record. If you call this function after you have reached the beginning of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
equiprefbrowseprev.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment database browse session exists, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipRefBrowseOpen call.

equipsetproperty.name: EquipSetProperty
equipsetproperty.doc: The EquipSetProperty function sets the property of an item of equipment.
equipsetproperty.returns: Returns 0 if successful otherwise it returns an error.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the equipment.
paramDocs.Field: Only properties coming from the scheduler engine can be set:
paramDocs.Value: The value to be set:

equipstatebrowseclose.name: EquipStateBrowseClose
equipstatebrowseclose.doc: The EquipStateBrowseClose function terminates a browsing session and cleans up the resources used by the session. This function uses iSession as the argument which is previously returned by the EquipStateBrowseOpen function.
equipstatebrowseclose.returns: Returns 0 if the equipment state database browse session has been closed successfully, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipStateBrowseOpen call

equipstatebrowsefirst.name: EquipStateBrowseFirst
equipstatebrowsefirst.doc: The EquipStateBrowseFirst function places the data browse cursor at the first record.
equipstatebrowsefirst.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment state database browse session exists, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipStateBrowseOpen call.

equipstatebrowsegetfield.name: EquipStateBrowseGetField
equipstatebrowsegetfield.doc: The EquipStateBrowseGetField function returns the value of the particular field in a record to which the data browse cursor is currently referencing. This function uses the field name whose value needs to be returned.
equipstatebrowsegetfield.returns: The value of the specified field as a string. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. The last error should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipStateBrowseOpen call.
paramDocs.Field: The name of the field that references the value to be returned. Available fields are:

equipstatebrowsenext.name: EquipStateBrowseNext
equipstatebrowsenext.doc: The EquipStateBrowseNext function places the data browse cursor at the next available record. This function will return an error if called when the data cursor is at end of the records.
equipstatebrowsenext.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment state database browse session exists, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipStateBrowseOpen call.

equipstatebrowsenumrecords.name: EquipStateBrowseNumRecords
equipstatebrowsenumrecords.doc: The EquipStateBrowseNumRecords function returns the number of records that match the current filter criteria.
equipstatebrowsenumrecords.returns: Returns the number of records which matches the current filter criteria. 0 means no records were found.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipStateBrowseOpen call.

equipstatebrowseopen.name: EquipStateBrowseOpen
equipstatebrowseopen.doc: The EquipStateBrowseOpen function initiates a new session for browsing the equipment states configured. It returns a handle for the browsing session which can be used for further browsing operations.
equipstatebrowseopen.returns: Returns an integer handle to the browse session. Returns -1 when an error is detected.

paramDocs.Filter: A filter expression specifying the records to return during the browse. An empty string indicates that every record will be returned. Where a field name is not specified in the filter, it is assumed to be tagname. For example, the filter "AAA" is equivalent to "name=AAA".
paramDocs.Fields: Specifies via a comma delimited string the columns to be returned during the browse. An empty string indicates that the server will return every available column. Available fields are:
paramDocs.Clusters: An optional parameter that specifies via a comma delimited string the subset of the clusters to browse. An empty string indicates that every connected cluster will be browsed.

equipstatebrowseprev.name: EquipStateBrowsePrev
equipstatebrowseprev.doc: The EquipStateBrowsePrev function places the data browse cursor at the previous record. This function will return an error if called when the data cursor is at beginning of the records.
equipstatebrowseprev.returns: 0 (zero) if the equipment state browse session exists, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a EquipStateBrowseOpen call.

errcom.name: ErrCom
errcom.doc: Gets the communication status for the current Cicode task. You can call this function in reports, Cicode that is associated with an object, and in any Cicode task.
errcom.returns: 0 (zero) if all I/O device data associated with the task is valid, otherwise an error is returned.

errdrv.name: ErrDrv
errdrv.doc: Gets a protocol-specific error message and native error code.
errdrv.returns: The error message (as a string), or an empty string ("") if the error is not found. The error code is returned into the nError variable.

paramDocs.sField: The field in the PROTERR.DBF database:
paramDocs.nError: The protocol specific error code. This field needs to be a variable as it also the place where the returned error code is stored.

errgethw.name: ErrGetHw
errgethw.doc: Gets the current hardware error status for an I/O device.

paramDocs.Device: For I/O devices that are created by the system engineer, select the IODevNo as the argument value.
paramDocs.DeviceType: Select a value from the following options to indicate the 'Type of Device' used in the Device argument:

errhelp.name: ErrHelp
errhelp.doc: Displays information about a hardware error.
errhelp.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error (274) is returned.

errinfo.name: ErrInfo
errinfo.doc: Gets extended error information on the last error that was detected.

paramDocs.nType: The type of error information. If type is 0 (zero), function returns the animation number where the error occurred.

errlog.name: ErrLog
errlog.doc: Logs a message to the Plant SCADA system log file.
errlog.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Message: The message to log. This field can also contain control (such as /n) and formatting characters.

errmsg.name: ErrMsg
errmsg.doc: Gets the error message associated with a detected hardware error.
errmsg.returns: The error message (as a string). A null value is returned if nError is not in the range of Cicode errors.

paramDocs.nError: The hardware error number returned from the IsError() function.

errset.name: ErrSet
errset.doc: Sets the error-checking mode. When Mode is set to 0 and an error occurs that causes a component to stop executing, Plant SCADA halts the execution of the Cicode task that caused the error, and generates a hardware error.
errset.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

errsethw.name: ErrSetHw
errsethw.doc: Sets the hardware error status for a hardware device. Call this function to generate a hardware error.
errsethw.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Device: For I/O devices that are created by the system engineer, select the IODevNo as the argument value.
paramDocs.DeviceType: Select a value from the following options to indicate the 'Type of Device' used in the Device argument:

errsetlevel.name: ErrSetLevel
errsetlevel.doc: Sets the nesting error level to enable Plant SCADA error checking inside a nested function (when Plant SCADA error checking has been disabled). This function returns the old error level and sets a new error level.
errsetlevel.returns: Returns the old error level and sets a new error level.

errtrap.name: ErrTrap
errtrap.doc: Generates an error trap. If Plant SCADA error checking is enabled, this function will generate a hardware error and may halt Cicode execution (see bHalt argument). If user error checking is enabled, the user function specified in OnEvent(2,Fn) is called.
errtrap.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.bHalt: Determines whether the Cicode execution will be halted.

exec.name: Exec
exec.doc: Executes an application, LNK file or PIF file (32 bit system only). The application or command starts up and continues to run in parallel with Plant SCADA.
exec.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Command: The operating system command to execute (maximum of 255 characters).

executedtspkg.name: ExecuteDTSPkg
executedtspkg.doc: Loads and executes a DTS (Data Transformation Services) package which initiates data transfer and transformations between OLE DB data sources.
executedtspkg.returns: 0 (zero) if the package was executed successfully, otherwise a DTS error number is returned.

paramDocs.sFileOrSQLSvrName: The path and name of the file containing the package (for file-based packages), or the SQL Server name (for SQL Server stored packages).
paramDocs.sPkgVer: The package version. If you don't specify a version, the most recent version is used.
paramDocs.sLogFile: AN optional path and name for a log file. The log file can track activity such as:
paramDocs.sSQLSvrUsr: The user name providing access to the SQL Server where the DTS package is stored. A user's account on the SQL Server consists of this user name and, in most cases, a password.
paramDocs.sSQLSvrPwd: The password providing access to the SQL Server, if the user's account on the server requires a password.

exp.name: Exp
exp.doc: Calculates the exponential of a number (natural logarithm base e).
exp.returns: The exponential of Number (to the base e).

fact.name: Fact
fact.doc: Calculates the factorial of a number.

fileclose.name: FileClose
fileclose.doc: Closes a file. All data written to the file is flushed to disk when the file is closed, and the file number becomes invalid.
fileclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

filecopy.name: FileCopy
filecopy.doc: Copies a file. You can use the DOS wild card characters (*) and (?) to copy groups of files. In asynchronous mode, this function will return immediately and the copy will continue in the background. Copying files does not interfere with the operation of other Plant SCADA tasks, because this function is time-sliced.
filecopy.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned. However, if you copy in asynchronous mode, the return value does not reflect whether the copy operation was successful or not, because the function returns before the actual copy is complete.

paramDocs.sSource: The name of the source file to copy.
paramDocs.sDest: The name of destination file to copy to. To copy a file to the printer, specify the name as "LPT1.DOS".
paramDocs.nMode: The copy mode:

filedelete.name: FileDelete
filedelete.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the file to delete.

fileeof.name: FileEOF
fileeof.doc: Determines if the end of the file has been reached.
fileeof.returns: 1 if the end of file has been reached, otherwise 0 (zero).

fileexist.name: FileExist
fileexist.doc: Checks if a file exists. If the return value is 1, the file exists.
fileexist.returns: TRUE (1) if the file exists, otherwise FALSE (0).

paramDocs.Name: The name of the file to check.

filefind.name: FileFind
filefind.doc: Finds a file that matches a specified search criteria. To find a list of files, you need to first call this function with the required path and mode (to find the first file), then call the function again with an empty path and a mode of 0 (to find the remaining files). After the last file is found, an empty string is returned.
filefind.returns: The full path and filename. If no files are found, an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.sPath: The name of the file to check. To search for multiple files, the wildcards * and ? can be used to match multiple entries.
paramDocs.nMode: The type of file to check:

filefindclose.name: FileFindClose
filefindclose.doc: Closes a find (started with FileFind) that did not run to completion.
filefindclose.returns: 0 if no error is detected, or a Cicode error code if an error occurred.

filegettime.name: FileGetTime
filegettime.doc: Gets the time on a file.
filegettime.returns: The file time of the file (in the Plant SCADA time/date variable format).

filemakepath.name: FileMakePath
filemakepath.doc: Creates a file path string from individual components.
filemakepath.returns: The full path as a string.

fileopen.name: FileOpen
fileopen.doc: Opens a file and returns a file number that can be used by other file functions. The maximum file size supported is 1 Megabyte for displaying text files.
fileopen.returns: The file number. If the file cannot be opened, -1 is returned and the code is halted.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the file to open.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the opened file:

fileprint.name: FilePrint
fileprint.doc: Prints a file on a device.
fileprint.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Devicename: The name of the target device.
paramDocs.Filename: The name of the file to print on the device.

fileread.name: FileRead
fileread.doc: Reads a number of characters from a file. The string can contain less characters than requested if the end of file is reached. A maximum of 255 characters can be read in each call.
fileread.returns: The text from the file (as a string).

paramDocs.Length: The number of characters to read.

filereadblock.name: FileReadBlock
filereadblock.doc: Reads a number of characters from a file. The buffer can contain less characters than requested if the end of file is reached. A maximum of 255 characters can be read in each call. The data should be treated as a binary data and should not be passed to string functions. You may use StrGetChar() function to extract each character from the buffer, or pass the buffer to another function which will accept binary data.
filereadblock.returns: The number of characters read from the file. When the end of the file is found 0 will be returned. If an error occurs -1 will be returned and IsError() will return the error code.

paramDocs.Buffer: The buffer to return the binary data. This may be a string or a string packed with binary data. The string terminator is ignored and the length argument specifies the number of characters to write. Must be a string variable.
paramDocs.Length: The number of characters to read.

filereadln.name: FileReadLn
filereadln.doc: Reads a line from a file. Up to 255 characters can be returned. The carriage return and newline characters are not returned. If the line is longer than 255 characters, the error overflow (code 275) is returned - you should call this function again to read the rest of the line.

filerename.name: FileRename
filerename.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Oldname: The original name of the file.
paramDocs.Newname: The new name of the file.

filerichtextprint.name: FileRichTextPrint
filerichtextprint.doc: Prints the rich text file sFilename to the printer given by sPortname.

paramDocs.sFilename: The filename of the rich text format file. The filename needs to be entered in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.PortName: The name of the printer port to which the rich text file will be printed. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks "". For example "LPT1", to print to the local printer, or "\\Pserver\canon1" using UNC to print to a network printer.

fileseek.name: FileSeek
fileseek.doc: Moves the file pointer to a specified position in a file.
fileseek.returns: The new file position, or -1 if an error is detected.

paramDocs.Offset: The offset in bytes, from 0 to (maximum file size -1). This value needs to be >= 0.

filesettime.name: FileSetTime
filesettime.doc: Sets the time on a file.
filesettime.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.iTime: The new file time, in the Plant SCADA time/date variable format.

filesize.name: FileSize
filesize.doc: Gets the size of a file.
filesize.returns: The size of the file in bytes.

filesplitpath.name: FileSplitPath
filesplitpath.doc: Splits a file path into individual string components. You enter the full path string as sPath. The individual components of the path name are returned in the arguments sDrive, sDir, sFile, and sExt. Arguments must be declared as Cicode variables. If declared as local variables or tags, an "Incompatible Types" error will be returned.
filesplitpath.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sDrive: The disk drive. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.sDir: The directory string. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.sFile: The file name (without the extension). Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.sExt: The file extension. Must be a String type variable.

filewrite.name: FileWrite
filewrite.doc: Writes a string to a file. The string is written at the current file position. The maximum number of characters allowed is 255.

filewriteblock.name: FileWriteBlock
filewriteblock.doc: Writes a string or buffer to a file. The data is written at the current file position. You may create the binary data by using the StrSetChar function or by reading the data from some other function. This function is similar to the FileWrite() function however you specify the length of data to write to the file. The FileWrite() function will send the data to the file until the sting terminator is found. FileWriteBlock() will ignore any string terminator and copy the length of bytes to the file. This allows this function to be used for binary data transfer.
filewriteblock.returns: The number of characters written to the file. If an error is detected -1 will be returned and IsError() will return the error code.

paramDocs.Buffer: The data to write to the file. This may be a string or a string packed with binary data. The string terminator is ignored and the length argument specifies the number of characters to write. Must be a string variable.
paramDocs.Length: The number of characters to write. The maximum number of characters you may write in one call is 255. (If you use a string without a terminator in a function that expects a string, or in a Cicode expression, you could get invalid results.) To use the string to build up a buffer, you do not need the terminating 0 (zero).

filewriteln.name: FileWriteLn
filewriteln.doc: Writes a string to a file, followed by a newline character. The string is written at the current file position. The maximum number of characters allowed is 255.
filewriteln.returns: The number of characters written (including the carriage return and newline characters).

fmtclose.name: FmtClose
fmtclose.doc: Closes a format template. After it is closed, the template cannot be used. Closing the template releases system memory.
fmtclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where all data on the associated format template is stored.

fmtfieldhnd.name: FmtFieldHnd
fmtfieldhnd.doc: Gets the handle of a field in a format template. You can then use the field handle in the FmtGetFieldHnd() and FmtSetFieldHnd() functions. By using a handle, you only need to resolve the field name once and then call other functions as required (resulting in improved performance.)
fmtfieldhnd.returns: The handle of the format template field, or -1 if the field cannot be found.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where all data on the associated format template is stored.
paramDocs.sName: The field name.

fmtgetfield.name: FmtGetField
fmtgetfield.doc: Gets field data from a format template. Use this function to extract data after a call to StrToFmt().
fmtgetfield.returns: The data (as a string). If the field does not contain any data, an empty string will be returned.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where data on the associated format template is stored.
paramDocs.sName: The field name.

fmtgetfieldcount.name: FmtGetFieldCount
fmtgetfieldcount.doc: Retrieves the number of fields in a format object.
fmtgetfieldcount.returns: Number of fields in the specified format.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where data on the associated format template is stored.

fmtgetfieldhnd.name: FmtGetFieldHnd
fmtgetfieldhnd.doc: Gets field data from a format template. Use this function to extract data after a call to StrToFmt(). This function has the same effect as FmtGetField(), except that you use a field handle instead of the field name.
fmtgetfieldhnd.returns: The data (as a string). If the field does not contain any data, an empty string will be returned.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where all data on the associated format template is stored.

fmtgetfieldname.name: FmtGetFieldName
fmtgetfieldname.doc: Retrieves the name of a particular field in a format object.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where data on the associated format template is stored.

fmtgetfieldwidth.name: FmtGetFieldWidth
fmtgetfieldwidth.doc: Retrieves the width of a particular field in a format object.

paramDocs.hFmt: The handle to a format object. The handle identifies the table where data on the associated format template is stored.

fmtopen.name: FmtOpen
fmtopen.doc: Creates a format template. After you create a template, you can use it for formatting data into strings or extracting data from a string. To format a template, use the same syntax as a device format, that is {<name>[,width[,justification]]}. The maximum number of formats that can be created in a project is 512. If you attempt to create formats in excess of this number, an error code (code 258: CT_ERROR_BUFFER_OVERRUN) will be generated.
fmtopen.returns: The format template handle, or -1 if the format cannot be created.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the format template or Alarm Category.
paramDocs.Format: The format of the template, as {<name>[,width[,justification]]}. Not used for alarm format. See Format Templates for more information.

fmtsetfield.name: FmtSetField
fmtsetfield.doc: Sets data in a field of a format template. After you have set all the fields, you can build the formatted string with the FmtToStr() function.
fmtsetfield.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where all data on the associated format template is stored.
paramDocs.sName: The name of the format template.

fmtsetfieldhnd.name: FmtSetFieldHnd
fmtsetfieldhnd.doc: The fields you can build the formatted string with the FmtToStr() function. This function has the same effect as FmtSetField() except that you use a field handle instead of the field name.
fmtsetfieldhnd.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where all data on the associated format template is stored.

fmttostr.name: FmtToStr
fmttostr.doc: Builds a formatted string from the current field data (in a format template).
fmttostr.returns: The formatted string as defined in the format description.

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where all data on the associated format template is stored.

formactive.name: FormActive
formactive.doc: Checks if a form is currently active (displayed on the screen). This function is useful when forms are being displayed in asynchronous mode and another Cicode task is trying to access the form.
formactive.returns: TRUE (1) if the form is active or FALSE (0) if it is not.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.

formaddlist.name: FormAddList
formaddlist.doc: Adds a text string to a list box or combo box. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function, and immediately after either the FormComboBox() or the FormListBox(), and before the FormRead() function otherwise an error is returned. The text is added at the end of the list box or combo box.
formaddlist.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sText: The text string to add to the list box or combo box.

formbutton.name: FormButton
formbutton.doc: Adds a button to the current form. You can add buttons that run callback functions (specified in Fn) to perform any actions you need, as well as the standard buttons - an [OK] button to save the operator's entries and close the form, and a [Cancel] button to close the form but discard the changes.
formbutton.returns: The field handle if the button is successfully added, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the button will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the button in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the button will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the button in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.sText: The text to display on the button.
paramDocs.Fn: The callback function to call when the button is selected. Set to 0 to call no function. Please be aware that the Fn parameter needs to be of type INT and the callback function cannot contain a blocking function.

formcheckbox.name: FormCheckBox
formcheckbox.doc: Adds a check box to the current form. The check box is a form control that allows the operator to make individual selections. Each check box can be either checked (true) or cleared (false).
formcheckbox.returns: The field handle if the check box is successfully added, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the check box will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the check box in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the check box will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the check box in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.sText: The text associated with the check box.
paramDocs.sBuf: The string buffer in which to put the state of the check box. You should initialize this buffer to the state of the check box. When the form returns, this buffer will contain either '1' or '0' if the box is checked.

formcombobox.name: FormComboBox
formcombobox.doc: Adds a combo box to the current form. A combo box is a form control that allows the operator to type a selection or make a single selection from a text list.
formcombobox.returns: The field handle if the combo box is successfully added, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the combo box will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the combo box in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the combo box will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the combo box in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the list box, which should be wide enough to display your widest item. Items wider than the list box are clipped.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the list box (the number of items that can be seen in the list box without scrolling).
paramDocs.sBuf: The string buffer in which to store the selected item. The sBuf parameter can also hold the starting selection for the Combo box. For example if you set the sBuf string to "HELLO" before calling FormComboBox, HELLO will be displayed in the box upon opening the form. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.Mode: The mode in which to create the combo box:

formcurr.name: FormCurr
formcurr.doc: Gets the form and field handles for the current form and field. You should call this function only from within a callback function. You can then use the same callback function for all forms and fields, regardless of how the boxes, buttons, etc. on the forms are used. You should use this function with the FormGetInst() function.
formcurr.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: Variable containing the form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.
paramDocs.hField: Variable containing the field handle of the field currently selected.

formdestroy.name: FormDestroy
formdestroy.doc: Destroys a form that is removes it from the screen. Use this function (from an event) to close a form.
formdestroy.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.

formedit.name: FormEdit
formedit.doc: Adds an edit field to the current form. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function. A user input/edit box is added to the form at the specified column and row position. The operator can enter or edit the text in the edit box. This text is then passed to this function as Text.
formedit.returns: The field handle if the string is successfully added, otherwise -1 is returned.
