paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the edit field will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the edit field in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the edit field will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the edit field in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Text: Variable containing the text in the edit field. Text initially contains the default text (if any) for the operator to edit. When the function closes, this argument is passed back with the operator's input.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the edit field.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the edit field as measured using average character height. When value specified is less than 1 or not specified, it is default to 1 (single line). When multiple lines are specified, the content of the edit box will be word wrapped.
paramDocs.bReadOnly: Flag to indicate whether the edit box is read only. Default is FALSE if not specified.
paramDocs.maxTextLength: This optional parameter specifies the maximum length of input text. The default value is 0 meaning the string can have the maximum length allowed in the system (Cicode allows strings of 255 characters).

formfield.name: FormField
formfield.doc: Adds a field control device (such as a button , check box, or edit field) to the current form. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function. This function allows you to specify a control device with more detail than the other field functions.
formfield.returns: The field handle if the field is successfully added, otherwise it will return -1.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the control will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the control in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the control will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the control in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the control device.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the control device.
paramDocs.nType: The type of control device:
paramDocs.Buffer: The output buffer for the field string. The default value of the control device is initialized to the value of the buffer. If you specify a Radio button or Check box, you should initialize the buffer to "0" or "1". The result of the field will also be set to "0" or "1".
paramDocs.Label: The display label for a button, or the default label for an edit field
paramDocs.Fn: The callback function to call when the button is selected. Set to 0 to call no function. Please be aware that the Fn parameter needs to be of type INT, and the callback function cannot contain a blocking function. For types other than 4,5, and 6, set this argument to 0.
paramDocs.maxTextLength: This optional parameter specifies the maximum length of input text for edit fields (this parameter is ignored for other controls). The default value is 0 meaning the string can have the maximum length allowed in the system (Cicode allows strings of 255 characters).

formgetcurrinst.name: FormGetCurrInst
formgetcurrinst.doc: Extracts data associated with a field (set by the FormSetInst() function). You should call this function only from within a field callback function. This function is the same as calling the FormCurr() function and then the FormGetInst() function.
formgetcurrinst.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

formgetdata.name: FormGetData
formgetdata.doc: Gets all data associated with a form and puts it into the output string buffers. Normally the field data is copied to the output string buffers only when the user selects the [OK] button. If you want to use the data while the form is displayed, call this function to get the data. You should call this function only while the form is displayed otherwise an error is returned, for example, from a field callback function.
formgetdata.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.

formgetinst.name: FormGetInst
formgetinst.doc: Extracts the data associated with a field (set by the FormSetInst() function). You would normally use this function in a field callback function. It allows single callback functions to know that the form and field are associated.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.
paramDocs.hField: The field handle of the field currently selected.

formgettext.name: FormGetText
formgettext.doc: Gets the current text from a form field. You should call this function only while the form is displayed; for example,, from a field callback function.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.
paramDocs.hField: The field handle of the field currently selected.

formgoto.name: FormGoto
formgoto.doc: Goes to a specified form. The form is displayed on top of all windows and the keyboard focus is set to this form.
formgoto.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.

formgroupbox.name: FormGroupBox
formgroupbox.doc: Adds a group box to the current form. A group box is a form control box drawn to the specified size. If the box contains radio buttons, they are grouped together. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function.
formgroupbox.returns: The field handle if the group box is successfully added, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the group box will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the group box in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the group box will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the group box in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the group box, which should be wide enough to display your widest item.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the group box.
paramDocs.Text: The text to display as the group box label.

forminput.name: FormInput
forminput.doc: Adds a prompt and edit field to the current form. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function. When FormRead() is called, the form will display with the prompt and edit box. The operator's input is passed back as a string (Text).
forminput.returns: The field handle if it is added successfully, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the prompt will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the prompt in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the prompt will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the prompt in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the edit field.
paramDocs.maxTextLength: This optional parameter specifies the maximum length of input text. The default value is 0 meaning the string can have the maximum length allowed in the system (Cicode allows strings of 255 characters).

formlistaddtext.name: FormListAddText
formlistaddtext.doc: Adds a new text entry to a combo box or a list box while the form is displayed. It only adds the text to the list - it does not select it. Use the FormListSelectText() function to select (highlight) an entry. Call this function only when the form is displayed, for example, from a field callback function.
formlistaddtext.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.
paramDocs.hField: The field handle of the field currently selected.
paramDocs.Text: The output text string containing the operator's input.

formlistbox.name: FormListBox
formlistbox.doc: Adds a list box to the current form. The list box is a form control that allows the operator to select from a list of items. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function.
formlistbox.returns: The field handle if the list box is successfully added, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the list box will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the list box in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the list box will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the list box in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the list box, in characters. Width should be wide enough to display your widest item. Items wider than the list box are clipped.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the list box, as the number of items that can be seen in the list box without scrolling.
paramDocs.sBuf: The string buffer in which to store the selected item. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.Mode: The mode in which to create the list box:

formlistdeletetext.name: FormListDeleteText
formlistdeletetext.doc: Deletes an existing text entry from a combo box or a list box while the form is displayed. It only deletes the text from the list - it does not change the selection. Call this function only when the form is displayed, for example, from a field callback function.
formlistdeletetext.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.
paramDocs.hField: The field handle of the field currently selected.

formlistselecttext.name: FormListSelectText
formlistselecttext.doc: Selects (highlights) a text entry in a Combo box or a List box while the form is displayed. The text to be selected needs to exist in the list. (Use the FormListAddText() function to add a text entry to a list.) Call this function only when the form is displayed, for example, from a field callback function.
formlistselecttext.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.
paramDocs.hField: The field handle of the field currently selected.
paramDocs.Text: The text to be selected. If this text is not present in the list, then no item will be selected (and this text will not be added).

formnew.name: FormNew
formnew.doc: Creates a new data entry form and defines its size and mode. After the form is created, you can add fields, and then display the form.
formnew.returns: The form handle if the form is created successfully, otherwise -1 is returned. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.

paramDocs.Title: The title of the form.
paramDocs.Width: The character width of the form (1 to 131).
paramDocs.Height: The character height of the form (1 to 131).

formnumpad.name: FormNumPad
formnumpad.doc: Provides a keypad form for the operator to add numeric values. You can customize the standard form as a mathematical keypad, with the +, -, and / operators and the decimal point. For a time keypad, use the AM, PM, and : (hour/minute divider) buttons. You can also include a password edit field.
formnumpad.returns: The string value entered by the operator. The IsError() function returns 0 (zero). If the form was cancelled, the value of Input is returned, and the IsError() function returns error number 299.

paramDocs.Title: The title to display on the number pad form.
paramDocs.Input: The existing or default value. This value is returned if the form is cancelled or accepted without changes.
paramDocs.Mode: The buttons to include on the keypad form. The Mode can be a combination of the following:

formopenfile.name: FormOpenFile
formopenfile.doc: Displays a File Open dialog box.
formopenfile.returns: The name and full path of the selected file (as a string) or an empty string ("") if the Cancel button is selected.

paramDocs.sFileName: The name of the default file to display in the "File Name" field.
paramDocs.sTitle: A title to display at the top of the form.
paramDocs.sFilter: A file filter list to display in the "List Files of Type" field. The file filter list has the following format:
paramDocs.bResetToDefault: Boolean parameter. When set forces the path to reset to the default path specified.

formpassword.name: FormPassword
formpassword.doc: Adds both a password prompt and edit field to the current form. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function. When FormRead() is called, the form will also display the password prompt and edit field.
formpassword.returns: The field handle if it is added successfully, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the prompt will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the prompt in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the prompt will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the prompt in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Password: Variable containing the password entered by the operator.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the edit field.

formposition.name: FormPosition
formposition.doc: Sets the position of a form on the screen, before it is displayed. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function.
formposition.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

formprompt.name: FormPrompt
formprompt.doc: Adds a prompt field to the current form. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function.
formprompt.returns: The field handle if it is added successfully, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the prompt will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the prompt in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the prompt will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the prompt in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the area that the prompt string will wrap within (measured using average character width). For this setting to be applied, you also need to specify a value for Height.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the area that the prompt string will display within (measured using average character height). For this setting to be applied, you also need to specify a value for Width.

formradiobutton.name: FormRadioButton
formradiobutton.doc: Adds a radio button to the current form, allowing the operator to make a selection from a multiple choice list. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function.
formradiobutton.returns: The field handle if the radio button is successfully added, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the button will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the button in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the button will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the button in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.sText: The text associated with the radio button.
paramDocs.sBuf: The string buffer in which to put the state of the radio button. You should initialize this buffer to the state of the button. When the form returns, this buffer will contain either '1' or '0' if the radio button is checked.

formread.name: FormRead
formread.doc: Displays the current form (created with the FormNew() function), with all the fields that were added (with the form field functions).
formread.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

formsaveasfile.name: FormSaveAsFile
formsaveasfile.doc: Displays a File Save As dialog box.
formsaveasfile.returns: The name and full path of the selected file (as a string) or an empty string ("") if the Cancel button is selected.

paramDocs.sTitle: A title to display at the top of the form.
paramDocs.sFileName: The name of the default file to display in the "File Name" field.
paramDocs.sFilter: A file filter list to display in the "List Files of Type" field. The file filter list has the following format:
paramDocs.sDefExt: The file extension that will be used as a default when you use the FormSaveAsFile() function. If you do not specify a default extension, files will be saved without an extension.

formsecurepassword.name: FormSecurePassword
formsecurepassword.doc: Adds both a password prompt and edit field to the current form. You should call this function only after the FormNew() function and before the FormRead() function. When FormRead() is called, the form will also display the password prompt and edit field.
formsecurepassword.returns: The field handle if it is added successfully, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.Col: The number of the column in which the prompt will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (column 1) to the form width - 1. For example, to place the prompt in column 8, enter 7.
paramDocs.Row: The number of the row in which the prompt will be placed. Enter a number from 0 (row 1) to the form height - 1. For example, to place the prompt in row 6, enter 5.
paramDocs.Prompt: The prompt string. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.Password: The encrypted password entered by the operator.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the edit field.

formselectprinter.name: FormSelectPrinter
formselectprinter.doc: Displays the Select Printer dialog box.
formselectprinter.returns: The name of the selected printer (as a string) or an empty string ("") if the Cancel button is selected.

formsetdata.name: FormSetData
formsetdata.doc: Sets all the edit data from the string buffers into the form. You should call this function only while the form is active.
formsetdata.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.

formsetinst.name: FormSetInst
formsetinst.doc: Associates an integer and string value with each field on a form. This data could then be used by a callback function. You can use a single callback function for all fields, and use the data to perform different operations for each field.
formsetinst.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.
paramDocs.hField: The field handle of the field currently selected.

formsettext.name: FormSetText
formsettext.doc: Sets new field text on a field. This function allows you to change field text while the form is displayed. Call this function only when the form is displayed, for example, from a field callback function.
formsettext.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where all data on the associated form is stored.
paramDocs.hField: The field handle of the field currently selected. If the hField is a handle to the secure edit field created with FormSecurePassword, the text in the secure edit field will not be changed. However, when an empty string is passed to FormSetText(), the contents of the secure edit field will be cleared.

formwndhnd.name: FormWndHnd
formwndhnd.doc: Gets the window handle for the given form. The window handle may be used by 'C' programs and Plant SCADAWnd... functions. You should call this function only after the FormRead() function.
formwndhnd.returns: The window handle if successful, otherwise a 0 is returned.

paramDocs.hForm: The form handle, returned from the FormNew() function. The form handle identifies the table where data on the associated form is stored.

ftpclose.name: FTPClose
ftpclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

ftpfilecopy.name: FTPFileCopy
ftpfilecopy.doc: Copies a file from the FTP server to the Internet Display Client.
ftpfilecopy.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hndFTP: The handle of a valid FTP session, as returned by FTPOpen().
paramDocs.sSrcPath: The file name and path of the file to be copied from the FTP Server to the Internet Display Client. This can be any FTP server.
paramDocs.sDestPath: The destination of the copied file (including the name of the file).

ftpfilefind.name: FTPFileFind
ftpfilefind.doc: Finds a file on the FTP server that matches a specified search criteria.
ftpfilefind.returns: The full path and filename. If no files are found, an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.0: Normal files (includes files with read-only and archived attributes)
paramDocs.hndFTP: The handle of a valid FTP session, as returned by FTPOpen().
paramDocs.sPath: The path you want to search for the desired file. Do not use path substitution here. To search for multiple files, the wildcards * and ? may be used to match multiple entries.
paramDocs.nMode: The type of file to check:

ftpfilefindclose.name: FTPFileFindClose
ftpfilefindclose.doc: Closes a find (started with FTPFileFind) that did not run to completion.
ftpfilefindclose.returns: 0 if no error is detected, or a Cicode error code if an error occurred.

ftpopen.name: FTPOpen
ftpopen.returns: A handle to the FTP server otherwise -1 if an error occurs (for example, the server cannot be found).

paramDocs.sIPAddress: The TCP/IP address of the FTP server you wish to connect to (for example, 10.5.6.7 or plant.yourdoman.com). If you do not specify an IP address, the Plant SCADA FTP server running on the Internet Server you are connected to will be used.
paramDocs.sUsername: The FTP login username. If you omit both the username and IP address, the Plant SCADA FTP password will be used. If you omit just the username, an anonymous logon will occur.
paramDocs.sPassword: The FTP server password. If you wish to log on anonymously or you wish to log on to the Plant SCADA FTP server, do not specify a password, here.

fullname.name: FullName
fullname.doc: Gets the full name of the user who is currently logged on to the system. The user can be a Plant SCADA or a Windows user. For a Plant SCADA user the full name is the one defined in the user settings. For a Windows user the full name is in the format of <DomainName>\<UserName>. When there is no one logged in or the logged in user is a "system user" this function returns an empty string.

fuzzyclose.name: FuzzyClose
fuzzyclose.doc: Frees all memory and information for the specified instance. After the fuzzy instance is closed, the handle given in the hFuzzy parameter is no longer valid.
fuzzyclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hFuzzy: The fuzzy instance handle (and integer greater than 0).

fuzzygetcodevalue.name: FuzzyGetCodeValue
fuzzygetcodevalue.doc: Gets a value for the specified input of the specified instance.
fuzzygetcodevalue.returns: The code value if the function was successful, otherwise -1. Use IsError() to find the error number if the function does not succeed.

paramDocs.hFuzzy: The fuzzy instance handle (and integer greater than 0).
paramDocs.iIOIndex: Specifies the variable to receive the value. The I/O-Indices start with 0 and increment by 1 for each variable. To find the correct index for a specific variable, the variables need to be sorted in alpha-numerical order, first the inputs and then the outputs.
paramDocs.NoHitFlag: Variable to receive the new value of the No-hit-flag. The No- hit-flag is TRUE if no rule was active for the variable specified by iIOIndex, otherwise it is FALSE. Must be an Integer type variable - it cannot be a constant or PLC variable tag.

fuzzygetshellvalue.name: FuzzyGetShellValue
fuzzygetshellvalue.doc: Gets a value for the specified input of the specified instance. The variables in the instance needs to have the data type REAL (floating point values).
fuzzygetshellvalue.returns: The shell value if the function was successful. Use IsError to find the error number if the function does not succeed.

paramDocs.hFuzzy: The fuzzy instance handle (and integer greater than 0).
paramDocs.iIOIndex: Specifies the variable to receive the value. The I/O-Indices start with 0 and increment by 1 for each variable. To find the correct index for a specific variable, the variables need to be sorted in alpha-numerical order, first the inputs and then the outputs.
paramDocs.NoHitFlag: Variable to receive the new value of the No-hit-flag. The No- hit-flag is TRUE if no rule was active for the variable specified by iIOIndex, otherwise it is FALSE. Must be an Integer type variable - it cannot be a constant or PLC variable tag.

fuzzyopen.name: FuzzyOpen
fuzzyopen.doc: This function loads a *.FTR file, allocates memory and creates a handle for this fuzzy instance. To use the FuzzyTech functions you need to be a registered user of one or more of the following fuzzyTech products: fuzzyTECH Online Edition, fuzzyTECH Precompiler Edition, or fuzzyTECH for Business PlusC. And you need to only use fuzzyTECH to generate the *.FTR file for FTRUN.
fuzzyopen.returns: The handle to the fuzzy instance, or -1 if the function cannot complete the operation. Use IsError to find the error number.

paramDocs.sFile: Specifies the filename of the .FTR file to load.

fuzzysetcodevalue.name: FuzzySetCodeValue
fuzzysetcodevalue.doc: Sets a value for the specified input of the specified instance.
fuzzysetcodevalue.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hFuzzy: The fuzzy instance handle (and integer greater than 0).
paramDocs.iIOIndex: Specifies the variable to receive the value. The I/O-Indices start with 0 and increment by 1 for each variable. To find the correct index for a specific variable, the variables need to be sorted in alpha-numerical order, first the inputs and then the outputs.
paramDocs.iCodeValue: The value to be copied to the variable specified by iIOIndex.

fuzzysetshellvalue.name: FuzzySetShellValue
fuzzysetshellvalue.doc: Sets a value for the specified input of the specified instance.
fuzzysetshellvalue.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hFuzzy: The fuzzy instance handle (and integer greater than 0).
paramDocs.iIOIndex: Specifies the variable to receive the value. The I/O-Indices start with 0 and increment by 1 for each variable. To find the correct index for a specific variable, the variables need to be sorted in alpha-numerical order, first the inputs and then the outputs.
paramDocs.rShellValue: The value to be copied to the variable specified by iIOIndex.

fuzzytrace.name: FuzzyTrace
fuzzytrace.doc: Controls the trace process (starting and stopping) of the specified instance.
fuzzytrace.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hFuzzy: The fuzzy instance handle (and integer greater than 0).
paramDocs.TraceOn: Specifies whether to start or to stop a trace process for the Fuzzy instance specified by hFuzzy. If this parameter is TRUE (1), the trace process is started. If this parameter is FALSE (0), the trace process is stopped.

getarea.name: GetArea
getarea.returns: The login area groups as an integer that represents a group handle. If this group is modified, the actual login areas do not change.

getbluevalue.name: GetBlueValue
getbluevalue.doc: Returns the blue component of a packed RGB color.
getbluevalue.returns: The red value (0-255) - if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

getenv.name: GetEnv
getenv.returns: The DOS environment variable (as a string).The return value returns up to 255 characters and is truncated if exceeds.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the environment variable. The length of the name should not exceed 255 characters.

getevent.name: GetEvent
getevent.doc: Gets the function handle of the existing callback event handler. You can use this function handle in the ChainEvent() function to chain call the existing event function, or in the SetEvent() function to restore the event handler.
getevent.returns: The function handle of the existing callback event handler, or -1 if there are no event handlers.

paramDocs.nType: The type of event:

getgreenvalue.name: GetGreenValue
getgreenvalue.doc: Returns the green component of a packed RGB color.
getgreenvalue.returns: The red value (0-255) - if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

getlanguage.name: GetLanguage
getlanguage.doc: Gets the language currently used on the display client.
getlanguage.returns: The specified information describing the language that is currently in use.

paramDocs.iType: The type of language information to be returned:

getlogging.name: GetLogging
getlogging.doc: Gets the current value for logging parameters.
getlogging.returns: If the function succeeds, the value is returned as a string. An empty string is returned if an error occurs. To get extended error information, call IsError().

paramDocs.sName: The system parameter name.

getpriv.name: GetPriv
getpriv.doc: Checks if the current user has a privilege for a specified area. With this function, you can write your own Cicode functions to control user access to the system.
getpriv.returns: Returns 1 if the user has the specified privilege in the area, or 0 (zero) if the user does not have the privilege.

getredvalue.name: GetRedValue
getredvalue.doc: Returns the red component of a packed RGB color.
getredvalue.returns: The red value (0-255) - if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

getwintitle.name: GetWinTitle
getwintitle.doc: Returns the name of the active window as a string.
getwintitle.returns: The title of the active window as a string if successful; otherwise, an error is returned.

grpclose.name: GrpClose
grpclose.doc: Closes a group. The group is destroyed and the group handle becomes invalid. You should close a group when it is not in use, to release the associated memory. Plant SCADA closes all groups on shutdown.
grpclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.

grpdelete.name: GrpDelete
grpdelete.doc: Deletes a single element or all elements from a group. You can also delete another group from within the group.
grpdelete.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.
paramDocs.Value: The element to delete from the group, from 0 to 16375.

grpfirst.name: GrpFirst
grpfirst.doc: Gets the value of the first element in a group. The first element in the group is the element with the lowest value. You can follow this function with a GrpNext() call, to get the value of all the elements in a group.
grpfirst.returns: The value of the first element in a group or -1 if the group is empty.

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.

grpin.name: GrpIn
grpin.doc: Determines if an element is in a group.
grpin.returns: 1 if the element is in the group, otherwise 0 is returned.

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.
paramDocs.Value: The element to locate, from 0 to 16375.

grpinsert.name: GrpInsert
grpinsert.doc: Adds an element (or another group) to a group.
grpinsert.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.
paramDocs.Value: The element to add to the group, from 0 to 16375.

grpmath.name: GrpMath
grpmath.doc: Performs mathematical operations on two groups, and stores the result in another group. You can add the two groups, subtract one from the other, or perform Boolean AND, NOT, and XOR operations on the two groups.
grpmath.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hResult: The group number where the result is placed.
paramDocs.hOne: Number of first group used in the mathematical operation.
paramDocs.hTwo: Number of the second group used in the mathematical operation.
paramDocs.nType: Type of mathematical operation:

grpname.name: GrpName
grpname.doc: Gets the name of a group from a group handle.
grpname.returns: The name of the group (as a string).

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.

grpnext.name: GrpNext
grpnext.doc: Gets the value of the next element in a group. You can get the value of all the elements in a group. Call the GrpFirst() function to get the value of the first element, and then call this function in a loop.
grpnext.returns: The value of the next element in a group, or -1 if the end of the group has been found.

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.
paramDocs.Value: The value returned from GrpFirst() or the latest GrpNext() call.

grpopen.name: GrpOpen
grpopen.doc: Creates a group and returns a group handle, or gets the group handle of an existing group. After you open a group, you can use the group number in functions that use groups, for example, SetArea() and AlarmSetInfo(). You can open a group that is specified in the Groups database. You can also create groups at runtime.
grpopen.returns: The group handle , or -1 if the group cannot be created or opened. The group handle identifies the table where data on the associated group is stored.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the group to open.

grptostr.name: GrpToStr
grptostr.doc: Converts a group into a string of values separated by " , " and " .. ". You can then display the group on the screen or in a report.

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.

halt.name: Halt
halt.doc: Stops the execution of the current Cicode task and returns to Plant SCADA. This function does not affect any other Cicode tasks that are running.
halt.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

hextostr.name: HexToStr
hextostr.doc: Converts a number into a hexadecimal string. The string is the width specified (padded with zeros).
hextostr.returns: A string containing the converted number.

paramDocs.Width: The width of the string (0 to 8).

highbyte.name: HighByte
highbyte.doc: Gets the high-order byte of a two-byte integer.

highword.name: HighWord
highword.doc: Gets the high-order word of a four-byte integer.
highword.returns: The high-order word (that is | X | X | - | - |)

htmlhelp.name: HtmlHelp
htmlhelp.doc: Invokes the Microsoft HTML Help application (hh.exe) to display a specific topic from an HTML help file (.chm).
htmlhelp.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sHelpFile: The help file to display. For example, "C:\Program Files (x86)\AVEVA Plant SCADA\Bin\ProcessAnalyst.chm".
paramDocs.sData: Optional data, depending on the value of nCommand.

hwalarmque.name: HwAlarmQue
hwalarmque.doc: Returns the handle of the hardware alarm queue. The Alarms Server writes hardware alarm information into this queue as each hardware alarm occurs. To read events from this queue, use the QueRead or QuePeek functions. The data written into the queue is the hardware alarm format, and is stored in the Str field.
hwalarmque.returns: The handle of the hardware alarm queue, or -1 if the queue cannot be opened.

ifdefanaalm.name: IFDEFAnaAlm
ifdefanaalm.doc: Based on the IFDEF macro, IFDEFAnaAlm allows you to define two possible outcomes based on whether or not a specified analog alarm tag exists within a project at the time of compiling. The macro can be implemented anywhere a simple expression is used, including fields within relevant Plant SCADA dialogs.
ifdefanaalm.returns: If the analog alarm tag specified in the first argument exists, the value defined by the second argument is returned. This could be a variable, expression, or constant, or the current tag value if the argument has been left blank. If the specified alarm does not exist, the variable, expression, or constant defined by the third argument is returned.

ifdefdigalm.name: IFDEFDigAlm
ifdefdigalm.doc: Based on the IFDEF macro, IFDEFDigAlm allows you to define two possible outcomes based on whether or not a specified digital alarm tag exists within a project at the time of compiling. The macro can be implemented anywhere a simple expression is used, including fields within relevant Plant SCADA dialogs.
ifdefdigalm.returns: If the digital alarm tag specified in the first argument exists, the value defined by the second argument is returned. This could be a variable, expression, or constant, or the current tag value if the argument has been left blank. If the specified alarm does not exist, the variable, expression, or constant defined by the third argument is returned.

ifdefhresalm.name: IFDEFHresAlm
ifdefhresalm.doc: Based on the IFDEF macro, IFDEFHresAlm allows you to define two possible outcomes based on whether or not a specified time stamped alarm tag exists within a project at the time of compiling. The macro can be implemented anywhere a simple expression is used, including fields within relevant Plant SCADA dialogs.
ifdefhresalm.returns: If the time stamped alarm tag specified in the first argument exists, the value defined by the second argument is returned. This could be a variable, expression, or constant, or the current tag value if the argument has been left blank. If the specified alarm does not exist, the variable, expression, or constant defined by the third argument is returned.

infoform.name: InfoForm
infoform.doc: Displays graphics object information for the object under the mouse pointer. If there is no object directly under the mouse pointer, it displays information for the nearest object. Each tag associated with the object is displayed, along with its raw and engineering values and a button that displays the details from the Variable Tags settings. The function also displays the Cicode expression, with any result that the expression has generated.
infoform.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Mode: For security purposes, the Write button on the information form displayed by this function can be disabled.

infoforman.name: InfoFormAn
infoforman.doc: Displays graphics object information for a specified AN. This function displays each tag associated with the object, along with its raw and engineering values and a button that displays the details from the Variable Tags form. The function also displays the Cicode expression, with any result that the expression has generated.
infoforman.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the graphics object for which information is displayed.
paramDocs.Mode: For security purposes, the Write button on the information form displayed by this function can be disabled.

input.name: Input
input.doc: Displays a dialog box in which an operator can input a single value. The dialog box has a title, a prompt, and a single edit field. For multiple inputs, use the Form Functions.
input.returns: The edit field entry (as a string). If the user presses the Cancel button , an empty string is returned and the IsError() function returns the error code 299.

paramDocs.Title: The title of the input box.
paramDocs.Default: The default text that the operator can edit or replace.

inttoreal.name: IntToReal
inttoreal.doc: Converts an integer into a real (floating point) number.

inttostr.name: IntToStr
inttostr.doc: Converts a number into a string.
inttostr.returns: A string containing the converted number.

iodevicecontrol.name: IODeviceControl
iodevicecontrol.doc: Provides control of individual I/O devices. You might need to call this function several times. If you use incompatible values for the various options of this function, you might get unpredictable results.
iodevicecontrol.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.IODevice: The number or name of the I/O device. If you call this function from an I/O server, you can use the I/O device name. If you call this function from a client, you may use either the I/O device number or name. To specify all I/O devices, use "*" (asterisk) or -1.
paramDocs.nType: The type of control action:
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the I/O Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the I/O server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.ServerName: Specifies the name of the the I/O Server. This parameter is only required if you are running more than one I/O server process from the same cluster on the same computer and need to instruct the system which process to redirect to. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

iodeviceinfo.name: IODeviceInfo
iodeviceinfo.doc: Gets information about a specified I/O device.
iodeviceinfo.returns: The type of information (as a string).

paramDocs.IODevice: The I/O device number, or the I/O device name enclosed in double quotes.
paramDocs.nType: The type of information:
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the I/O Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the I/O server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.ServerName: Specifies the name of the I/O Server. This parameter is only required if you are running more than one I/O server process from the same cluster on the same computer and need to instruct the system which process to redirect to. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

iodevicestats.name: IODeviceStats
iodevicestats.doc: Gets statistical information for all I/O devices, and displays the information in a dialog box.
iodevicestats.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

iserror.name: IsError
iserror.doc: Gets the current error value. The error value is set when any error is detected, and is reset after this function is called. You can call this function if user error-checking is enabled or disabled.
iserror.returns: The current error value. The current error is reset to 0 after this function is called.

kercmd.name: KerCmd
kercmd.doc: Executes a command in a Kernel window.
kercmd.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Window: The name of the Kernel window.
paramDocs.sCommand: The command to execute in the Kernel window.

kernelqueuelength.name: KernelQueueLength
kernelqueuelength.doc: Obtains the number of records in a queue.
kernelqueuelength.returns: This function returns the Length value of the page queue command.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the queue, which can be enumerated by the page queue kernel command.

kerneltableinfo.name: KernelTableInfo
kerneltableinfo.doc: Provides a consistent method of accessing items within Kernel Table.
kerneltableinfo.returns: Returns the content of a field of the given table in the format of a Cicode STRING.

paramDocs.sTable: The name of the table. The following tables are supported:
paramDocs.sRecord: The key to a column in the table depending on the sTable parameter.
paramDocs.sField: The key to a column in the table depending on the sTable parameter.

kerneltableitemcount.name: KernelTableItemCount
kerneltableitemcount.doc: Obtains the number of rows in a Kernel Table.
kerneltableitemcount.returns: Returns the number of active records in the table (not the length value displayed by the page table kernel command).

paramDocs.sName: The name of the table that can be enumerated by the page table kernel command.

keyallowcursor.name: KeyAllowCursor
keyallowcursor.doc: Allows (or disallows) the command cursor to move to the specified AN or to all ANs. The command cursor normally moves only to ANs that have commands defined.
keyallowcursor.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the command cursor can move. If 0, all ANs are implied.

keybs.name: KeyBs
keybs.doc: Removes the last key from the key command line. If the key command line is empty, this function will not perform any action.
keybs.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

keydown.name: KeyDown
keydown.doc: Moves the command cursor down the page to the closest AN. If an AN-Down cursor override is specified (in the Page Keyboard database) for the graphics page, the command cursor moves to that AN instead.
keydown.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

keyget.name: KeyGet
keyget.doc: Gets the last key code from the key command line. The key is removed from the command line. Use this function to process the operator key commands directly. You should call this function from the keyboard event function.
keyget.returns: The last key code from the key command line. If the key command line is empty, 0 (zero) is returned.

keygetcursor.name: KeyGetCursor
keygetcursor.doc: Gets the AN at the position of the command cursor.
keygetcursor.returns: The AN at the position of the command cursor. If no cursor is visible, -1 is returned.

keyleft.name: KeyLeft
keyleft.doc: Moves the command cursor left (across the page) to the closest AN. If an AN-Left cursor override is specified (in the Page Keyboard database) for the graphics page, the command cursor moves to that AN instead.
keyleft.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

keymove.name: KeyMove
keymove.doc: Moves the command cursor in a specified direction to the closest AN. If an AN cursor override is specified, the command cursor moves to that AN directly. This function is equivalent to the KeyUp(), KeyDown(), KeyLeft(), and KeyRight() functions.
keymove.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

keypeek.name: KeyPeek
keypeek.doc: Gets the ascii key code from the key command line (at a specified offset), without removing the key from the key command line. An offset of 0 returns the key code from the last position in the key command line.

paramDocs.Offset: The offset from the end of the key command line

keyput.name: KeyPut
keyput.doc: Puts an ASCII key code or Keyboard key code into the last position of the key command line. If this key completes any command, that command will execute.
keyput.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.KeyCode: The key code to put into the key command line.

keyputstr.name: KeyPutStr
keyputstr.doc: Puts a string at the end of the key command line. The string can contain either key names or data characters. If this string completes any command, that command will execute.
keyputstr.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.String: The string to put into the key command line.

keyreplay.name: KeyReplay
keyreplay.doc: Replays the last key sequence (except for the last key, which would execute the command). This function is useful when a command is to be repeated. To call this function from the keyboard, use a Hot Key "*" (asterisk) command, otherwise the KeyReplay() function itself is replayed.
keyreplay.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Sub: Number of characters to subtract before replay. Default value is 1.

keyreplayall.name: KeyReplayAll
keyreplayall.doc: Replays the last key sequence and executes the command. To call this function from the keyboard, use a Hot Key " * " (asterisk) command, otherwise the KeyReplayAll() function itself is replayed.
keyreplayall.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

keyright.name: KeyRight
keyright.doc: Moves the command cursor right (across the page) to the closest AN. If an AN-Right cursor override is specified (in the Page Keyboard database) for the graphics page, the command cursor moves to that AN instead.
keyright.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

keysetcursor.name: KeySetCursor
keysetcursor.doc: Displays the command cursor at a specified AN. A keyboard command needs to exist, or you need to first call the KeyAllowCursor() function (at the AN) to allow the cursor to move to the AN. If the AN does not exist, or if a command does not exist at that AN, or if KeyAllowCursor() has not been called, the command cursor does not move.
keysetcursor.returns: If the AN does not exist, or if a command does not exist at that AN, or if KeyAllowCursor() has not been called, the return value is 1. Otherwise, the function will return 0.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the command cursor will be displayed.

keysetseq.name: KeySetSeq
keysetseq.doc: Adds a keyboard sequence to the current page at runtime. The key sequence is only added to the current window. When the page is closed, the keyboard sequence is deleted.
keysetseq.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the keyboard sequence will apply. If you set AN to 0 (zero), the keyboard sequence will apply to all ANs on the page.
paramDocs.Fn: The function to call when the keyboard sequence matches. This function needs to be a callback function.

keyup.name: KeyUp
keyup.doc: Moves the command cursor up the page to the closest AN. If an AN-Up cursor override is specified (in the Page Keyboard database) for the graphics page, the command cursor moves to that AN.
keyup.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

languagefiletranslate.name: LanguageFileTranslate
languagefiletranslate.doc: Translates an ASCII file into a local language. Use this function to translate RTF reports for viewing on client screens.

paramDocs.sSourceFile: The name of the ASCII file containing multi-language text, which will be copied and translated. You should specify the full path or use path substitution. The path and name should be contained within quotation marks.
paramDocs.sDestFile: The name of the destination file which will be created/ replaced with the local/translated version of the source file. You should specify the full path or use path substitution. The path and name should be contained within quotation marks.

leavecriticalsection.name: LeaveCriticalSection
leavecriticalsection.doc: Relinquishes the current thread's ownership of a critical section (shared critical resource). Once ownership is relinquished, access to the critical section is available to the next thread that requests it (using the EnterCriticalSection() function). If a thread has been waiting for access, it will be granted at this point.
leavecriticalsection.returns: This function does not return a value.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the critical section. The name needs to be entered in quotation marks.

libalarmfilterform.name: LibAlarmFilterForm
libalarmfilterform.doc: Displays a generic alarm filter pop-up for specifying filtering criteria for either an alarm list or a named filter. This function uses the AlarmFilterEdit family of Cicode functions to set the filter.
libalarmfilterform.returns: 1 if filter has been applied, 0 if filter has been cleared, or -1 if no change is made.

paramDocs.sFilterSrc: The source where the filter will be applied to. It can either be the Animation Number (AN) of an alarm list or the name of a filter created via the AlarmFilterOpen() Cicode function. If it is not specified, it is defaulted to -1 which refers to all alarm lists on the current page. If the FilterSrc cannot be opened, it will prompt the user to create the filter source.
paramDocs.sTitle: The title for the filter form. If it is not specified or left blank, the title is determined by the form type:
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the form:
paramDocs.sAppliedCallbackFn: The callback function statement to be called when the criteria (rules) specified in the form is applied either via the OK or Apply buttons. Like other callback functions available to other library controls genie. The callback function supports keyword substitutions during callback:

ln.name: Ln
ln.doc: Calculates the natural (base e) logarithm of a number.
ln.returns: The natural (base e) logarithm of Number.

log.name: Log
log.doc: Calculates the base 10 logarithm of a number.

login.name: Login
login.doc: Not available when logged in as Windows user.

paramDocs.sUserName: The user's name, as defined in the Users database.
paramDocs.sPassword: The user's password, as defined in the Users database.
paramDocs.bSync: Optionally specifies whether the function operates in blocking or non-blocking mode. If set to 1 blocks caller until login is complete. If set to 0 (default) does not block caller.
paramDocs.sLanguage: The specified language needs to be one of the languages defined in the Languages view in Plant SCADA Studio's Setup activity. If the specified language is undefined, the default language is used by the login user, and a message "Undefined language" is shown in the prompt line.

loginform.name: LoginForm
loginform.doc: Displays a form in which a user can log in to the Plant SCADA system by entering their name and password and local language. If the login is correct, the user is logged into the Plant SCADA system with the area(s) and privilege(s) assigned to them in the Users database.
loginform.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sUserName: Optionally, the user's name, as defined in the Users database.
paramDocs.sPassword: Optionally, the user's password, as defined in the Users database.
paramDocs.sLanguage: The specified language must be one of the languages defined in the Languages view in Plant SCADA Studio's Setup activity. If the specified language is undefined, the default language is used by the login user, and a message "Undefined language" is shown in the prompt line.

logout.name: Logout
logout.doc: Logs the current user out of the Plant SCADA system. Plant SCADA continues to run, but with access to area 0 (zero) and privilege 0 (zero) only. If the current page requires access for a specified area (as defined by the page's area property), the system returns to the home page as specified by the parameter [Page]HomePage, and if unsuccessful that returns to the startup page. When multiple pages are currently displayed, this occurs for each open window.
logout.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

logoutidle.name: LogoutIdle
logoutidle.doc: Sets an idle time for logging out the current user. If the current user does not execute a command within the specified idle time, a prompt is displayed. If the prompt is ignored, then the user is logged out. For every user to have the same idle time, you would call this function at startup. Otherwise, you can call the function from the Users database to specify an idle time for each user. This function will not log out an automatically logged on user.

paramDocs.Idle: The number of minutes the user needs to be idle before logout will occur. Set Idle to -1 to disable the current logout timeout.

lowbyte.name: LowByte
lowbyte.doc: Gets the low-order byte of a two-byte integer.

lowword.name: LowWord
lowword.doc: Gets the low-order word of a four-byte integer.
lowword.returns: The low-order word (that is | - | - | X | X |)

mailerror.name: MailError
mailerror.doc: Gets the last mail error code. The error code is extracted from the MAPI mail system and explains what caused the MAPI error.
mailerror.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned. Refer also to MAPI errors.

maillogoff.name: MailLogoff
maillogoff.doc: Logs off from the mail system. You should log off the mail system when all mail operations are complete. Plant SCADA automatically logs off the mail system on shutdown.
maillogoff.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

maillogon.name: MailLogon
maillogon.doc: Logs on to the mail system. You need to call this function before any other mail function.
maillogon.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the mail user. This name is the user's mail box name (the unique shorthand name, not the full user's name).
paramDocs.sPassword: The password of the mail user.

mailread.name: MailRead
mailread.doc: Reads a standard mail message. The mail message can contain text, an attached file, or both.
mailread.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the mail user who sent the message. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.sSubject: The subject text of the mail message. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.sNote: The note section of the message. If the message is longer than 255 characters, Plant SCADA will save the message in a file and return the file name in sNote. Use the file functions to read the message. The name of the file will be in the form CTxxxxx where x is a unique number. You need to delete the file after you have finished with the mail message. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.sFileName: The name of any attached file. If there is no attached file in the message, specify sFileName as an empty string "". Must be a String type variable.

mailsend.name: MailSend
mailsend.doc: Sends a standard mail message. The mail message can contain text, an attached file, or both.
mailsend.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the mail user who will receive the message. This name is the user's full name (not their mailbox name).
paramDocs.sSubject: The subject text of the mail message (a short description of what the message is about).
paramDocs.sNote: The note section of the message (the main section of the message text). You can enter up to 255 characters, or a file name for longer messages. If you enter a file name, set iMode to 1.
paramDocs.sFileName: The name of any attached file. If there is no attached file in the message, set sFileName to an empty string "".

makecitectcolour.name: MakeCitectColour
makecitectcolour.doc: Creates a color from red, green and blue component parts.
makecitectcolour.returns: An integer that is an encoded representation of the color created.

paramDocs.nRed: The color value for red, from 0-255
paramDocs.nGreen: The color value for green, from 0-255
paramDocs.nBlue: The color value for blue, from 0-255

makecolour.name: MakeColour
makecolour.doc: Creates a color from red, green and blue component parts.
makecolour.returns: An integer that is an encoded representation of the color created.

paramDocs.nRed: The color value for red, from 0-255
paramDocs.nGreen: The color value for green, from 0-255
paramDocs.nBlue: The color value for blue, from 0-255

mapclear.name: MapClear
mapclear.doc: Clears all entries in a map and returns the error status.
mapclear.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sMapName: Name of the map to be cleared.

mapclose.name: MapClose
mapclose.doc: Closes a map and returns the error status.
mapclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sMapName: Name of the map to be closed.

mapexists.name: MapExists
mapexists.doc: Checks for the existence of the map.
mapexists.returns: TRUE if the map exists, or FALSE if not.

mapkeycount.name: MapKeyCount
mapkeycount.doc: Use this function to retrieve the number of keys in a map.
mapkeycount.returns: The number of keys in the map, or a value less than 0 if an error is encountered.

mapkeydelete.name: MapKeyDelete
mapkeydelete.doc: Use this function to delete a key and value from a map.
mapkeydelete.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sKeyName: Name of key and value to be deleted.

mapkeyexists.name: MapKeyExists
mapkeyexists.doc: Use this function to check if a key exists in a map.
mapkeyexists.returns: TRUE if the map exists, or FALSE if not.

paramDocs.sMapName: Name of map to get the value from.
paramDocs.sKeyName: Name of the key to get the value from.

mapkeyfirst.name: MapKeyFirst
mapkeyfirst.doc: Use this function to retrieve the first key in a map so that all the keys in a map can be discovered.
mapkeyfirst.returns: The first key in the map, if there are no keys in the map and empty string is returned.

paramDocs.sMapName: Name of map to get the value from.

mapkeynext.name: MapKeyNext
mapkeynext.doc: Use this function to retrieve the next key after the supplied key in a map so that all the keys in a map can be discovered
mapkeynext.returns: The next key if successful or, an empty string if no next key exists.

paramDocs.sMapName: Name of map to retrieve the value from.
paramDocs.sKeyName: Name of the key to retrieve the value for.

mapopen.name: MapOpen
mapopen.doc: Use this function to create a new map or to open an existing map.
mapopen.returns: Name of map if successful, otherwise an empty string will be returned.

paramDocs.sMapName: Name of the map to create or open. The default name is an empty string. If name is empty, it will generate an available random name.
paramDocs.nOpenMode: Indicates the open or create mode of the map. Modes include:
paramDocs.sCloseCallback: The function to call when this instance is closed.

mapvalueget.name: MapValueGet
mapvalueget.doc: Use this function to retrieve the value from a key in a map.
mapvalueget.returns: Value returned is a VARIANT that also contains QUALITY and TIMESTAMP components, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sKeyName: Name of the key to retrieve the value from.

mapvalueset.name: MapValueSet
mapvalueset.doc: Use this function to set a value of a map key.
mapvalueset.returns: If the value is set correctly, the result is "No Error" (0), otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sMapName: Name of the map to create or open.
paramDocs.sKeyName: Name of the key to set.
paramDocs.Value: Name of the value to be set

mapvaluesetquality.name: MapValueSetQuality
mapvaluesetquality.doc: Use this function to set the quality of a property in a map.
mapvaluesetquality.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sKeyName: Name of the key to override the quality for
paramDocs.Quality: Quality to override in an existing value. There is no default value. The QUALITY type is created using the QualityCreate function.

max.name: Max
max.doc: Gets the higher of two numbers.
max.returns: The higher of numbers Number1 and Number2.

menugetchild.name: MenuGetChild
menugetchild.doc: Returns the handle to the child node with the specified name.
menugetchild.returns: The handle of the child node with the requested name, or -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.hParent: Handle to the parent node in the menu tree.
paramDocs.sName: The name of the child Menu node requested.

menugetfirstchild.name: MenuGetFirstChild
menugetfirstchild.doc: Returns the handle to the first child of a menu node.
menugetfirstchild.returns: The handle to the first child node of a menu node, or -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.hNode: The handle to the parent node in the menu tree.

menugetgenericnode.name: MenuGetGenericNode
menugetgenericnode.doc: Returns the handle to the base node of the menu tree for the generic pages. Its child nodes represent the menu items that do not have a page specified in the menu configuration database.
menugetgenericnode.returns: The handle to the base node of the menu tree, or -1 if it cannot find the node.

paramDocs.bCreate: Determines if the node should be created if it does not exist. Defaults to 0, do not create.

menugetnextchild.name: MenuGetNextChild
menugetnextchild.doc: Returns the next node that shares the same parent.
menugetnextchild.returns: The handle to next node that shares the same parent, or -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.hChild: Handle to the current node in the menu tree

menugetnodebypath.name: MenuGetNodeByPath
menugetnodebypath.doc: Returns a menu handle corresponding to a menu item expressed as a string path in the format <level>.<level>.<level>.<level>.

menugetpagenode.name: MenuGetPageNode
menugetpagenode.doc: Returns the handle to the menu tree for a specified page. Its child nodes represent the menu items that have the particular page specified in the menu configuration database.
menugetpagenode.returns: The handle of the menu tree, or -1 if no menu tree exists for a specified page.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the page for which to return the menu tree handle.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode to use for generating the menu handle for the page:

menugetparent.name: MenuGetParent
menugetparent.doc: Returns the parent node of the menu item.
menugetparent.returns: The handle to parent menu node of the given menu item, or -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle to the current node in the menu tree.

menugetprevchild.name: MenuGetPrevChild
menugetprevchild.doc: Returns the previous node that shares the same parent.
menugetprevchild.returns: The handle to previous node that shares the same parent, or -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.hChild: Handle to the current node in the menu tree.

menugetwindownode.name: MenuGetWindowNode
menugetwindownode.doc: Returns the handle to the root node for a given window. This menu node is dynamically created for each page instance. Its child nodes represent the menu items for the generic pages merged with the ones specific to this page.
menugetwindownode.returns: The handle to the root node of a given window, or -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.hWin: The window number of the desired window. You can call WinNumber() to get the window number of the page that calls this Cicode function.

menunodeaddchild.name: MenuNodeAddChild
menunodeaddchild.doc: Dynamically add a new item to the menu at runtime. Be reminded that the changes are for the current session only and will not be persisted to the _Pagemen.RDB file.
menunodeaddchild.returns: The handle of the new node, or -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.hParent: Handle of the parent node to add the new menu item under.
paramDocs.sName: The string label of the new menu item.
paramDocs.sCommandName: Specifies the name of the Cicode function to run.
paramDocs.sCommandArgs: Specifies the parameters of the Cicode function to run.
paramDocs.sSymbol: The symbol to be associated with the menu item.
paramDocs.iOrder: The relative position in the menu for new item.

menunodegetcurr.name: MenuNodeGetCurr
menunodegetcurr.doc: Each menu node can have a Command associated with it when a menu is configured. This function allows you to get the handle of the menu node when this associated command is called.
menunodegetcurr.returns: The handle of the menu node.

menunodegetdepth.name: MenuNodeGetDepth
menunodegetdepth.doc: Returns the depth of a specified menu node within a menu hierarchy.
menunodegetdepth.returns: The depth of the specified node within the menu hierarchy. For example, 0 indicates it is on the root node of the menu, 1 indicates one level below the root node, and so on.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the menu node.

menunodegetexpanded.name: MenuNodeGetExpanded
menunodegetexpanded.doc: Gets the expansion state value of the specified menu node in number. The expansion state value is user defined can be any integer value. The value is set by MenuNodeSetExpanded function and the initial value is zero(0).
menunodegetexpanded.returns: The expansion state value to set for the Menu node or -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle to the current node in the menu tree.

menunodegetproperty.name: MenuNodeGetProperty
menunodegetproperty.doc: Return the item value of the specified menu node.
menunodegetproperty.returns: The value for the specified menu node field.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle to the current node in the menu tree.
paramDocs.iField: Field for which you want the value:

menunodegettargetpage.name: MenuNodeGetTargetPage
menunodegettargetpage.doc: Returns the target page for a specified menu node.
menunodegettargetpage.returns: The name of the target page for the specified node.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the menu node. If not specified, the handle of the menu node will be determined through it's association with the command that is currently being called. Each menu node can have a Command associated with it when a menu is configured.

menunodehascommand.name: MenuNodeHasCommand
menunodehascommand.doc: Checks whether the menu node has a valid Cicode command associated with it.
menunodehascommand.returns: 1 if the menu node has a valid Cicode command, 0 if the menu node has no Cicode command.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of node to check.

menunodeisdisabled.name: MenuNodeIsDisabled
menunodeisdisabled.doc: Checks whether the menu node is disabled by evaluating its DisabledWhen Cicode expression.
menunodeisdisabled.returns: 1 if menu node DisabledWhen expression evaluates to true, 0 if menu node DisabledWhen expression evaluates to false.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of node to check.

menunodeishidden.name: MenuNodeIsHidden
menunodeishidden.doc: Checks whether the menu node is hidden by evaluating its HiddenWhen Cicode expression.
menunodeishidden.returns: 1 if menu node HiddenWhen expression evaluates to true, 0 if menu node HiddenWhen expression evaluates to false.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of node to check.

menunoderemove.name: MenuNodeRemove
menunoderemove.doc: Remove the menu node from the menu tree.
menunoderemove.returns: Zero (0) if node successfully removed. -1 if hNode is an invalid menu handle.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of node to remove.

menunoderuncommand.name: MenuNodeRunCommand
menunoderuncommand.doc: Run the associated command for a menu node.
menunoderuncommand.returns: No error(0) on success. Bad handle specified (269) if hNode does not refer to a valid node.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of node to run command.

menunodesetdisabledwhen.name: MenuNodeSetDisabledWhen
menunodesetdisabledwhen.doc: Set the DisabledWhen expression for a newly added node. Be aware this function only works for menu nodes added with MenuNodeAddChild(). The DisabledWhen expression may only be set once for a node.
menunodesetdisabledwhen.returns: No Error(0) on success, Bad handle specified (269) if hNode does not refer to a valid node, Invalid argument passed (274) if DisabledWhen Cicode has already been set or is not a valid expression.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of node to run command
paramDocs.sDisabledWhenName: Cicode function for DisabledWhen expression. The function needs to return an INT.
paramDocs.sDisabledWhenArgs: Cicode parameters for DisabledWhen expression. Only supports static arguments.
paramDocs.iDisabledStyle: Disabled Style. Allows different display styles for a disabled menu item.

menunodesetexpanded.name: MenuNodeSetExpanded
menunodesetexpanded.doc: Set the expansion state value of the specified menu node in number. The expansion state value is defined by project designer and can be any integer value. The initial value is zero(0). It is not recommended to use -1 for the expansion state value though because this number indicates an error for MenuNodeGetExpanded function.
menunodesetexpanded.returns: Zero (0) if successful. -1 if hNode is invalid or an error code for any other error.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle to the current node in the menu tree.
paramDocs.iValue: The expansion state value to set for the Menu node.

menunodesethiddenwhen.name: MenuNodeSetHiddenWhen
menunodesethiddenwhen.doc: Set the HiddenWhen expression for a newly added node. Be aware this function only works for menu nodes added with MenuNodeAddChild(). The HiddenWhen expression may only be set once for a node.
menunodesethiddenwhen.returns: No Error (0) on success, Bad handle specified (269) if hNode does not refer to a valid node, or Invalid argument passed (274) if HiddenWhen Cicode has already been set or is not a valid expression.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle of node to run command.
paramDocs.sHiddenWhenName: Cicode function for HiddenWhen expression. The function needs to return an INT.
paramDocs.sHiddenWhenArgs: Cicode parameters for HiddenWhen expression. Only supports static arguments.

menunodesetproperty.name: MenuNodeSetProperty
menunodesetproperty.doc: Set the item value of the specified menu node.
menunodesetproperty.returns: Zero (0) if successful. -1 if hNode or iField is invalid. An error code for others.

paramDocs.hNode: Handle to the current node in the menu tree.
paramDocs.iField: Field for which you want to set the value:
paramDocs.sValue: The item value to set for the Menu node.

menureload.name: MenuReload
menureload.doc: Reload base Menu Configuration from the compiled database.

message.name: Message
message.doc: Displays a message box on the screen and waits for the user to select the OK or Cancel button.
message.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned. If the user presses the Cancel button the function returns an error code of 299.

paramDocs.Title: The title of the message box. The maximum length is 254 chars.
paramDocs.Prompt: The prompt displayed in the message box.
paramDocs.Mode: The mode of the message box:

min.name: Min
min.doc: Returns the lower of two numbers.
min.returns: The lower of numbers Number1 and Number2.

msgbrdcst.name: MsgBrdcst
msgbrdcst.doc: Broadcasts a message to all the clients of a server. You should call this function only on a Plant SCADA server. The message is only received by clients that have a current message session (opened with the MsgOpen() function).
msgbrdcst.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the Plant SCADA server.
paramDocs.nType: The message number.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to which the server being communicated with belongs. This is optional if you have one cluster.

msgclose.name: MsgClose
msgclose.doc: Closes a message. After the message is closed, the message post function (the callback function specified in the MsgOpen() function) is not called if a message is received. When the server side is closed, all clients are closed. When the client side is closed, only the specified client is closed.
msgclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the Plant SCADA server.
paramDocs.hMsg: The message handle, returned from the MsgOpen() function. The message handle identifies the table where all data on the associated message is stored.

msggetcurr.name: MsgGetCurr
msggetcurr.doc: Gets the handle of the client message that called the report or remote procedure that is currently running. You can call this function only in a report or a remote procedure call.
msggetcurr.returns: The handle for the client message. The message handle identifies the table where all data on the associated message is stored. The function returns -1 if no client called the report or function.

msgopen.name: MsgOpen
msgopen.doc: Opens a message session with a Plant SCADA server. You can specify a message post function - a callback function that is automatically called when a message arrives. In this function you can call MsgRead() to get the message, and perform other tasks common to your message sessions. You can then call MsgWrite() to send a message back to the caller, MsgRPC() to call a procedure on the caller, and so on.
msgopen.returns: The message handle, or -1 if the session cannot be opened. The message handle identifies the table where data on the associated message is stored. The exception to this is mode 1 where the handle 4096 will be returned if the session can be opened.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the server to open, either:
paramDocs.Mode: The mode of the message session to open:
paramDocs.Fn: The message post function, that is a callback function for the message event. Set Fn to 0 if no event callback function is required.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster the server being communicated with belongs to, this is used when mode is 0, 1 or 3. This is not required if the client is connected to only one cluster containing a server of the type set in the name parameter.

msgread.name: MsgRead
msgread.doc: Reads a message from a message session. You can call this function only in a message post function (the callback function specified in the MsgOpen() function), to read the current message.
msgread.returns: The message handle of the message being read.

paramDocs.nType: The message number. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.Str: The message text. Must be a String type variable.

msgrpc.name: MsgRPC
msgrpc.doc: Calls a remote procedure on another Plant SCADA computer. You can call any of the built-in Cicode functions remotely, or your own functions. You pass the sName of the function as a string, not as the function tag, and pass all the arguments for that function in Arg.
msgrpc.returns: The result of the remote function call (as a string). If the function is called in asynchronous mode the result of the remote function cannot be returned, so an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.hMsg: The message handle, returned from the MsgOpen() function. The message handle identifies the table where all data on the associated message is stored.
paramDocs.sName: The name of the function to call remotely, as a string.
paramDocs.Arg: The arguments to pass to the function, separated by commas (,). Enclose string arguments in quotes "" and use the string escape character (^) around strings enclosed within a string. If you do not enclose the string in quotes, then the string is only the first tag found.

msgstate.name: MsgState
msgstate.doc: Verifies the status of a message session. Use MsgState() to check the return value of MsgOpen(). A message post function is set effectively only if MsgState() returns 1, which means the message session is online.
msgstate.returns: This function has the following possible return values:

paramDocs.hMsg: The message handle, returned from the MsgOpen() function. The message handle identifies the table where all data on the associated message is stored.

msgwrite.name: MsgWrite
msgwrite.doc: Writes a message to a message session. The message is sent to the remote computer's callback function and can be read by calling MsgRead(). If the remote computer has not opened the session, this message is disregarded.
msgwrite.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hMsg: The message handle, returned from the MsgOpen() function. The message handle identifies the table where all data on the associated message is stored.
