paramDocs.nType: The integer message data, that is the message number.

multimonitorstart.name: MultiMonitorStart
multimonitorstart.doc: Displays a Plant SCADA window on each of the configured monitors when a display client starts up. It sets up the windows according to the Multi-Monitor Parameters [MultiMonitors]Monitors and [MultiMonitors]StartupPage<n>.

multisignatureform.name: MultiSignatureForm
multisignatureform.doc: Displays a form that allows up to four users to have their credentials verified in order to approve an operation. The usernames can be Plant SCADA or Windows users.
multisignatureform.returns: TRUE (1) if the operation approved (that is all users' credentials were verified and the operator clicked the "Approve" button, otherwise FALSE (0).

paramDocs.sOperationDescription: A description of the operation that requires approval. This string will be displayed on the signature form and logged to the log device if the operation is approved.
paramDocs.sLogDevice: The name of a log device if logging is required, otherwise pass an empty string.
paramDocs.sUser1..4: Each sUser argument needs to be either a Plant SCADA user name, a Windows user name (including domain\ prefix) or a blank string. Even though the sUser arguments are numbered 1 through 4, this only controls the order in which users are displayed on the multi-signature form. You can pass empty strings for any of these arguments, but at least one user needs to be specified.

multisignaturetagwrite.name: MultiSignatureTagWrite
multisignaturetagwrite.doc: Displays a form that allows up to four users to have their credentials verified in order to approve a write of a specific value to a specific tag. If all users are verified successfully, the write to the tag is performed by this function before it returns. The usernames can be Plant SCADA or Windows users.
multisignaturetagwrite.returns: TRUE (1) if the operation was approved (that is all users' credentials were verified and the operator clicked the "Approve" button, otherwise FALSE (0).

paramDocs.sTagName: The name of the tag to which a write needs to be approved.
paramDocs.sValuetoWrite: The value to write to the tag if approval succeeds.
paramDocs.sLogDevice: The name of a log device if logging is required, otherwise pass an empty string.
paramDocs.sUser: Each sUser argument needs to be either a Plant SCADA user name, a Windows user name (including domain\ prefix) or an empty string. Even though the sUser arguments are numbered 1 through 4, this only controls the order in which users are displayed on the multi-signature form. You can pass empty strings for any of these arguments, but at least one user needs to be specified.

name.name: Name
name.doc: Gets the name of the operator who is currently logged on to the display system. The user can be a Plant SCADA or a windows user. If this function is called on a server, it returns the name of the local operator. If there is no one logged on, or the logged on user is a "system user" this function returns an empty string.
name.returns: The name of the user as a string. If the user is logged on as a Windows user the name will be the Windows user account name.

paramDocs.bIncludeDomain: • bIncludeDomain = 1: (Default) Return Windows user name with domain name

objectassociateevents.name: ObjectAssociateEvents
objectassociateevents.doc: Allows you to change the ActiveX object's event class. If you have inserted an object on a graphics page using Graphics Builder, it allows you to change the event class to something other than the default of "PageName_ObjectName".
objectassociateevents.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sClass: The class of the object. You can use the object's human readable name, its program ID, or its GUID. If the class does not exist, the function will report an error.
paramDocs.hSource: The source object firing the events which are to be handled by the event handler.

objectassociatepropertywithtag.name: ObjectAssociatePropertyWithTag
objectassociatepropertywithtag.doc: Establishes an association between an ActiveX property and a variable tag. This means that any changes made to an ActiveX object property will be mirrored in the variable tag.
objectassociatepropertywithtag.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sObject: The object instance that associates a property with a tag.
paramDocs.sPropertyName: The name of the ActiveX property to associate with the tag.
paramDocs.sTagName: The name of the Plant SCADA variable tag to associate with the property.
paramDocs.sOnChangeEvent: The name of the "on change" event that informs Plant SCADA of a change to the ActiveX object. This is required where the ActiveX object does not automatically generate a property change notification. Choose an event that happens to be fired whenever the ActiveX object property changes, for example, the MS Calendar Control fires an AfterUpdate event whenever a day button is pressed.

objectbyname.name: ObjectByName
objectbyname.doc: Retrieves an ActiveX object. This is useful when you know the object by name only (this will often be the case for objects created during configuration, rather than those created at runtime using a Cicode function).
objectbyname.returns: The requested object, if successful, otherwise an error is generated.

paramDocs.Name: The name used to access the object, as specified when creating it in Cicode. For objects created in the Graphics Builder, the object name is set in the Access (Identification) tab, and defaults to "AN" followed by its AN number, for example, "AN35". The Name argument should be enclosed in quotes:

objecthasinterface.name: ObjectHasInterface
objecthasinterface.doc: Queries the ActiveX component to determine if its specific interface is supported. (Refer to the ActiveX object's documentation for details of its interfaces.)
objecthasinterface.returns: 0 if the interface is not supported, otherwise 1.

paramDocs.hObject: The handle for the object (as returned by the ObjectByName function).
paramDocs.sInterface: The name of the interface (case sensitive).

objectisvalid.name: ObjectIsValid
objectisvalid.doc: Determines if the given handle for an object is a valid handle. This function is useful for programmatically checking that an object was returned for a call.
objectisvalid.returns: 0 if the handle is not valid, otherwise 1.

paramDocs.hObject: The handle for the object (as returned by the ObjectByName function).

objecttostr.name: ObjectToStr
objecttostr.doc: Converts an object handle to a string. This means you can print the object handle in a trace message, which allows you confirm if the handle is valid.
objecttostr.returns: A string containing the converted object handle

paramDocs.hObject: The handle for the object (as returned by the ObjectByName function).

oledatetotime.name: OLEDateToTime
oledatetotime.doc: Converts an OLE DATE value (stored in a REAL) to a Plant SCADA time/date value.
oledatetotime.returns: Returns a Plant SCADA time/date value.

paramDocs.OLEDate: The OLE DATE value to convert (stored as a REAL).

onevent.name: OnEvent
onevent.doc: Sets an event callback function for an event type. The callback function is called when the event occurs.
onevent.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nType: The type of event:
paramDocs.Fn: The function to call when the event occurs. This callback function needs to have no arguments, so you specify the function with no parentheses (). The callback function needs to return INT as its return data type. You cannot specify a Plant SCADA built-in function as a callback function.

packedrgb.name: PackedRGB
packedrgb.doc: Returns a packed RGB color based on specified red, green, and blue values.
packedrgb.returns: The packed RGB color value - if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.nRed: The red component of the desired packed RGB color.
paramDocs.nGreen: The green component of the desired packed RGB color.
paramDocs.nBlue: The blue component of the desired packed RGB color.

packedrgbtocitectcolour.name: PackedRGBToCitectColour
packedrgbtocitectcolour.doc: Converts a packed RGB color into a calculated Plant SCADA color value.
packedrgbtocitectcolour.returns: The Plant SCADA color value if successful; otherwise an error is returned.

pagealarm.name: PageAlarm
pagealarm.doc: Displays a category of active alarms on the alarm page.
pagealarm.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Category: The alarm category to display. Set to 0 (the default) to display all alarm categories.

pageback.name: PageBack
pageback.doc: Displays the previously displayed page in the Window.
pageback.returns: No Error (0) on success. Bad handle specified (269) if current window handle does not correspond to a valid window. Invalid argument passed (274) if count is outside of allowable bounds.

paramDocs.iCount: Optional parameter to specify the number of pages to move back. Default value is 1.

pagedisabled.name: PageDisabled
pagedisabled.doc: Displays a category of disabled alarms on the disabled alarms page.
pagedisabled.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Category: The alarm category to display. Set to 0 (the default) to display all alarm categories.

pagedisplay.name: PageDisplay
pagedisplay.doc: Displays a graphics page in the active window. The page needs to be in one of the operator's current areas. The page to be displayed is identified by its Page Name or the Page Number.
pagedisplay.returns: 0 (zero) if the page is successfully displayed, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Page: The name or page number of the page to display (in quotation marks ""). Can be prefixed by the name of a host cluster, that is "ClusterName.Page". This will take precedence over the use of the ClusterName parameter if the two differ.
paramDocs.ClusterName: The name of the cluster that will accommodate the page at runtime (in quotation marks ""). The specified cluster is used to resolve any tags that have a cluster omitted. If the Page parameter is prefixed with the name of a cluster, this parameter will not be used.

pageexists.name: PageExists
pageexists.doc: Use this function to check if a particular page exists in your project.
pageexists.returns: 1 if the page does exist, 0 if the page does not.

paramDocs.sPageName: The name of the page to check for.

pagefile.name: PageFile
pagefile.doc: Displays a file on the page. After the file is displayed, you can scroll up and down through the file. To use this function, you need to use the Graphics Builder to create a page called "File" (using the file template).
pagefile.returns: 0 (zero) if the file is successfully displayed, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the file to display.

pagefileinfo.name: PageFileInfo
pagefileinfo.doc: Returns the width or height of an unopened page.
pagefileinfo.returns: The height or width of the specified page in pixels, depending on the value set for nMode.

paramDocs.sPageName: The name of the page you would like to retrieve size information for.
paramDocs.nMode: Retrieves either the width or the height of the specified page in pixels.

pagefileinfoex.name: PageFileInfoEx
pagefileinfoex.doc: Returns the width, height, content type, parent or title of an unopened page.
pagefileinfoex.returns: The height, width, content type, parent or title of the specified page, depending on the value set for nMode.

paramDocs.sPageName: The name of the page for which you would like to retrieve information.
paramDocs.nMode: Determines if the width, height, content type, parent or title is returned for the specified page.

pageforward.name: PageForward
pageforward.doc: If PageBack() is called, PageForward() will restore the previously displayed page in the window. PageForward requires PageBack to have been called and no other page display functions to have been called in between. Calling the display functions PageDisplay or PageGoto will remove the forward pages from the Page Navigation History.
pageforward.returns: No Error (0) on success. Bad handle specified (269) if current window handle does not correspond to a valid window. Invalid argument passed (274) if count is outside of allowable bounds.

paramDocs.iCount: Optional parameter to specify the number of pages to move forward. Default value is 1.

pagegetint.name: PageGetInt
pagegetint.doc: Returns the integer value associated with a variable name on a particular page. If two or more windows are displayed, each window has a unique copy of the variable. You can use these variables in Cicode to keep track of variables unique to each window.

paramDocs.sLabel: String name of the variable to return
paramDocs.iWinNum: Window number of the page. Default is current window.

pagegetstr.name: PageGetStr
pagegetstr.doc: Gets the string associated with a variable name on a particular page. Page-based variables are local to each display page. If two or more windows are displayed, each window has a unique copy of the variable. You can use these variables in Cicode to keep track of variables unique to each window.

paramDocs.sLabel: String name of the variable to return
paramDocs.iWinNum: Window number of the page. Default is current window.

pagegoto.name: PageGoto
pagegoto.doc: Displays a graphics page in the active window. The page needs to be in one of the operator's current areas. You can specify either the Page Name or the Page Number of the graphics page.
pagegoto.returns: 0 (zero) if the page is successfully displayed, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Page: The name or page number of the page to display (in quotation marks ""). Can be prefixed by the name of a host cluster, that is "ClusterName.Page". This will take precedence over the use of the ClusterName parameter if the two differ.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster that will accommodate the page at runtime (in quotation marks ""). The specified cluster is used to resolve any tags that have the cluster name omitted. If the Page parameter is prefixed with the name of a cluster, this parameter will not be used.

pagehardware.name: PageHardware
pagehardware.doc: Displays the active hardware alarms on the hardware alarms page.
pagehardware.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

pagehistorydspmenu.name: PageHistoryDspMenu
pagehistorydspmenu.doc: Displays a pop-up menu which lists the page history of current window. The user can select any page in the history to recall the page. When full page history is specified, the currently displayed page will also be listed and marked in the menu.
pagehistorydspmenu.returns: Zero (0) if the function is executed successfully. Otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.iType: The type of page history to be listed:

pagehistoryempty.name: PageHistoryEmpty
pagehistoryempty.doc: Used to determine if the page history of the current window is empty. The currently displayed page is not counted as history.
pagehistoryempty.returns: 1 if page history of specified type is empty, or 0 if it is not empty.

paramDocs.iType: The type of page history to be checked:

pagehome.name: PageHome
pagehome.doc: Displays the predefined home page in the window.
pagehome.returns: No error(0) on success. Bad handle specified (269) if current window handle does not correspond to a valid window. Bad handle specified (274) if INI parameter [Page]HomePage is not set.

paramDocs.sCluster: Optional parameter to the Cluster to associate the page being opened with. Default value "".

pageinfo.name: PageInfo
pageinfo.doc: Gets information about the current page.

paramDocs.nType: The type of page information required.

pagelast.name: PageLast
pagelast.doc: Displays the graphics page that was last displayed. With this function, you can successively recall the last ten pages that were displayed.
pagelast.returns: 0 (zero) if the page is successfully displayed, otherwise an error is returned.

pagelistcount.name: PageListCount
pagelistcount.doc: Gets number of pages in the page list of the current window.
pagelistcount.returns: Number of pages in the list

pagelistcurrent.name: PageListCurrent
pagelistcurrent.doc: Gets Index of the current page in the page list of current window.
pagelistcurrent.returns: List index (0 to list size -1), or -1 if unable to get index

pagelistdelete.name: PageListDelete
pagelistdelete.doc: Removes a page at the specific index from the page list of the current window. This function will return an error if only one page is in the list. If the page is currently displayed, the next page will be displayed. If there is no next page, the previous page will be displayed.
pagelistdelete.returns: 0 (zero) if the page is successfully removed, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Index: Index to the page list (valid range 0 to list size minus 1)

pagelistdisplay.name: PageListDisplay
pagelistdisplay.doc: Recalls (displays) a page at the specific index in the page list of current window, and moves the current index to the page. When a page is recalled, the original parameters (such as cluster context, supergenie associations, PageTask arguments if applicable) used to display the page will be restored.
pagelistdisplay.returns: 0 (zero) if the page is successfully displayed, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Index: Index to the page list (valid range 0 to list size minus 1)

pagelistinfo.name: PageListInfo
pagelistinfo.doc: Gets information of a page at the specific index in the page list of the current window.
pagelistinfo.returns: String value of the requested information, or empty string if no valid information can be found

paramDocs.Index: Index to the page list (valid range 0 to list size minus 1)

pagemenu.name: PageMenu
pagemenu.doc: Displays a menu page with page selection buttons. A page goto button is displayed for each of the first 40 pages defined in the project.
pagemenu.returns: 0 (zero) if the page is successfully displayed, otherwise an error is returned.

pagenext.name: PageNext
pagenext.doc: Displays the next page as specified in the project.
pagenext.returns: 0 (zero) if the page is successfully displayed, otherwise an error is returned.

pagepeekcurrent.name: PagePeekCurrent
pagepeekcurrent.doc: Return the index in the page navigation history for the current page.
pagepeekcurrent.returns: Index in the page navigation history for the current page. -1 indicates that current window handle does not correspond to a valid window.

pagepeeklast.name: PagePeekLast
pagepeeklast.doc: Gets information about a page at an offset in the page navigation history.
pagepeeklast.returns: String value of the requested information, or empty string if no valid result for given arguments.

paramDocs.iOffset: Pages are navigated using page navigation history. iOffset is used to indicate the position in that history. An iOffset value of "0" represents the currently viewed page. Positive increments of iOffset indicate previous pages visited in the navigation history. Negative values of iOffset are used to indicate pages in the future of the navigation history (negative iOffsets exist only if the user has used the back button to revisit earlier pages in the history).
paramDocs.iType: An enumeration representing the type of information required. The default value is 0.

pagepoplast.name: PagePopLast
pagepoplast.doc: Gets the Page Name of the last item in the page navigation history and removes the page from the history.
pagepoplast.returns: The page name or an empty string if there is no last page.

pagepopup.name: PagePopUp
pagepopup.doc: Display pop up window at the mouse position. If the mouse position is not known then the pop up will display in the centre of the screen. The window is displayed with no resize and will be closed if the page is changed.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the page (drawn with the Graphics Builder).
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster that will accommodate the page at runtime (in quotation marks ""). The specified cluster is used to resolve any tags that have a cluster omitted. If the Page parameter is prefixed with the name of a cluster, this parameter will not be used.

pageprev.name: PagePrev
pageprev.doc: Displays the previous page as specified in the project.
pageprev.returns: 0 (zero) if the page is successfully displayed, otherwise an error is returned.

pageprocessanalyst.name: PageProcessAnalyst
pageprocessanalyst.doc: Displays a Process Analyst page (in the same window) preloaded with the pre-defined Process Analyst View (PAV) file.
pageprocessanalyst.returns: Zero (0) if the page is successfully displayed. Otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the page that contains Process Analyst object(s). For example, pages based on the Process Analyst templates found in the Tab_Style_Include project.
paramDocs.iFileLocation1: PAV file location code for the 1st PAV file, see PA doc LoadFromFile() for details.
paramDocs.iButtonMask1: Bit mask for removing command buttons from the 1st PA, bit flags as shown below:
paramDocs.sObjName1: Name of the PA object on the given Page where the 1st PAV file will be loaded. If this parameter is not specified or empty string, it is defaulted to the object name used in the tab style templates, that is "_templatePA1".
paramDocs.iFileLocation2: PAV file location code for the 2nd PAV file
paramDocs.iButtonMask2: Bit mask for removing command buttons from the 2nd PA, refer iButtonMask1 for details
paramDocs.sObjName2: Name of the PA object on the given Page where the 2nd PAV file will be loaded. If this parameter is not specified or empty string, it is defaulted to the object name used in the tab style templates, that is "_templatePA2".

pageprocessanalystpens.name: PageProcessAnalystPens
pageprocessanalystpens.doc: Display a page and add the specified pens to the first pane of the specified PA object on the page. If a PAV file is also specified, it will be loaded first, and the pens in the first pane will be removed before the specified pens are created on the PA.
pageprocessanalystpens.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the page that displays the PA.
paramDocs.sTag1..sTag8: Up to 8 Trend tags can be added to the PA.
paramDocs.iButtonMask: Mask to remove button(s) from the main tool bar of PA. The following values can be combined to remove multiple buttons:
paramDocs.sObjName: The name of the PA object. If not specified it is defaulted to "_templatePA1" which is the name used by the built-in templates.
paramDocs.iPane: The pane in PA where the trend or variable tags are added. If this is not specified or less than 1, it is defaulted to 1 (the 1st pane). If the specified pane does not exist in the PA object, a new pane will be created.
paramDocs.sPAVFile: Optional Process Analyst View file to be loaded, default ="".
paramDocs.iFileLocation: Optional location of the PAV file. The allowed values are:

pagepushlast.name: PagePushLast
pagepushlast.doc: Places a page at the end of the page navigation history.
pagepushlast.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Page: The Page Name or Page Number (of the page) to place at the end of the page navigation history.

pagerecall.name: PageRecall
pagerecall.doc: Displays the page at a specified depth in the page navigation history.
pagerecall.returns: No error(0) on success. Bad handle specified (269) if current window handle does not correspond to a valid window. Bad handle specified (274) if index is outside of allowable bounds.

paramDocs.iIndex: The index into the page navigation history of the Page to be displayed. To get the index for the currently displayed page, call PagePeekCurrent(). Then increment it to access pages in the forward history, or decrement it to access pages in the backward history. Be reminded that you cannot recall the page that is currently displayed.

pagerichtextfile.name: PageRichTextFile
pagerichtextfile.doc: This function creates a rich edit object, and loads a copy of the rich text file Filename into that object. The rich text object will be rectangular in shape, with dimensions determined by nHeight, and nWidth. If you do not specify nHeight and nWidth, nAN will define the position of one corner, and (AN + 1) the position of the diagonally opposite corner. This function would often be used as a page entry function.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation point at which to display the rich text object.
paramDocs.Filename: The name of the file to be copied and loaded into the rich text object. The filename needs to be entered in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.nMode: The display mode for the rich text object. The mode can be any combination of:
paramDocs.nHeight: The height of the rich text object in pixels. The height is established by measuring down from the animation point.
paramDocs.nWidth: The width of the rich text object in pixels. The width is established by measuring across to the right of the animation point.

pageselect.name: PageSelect
pageselect.doc: Displays a dialog box with a list of graphics pages defined in the project. AN operator can select a page name for display.
pageselect.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

pagesetint.name: PageSetInt
pagesetint.doc: Associates an integer variable with a particular page. Page-based variables are stored in an array, local to each display page. This function allows you to save integer variables in temporary storage.
pagesetint.returns: No error(0) on success. 269 if WinNum handle does not correspond to a valid window. 274 if Label or Var is not a valid variable.

paramDocs.sLabel: String name of the variable which will contain sValue.
paramDocs.iWinNum: Window number of the page. Default is current window.

pagesetstr.name: PageSetStr
pagesetstr.doc: Stores a local page-based string and associates the string with the page. Page-based variables are stored in an array, local to each display page. This function allows you to save string variables in temporary storage.
pagesetstr.returns: No error(0) on success. 269 if WinNum handle does not correspond to a valid window. 274 if Label or Var is not a valid variable.

paramDocs.sLabel: String name of the variable which will contain sVar.
paramDocs.sVar: The string to store. The string length is 128 characters.
paramDocs.iWinNum: Window number of the page. Default is current window.

pagesoe.name: PageSOE
pagesoe.doc: Displays a category of sequence of events (SOE) entries on the SOE page.
pagesoe.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Category: The category number for the alarms you want to display their events
paramDocs.Fallback: Whether to display the Summary page instead if the SOE page does not exist. If not specified it defaults to FALSE (0).

pagesummary.name: PageSummary
pagesummary.doc: Displays a category of alarm summary entries on the alarms summary page.
pagesummary.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.Category: The category number for the alarms you want to summarise.

pagetask.name: PageTask
pagetask.doc: PageTask() is used for running preliminary Cicode before displaying a page in a window. It makes it possible for the same Cicode to be run if the page is re-entered by navigating forward or back. PageTask() is similar to TaskNew().
pagetask.returns: A handle to a code task the first time it is run. BAD_HANDLE (-1) if the function did not complete.

paramDocs.iWinNum: The Window number of the window in which to display the page.
paramDocs.sFunctionName: String representing the Cicode function to run each time the page is navigated to using the forward and backward navigation functions.
paramDocs.sFunctionArg: String representing the parameters to use with function fnTask.

pagetransformcoords.name: PageTransformCoords
pagetransformcoords.doc: Converts Page coordinates to absolute screen coordinates.

paramDocs.hPage: Page handle of the relevant Window.
paramDocs.iDisplayX: Output parameter: Transformed X coordinate. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.iDisplayY: Output parameter: Transformed Y coordinate. Must be a Long type variable.

pagetrend.name: PageTrend
pagetrend.doc: Displays a trend page with the specified trend pens. Use this function to display trends in a single cluster system with a single trend page. You need to create the trend page with the Graphics Builder and set the pen names to blank. Then display that page by calling this function and passing the required trend tags. Call this function from a menu of trend pages.
pagetrend.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: Name of the trend page (drawn with the Graphics Builder).
paramDocs.sTag1: The first trend tag to display on the page.
paramDocs.sTag2..sTag8: Optionally trend tags 2 to 8 to display on the page.

pagetrendex.name: PageTrendEx
pagetrendex.doc: Displays a trend page of a specified cluster in a multi-cluster system with the specified trend pens. Use this function to display trends in a mult-cluster system with a single trend page. You need to create the trend page with the Graphics Builder and set the pen names to blank. Then display that page by calling this function and passing the required trend tags. Call this function from a menu of trend pages. This function can also be used in a single cluster system, the sCluster argument is optional in such a case.
pagetrendex.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: Name of the trend page (drawn with the Graphics Builder).
paramDocs.sCluster: Name of the cluster in which the trend page is located.
paramDocs.sTag1: The first trend tag to display on the page.
paramDocs.sTag2..sTag8: Optionally trend tags 2 to 8 to display on the page.

parameterget.name: ParameterGet
parameterget.doc: Gets the value of a parameter. The parameter can exist in a local Citect.ini file, a profile INI file, or the parameters database.

paramDocs.sName: The parameter name.
paramDocs.Default: The default value of the parameter.

parameterput.name: ParameterPut
parameterput.doc: Updates a system parameter in the CITECT.INI file. If the system parameter does not exist, it is added to the CITECT.INI file.
parameterput.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The system parameter name.
paramDocs.Value: The value to put in the system parameter.

pathtostr.name: PathToStr
pathtostr.doc: Converts a Plant SCADA path into a string. The path string can contain one of the standard Plant SCADA path operators, BIN, DATA, RUN, USER or a user-configured path. If the string does not contain a Plant SCADA path, it is unchanged.
pathtostr.returns: A string containing the converted path.

paramDocs.sPath: The Plant SCADA path to convert.

pi.name: Pi
pi.doc: Gets the value of pi (the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter).

plotclose.name: PlotClose
plotclose.doc: Displays the plot on screen or sends it to the printer (depending on the output device you specified in the PlotOpen() function), then closes the plot. Once the plot is closed, it cannot be used.
plotclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hPlot: The plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where all data on the plot is stored.

plotdraw.name: PlotDraw
plotdraw.doc: Constructs drawings on your plot. Use the coordinates (X1,Y1) and (X2,Y2) to define a point, line, rectangle, square, circle, or ellipse. You can specify the style, color, and width of the pen, and a fill color for a box or circular shape.
plotdraw.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hPlot: The plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where data on the plot is stored.
paramDocs.nType: The type of drawing:
paramDocs.PenStyle: The style of the pen used to draw:
paramDocs.PenCol: The color of the pen (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.PenWidth: Pen width in pixels. If the width is thicker than one pixel, you need to use a solid pen (PenStyle = 0). Maximum width is 32.
paramDocs.nFill: The fill color of the rectangle, square, circle, or ellipse (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of predefined color names and codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour. For a point or line, nFill is ignored.

plotgetmarker.name: PlotGetMarker
plotgetmarker.doc: Gets the marker number of a symbol. The symbol needs to be a symbol and registered with the PlotSetMarker() function.
plotgetmarker.returns: The marker number if successful, otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.sSymbolName: The library name and symbol name ("Library.Symbol") of the symbol that is registered as a marker.

plotgrid.name: PlotGrid
plotgrid.doc: Defines a frame and draws horizontal and vertical grid lines within this frame. These grid lines can then be used by the PlotLine(), PlotXYLine(), and PlotScaleMarker() functions. You need to define the frame for a plot before you can plot points with the PlotLine() and PlotXYLine() functions. nSamples specifies the maximum number of samples that can be plotted for a single line. If you set FrameWidth to 0 (zero), the frame will be defined but not displayed (however, the plot will still be displayed).
plotgrid.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hPlot: Plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where data on the plot is stored.
paramDocs.nSamples: The maximum number of samples that can be plotted for a single line in this grid (valid values between 2 and 16000 inclusive). For example, if you set nSamples to 10, then plot 2 lines in this grid (using the PlotLine() function), each line will be plotted with a maximum of 10 samples. For this example, a line can possess less than 10 samples, but if it has more, it will be shortened to 10 samples.
paramDocs.nHorGrid: The number of rows (formed by the horizontal grid lines) to draw within the frame. If there is no need of grid lines, set nHorGrid to 0 (zero) and HorGridCol to 0. nHorGrid cannot exceed the pixel width of the plot.
paramDocs.HorGridCol: The color of the horizontal grid lines (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.nVerGrid: The number of columns (formed by the vertical grid lines) to draw within the frame. If there is no need of grid lines, set nVerGrid to 0 (zero) and VerGridCol to 0. nVerGrid cannot exceed the pixel height of the plot.
paramDocs.VerGridCol: The color of the vertical grid lines (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.FrameWidth: The width (also called pen width) of the frame enclosing the grid, in pixels. To define the frame without drawing its boundaries, set FrameWidth to 0 (zero) and FrameCol to 0. The maximum is 32.
paramDocs.FrameCol: The color of the frame enclosing the grid (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.nFill: The background color for the frame (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the plot. For future use only - set it to 0 (zero).

plotinfo.name: PlotInfo
plotinfo.doc: Gets information about the plot. You can call this function to determine the number of pixels per page or inch, the resolution of a plot, and the size and spacing of characters for a specified text font. You can also check whether a printer can print rotated text. (See PlotText.)
plotinfo.returns: The attributes of the plot as a string.

paramDocs.hPlot: The plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where all data on the plot is stored.
paramDocs.nType: The type of plot information to get:
paramDocs.sInput: The font handle (hFont), returned from the DspFont() function. Useful only for Type 6, 7, 8, or 10.

plotline.name: PlotLine
plotline.doc: Draws a line (in the Plant SCADA plot system) for a set of data points. You specify the data points in the table pTable, and plot these points between the LoScale and HiScale values. The line is drawn inside the frame defined by the PlotGrid() function.
plotline.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hPlot: The plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where all data on the plot is stored.
paramDocs.PenStyle: The style of the pen used to draw:
paramDocs.PenCol: The color of the pen (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.PenWidth: The width of the pen, in pixels. If the width is thicker than one pixel, you need to use a solid pen (PenStyle = 0). The maximum width is 32.
paramDocs.MarkerCol: The color of the markers (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of predefined color names and codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.nMarker: The number of samples between markers.
paramDocs.Length: The length of the array, that is, the number of points in the table pTable for PlotLine(), or in tables xTable and yTable for PlotXYLine().
paramDocs.pTable: The points to be plotted (as an array of floating-point values).
paramDocs.LoScale: The lowest value that will be displayed on the plot (that is the value assigned to the origin of your grid). The LoScale and HiScale values determine the scale of your grid. This scale is used to plot values. for example, If LoScale = 0 (zero) and HiScale = 100, a value of 50 will be plotted half way up the Y-axis of your grid. LoScale needs to be in the same units as the values in pTable.
paramDocs.HiScale: The highest value that will be displayed on the plot. The LoScale and HiScale values determine the scale of your grid. This scale is used to plot values. for example, If LoScale = 0 (zero) and HiScale = 100, a value of 50 will be plotted half way up the Y- axis of your grid. HiScale needs to be in the same units as the values in pTable.
paramDocs.Mode: The origin of your grid, and the direction of the plotted line:

plotmarker.name: PlotMarker
plotmarker.doc: Draws markers on a plotted line or at a specified point. You can plot any one of the standard markers, or use a symbol of your choice. (you need to first register your symbol as a marker, by using the PlotSetMarker() function.)
plotmarker.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hPlot: The plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where data on the plot is stored.
paramDocs.MarkerCol: The color of the marker (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.nMarker: The number of samples between markers.
paramDocs.Length: The length of the array (the number of line points in the table pTable) plotted in the PlotLine() or PlotXYLine() function. To draw only one marker at a specified point, set Length to 1.

plotopen.name: PlotOpen
plotopen.doc: Opens a new plot, sets its output device, and returns its plot handle. You can send the plot to any one of your system printers, or display it on screen at the specified AN.
plotopen.returns: The plot handle if the plot is opened successfully, otherwise -1 is returned. The plot handle identifies the table where all data on the associated plot is stored.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation point (AN) where the plot will display. Set the AN to 0 (zero) when sOutput is a printer.
paramDocs.sOutput: The output device where the plot is sent, for example:
paramDocs.Mode: When a plot is removed or updated, the portion of the background screen beneath it is blanked out. The mode determines how the background screen is restored. The mode of the plot system:

plotscalemarker.name: PlotScaleMarker
plotscalemarker.doc: Draws scale lines beside the grid on your plot (if there is one) and places markers on them. The height of the scale line is automatically set to the height of the frame set in the PlotGrid() function.
plotscalemarker.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hPlot: The plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where data on the plot is stored.
paramDocs.nMarker: The number of markers on the scale line.
paramDocs.PenWidth: The width of the scale line, in pixels.
paramDocs.PenCol: The color of the pen (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.

plotsetmarker.name: PlotSetMarker
plotsetmarker.doc: Registers a symbol as a marker. You can then draw the new marker at points and on plotted lines, by specifying the MarkerNo of the symbol as the MarkerStyle in the PlotMarker() function. Call the PlotGetMarker() function if you do not know the number of a marker.
plotsetmarker.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.MarkerNo: The number of the marker, to be used as the MarkerStyle in the PlotMarker() function. Your marker numbers need to be greater than or equal to 20 (to a maximum of 32000).
paramDocs.sSymbolName: The name and path of the symbol to be defined as a marker.

plottext.name: PlotText
plottext.doc: Prints text on a plot. You can specify the font, position, and orientation of the text. If you specify an orientation other than 'left-to-right', you need to check that the font (and the printer) supports the orientation.
plottext.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hPlot: The plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where all data on the plot is stored.
paramDocs.hFont: The font handle, returned from the DspFont() function. The font handle identifies the table where details of that font are stored.
paramDocs.sText: The text string to be plotted.

plotxyline.name: PlotXYLine
plotxyline.doc: Plots values from two different tables. Values from one table are considered X coordinates, and values from the other are considered Y coordinates. Points are plotted between the low and high scale values specified for x and y. The line is plotted inside the frame defined by the PlotGrid() function.
plotxyline.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error is returned.

paramDocs.hPlot: The plot handle, returned from the PlotOpen() function. The plot handle identifies the table where all data on the plot is stored.
paramDocs.PenStyle: The style of the pen used to draw:
paramDocs.PenCol: The color of the pen (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.PenWidth: The width of the pen, in pixels. If the width is thicker than one pixel, you need to use a solid pen (PenStyle = 0). The maximum width is 32.
paramDocs.MarkerCol: The color of the markers (flashing color is not supported). Select a color from the list of Predefined Color Names and Codes or create an RGB-based color using the function MakeColour.
paramDocs.nMarker: The number of samples between markers.
paramDocs.Length: The length of the array, that is the number of points in the table pTable for PlotLine(), or in tables xTable and yTable for PlotXYLine().
paramDocs.xTable: The x coordinates for the points in the line, as an array of floating point values.
paramDocs.LoXScale: The lowest X-axis value that will be displayed on the plot (that is the X-coordinate of the origin of your grid). The LoXScale and HiXScale values determine the scale of your grid. This scale is used to plot values. for example, If LoXScale = 0 (zero) and HiXScale = 100, a value of 50 will be plotted half way along the X-axis of your grid.
paramDocs.HiXScale: The highest X-axis value that will be displayed on the plot. The LoXScale and HiXScale values determine the scale of your grid. This scale is used to plot values. for example, If LoXScale = 0 (zero) and HiXScale = 100, a value of 50 will be plotted half way along the X-axis of your grid.
paramDocs.yTable: The y coordinates for the points in the line, as an array of floating point values.
paramDocs.LoYScale: The lowest Y-axis value that will be displayed on the plot (that is the Y-coordinate of the origin of your grid). The LoYScale and HiYScale values determine the scale of your grid. This scale is used to plot values. for example, If LoYScale = 0 (zero) and HiYScale = 100, a value of 50 will be plotted half way up the Y-axis of your grid.
paramDocs.HiYScale: The highest Y-axis value that will be displayed on the plot. The LoYScale and HiYScale values determine the scale of your grid. This scale is used to plot values. for example, If LoYScale = 0 (zero) and HiYScale = 100, a value of 50 will be plotted half way up the Y-axis of your grid.
paramDocs.Mode: The origin of your grid, and the direction of the plotted line:

pow.name: Pow
pow.doc: Calculates x to the power of y.
pow.returns: X to the power of Y.

print.name: Print
print.doc: Prints a string on the current device. You should call this function only in a report. The output is sent to the device (or group of devices) defined in the Reports database (in the output device field).
print.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

printfont.name: PrintFont
printfont.doc: Changes the printing font on the current device. You should call this function only in a report. It will change the font style for the device (or group of devices) defined in the Reports database (output device field). It has effect only on reports being printed to a PRINTER_DEV - it has no effect on other types of devices, such as ASCII_DEV and dBASE_DEV.
printfont.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Font: The Plant SCADA font (defined in the Fonts database).

println.name: PrintLn
println.doc: Prints a string on the current device, followed by a newline character. You should call this function only in a report. The output will be sent to the device or group of devices defined in the Reports database (in the output device field).
println.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

processanalystloadfile.name: ProcessAnalystLoadFile
processanalystloadfile.doc: Loads the specified PAV file to a Process Analyst object, which is identified by parameter sObjName.
processanalystloadfile.returns: Zero (0) if the function is successfully run. otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iFileLocation: PAV file location code for the PAV file. Indicates which known location to load the file from.
paramDocs.iButtonMask: Bit mask for removing command buttons from the PA, bit flags as shown below:
paramDocs.sObjName: Name of the PA object on the given Page where the PAV file will be loaded.

processanalystpopup.name: ProcessAnalystPopup
processanalystpopup.doc: Displays a Process Analyst page (in a new page child window) at the current mouse position preloaded with the pre-defined Process Analyst View (PAV) file.
processanalystpopup.returns: Window number if the window is successfully displayed. Otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the page that contains Process Analyst object(s). For example, pages based on the Process Analyst templates found in the Tab_Style_Include project.
paramDocs.iFileLocation: PAV file location code for the PAV file, see PA doc LoadFromFile() for details.
paramDocs.iButtonMask: Bit mask for removing command buttons from the PA, bit flags as shown below:
paramDocs.sObjName: Name of the PA object on the given Page where the PAV file will be loaded. If this parameter is not specified or empty string, it is defaulted to the object name used in the tab style templates, that is "_templatePA1".
paramDocs.iMode: The mode of the window (see WinNewAt() for details).

processanalystselect.name: ProcessAnalystSelect
processanalystselect.doc: Works like the existing Cicode Function TrnSelect(). It allows a set of pens to be selected before displaying the PA page. When PageProcessAnalystPens() is called after ProcessAnalystSelect(), the pens specified by both functions will be available in the final PA display. You can also repeat the call sequence of ProcessAnalystSelect() and ProcessAnalystSetPen() multiple times to set up multiple PA objects for the same page before displaying the page.
processanalystselect.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iWindow: The window number (returned from the WinNumber() function):
paramDocs.sPage: The name of the page that displays the PA.
paramDocs.sObjName: The name of the PA object. If this is not specified, it is defaulted to "_TemplatePA1" which is the name used by the built-in templates.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster that is associated with any trend tag for this PA. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".
paramDocs.iButtonMask: Bit mask for removing command buttons from the PA, bit flags as shown below:
paramDocs.iFileLocation: PAV file location code for the PAV file, see PA doc LoadFromFile() for details.

processanalystsetpen.name: ProcessAnalystSetPen
processanalystsetpen.doc: Works like the existing function TrnSetPen(). Allows a new pen to be added to a PA display. The pane defaults to the first pane of the PA if it is not specified.
processanalystsetpen.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iPen: Pen number. The allowed values are:
paramDocs.sTag: The trend tag name to be assigned to the pen.
paramDocs.sObjName: The name of the PA object. If this is set to "-2", the pen is set to the next displayed PA page set up by ProcessAnalystSelect(). If the specified ObjName is valid, the changes will be applied to the currently displayed PA. Otherwise, the function will try to set the pen to the specified object on the currently displayed page. If this parameter is not specified or is an empty string, it will default to the object name used in the tab style templates, that is "_templatePA1".
paramDocs.iPane: Optional number of the pane where the trend or variable tags are added. Please see the same parameter for function PageProcessAnalystPens() for details. Defaulted to 0, that is, the first pane.
paramDocs.iPenType: Pen type for creation. The allowed values are:

processanalystwin.name: ProcessAnalystWin
processanalystwin.doc: Displays a Process Analyst page (in a new window) preloaded with the pre-defined Process Analyst View (PAV) file.
processanalystwin.returns: Window number if the window is successfully displayed. Otherwise -1 is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the page that contains Process Analyst object(s). For example, pages based on the Process Analyst templates found in the Tab_Style_Include project.
paramDocs.iMode: The mode of the window (see WinNewAt() for details).
paramDocs.iFileLocation: PAV file location code for the PAV file, see PA doc LoadFromFile for details.
paramDocs.iButtonMask: Bit mask for removing command buttons from the PA, bit flags as shown below:
paramDocs.sObjName: Name of the PA object on the given Page where the PAV file will be loaded. If this parameter is not specified or empty string, it is defaulted to the object name used in the tab style templates, that is "_templatePA1".

processisclient.name: ProcessIsClient
processisclient.doc: Determines if the currently executing process contains a Client component.
processisclient.returns: TRUE (1) if the process contains a Client component, otherwise FALSE (0).

processisserver.name: ProcessIsServer
processisserver.doc: Determines if the currently executing process contains a particular server component.
processisserver.returns: TRUE (1) if the process contains the specified component, otherwise FALSE (0).

paramDocs.sServerType: Case insensitive string specifying the type of server to check for. Supported values are "IOServer", "Trend", "Alarm" and "Report".
paramDocs.sClusterName: Optional case insensitive string specifying the cluster name to combine with the server type specified in the first argument and the server name (if specified).
paramDocs.sServerName: Optional case insensitive string specifying a server name to combine with the server type specified in the first argument and the cluster name (if specified).

processrestart.name: ProcessRestart
processrestart.doc: Restarts the current process in which Cicode is running.
processrestart.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise the following error is returned:

productinfo.name: ProductInfo
productinfo.doc: Returns information about the Plant SCADA product.
productinfo.returns: The product information. An empty string will be returned if the type is invalid.

projectinfo.name: ProjectInfo
projectinfo.doc: Returns information about a particular project, which is identified by a project enumerated number.
projectinfo.returns: The specified project information. An empty string will be returned if the project number or type is invalid

paramDocs.iProject: Project number. This is a sequential number generated by the Compiler starting from 0,1,2,3,4,5.... to 1026, so the maximum include projects are limited to 1027.

projectrestartget.name: ProjectRestartGet
projectrestartget.doc: Gets the path to the project to be run the next time Plant SCADA is restarted. You need to have a project already set using either ProjectSet or ProjectRestartSet. Use this function with the Shutdown() function to shut down and then restart the project that is currently running.
projectrestartget.returns: The path to the project to be run the next time Plant SCADA is restarted.

projectrestartset.name: ProjectRestartSet
projectrestartset.doc: Sets the path to the project to be run the next time Plant SCADA is restarted.
projectrestartset.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPath: The path to the project. You need to use the full path.

projectset.name: ProjectSet
projectset.doc: Sets either the name or the path of the project to be run next time Plant SCADA is restarted. The project path is written to the [CtEdit]Run parameter.
projectset.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sProject: The name of the project (for example "DEMO"), or the path to the project. If you specify the path to the project, you need to use the full path. If you do not specify a project, the current project will be used.

prompt.name: Prompt
prompt.doc: Displays a message in the prompt line (AN=2) on the operator's computer.
prompt.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

pulse.name: Pulse
pulse.doc: Pulses (jogs) a variable tag on, then off. The variable tag is switched ON (1) and two seconds later it is switched OFF (0). The exact period of the pulse is determined by the communication channel to the I/O device. If the communication channel is busy, the pulse time may be longer than two seconds. The code in the I/O device should not be dependant on a pulse time of exactly 2 seconds. Use the pulse as a trigger only.
pulse.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

qualitycreate.name: QualityCreate
qualitycreate.doc: Creates a quality value based on the quality fields provided. When the value of a particular quality field is out of range, the value of its corresponding part in the returned quality remains at 0, and hardware error is generated.
qualitycreate.returns: The Quality value of the element.

paramDocs.bOverride: Specifies the Tag Status Override Flag.
paramDocs.bControlInhibit: Specifies the Tag Status Control Inhibit Flag.
paramDocs.datasourceErrorCode: Specifies the data source error code.

qualitygetpart.name: QualityGetPart
qualitygetpart.doc: Extracts a requested part of the quality value from a variable tag's quality item.
qualitygetpart.returns: The value of the requested Quality part (see tables below), or -1 if error.

qualityisbad.name: QualityIsBad
qualityisbad.doc: This function will return a value indicating whether the general part of quality is bad.

qualityiscontrolinhibit.name: QualityIsControlInhibit
qualityiscontrolinhibit.doc: Returns a value indicating whether the tag is in Control Inhibit Mode.
qualityiscontrolinhibit.returns: 0: the tag is not in Control inhibit Mode.

qualityisgood.name: QualityIsGood
qualityisgood.doc: This function will return a value indicating whether the general part of quality is good.

qualityisoverride.name: QualityIsOverrride
qualityisoverride.doc: Returns a value indicating whether the tag is in Override Mode.
qualityisoverride.returns: 0: the tag is not in Override Mode.

qualityisuncertain.name: QualityIsUncertain
qualityisuncertain.doc: This function will return a value indicating whether the general part of quality is uncertain.

qualitysetpart.name: QualitySetPart
qualitysetpart.doc: Sets a Quality part’s value to the QUALITY variable. This function can only be used to manipulate the quality of Cicode variables. The quality item of a variable tag element (for example, 'Tag1.Field.Q') can only be used by QualityGetPart() as it is read only.
qualitysetpart.returns: The modified Quality value, or the original value if the given part is not applicable.

paramDocs.value: The new value for the given part.

qualitytostr.name: QualityToStr
qualitytostr.doc: Returns a textual representation of the quality.
qualitytostr.returns: A textual representation of the quality, or an empty string if the part given is not applicable.

paramDocs.part: Specifies the part of quality to obtain the textual representation.
paramDocs.localized: The flag indicating if the returned text should be in native language or in Runtime localized language.

queclose.name: QueClose
queclose.doc: Closes a queue opened with the QueOpen() function. All data is flushed from the queue.
queclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hQue: The queue handle, returned from the QueOpen() function. The queue handle identifies the table where all data on the associated queue is stored.

quelength.name: QueLength
quelength.doc: Gets the current length of the queue.
quelength.returns: The current length of the queue. If the queue is closed then 0 is returned.

paramDocs.hQue: The queue handle, returned from the QueOpen() function. The queue handle identifies the table where all data on the associated queue is stored.

queopen.name: QueOpen
queopen.doc: Open a queue for reading and writing data elements. Use this function to create a new queue or open an existing queue. Use queues for sending data from one task to another or for other buffering operations.
queopen.returns: The queue handle, or -1 if the queue cannot be opened. The queue handle identifies the table where all data on the associated queue is stored.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the queue. You need to use the following syntax:
paramDocs.Mode: The mode of the queue open:

quepeek.name: QuePeek
quepeek.doc: Searches a queue for a queue element. You can search for the element by specifying a string, an integer, or both. You can remove the element from the queue by adding 8 to the Mode.
quepeek.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hQue: The queue handle, returned from the QueOpen() function. The queue handle identifies the table where all data on the associated queue is stored.
paramDocs.nType: The number to search for (if using the search mode for a matching number). If you are using a matching string mode, the number found is returned in Type. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.Str: The string to search for (if using the search mode for a matching string). If you are using a matching number mode, the string found is returned in Str. Must be a String type variable.

queread.name: QueRead
queread.doc: Reads data from a queue, starting from the head of the queue. Data is returned in the same order as it was written onto the queue and is removed from the queue when read. If the Mode is 0 (non-blocking) and the queue is empty, the function returns with an error. If the Mode is 1 (blocking) the function does not return until another Cicode task writes data onto the queue.
queread.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hQue: The queue handle, returned from the QueOpen() function. The queue handle identifies the table where all data on the associated queue is stored.
paramDocs.nType: The integer to read from the queue (written to the queue as Type by the QueWrite() function). Must be an Integer type variable.
paramDocs.Str: The string to read from the queue (written to the queue as Str by the QueWrite() function). Must be a String type variable.

quewrite.name: QueWrite
quewrite.doc: Writes an integer and string onto the end of a queue. The integer and string have no meaning to the queue system, they are just passed from QueWrite() to QueRead(). Queue data is written to the end of the queue. When the data is later read from the queue, it is returned on a first-in-first-out basis.
quewrite.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

report.name: Report

report.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.ReportName: The name of the report to run (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.ReportName).
paramDocs.sClusterName: Name of the cluster in which the report resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the report server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

repsetcontrol.name: RepSetControl
repsetcontrol.doc: Sets report control information to temporarily override the normal settings for a specified report. You can change the report schedule for a periodic report, and run one-time or event-triggered reports. These new settings are set on both the primary and standby report servers, but are not saved to the database. When you restart your system, Plant SCADA uses the existing settings, defined in the Reports database.
repsetcontrol.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.ReportName: The name of the report (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.ReportName).
paramDocs.nType: The type of report control information to set:
paramDocs.Data: The new data value, dependent on the Type.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Name of the cluster in which the report resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the report server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

scheduleitemadd.name: ScheduleItemAdd
scheduleitemadd.doc: The ScheduleItemAdd function adds a new schedule to the scheduler engine. It returns the Id of the schedule which can be used for modifying, setting recurrence and deleting this schedule.

paramDocs.Equipment: The name of the equipment to browse.
paramDocs.Start: The start time of the schedule. The type of this parameter is TIMESTAMP. Use TimestampCreate or StrToTimestamp to get a TIMESTAMP value.
paramDocs.End: The end time of the schedule. The type of this parameter is TIMESTAMP. Use TimestampCreate or StrToTimestamp to get a TIMESTAMP value.

scheduleitemdelete.name: ScheduleItemDelete
scheduleitemdelete.doc: The ScheduleItemDelete function deletes an existing schedule.
scheduleitemdelete.returns: Returns 0 if successful otherwise it returns an error.

paramDocs.ID: The unique ID of the schedule within the schedule engine.

scheduleitemmodify.name: ScheduleItemModify
scheduleitemmodify.doc: The ScheduleItemModify function modifies an existing schedule.
scheduleitemmodify.returns: Returns 0 if successful otherwise it returns an error.

paramDocs.ID: The unique ID of the schedule within the schedule engine
paramDocs.Start: The start time of the schedule. The type of this parameter is TIMESTAMP. Use TimestampCreate or StrToTimestamp to get a TIMESTAMP value.
paramDocs.End: The end time of the schedule. The type of this parameter is TIMESTAMP. Use TimestampCreate or StrToTimestamp to get a TIMESTAMP value.

scheduleitemsetrepeat.name: ScheduleItemSetRepeat
scheduleitemsetrepeat.doc: The ScheduleItemSetRepeat function adds recurrence information to an existing schedule to the scheduler engine. The same function is used if the schedule already has recurrence information that need to be changed.
scheduleitemsetrepeat.returns: Returns 0 if successful otherwise it returns an error.

paramDocs.ID: The existing schedule id to apply recurrence.
paramDocs.Freq: The type of the recurrence: 4 – daily, 5 – weekly, 6- monthly, 7 – yearly, 8 – special days.
paramDocs.Interval: The interval of the recurrence. 1 – every 1 day/week/month etc., 2 – every second and so on.
paramDocs.WeekDay: The first day of week – Sunday (0) or Monday (1)
paramDocs.WeekDayMask: The day of week mask. Defines day of week where recurrence happens.
paramDocs.MaxRec: The maximum number recurrences (-1 means does not stop)
paramDocs.RecUntil: The time specifies the time until recurrence is occurring. The type of this parameter is TIMESTAMP. Use TimestampCreate or StrToTimestamp to get a TIMESTAMP value. To create a recurring schedule that does not end use TimestampCreate(1601, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1)
paramDocs.DayOrd: Day ordinal. Applicable for monthly and yearly recurrence patterns. Can be 1-4 or -1 (every 1, second, third, fourth or last week of a month).
paramDocs.SpecialInc: Defined whether the special day is included in the pattern. 0 – none, 1 – every, 2 – selected.
paramDocs.GroupIds: A list of group’s ID included in the recurring pattern (used only when SpecialIncl is defined as 2 ("selected")).

semclose.name: SemClose
semclose.doc: Closes a semaphore opened with SemOpen(). You should close all semaphores when they are no longer required, because they consume memory. If any Cicode tasks are waiting on this semaphore, the tasks are released with an error.
semclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hSem: The semaphore handle, returned from the SemOpen() function. The semaphore handle identifies the table where all data on the associated semaphore is stored.

semopen.name: SemOpen
semopen.doc: Opens a semaphore for access control. When the semaphore is opened, it is initially signaled. Use a semaphore for controlling access to a restricted device, for example, to stop another Cicode task accessing a device while it is in use. You might require semaphores for some Cicode operations, because they can access a device that is critical. (Cicode is a multi-tasking system.)
semopen.returns: The semaphore handle, or -1 if the semaphore was not opened successfully. The semaphore handle identifies the table where all data on the associated semaphore is stored.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the semaphore. Follow the naming convention outlined in the topic Tag Name Syntax in the main help.

semsignal.name: SemSignal
semsignal.doc: Signals a semaphore. If several Cicode tasks are waiting on this semaphore, the first task is released. This function is a blocking function. It will block the calling Cicode task until the operation is complete.
semsignal.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hSem: The semaphore handle, returned from the SemOpen() function. The semaphore handle identifies the table where all data on the associated semaphore is stored.

semwait.name: SemWait
semwait.doc: Waits on a semaphore to be signaled. This function is a blocking function. It will block the calling Cicode task until the operation is complete.
semwait.returns: 0 (zero) if the semaphore has been gained, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hSem: The semaphore handle, returned from the SemOpen() function. The semaphore handle identifies the table where all data on the associated semaphore is stored.

sendkeys.name: SendKeys
sendkeys.doc: Sends a keystroke (or string of keystrokes) to a window as if they were typed on the keyboard. The window receives input focus and is brought to the foreground.
sendkeys.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sTitle: The title (caption) of the destination window.
paramDocs.sKeys: The key (or keys) to send to sTitle.

serialkey.name: SerialKey
serialkey.doc: Redirects all serial characters from a port to the keyboard. If using a keyboard attached to a serial port, you should call this function at startup, so that Plant SCADA copies all characters (read from the port) to the keyboard. The Port needs to be defined in the Ports database.
serialkey.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPort: The name of the port connected to the serial keyboard.

paramDocs.iSession: Handle to a browse session previously opened by a ServerBrowseOpen call.

serverbrowsefirst.name: ServerBrowseFirst
serverbrowsefirst.doc: The ServerBrowseFirst function places the data browse cursor at the first record.
serverbrowsefirst.returns: 0 (zero) if the server browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: Handle to a browse session previously opened by a ServerBrowseOpen call.

serverbrowsegetfield.name: ServerBrowseGetField
serverbrowsegetfield.doc: The ServerBrowseGetField function retrieves the value of the specified field from the record the data browse cursor is currently referencing.
serverbrowsegetfield.returns: The value of the specified field as a string. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. The last error should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred.

paramDocs.iSession: Handle to a browse session previously opened by a ServerBrowseOpen call.
paramDocs.sFieldName: The name of the field that references the value to be returned. Supported fields are:

serverbrowsenext.name: ServerBrowseNext
serverbrowsenext.doc: The ServerBrowseNext function moves the data browse cursor forward one record. If you call this function after you have reached the end of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
serverbrowsenext.returns: 0 (zero) if the server browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: Handle to a browse session previously opened by a ServerBrowseOpen call.

serverbrowsenumrecords.name: ServerBrowseNumRecords
serverbrowsenumrecords.doc: The ServerBrowseNumRecords function returns the number of records that match the filter criteria.
serverbrowsenumrecords.returns: The number of records that matched the filter criteria. A value of 0 denotes that no records matched. A value of -1 denotes that the browse session is unable to provide a fixed number. This could be the case if the data being browsed changed during the browse session.

paramDocs.iSession: Handle to a browse session previously opened by a ServerBrowseOpen call.

serverbrowseopen.name: ServerBrowseOpen
serverbrowseopen.doc: The ServerBrowseOpen function initiates a new browse session and returns a handle to the new session that can be used in subsequent data browse function calls.
serverbrowseopen.returns: An integer handle to the browse session. Returns -1 on error.

paramDocs.Filter: A semicolon delimited list of field name=field value pairs, specifying the records to return during the browse. An empty string indicates that all records will be returned.
paramDocs.Fields: Specifies via a comma-delimited string the columns to be returned during the browse. An empty string indicates that the server will return available columns. Supported fields are:
paramDocs.Clusters: An optional parameter that specifies via a comma delimited string the subset of clusters to browse. An empty string indicates that connected clusters will be browsed.

serverbrowseprev.name: ServerBrowsePrev
serverbrowseprev.doc: The ServerBrowsePrev function moves the data browse cursor back one record. If you call this function after you have reached the beginning of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
serverbrowseprev.returns: 0 (zero) if the server browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: Handle to a browse session previously opened by a ServerBrowseOpen call.

serverdumpkernel.name: ServerDumpKernel
serverdumpkernel.doc: Dumps Kernel data to the KERNEL.DAT file (written to the Logs folder) either on a local server or on a remote server. The server is specified with the server and cluster parameters. Instead of creating a new file subsequent calls to this function will append Kernel data to the KERNEL.DAT file. This is a blocking function.
serverdumpkernel.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The queue or table name (empty for all queues or tables). Only valid if iMode is 0x0020 and 0x0040.
paramDocs.sServer: Specifies the name of the server, as defined in the project, on which kernel data will be dumped.
paramDocs.sCluster: Specifies the cluster of the server on which kernel data will be dumped. This parameter is optional in a single cluster environment.

servergetproperty.name: ServerGetProperty
servergetproperty.doc: This function returns information about a specified server and can be called from any client.
servergetproperty.returns: The value of the server property requested.

paramDocs.sServer: The name of the server to be queried in quotations marks "". Can be prefixed by the name of the host cluster, that is "ClusterName.ServerName".
paramDocs.sProperty: The name of the requested property. Can be one of the following:
paramDocs.sCluster: The cluster of the server to be queried in quotation marks "". This parameter is optional. However, if the Server Name is not local or not specified in ClusterName.ServerName format an error code is returned.

serverinfo.name: ServerInfo
serverinfo.doc: Gets status information on clients and servers.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the client or server, either "Client", "Server", "Alarm", "Trend", or "Report".
paramDocs.Type: The type of information required (depends on the Name you specify):
paramDocs.ClusterName: The name of the cluster that the server belongs to. This is only relevant if:

serverinfoex.name: ServerInfoEx
serverinfoex.doc: Gets status information on clients and servers from a specified component in a multiprocess runtime environment.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the client or server, either "Client", "Server", "Alarm", "Trend", or "Report".
paramDocs.Type: The type of information required (depends on the Name you specify):
paramDocs.Component: Specifies the component name from which to retrieve the status information:
paramDocs.ClusterName: The name of the cluster that the server belongs to. This is only relevant if:
paramDocs.ServerName: Specifies the name of the the I/O Server. This parameter is only required if you are running more than one I/O server process from the same cluster on the same computer and need to instruct the system which process to redirect to. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

serverisonline.name: ServerIsOnline
serverisonline.doc: The ServerIsOnline function checks if the given server can be contacted by the client for giving the online/offline status of the server.
serverisonline.returns: An integer value of online/offline status. Returns 1 for online, 0 for offline.

paramDocs.ServerName: The name of the server to be queried in quotations marks "".
paramDocs.Cluster: The cluster of the server to be queried in quotation marks "". An empty string indicates that the default cluster will be used.
paramDocs.bLocal: The mode of the server status check.

serverreload.name: ServerReload
serverreload.doc: This function can only be called for Alarm, Report and Trend Servers and reloads the server specified by cluster and server name. If the server is not found an error code is returned. ServerReload can be used in blocking or non-blocking modes using the bSync parameter. When used in non-blocking mode, the server status can be returned using the ServerGetProperty function.
serverreload.returns: 0 (zero) if the function was successful. Returns an error if unsuccessful.Outline of errors:

paramDocs.sServer: The name of the server to be reloaded in quotations marks "". Can be prefixed by the name of the host cluster, that is "ClusterName.ServerName".
paramDocs.sCluster: The cluster of the server to be reloaded in quotation marks "". This parameter is optional. However, if the server name is not local or not specified in ClusterName.ServerName format, an error code is returned.
paramDocs.bSync: Specifies whether the function operates in blocking or non-blocking mode. If bSync is set to 1, the function will not return until the server reload is complete. The reload is complete when all the records of all rdb files have been processed and updated. Blocking mode cannot be used from a foreground task (for example on graphic pages). When bSync is set to 0, the function operates in non-blocking mode. You can get the latest status of the reload using the ServerGetProperty function. Default value is 0.

serverrestart.name: ServerRestart
serverrestart.doc: Allows you to restart any specific alarm, report, trend or I/O server from any Cicode node in a system, without affecting other server processes running on the same machine. To call this function, a valid user needs to be logged in.
serverrestart.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise one of the following error codes is returned:

paramDocs.sServerName: The name of the server to restart
paramDocs.sCluster: The cluster the server belongs to. This parameter is optional. If sCluster is not specified the current system cluster is used.

serverrpc.name: ServerRPC
serverrpc.doc: Calls a remote procedure on the Plant SCADA server specified by the ServerName argument. You can call any of the built-in Cicode functions remotely, or your own functions. You pass the Name of the function as a string and pass the arguments for that function in Arg.
serverrpc.returns: The result of the remote function call (as a string). If the function is called in asynchronous mode the result of the remote function cannot be returned, so an empty string is returned. If the function cannot work due to an error, empty string is also returned and the error can be obtained by calling the IsError function. If current user has view-only access on client side, the function will return an error code.

paramDocs.sServerName: Plant SCADA server name where the Cicode function needs to be executed. You can optionally specify this name in <ClusterName>.<ServerName> syntax.
paramDocs.sName: The name of the Cicode function to call remotely as string.
