paramDocs.sArg: The arguments to pass to the function, separated by commas (,).Enclose string arguments in quotes "" and use the string escape character (^) around strings enclosed within a string. If you forget to enclose the string in quotes, then the string is only the first tag found.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster that the server resides in. This argument is optional, as in several situations it may not be required. In single cluster systems, it is not required, or if the current Cicode task already has the correct cluster context for the server you may omit this argument.

servicegetlist.name: ServiceGetList
servicegetlist.doc: Determines the service type(s), cluster name(s), and service name(s) of all services currently running in the component that called this function. It also determines if the client component is running.

setarea.name: SetArea
setarea.doc: Sets the current viewable areas. You can pass a single area number, or a group of areas to set multiple areas. You can only set areas that are flagged for the current user.
setarea.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

setevent.name: SetEvent
setevent.doc: Sets an event callback function by specifying a function handle. You can use this function with the GetEvent function to restore an old event handler.
setevent.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nType: The type of event:
paramDocs.hFn: The function handle, as returned from the GetEvent function.

setlogging.name: SetLogging
setlogging.doc: Adjusts logging parameters while online. The parameters you can modify include the following:
setlogging.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The system parameter name.
paramDocs.Value: The value you would like to set the parameter to.
paramDocs.Persist: Makes the value persistent across restarts by writing the value to the INI file.

shutdown.name: Shutdown
shutdown.doc: Terminates Plant SCADA's operation. Use this function to shut down the Plant SCADA system, otherwise buffered data could be lost. This function impacts the operation of the computer as a whole, it is not process-based. If a computer is the target for shutdown, all Plant SCADA processes on the computer will be shutdown.
shutdown.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sDest: The destination computer(s) on which Plant SCADA will be shut down, as a string:
paramDocs.sProject: The full path of the project to run on restart as a string. The path is written to the configuration files and is used when the system restarts. The default value is "", which means that no changes are made to the configuration and the current project is restarted.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster to which the machine(s) named in Dest belong. This is not required if:
paramDocs.CallEvent: Flag for initiating a user-specified shutdown event prior to shutting down. Refer to OnEvent() type code for the value of shutdown event.

shutdownform.name: ShutdownForm
shutdownform.doc: Displays a dialog box to verify that the user really wants to shut down the Plant SCADA system. If the user selects [Yes], Plant SCADA is shut down.
shutdownform.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

shutdownmode.name: ShutdownMode
shutdownmode.doc: Gets the mode of the last Shutdown function call. The mode is useful to identify the type of Shutdown that was performed.
shutdownmode.returns: The shutdown mode set when shutdown was called.

sign.name: Sign
sign.doc: Gets the sign of a number.

sin.name: Sin
sin.doc: Calculates the trigonometric sine of an angle.

sleep.name: Sleep
sleep.doc: Suspends the current Cicode task for a specified number of seconds. After the time delay, the Cicode task wakes and continues execution. If the sleep time is 0, the Cicode task is pre-empted for 1 time slice only.
sleep.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Seconds: The number of seconds. Set to 0 to pre-empt the task for one time-slice.

sleepms.name: SleepMS
sleepms.doc: Suspends the current Cicode task for a specified number of milliseconds. After the time delay, the Cicode task wakes and continues execution. This function is similar to the Sleep function but with greater resolution.
sleepms.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Milliseconds: The number of milliseconds (1000 milliseconds per second). Set to 0 to pre-empt the task for one time-slice. Be careful not to use a value that is too small. Setting the value to 0 would generally have no desirable effect.

soearchive.name: SOEArchive
soearchive.doc: Use this function to archive event journals. To use this function you need to log in with a user assigned to a role that has full privileges (privilege 1..8).
soearchive.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sClusterName: Optional cluster on which to perform mounting operation. If not specified, the operation will be performed on all clusters.

soedismount.name: SOEDismount
soedismount.doc: Use this function to dismount archive volume. To use this function you will need to log in with a role (e.g.Engineer) who has full privilege (privilege 1..8).
soedismount.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sClusterName: Optional cluster on which to perform mounting operation. If not specified, the operation will be performed on all clusters.

soeeventadd.name: SOEEventAdd
soeeventadd.doc: Use this function to insert an event into the Event Journal.
soeeventadd.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.TimeStamp: The time of the inserted event.
paramDocs.Tag: Alarm tag associated with the event. This can be Cluster.Tag or Tag if running on a single cluster system. If not specified the event is classed as a ‘User’ event.
paramDocs.Cluster: Specify if running on a multi-cluster system and Tag has been specified. If Tag has not been specified and the Cluster is blank, the User event will be broadcast to all of the clusters to which the client is currently connected.

soemount.name: SOEMount
soemount.doc: Use this function to mount an archive volume. Archived data from the volume can be displayed on the Alarm Summary and Sequence of events page. To use this function you will need to log in with a role (e.g.Engineer) who has full privilege (privilege 1..8).
soemount.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sClusterName: Optional cluster on which to perform mounting operation. If not specified, the operation will be performed on all clusters.

spcalarms.name: SPCAlarms
spcalarms.doc: Returns the status of the specified SPC alarm. This function is used to configure SPC alarms, by defining alarms with this trigger in Advanced Alarms.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.AlarmType: The description of the alarm type. The following types are valid:

spcclientinfo.name: SPCClientInfo
spcclientinfo.doc: Returns SPC data for the given SPC tag. The information retrieved through this function is from the cache maintained by the client. This function will give a faster response than the related functions which access the SPC (trend) server.
spcclientinfo.returns: The requested data specified by iType. It is of type REAL.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.

spcgethistogramtable.name: SPCGetHistogramTable
spcgethistogramtable.doc: Returns an array containing the frequencies of particular ranges for the given SPC tag. The histogram structure is implied in the order of the table as follows - the first array element is the data less than -3 sigma. The second value is the data between -3 sigma and -3 sigma plus the bar width etc. The last value is the data greater than +3 sigma.
spcgethistogramtable.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. The histogram table is written to TableVariable.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.iNoBars: The number of bars in the table. The valid range is restricted to values from 7 to 100. This also indicates the size of the array to be returned.
paramDocs.TableVariable: The Cicode array that will store the histogram data. The number of elements in the array needs to be equal to (or greater than) iNoBars. Must be a Real type global array variable.

spcgetsubgrouptable.name: SPCGetSubgroupTable
spcgetsubgrouptable.doc: Returns an array containing the specified subgroup's elements with the mean, range and standard deviation. The data will be in the following order:
spcgetsubgrouptable.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. The subgroup's data is written to TableVariable.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.iSubgroup: The number of the subgroup being displayed whose data is to be retrieved. Zero ('0') represents the latest subgroup.
paramDocs.TableVariable: The first element of the Cicode array that will store the sample data. The number of elements in the array needs to be equal to (or greater than) the subgroup size + 3. Must be a Real type global array variable.

spcplot.name: SPCPlot
spcplot.doc: This function is designed to work only on an SPCXRSChart page. It prints a single page showing three separate trends of the SPC Mean, Range, and Standard Deviation. The Mean needs to be at nAN, the Range at AN + 1, and the Standard Deviation at AN + 2. You can specify a title and a comment for the plot, and whether it is printed in color or in black and white.
spcplot.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPort: The name of the printer port to which the plot will be printed. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks. For example LPT1:, to print to the local printer, or \\Pserver\canon1 using UNC to print to a network printer.
paramDocs.nAN: The animation point at which the Mean chart is currently situated. The Range and Standard Deviation charts need to be on the next two consecutive animation numbers. For example, if the Mean chart is at animation point 40, the Range chart needs to be at animation point 41, and the Standard Deviation chart needs to be at animation point 42.
paramDocs.sTitle: The title of the trend plot.
paramDocs.sComment: The comment that is to display beneath the title of the trend plot. You do not have to enter a comment.
paramDocs.nMode: The color mode of the printer.

spcprocessxrsget.name: SPCProcessXRSGet
spcprocessxrsget.doc: Gets the process mean, range, and standard deviation overrides for the specified SPC tag. The values that are returned are the values that are currently being used by the SPC (trend) server, not necessarily the values specified in the SPC Tag definition.
spcprocessxrsget.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. The process mean is written to XVariable, the process range to RVariable, and the standard deviation to SVariable.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.XVariable: The Cicode variable that stores the process mean (X double bar). A constant is not allowed. Must be a Real type global variable.
paramDocs.RVariable: The Cicode variable that stores the range (R). A constant is not allowed. Must be a Real type global variable.
paramDocs.SVariable: The Cicode variable that stores the standard deviation (S). A constant is not allowed. Must be a Real type global variable.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster of the SPC tag.

spcprocessxrsset.name: SPCProcessXRSSet
spcprocessxrsset.doc: Sets the process mean, range and standard deviation overrides for the specified SPC tag. The values entered here will override Plant SCADA's automatic calculations, and the overrides specified in the SPC Tags definition.
spcprocessxrsset.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.rMean: The new value of process mean (x double bar) to set.
paramDocs.rRange: The new value of process range to set.
paramDocs.rStdDev: The new value of process standard deviation to set.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster of the SPC tag.

spcsetlimit.name: SPCSetLimit
spcsetlimit.doc: Sets the upper or lower control limits of X-bar, range, or standard deviation charts. Using this function will only set the controller limits on the Client display which will not affect the SPC Alarms. To set the server control limits, use the SPCProcessXRSSet function.
spcsetlimit.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the SPC chart is located.
paramDocs.nType: The SPC type:
paramDocs.Value: The value for the control limit.
paramDocs.Setting: Automatic calculation or manual setting of control limits:

spcspeclimitget.name: SPCSpecLimitGet
spcspeclimitget.doc: Gets the process Upper and Lower Specification Limits (USL and LSL) for the specified SPC tag. The values that are returned are the values that are currently being used by the SPC (trend) server, not necessarily the values specified in the SPC Tag definition.
spcspeclimitget.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. The LSL is written to LSLVariable, while the USL is written to USLVariable.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.LSLVariable: The Cicode variable that stores the Lower Specification Limit (LSL). Do not specify a constant in this field. Must be a Real type global variable.
paramDocs.USLVariable: The Cicode variable that stores the Upper Specification Limit (USL). Do not specify a constant in this field. Must be a Real type global variable.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster of the SPC tag.

spcspeclimitset.name: SPCSpecLimitSet
spcspeclimitset.doc: Sets the process Upper and Lower Specification Limits (USL and LSL) for the specified SPC tag. The values entered here will override those specified in the SPC Tags definition.
spcspeclimitset.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.rLSL: The new value of Lower Specification Limit (LSL) to set.
paramDocs.rUSL: The new value of Upper Specification Limit (USL) to set.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster of the SPC tag.

spcsubgroupsizeget.name: SPCSubgroupSizeGet
spcsubgroupsizeget.doc: Gets the subgroup size for the specified SPC tag. The value that is returned is the value that is currently being used by the SPC (trend) server, not necessarily the value specified in the SPC Tag definition.
spcsubgroupsizeget.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. The subgroup size is written to SizeVariable.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.SizeVariable: The Cicode variable that stores the subgroup size. This variable needs to be defined as a global of type INT. A constant is not allowed. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster of the SPC tag.

spcsubgroupsizeset.name: SPCSubgroupSizeSet
spcsubgroupsizeset.doc: Sets a new subgroup size for the specified SPC tag. The new subgroup size becomes the new size as long as the SPC (trend) server is running. The subgroup size is updated first in the SPC server, which then informs the clients to update. This will force re-calculation of SPC values (UCL and LCL) across the span of any displayed charts.
spcsubgroupsizeset.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned.

paramDocs.sSPCTag: The SPC Tag name as defined in SPC Tags.
paramDocs.iSize: The new size of the subgroup to set.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster of the SPC tag.

sqlappend.name: SQLAppend
sqlappend.doc: Appends a query string to the SQL buffer. Cicode cannot send an SQL query that is longer than 255 characters. If you have an SQL query that is longer than the 255 character limit, you can split the query into smaller strings, and use this function to append the query in the SQL buffer.
sqlappend.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hGeneral: The handle either to the DB connection object (returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function) or to the query handle (returned from SQLQueryCreate()). When it is the connection handle, the operation is performed on the default query in that DB connection object. When it is the query handle, the operation is performed on that query through the DB object which is associated to it.
paramDocs.String: The query string to append to the SQL buffer.

sqlbegintran.name: SQLBeginTran
sqlbegintran.doc: Starts a database transaction. When you make a transaction, your changes are not written to the database until you call the SQLCommit() function. Alternatively, you can use the SQLRollBack() function to discard all changes made during the transaction.
sqlbegintran.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlcall.name: SQLCall
sqlcall.doc: Executes an SQL query on a database. The function returns the number of rows affected by the executed query. With this function, you can execute any SQL query or command supported by the SQL database. If it returns some data (as for SELECT query), the data is ignored.
sqlcall.returns: The number of affected records or -1 if an error is detected. (For details call the SQLErrMsg() function). The presence of error code can be tested by calling the IsError CiCode function.

paramDocs.hGeneral: The handle either to the DB connection object (returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function) or to the query handle (returned from SQLQueryCreate()). When it is the connection handle and sSelect is an empty string, the operation is performed on the first query in that DB connection object. When it is the query handle, the operation is performed on that query through the DB object which is associated to it.
paramDocs.sSelect: The SQL query to be sent to the SQL database.

sqlcancel.name: SQLCancel
sqlcancel.doc: This function cancels both the current operation on the given connection and all other pending operations on the given connection. The cancellation means that the current operation on the SCADA side is immediately finished. The cancelled operation returns error code 299 and its state on the database side should be considered as undefined, that is, it is not known that it either succeeded, partially succeeded, or was unsuccessful.
sqlcancel.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg() function).

sqlclose.name: SQLClose
sqlclose.doc: Closes a SQL connection between the DB connection object specified by the function's parameter and a database. The DB connection object is not deleted from the memory until calling SQLDispose function.
sqlclose.returns: 0 if success, otherwise an error code (for details call the SQLErrMsg() function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from the SQLCreate() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlcommit.name: SQLCommit
sqlcommit.doc: Commits (to the database) all changes made within a transaction. If you call the SQLBeginTran() function to begin a transaction, you need to call the SQLCommit() function to save the changes you make to the database during that transaction (with the Insert, Delete, and Update SQL commands).
sqlcommit.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg() function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlconnect.name: SQLConnect
sqlconnect.doc: Creates an internal database connection object and tries to connect it to a database specified by the connection string. Returns a handle to the database connection object for use by the other database functions.
sqlconnect.returns: The handle to the database connection object if the connection is successful, otherwise -1 is returned. (For details call the SQLErrMsg() function). The handle identifies the database connection object where details of the associated SQL connection to a DB are stored.

paramDocs.sConnect: The connection string, in the format:

sqlcreate.name: SQLCreate
sqlcreate.doc: Creates an internal DB connection object and returns a handle to the object for use by the other DB functions. The object is in disconnected state and can be connected to a database by executing the SQLOpen function.
sqlcreate.returns: The handle to the DB connection object if the connection is successful, otherwise -1 is returned. (For details call the SQLErrMsg() function). The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection to a DB are stored.

paramDocs.sConnect: The connection string, in the format:

sqldisconnect.name: SQLDisconnect
sqldisconnect.doc: Closes the SQL connection to a database and disposes the DB connection object specified by the function parameter.
sqldisconnect.returns: 0 if success, otherwise an error code (for details call the SQLErrMsg() function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from the SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqldispose.name: SQLDispose
sqldispose.doc: Disposes the DB connection object specified by its parameter. If there is an active SQL connection to a database, the SQL connection has to be closed before disposal.
sqldispose.returns: 0 – if success, otherwise an error code (For details call the SQLErrMsg() function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either the SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlend.name: SQLEnd
sqlend.doc: The function can be called with:
sqlend.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned. (For details on the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg() function).

sqlerrmsg.name: SQLErrMsg
sqlerrmsg.doc: Returns an error message from either a particular data object or entire data system. If a 307 error code occurs when one of the SQL functions is called, an SQL error message is generated. Call this function to get that error message.

paramDocs.hGeneral: The handle to any data object either to the database connection object, recordset or query. The default value is -1 and then the function returns the error message for entire SQL system.

sqlexec.name: SQLExec
sqlexec.doc: Executes an SQL query on a database. With this function, you can execute any SQL query or command supported by the SQL database.
sqlexec.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg() function).

paramDocs.hGeneral: The handle either to the DB connection object (returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function) or to the query handle (returned from SQLQueryCreate()). When it is the connection handle and sSelect is an empty string, the operation is performed on the first query in that DB connection object. When it is the query handle, the operation is performed on that query through the DB object which is associated to it.
paramDocs.sSelect: The SQL query to be sent to the SQL database.

sqlfieldinfo.name: SQLFieldInfo
sqlfieldinfo.doc: Gets information about the fields or columns selected by a SQL query. The function returns the name and width of the specified field. If you call the function within a loop, you can return the names and sizes of all the fields in the database.
sqlfieldinfo.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hField: The field (or column) handle, indicating the position of the field in the database.
paramDocs.sName: Output Parameter: A string in which the function stores the field name. The argument is returned by the function. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.Width: Output Parameter: An integer in which the function stores the maximum number of characters in the field. The argument is returned by the function. Must be an Integer type variable.

sqlgetfield.name: SQLGetField
sqlgetfield.doc: Gets field or column data from a database field. To get to a specific record in the recordset, use either the SQLNext() or SQLPrev() functions or, in case of disconnected recordsets, the nRowIndex argument.
sqlgetfield.returns: The field or column data (as a string).

paramDocs.sField: The name of the field or column.
paramDocs.nRowIndex: If hGeneral is a connection handle and nRowindex is not equal -1, then the function returns an empty string.

sqlgetrecordset.name: SQLGetRecordset
sqlgetrecordset.doc: Executes an SQL query on a database and returns a handle to any resulting disconnected recordset. All recordsets created in this way should be closed by the SQLEnd() function. If unsuccessful, the function returns an invalid handle and an error code is returned (can be tested by IsError()). In case of no data returned, the function returns an invalid handle and no error. With this function, you can execute any SQL query or command supported by the SQL database, but it is designed mainly to work with queries returning data like for example SELECT. Queries which don't return database data, like INSERT or UPDATE, should be executed via SQLCall.
sqlgetrecordset.returns: The handle to a recordset holding the result of the query. If unsuccessful an invalid handle and an error code are returned (for details call the SQLErrMsg() function). If no data is returned, an invalid handle and no error message are returned. The presence of an error can be tested by calling the IsError() Cicode function

paramDocs.hGeneral: The handle either to the DB connection object (returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function) or to the query handle (returned from SQLQueryCreate()). When it is the connection handle and sSelect is an empty string, the operation is performed on the first query in that DB connection object. When it is the query handle, the operation is performed on that query through the DB object which is associated to it.
paramDocs.sSelect: The SQL query to be sent to the SQL database.

sqlgetscalar.name: SQLGetScalar
sqlgetscalar.doc: Executes an SQL query on a database. The value from the first column of the first row is returned. With this function, you can execute any SQL query or command supported by the SQL database. If it doesn’t return any data (like INSERT or UPDATE), a respective error code is set which can be tested by calling IsError()).
sqlgetscalar.returns: String representing a value from the first column and the first row of the result of executing the SQL query. If the value is NULL, the string is empty and isNull parameter is set to TRUE. If there are no records in the result, the string is empty and the error code is set to 294. For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg() function. The presence of error code can be tested by calling the IsError() Cicode function.

paramDocs.hGeneral: The handle either to the DB connection object (returned from either SQLCreate or SQLConnect function) or to the query handle (returned from SQLQueryCreate). When it is the connection handle and sSelect is an empty string, the operation is performed on the first query in that DB connection object. When it is the query handle, the operation is performed on that query through the DB object which is associated to it.
paramDocs.sSelect: The SQL query to be sent to the SQL database.
paramDocs.isNull: Output Parameter: Indicated whether the returned variable is NULL. The argument is returned by the function.

sqlinfo.name: SQLInfo
sqlinfo.doc: Gets information about a database connection, recordset or query properties.

paramDocs.nType: The type of information to get:

sqlisnullfield.name: SQLIsNullField
sqlisnullfield.doc: Checks presence of null value in field from a recordset. To get to a specific record in the recordset, use either the SQLNext()/SQLPrev() functions or the nRowIndex argument.
sqlisnullfield.returns: TRUE if the value is NULL, FALSE otherwise.

paramDocs.sField: The name of the field or column.
paramDocs.nRowIndex: The number of the row which data is requested. The first row has index 0. -1 means that an internal pointer is used instead. The pointer can be moved forward and backward by executing SQLNext() or SQLPrev() functions.

sqlnext.name: SQLNext
sqlnext.doc: Gets the next database record from an SQL query. Use the SQLExec/SQLGetRecordset function to select a number of records or rows from the SQL database, and then use the SQLNext function to step through each record separately.
sqlnext.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

sqlnofields.name: SQLNoFields
sqlnofields.doc: When the hGeneral is the connection handle, the function returns the number of fields or columns that were returned by the last SQL statement. When the hGeneral is the recordset handle, the function returns the number of fields or columns in the recordset itself.
sqlnofields.returns: The number of fields. A value of 0 is returned if no fields were returned or if an error has been detected. (For details of an error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

sqlnumchange.name: SQLNumChange
sqlnumchange.doc: Gets the number of records that were modified in the last SQL Insert, Update, or Delete statement.
sqlnumchange.returns: The number of records that were modified. A value of 0 is returned if no fields were returned or if an error has occurred. (For details of an error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlnumfields.name: SQLNumFields
sqlnumfields.doc: When hGeneral is the connection handle, the function returns the number of fields or columns that were returned by the last SQL statement. When hGeneral is the recordset handle, the function returns the number of fields or columns in the recordset itself.
sqlnumfields.returns: The number of fields. A value of 0 is returned if no fields were returned or if an error has been detected. (For details of an error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

sqlopen.name: SQLOpen
sqlopen.doc: Opens an SQL connection between the DB connection object specified by the function's parameter and the database defined by the connection string given before as the parameter to either SQLCreate or SQLConnect function.
sqlopen.returns: 0 if success, otherwise an error code (For details call the SQLErrMsg() function)

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either the SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlparamsclearall.name: SQLParamsClearAll
sqlparamsclearall.doc: Remove all parameters associated with a particular connection object.
sqlparamsclearall.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function.)

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlparamssetasint.name: SQLParamsSetAsInt
sqlparamssetasint.doc: Adds or replace a parameterized query parameter and its value in the specified connection. The value of the parameter is given as integer.
sqlparamssetasint.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.
paramDocs.ParamName: The name of the parameter to add or change.
paramDocs.ParamValue: The value of the parameter as an integer.

sqlparamssetasreal.name: SQLParamsSetAsReal
sqlparamssetasreal.doc: Adds or replaces a parameterized query's parameter and its value in the specified connection. The value of the parameter is given as a real.
sqlparamssetasreal.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.
paramDocs.ParamName: The name of the parameter to add or change.
paramDocs.ParamValue: The value of the parameter as a real.

sqlparamssetasstring.name: SQLParamsSetAsString
sqlparamssetasstring.doc: Adds or replaces a parameterized query's parameter and its value in the specified connection. The value of the parameter is given as a string.
sqlparamssetasstring.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.
paramDocs.ParamName: The name of the parameter to add or change.
paramDocs.ParamValue: The value of the parameter as a string.
paramDocs.nStrType: The index specifying the type of the string:

sqlprev.name: SQLPrev
sqlprev.doc: Gets the previous database record from an SQL query. The function works only with disconnected recordsets. Use the SQLGetRecordset() function to select a number of records or rows from the SQL database, and then use the SQLNext()/SQLPrev() function to step through each record separately.
sqlprev.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hGeneral: The handle to the disconnected recordset.

sqlquerycreate.name: SQLQueryCreate
sqlquerycreate.doc: The function creates a new query and returns its handle. The query is empty and has to be set by using SQLSet() and/or SQLAppend() functions. The query handle can be used with the statement functions as SQLExec() or SQLGetRecordset().
sqlquerycreate.returns: The handle to the query if successful, otherwise the invalid handle.

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlquerydispose.name: SQLQueryDispose
sqlquerydispose.doc: The function disposes the query which handle is given as the argument.
sqlquerydispose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg() function).

paramDocs.hQuery: The handle to the query, returned from SQLQueryCreate() function.

sqlrollback.name: SQLRollBack
sqlrollback.doc: Rolls back (discards) all changes made to the database within the current transaction. If you call the SQLBeginTran() function to begin a transaction, you are not committed to changes to the database made by the Insert, Delete, and Update commands until you call the SQLCommit() function. You can discard these changes by calling the SQLRollBack() function.
sqlrollback.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object, returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function. The handle identifies the DB connection object where details of the associated SQL connection are stored.

sqlrowcount.name: SQLRowCount
sqlrowcount.doc: Gets the number of rows in the recordset.
sqlrowcount.returns: The number of rows in the given recordset for disconnected recordsets. For the connected recordset, the function returns always -1.

sqlset.name: SQLSet
sqlset.doc: Sets a query string in the SQL buffer. Cicode cannot send an SQL query that is longer than 255 characters. If you have an SQL query that is longer than the 255 character limit, you can split the query into smaller strings, and use this function and the SQLAppend() function to append the query in the SQL buffer.
sqlset.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg() function).

paramDocs.hGeneral: The handle either to the DB connection object (returned from either SQLCreate() or SQLConnect() function) or to the query handle (returned from SQLQueryCreate()). When it is the connection handle, the operation is performed on the first query in that DB connection object. When it is the query handle, the operation is performed on that query through the DB object which is associated to it.
paramDocs.sString: The query string to set in the SQL buffer. The string needs to contain the first part of an SQL query.

sqltraceoff.name: SQLTraceOff
sqltraceoff.doc: Turns off the debug trace. Use this function to stop tracing function calls that are made to the database. The trace can be turned off globally for all connections or for a specific one.
sqltraceoff.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object: INVALID HANDLE - The trace is deactivated for all DB connections (default), otherwise - The trace is deactivated for this specific DB connection object.

sqltraceon.name: SQLTraceOn
sqltraceon.doc: Turns on a debug trace. Use this function to begin tracing function calls that are made to the database. The information is written to TraceLog.dat file (the strFileName argument is currently ignored). The trace can be turned on globally for all connections or for a specific connection.
sqltraceon.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error number is returned. (For details of the 307 error code, call the SQLErrMsg function).

paramDocs.sFileName: The output file name for the debug trace. Currently ignored.
paramDocs.hSQL: The handle to the DB connection object: INVALID HANDLE - The trace is activated for all DB connections (default), otherwise - The trace is activated for this specific DB connection object.
paramDocs.nTraceLevel: Defines the level of details written to the trace file. The following values are allowed:

sqrt.name: Sqrt
sqrt.doc: Gets the square root of a number.

strcalcwidth.name: StrCalcWidth
strcalcwidth.doc: Retrieves the pixel width of a string using a particular font.
strcalcwidth.returns: The pixel width of a string using the particular font.

paramDocs.sText: The text to determine the pixel width of
paramDocs.iFont: The font number used to calculate the pixel width of the text. (To use the default font, set to -1).

strclean.name: StrClean
strclean.doc: Removes control characters from a string. Any character that is not a displayable ASCII character is removed from the string.
strclean.returns: The string with all control characters removed.

strendswith.name: StrEndsWith
strendswith.doc: Verifies whether the given string ends with a specific string.
strendswith.returns: Returns TRUE if sSource ends with sSearchTerm, otherwise returns FALSE.

paramDocs.sSearchTerm: The string to search for in the source string.

strfill.name: StrFill
strfill.doc: Fills a string with a number of occurrences of another string.

paramDocs.Length: The length of the string.

strformat.name: StrFormat
strformat.doc: Converts a variable into a formatted string. This function is the equivalent of the Cicode " :#### " operator.

paramDocs.Variable: The variable to format into a string.
paramDocs.Width: The width of the variable after it has been converted to string format.
paramDocs.DecPlaces: The number of decimal places in the converted string.
paramDocs.EngUnits: The engineering units of the variable.

strgetchar.name: StrGetChar
strgetchar.doc: Gets a single character from a string or buffer. Use this function to read a string, character by character.
strgetchar.returns: The character at the offset in the string.

paramDocs.String: The source string. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.iOffset: The offset in the string, commencing at 0.

strleft.name: StrLeft
strleft.doc: Gets the left-most characters from a string.
strleft.returns: A string containing the left-most N characters of String.

paramDocs.N: The number of characters to get from the source string.

strlength.name: StrLength
strlength.doc: Gets the length of a string.
strlength.returns: The length of the string (as an integer).

strlistcontainsitem.name: StrListContainsItem
strlistcontainsitem.doc: Checks whether the string passed is an item contained in a delimited list of strings. String comparison is case insensitive. Leading and trailing spaces are removed before comparing.
strlistcontainsitem.returns: Returns TRUE if the item is found in the list, otherwise returns FALSE

paramDocs.sItem: Item that you wish to search for.
paramDocs.sDelim: The string to use as a delimiter. If this is not specified, a comma (,) is used.

strmid.name: StrMid
strmid.doc: Gets characters from the middle of a string.
strmid.returns: A string containing the number of characters from the offset.

paramDocs.Offset: The offset in the string, commencing at 0.
paramDocs.Characters: The number of characters to get, commencing at the offset.

strpad.name: StrPad
strpad.doc: Pads a string with a number of occurrences of another string. Padding can be added to the left or to the right of a string. If the string is already longer than the required string length, the string is truncated.

paramDocs.Length: The length of the string. If a positive length is specified, padding will be added to the right of the string. If a negative length is specified, padding will be added to the left of the string.

strreplace.name: StrReplace
strreplace.doc: Replaces a substring in a string with replacement substring.

paramDocs.sReplaceSubstring: The replacement substring. If this is not specified, it defaults to an empty string, that is, the matched substring will be removed from the original string.
paramDocs.sTerminators: Optional set of characters to terminate the substring. If this is not specified, it defaults to an empty string. When it is specified, the substring is only considered a match if it is enclosed by one of the characters specified by this argument.

strright.name: StrRight
strright.doc: Gets the rightmost characters from a string.
strright.returns: A string containing the rightmost N characters of String.

paramDocs.N: The number of characters to get from the source string.

strsearch.name: StrSearch
strsearch.doc: Searhes for a string within a string, commencing at a specified offset. The result of the search is the index in the source string, where the first character of the sub-string is found. Index 0 is the first character in the string, index 1 is the second, and so on.
strsearch.returns: The index in the search string, or -1 if the sub-string does not exist in the string.

paramDocs.Offset: The offset in the string, commencing at 0.

strsetchar.name: StrSetChar
strsetchar.doc: Sets a single character into a string or buffer. Use this function to build up a string, character by character, and terminate the string with the end-of-string character 0 (zero). (If you use a string without a terminator in a function that expects a string, or in a Cicode expression, you could get invalid results.) To use the string to build up a buffer, you do not need the terminating 0 (zero).
strsetchar.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sText: The destination string. Must be a String type variable.
paramDocs.iOffset: The offset in the string, commencing at 0.
paramDocs.Char: The ASCII character to set into the string.

strsplit.name: StrSplit
strsplit.doc: Splits a string into sub-strings based on the specified delimiter.

strtobool.name: StrToBool
strtobool.doc: Converts a string value to a Boolean value.

paramDocs.sVal: Boolean value as a string. Allowable values are: TRUE, FALSE or any numeric value.

strtochar.name: StrToChar
strtochar.doc: Gets the ASCII code of the first character in a string.
strtochar.returns: The ASCII code of the first character in String.

strtodate.name: StrToDate
strtodate.doc: Converts a "date" string into a time/date variable. This variable is the same as returned from the TimeCurrent() function. To set the order of the day, month, and year, and the delimiter, use the Windows Control panel.
strtodate.returns: A time/date variable, or 274 if the time/date is out of range.

strtofmt.name: StrToFmt
strtofmt.doc: Converts a string into field data for a format template. This function is useful for splitting a string into separate strings. After the string is converted, you can call the FmtGetField() function to extract the individual data from the template fields.
strtofmt.returns: The string (formatted as template field data).

paramDocs.hFmt: The format template handle, returned from the FmtOpen() function. The handle identifies the table where all data on the associated format template is stored.

strtogrp.name: StrToGrp
strtogrp.doc: Converts a string into a group and places it into a group number. Any existing values in the group are cleared before the new values are inserted. The group string is a series of numbers separated by " , " to list individual values or " .. " to specify a range of values.
strtogrp.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hGrp: The group handle, returned from the GrpOpen() function. The group handle identifies the table where all data on the associated group is stored.

strtohex.name: StrToHex
strtohex.doc: Converts a hexadecimal string into an integer. This function will search the string for the first non-blank character, and then start converting until it finds the end of the string or a non-hexadecimal numeric character. If the first non-blank character is not one of the following hexadecimal characters, the return value is 0 (zero):

strtoint.name: StrToInt
strtoint.doc: Converts a string into an integer. This function will search the string for the first non-blank character, and then start converting until it finds the end of the string or a non-numeric character. If the first non-blank character is not a numeric character (0-9), a space, a " + " or a " - " sign, the return value is 0 (zero).

strtolines.name: StrToLines
strtolines.doc: Converts a string into separate lines that contain no more than the number of characters specified in the MaxChars argument.
strtolines.returns: A string containing the input string with new line characters inserted into it.

paramDocs.MaxChars: The maximum number of characters permitted in each new line produced by the StrToLines() function.
paramDocs.nLines: Output Parameter: Returns the number of lines produced by the StrToLines() function from the input string. This should be a Cicode INT type variable.

strtolocaltext.name: StrToLocalText
strtolocaltext.doc: Converts a native string into the local version of that string. (The string needs to be contained within quotation marks, as shown in the example below.) The local version is taken from the current language database(as specified using the [Language]LocalLanguage parameter).
strtolocaltext.returns: The local version of the text if it was found, otherwise the native text or "#MESS" is returned, depending on the setting of the [Language]DisplayError parameter.

paramDocs.sText: The string for which you would like the local translation returned. This string needs to be enclosed in quotation marks. For example:

strtoperiod.name: StrToPeriod
strtoperiod.doc: Converts a string into a time period. You would normally use this function to convert operator input, for example, to set a trend period.
strtoperiod.returns: A period (converted from String), or -1 if no conversion can be performed.

strtoreal.name: StrToReal
strtoreal.doc: Converts a string into a floating-point number. This function will search the string for the first non-blank character, and then start converting until it finds the end of the string or a non-numeric character. If the first non-blank character is not a numeric character (0-9), a space, a decimal point, a " + " or a " - " sign, the return value is 0 (zero).

strtotime.name: StrToTime
strtotime.doc: Converts a "time" string into a time/date variable. The value returned is the number of seconds from midnight. You can add this value to the date to get the current time value. To set the time delimiter, use the Windows Control Panel.
strtotime.returns: A time/date variable, or -1 if no conversion can be performed.

strtotimestamp.name: StrToTimestamp
strtotimestamp.doc: This function converts timestamp in a STRING format into a TIMESTAMP format. This function can be used in browsing functions to convert timestamp fields returned as a string.
strtotimestamp.returns: This function returns a date in TIMESTAMP format if successful, otherwise returns TIMESTAMP of January 1, 1601, 00:00:00 (UTC). If the function is unsuccessful you can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.String: The date and time as a STRING or TIMESTAMP
paramDocs.Format: The format of the string. Should be 15. Other types reserved for future use.
paramDocs.UTC: If 1, the date is considered to be in UTC. Otherwise, local time is used. This field is only applicable for format STRING formats (i.e. format is not equal 15).

strtovalue.name: StrToValue
strtovalue.doc: Converts a string into a floating-point number. This function is similar to the StrToReal() function except that the function halts if it is passed an invalid string. The function will search the string for the first non-blank character, and then start converting until it finds the end of the string or a non-numeric character. If the first non-blank character is not a numeric character (0-9), a space, a decimal point, a " + " or a " - " sign, the function will halt.

strtrim.name: StrTrim
strtrim.doc: Removes leading and trailing spaces from a string. Internal spaces are not removed from the string.
strtrim.returns: String with leading and trailing spaces removed.

strtruncfont.name: StrTruncFont
strtruncfont.doc: Returns the truncated string using a particular font (specified by name) or the specified number of characters.
strtruncfont.returns: A truncated string or the original one.

paramDocs.sFont: The name of the font that is used to display the text. The Font Name needs to be defined in the Fonts database. If the font is not found, the default font is used.
paramDocs.iLength: Length of the Text to display, either in characters or pixels depending on iLengthMode (default -1, no truncation)
paramDocs.iLengthMode: The length mode of the text string:

strtruncfonthnd.name: StrTruncFontHnd
strtruncfonthnd.doc: Returns the truncated string using a particular font (specified by font number) or the specified number of characters.
strtruncfonthnd.returns: A truncated string or the original one.

paramDocs.hFont: The font handle used to calculate the pixel width of the text. (To use the default font, set to -1).
paramDocs.iLength: Length of the Text to display, either in characters or pixels depending on iLengthMode (default -1, no truncation)
paramDocs.iLengthMode: The length mode of the text string:

strtruncfonttooltip.name: StrTruncFontTooltip
strtruncfonttooltip.doc: Returns a truncated string with ellipsis, and sets an AN with a tooltip containing the complete string if a truncation occurs.

paramDocs.nANForTooltip: The AN for which the tooltip needs to be set.
paramDocs.sFont: The name of the font that is used to display the text. The font name needs to be defined in the Fonts database. If the font is not found, the default font is used.
paramDocs.nPixels: Number of pixels that the text can display before truncation occurs.

strword.name: StrWord
strword.doc: Gets the first word from a string. The word is removed from the string to allow the function to be repeated. Word separators can be a space, newline, carriage return, or tab character.
strword.returns: A string containing the first word from String .

subscriptionaddcallback.name: SubscriptionAddCallback
subscriptionaddcallback.doc: Adds a function callback to a tag subscription. When the value change for a subscribed tag is detected, a callback function can be called. This implements change based Cicode and avoids continuously polling a tag value to monitor changes.
subscriptionaddcallback.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iHandle: Integer handle of the subscription to add a callback to.
paramDocs.sCallback: String stating the name of a function to call when the value is updated. The function should have the structure:

subscriptiongetattribute.name: SubscriptionGetAttribute
subscriptiongetattribute.doc: Reads the specified attribute value of a subscribed tag. Similar to TagRead.
subscriptiongetattribute.returns: String representation of the cached value for a subscribed tag. On error, an empty string and an error is set.

paramDocs.iHandle: Integer handle of the subscription to read from.
paramDocs.sAttribute: Attribute of the tag to read. Supported Attributes are:
paramDocs.iOffset: Optional integer expressing the zero based index of an array attribute. This is only valid for the Value attribute. Default value is 0.

subscriptiongetinfo.name: SubscriptionGetInfo
subscriptiongetinfo.doc: Reads the specified text information about a subscribed tag.
subscriptiongetinfo.returns: String representation of the requested information for a subscribed tag. On error, returns an empty string and an error is set.

paramDocs.iHandle: Integer handle of the subscription to read from.
paramDocs.sAttribute: Attribute of the tag to read. Supported Attributes are:

subscriptiongetquality.name: SubscriptionGetQuality
subscriptiongetquality.doc: Reads quality of a subscribed tag.
subscriptiongetquality.returns: The quality for a subscribed tag. On error, QUAL_BAD.

paramDocs.iHandle: Integer handle of the subscription to read from.

subscriptiongettag.name: SubscriptionGetTag
subscriptiongettag.doc: Reads a value, quality and timestamps of a subscribed tag.
subscriptiongettag.returns: Returns a value, quality and timestamps of a subscribed tag. The type of the returned value depends on a type of the subscribed tag. The quality and timestamps of the subscribed tag are read and passed with the returned value.

paramDocs.iHandle: Integer handle of the subscription to read from.
paramDocs.sOffset: Optional integer expressing the zero based index of an array attribute. This is only valid for the Value attribute. Default value is 0.

subscriptiongettimestamp.name: SubscriptionGetTimestamp
subscriptiongettimestamp.doc: Reads the specified timestamp of a subscribed tag.
subscriptiongettimestamp.returns: The requested timestamp for a subscribed tag. On error, 0 (INVALID TIMESTAMP).

paramDocs.iHandle: Integer handle of the subscription to read from.
paramDocs.sAttribute: Attribute of the tag to read. Supported Attributes are:

subscriptiongetvalue.name: SubscriptionGetValue
subscriptiongetvalue.doc: Reads a value of a subscribed tag.
subscriptiongetvalue.returns: Returns a value of a subscribed tag. The type of the returned variable depends on a type of the subscribed tag. The quality and timestamps of the subscribed tag are not read i.e. quality of the returned value can be consider as GOOD and its timestamps as 0 (INVALID TIMESTAMP).

paramDocs.iHandle: Integer handle of the subscription to read from.
paramDocs.sOffset: Optional integer expressing the zero based index of an array attribute. Default value is 0.

subscriptionremovecallback.name: SubscriptionRemoveCallback
subscriptionremovecallback.doc: Removes a function callback from a tag subscription. The subscription handle and callback function needs to match those used when adding the callback.
subscriptionremovecallback.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iHandle: Integer handle of the subscription of the callback.
paramDocs.sCallback: String stating the name of the callback function.

switchconfig.name: SwitchConfig
switchconfig.doc: Switches focus to a specific Plant SCADA configuration application. If the specified application is not running, it will be started.
switchconfig.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

systime.name: SysTime
systime.doc: Gets the Plant SCADA internal system millisecond counter. The counter is not based on time, but counts from 0 up to the maximum unsigned integer value and then back to 0.
systime.returns: The Plant SCADA internal system millisecond counter (as an integer).

systimedelta.name: SysTimeDelta
systimedelta.doc: Calculates the time difference between a start time and the current time, and updates the start time to the current time. You can time continuous events in a single operation. See the SysTime() function for information on its use.
systimedelta.returns: The time difference from a start time and the current time.

paramDocs.Start: The start time returned from the SysTime() function. Must be a Long type variable.

tablelookup.name: TableLookup
tablelookup.doc: Searches for a value in a table, and returns the position (offset) of the value in the table. Be aware that the first item in a table is offset 0 (zero), the next item is offset 1, etc.
tablelookup.returns: The offset to the table value, or -1 if the value does not exist.

paramDocs.Table: The table to search. The table needs to be an array of real numbers. Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.Size: The maximum number of items in the table.
paramDocs.Value: The value to locate.

tablemath.name: TableMath
tablemath.doc: Performs mathematical operations on a table of real (floating-point) numbers. This function supports minimum, maximum, average, standard deviation, and total operations on a table of values. Use this function for operating on tables returned from the trend system with the TrnGetTable() function. You can set the Mode to either accept or ignore invalid or gated data returned from TrnGetTable().
tablemath.returns: Returns the value related to the requested mathematical operation performed on the table (Minimum, Maximum, Average, Standard deviation or Total).\

paramDocs.Table: Any table of floating-point numbers. Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.Size: The maximum number of items in the table.
paramDocs.Command: The mathematical operation to perform on the table:

tableshift.name: TableShift
tableshift.doc: Shifts table items in a table by a number of positions. You can shift the table left or right. Items shifted off the end of the table are lost. Items within a table that are not replaced by other items (that have moved) are set to 0.
tableshift.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Table: The table to shift, an array of real numbers. Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.Size: The maximum number of items in the table.
paramDocs.Count: The number of positions to shift the table items. A negative Count moves items to the right and a positive Count moves items to the left.

tagbrowseclose.name: TagBrowseClose
tagbrowseclose.doc: The TagBrowseClose function terminates an active data browse session and cleans up resources associated with the session.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TagBrowseOpen call.

tagbrowsefirst.name: TagBrowseFirst
tagbrowsefirst.doc: The TagBrowseFirst function places the data browse cursor at the first record.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TagBrowseOpen call.

tagbrowsegetfield.name: TagBrowseGetField
tagbrowsegetfield.doc: The TagBrowseGetField function retrieves the value of the specified field from the record the data browse cursor is currently referencing.
tagbrowsegetfield.returns: The value of the specified field as a string if successful. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. The last error should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred. -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TagBrowseOpen call.

tagbrowsenext.name: TagBrowseNext
tagbrowsenext.doc: The TagBrowseNext function moves the data browse cursor forward one record.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TagBrowseOpen call.

tagbrowsenumrecords.name: TagBrowseNumRecords
tagbrowsenumrecords.doc: The TagBrowseNumRecords function gets the number of records for a given browsing session. This function may not be accurate if the following occurs:
tagbrowsenumrecords.returns: Number of records (INT) if successful -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TagBrowseOpen call.

tagbrowseopen.name: TagBrowseOpen
tagbrowseopen.doc: The TagBrowseOpen function initiates a new browse session and returns a handle to the new session that can be used in subsequent data browse function calls. Tag records are sorted on the server and, arrive at the client in the order specified by the sorting fields parameter, or default sorting order as described below under the Sort parameter.
tagbrowseopen.returns: Session handle (LONG) if successful, -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.Filter: Semicolon delimited list of predefined field name filters specifying the records to return during the browsing session. If you do not specify a filter string then all tag records will be displayed.
paramDocs.Field: Comma separated list of record fields to be returned during the browsing session. An empty field string will return all possible fields.
paramDocs.Sort: Comma delimited list of record fields to be returned in order of sorting preferences (each with an indication of whether the sort is A - ascending or D - descending). For example "TYPE:D". By default tag browsing records are sorted by the tag primary key Cluster.TagName. which is implicitly appended to the list of sorting fields, since all the other fields may end up not being unique.
paramDocs.Clusters: An optional parameter that specifies via a comma delimited string the subset of the clusters to browse. An empty string indicates that the all clusters will be browsed.

tagbrowseprev.name: TagBrowsePrev
tagbrowseprev.doc: The TagBrowsePrev function moves the data browse cursor back one record. If you call this function after you have reached the beginning of a browse, error code 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TagBrowseOpen call.

tagdebug.name: TagDebug
tagdebug.doc: Displays a dialog which allows you to select from a list of the configured variable tags in your system. Once you have selected a tag, you can either press the Read button to get the tag's current value; or change the value by entering a new one, and pressing the Write button. This function should only be used for debugging or commissioning.
tagdebug.returns: The name of the tag entered in the dialog.

tagdebugform.name: TagDebugForm
tagdebugform.doc: The TagDebugForm Cicode function displays a dialog that allows you to select a variable tag and perform some basic read/write operations on it. This function is useful for debugging or commissioning a project.
tagdebugform.returns: The name of the tag entered in the dialog.

tageventformat.name: TagEventFormat
tageventformat.doc: Returns a handle to the format of the data used by the TagEventQueue().

tageventqueue.name: TagEventQueue
tageventqueue.doc: Opens the tag update event queue. The I/O server writes events into this queue as they are processed. These events include tag updates from drivers that support time-stamped data.
tageventqueue.returns: The queue handle of the Tag Update Event queue.

taggetproperty.name: TagGetProperty
taggetproperty.doc: This function reads a property of a variable tag from the data source. This function replaces TagInfo.
taggetproperty.returns: String representation of the property of the tag. If unsuccessful, an empty string and an error code is set.

paramDocs.Name: STRING TagGetProperty(STRING Name, STRING Property [, INT CachedMode] [, STRING ClusterName] )
paramDocs.Property: The property to read. Property names are case sensitive. Supported properties are:
paramDocs.Address: Returns the configured address of the tag (as specified in the variable tags form).
paramDocs.ArraySize: Array size of the associated tag. Returns 1 for non-array types.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Name of the cluster the tag resides on.
paramDocs.DataBitWidth: Number of bits used to store the value
paramDocs.Equipment: Name of the equipment associated with the Tag.
paramDocs.Format: Format bit string. The format information is stored in the integer as follows:
paramDocs.FormatDecPlaces: Number of decimal places for default format
paramDocs.FormatWidth: Number of characters used in default format
paramDocs.FullName: Full name of the tag in the form cluster.tagname.
paramDocs.Item: Name of the equipment item associated with the Tag. If the tag is not resolved, returns an empty string.
paramDocs.Type: General type of tag. Allowed values are:
paramDocs.Units: Engineering Units for example, %, mm, Volts.
paramDocs.CachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.

taggetscale.name: TagGetScale
taggetscale.doc: Gets the value of a tag at a specified scale from the datasource. The value is returned as a formatted string using the tags format specification and (optionally) the engineering units. Use this function to write generic Cicode that will work with any type of tag. This function replaces TagScaleStr.
taggetscale.returns: The scale of the tag (as a string).

paramDocs.Name: The name of the tag, or the equipment and item name of a variable tag (using equipment.item notation). The tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag".
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of full scale of the returned value.
paramDocs.EngUnits: Flag to determine if the value is returned with engineering units:
paramDocs.CachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

taggetvalue.name: TagGetValue
taggetvalue.doc: Reads the value, quality and timestamp of a tag based on the tag subscription.
taggetvalue.returns: Returns the value, quality and timestamp of a subscribed tag. The data type of the value returned depends on the type of the subscribed tag and also the tag extension. The quality and timestamp of the subscribed tag are read and passed with the value returned by the function.

paramDocs.TagName: String representing the tag/tag element/ the equipment and item name (using equipment.item notation) associated with that tag, to subscribe to in the form of "cluster_name.tag_name.element name" or "cluster_name.equipment. item.element_name". If the element name (for example, 'Field') is not specified, it will be resolved at runtime as an unqualified tag reference. . If you need to access a specific tag element item to get timestamp and quality values, use the nItem parameter as well (for further information, refer to the Tag Extensions documentation in the main help).
paramDocs.Item: Optional element number to access tag element values. For more information, refer to the Tag Extensions documentation in the main help.
paramDocs.Index: Optional index for an array variable. If not specified, it has a default value of 0. Since the TagName parameter does not support array indexing, use the Index parameter to access an element in an array. Note that the address of the first element in an array is 0 (zero).
paramDocs.PollTime: Optional integer representing the Datasource Poll time in milliseconds. Default is 250 milliseconds.
paramDocs.ScaleMode: Optional number to specify scaling mode of subscription.
paramDocs.Deadband: Optional real value specifying the percentage of the variable tag's engineering range by which a tag needs to change for an update to be sent through the system. Default is -1.0, indicating the deadband specified by the tag definition is to be used.
paramDocs.Lightweight: This optional boolean argument indicates whether or not subscription updates use a "lightweight" version of the tag value that does not include a quality timestamp or a value timestamp.
paramDocs.KeepAliveSeconds: Optional length of time (in seconds) for which the subscription will remain in memory. The default is 30 seconds. If there are multiple requests to the same tag with different timeout values, only the first timeout value will be taken into account.

taginfo.name: TagInfo
taginfo.doc: Gets information about a variable tag. This function allows you to develop generic Cicode and Super Genies.
taginfo.returns: The value of the information as a string.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the tag or the equipment and item reference of a variable tag (using equipment.item notation) from which to get information. The tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag" or "ClusterName.Equipment.Item".
paramDocs.Type: The type of information to get:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.
paramDocs.CachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.

taginfoex.name: TagInfoEx
taginfoex.doc: This function replaces TagInfo and is identical in operation. It supports online changes. It is recommended therefore that instances of TagInfo in legacy code are migrated to either TagInfoEx or TagGetProperty. New Cicode should use TagGetProperty.
taginfoex.returns: The value of the information as a string. If unsuccessful, an empty string is returned. The error code can be obtained by calling the IsError Cicode function.

paramDocs.Name: The name of the tag or the equipment and item name of a variable tag (using equipment.item notation) from which to get information. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag" or "ClusterName.Equipment.Item".
paramDocs.Type: The type of information to get:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.
paramDocs.CachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.

tagramp.name: TagRamp
tagramp.doc: This function will increment a Tag by the amount defined by iPercentInc. It is often used for incrementing a tag while a button is held down.
tagramp.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: The variable tag name (or alarm property name), as a string. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag".
paramDocs.PercentInc: The percentage by which you want to increase the value of the variable. A negative number will decrease the variable. The increment is calculated as a percentage of the full range.

tagrdbreload.name: TagRDBReload
tagrdbreload.doc: Works in conjunction with the TagInfo function. Reloads the variable tag database so when TagInfo is called it picks up all online changes to the tag database.
tagrdbreload.returns: Returns 1 if the tag database was successfully reloaded, and 0 if the tag database fails to load.

tagread.name: TagRead
tagread.doc: Reads a variable from an I/O device or a local variable. The variable tag needs to be defined in the Variable Tags database. Because the variable tag is specified as a string (not as a tag), you can ignore the data type of the variable.

paramDocs.Tag: A string that can be one of the following:
paramDocs.Offset: The offset for an array variable. This argument is optional - if not specified, it has a default value of 0.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tagreadex.name: TagReadEx
tagreadex.doc: Reads the value, quality or timestamp of a particular tag from the I/O device. The variable tag needs to be defined in the Variable Tags database. Because the variable tag is specified as a string (not as a tag), you can ignore the data type of the variable.

paramDocs.Tag: A string that can be one of the following:
paramDocs.Offset: The offset for an array variable. This argument is optional - if not specified, it has a default value of 0.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tagresolve.name: TagResolve
tagresolve.doc: This function can be used to increment a reference count on a tag to keep it resolved, making it readily available to a client.
tagresolve.returns: The returned integer is a handle to the tag that has been resolved, or -1 if an error occurred.

paramDocs.TagName: The name of the tag or the equipment and item name (using equipment.item notation) associated with that tag to resolve (in the format "clusterName.tagName" or "clusterName.equipment.item" if you need to specify a cluster).

tagscalestr.name: TagScaleStr
tagscalestr.doc: Gets the value of a tag at a specified scale. The value is returned as a formatted string using the tags format specification and (optionally) the engineering units. Use this function to write generic Cicode that will work with any type of tag.
tagscalestr.returns: The scale of the tag (as a string).

paramDocs.Tag: The name of the tag, or the equipment and item name of a variable tag (using equipment.item notation).
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of full scale of the returned value.
paramDocs.EngUnits: Determines if the value is returned with engineering units:
paramDocs.ClusterName: Name of the cluster
paramDocs.CachedMode: Optional parameter that specifies from where to retrieve the value for the property.

tagsetoverridebad.name: TagSetOverrideBad
tagsetoverridebad.doc: Sets a quality Override element for a specified tag to Bad Non Specific.
tagsetoverridebad.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: The variable tag name or the equipment and item name (using equipment.item notation) associated with that tag as a string. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag" or "ClusterName.Equipment.Item".
paramDocs.Synch: An optional boolean argument that specifies whether the command is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous (non- blocking). By default, this parameter is set to "True", synchronous (blocking), and the function will wait until the write has completed and returned from the server before further code execution. If you specify this parameter the other parameters need to be explicitly specified.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tagsetoverridegood.name: TagSetOverrideGood
tagsetoverridegood.doc: Sets a quality Override element for a specified tag to Good Non Specific.
tagsetoverridegood.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: The variable tag name or the equipment and item name (using <equipment>.<item> notation) associated with that tag as a string. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag" or "ClusterName.Equipment.Item".
paramDocs.Synch: An optional boolean argument that specifies whether the command is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous (non- blocking). By default, this parameter is set to "True", synchronous (blocking), and the function will wait until the write has completed and returned from the server before further code execution. If you specify this parameter the other parameters need to be explicitly specified.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tagsetoverridequality.name: TagSetOverrideQuality
tagsetoverridequality.doc: Sets a quality of Override element for a specified tag.
tagsetoverridequality.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: The variable tag name or the equipment and item name (using equipment.item notation) associated with that tag as a string. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag" or "ClusterName.Equipment.Item".
paramDocs.qualityNew: The new quality for the tag’s Override element.
paramDocs.Synch: An optional boolean argument that specifies whether the command is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous (non- blocking). By default, this parameter is set to "True", synchronous (blocking), and the function will wait until the write has completed and returned from the server before further code execution. If you specify this parameter the other parameters need to be explicitly specified.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tagsetoverrideuncertain.name: TagSetOverrideUncertain
tagsetoverrideuncertain.doc: Sets a quality Override element for a specified tag to Uncertain Non Specific.
tagsetoverrideuncertain.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: The variable tag name or the equipment and item name (using equipment.item notation) associated with that tag as a string. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag" or "ClusterName.Equipment.Item".
paramDocs.Synch: An optional boolean argument that specifies whether the command is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous (non- blocking). By default, this parameter is set to "True", synchronous (blocking), and the function will wait until the write has completed and returned from the server before further code execution. If you specify this parameter the other parameters need to be explicitly specified.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tagsubscribe.name: TagSubscribe
