tagsubscribe.doc: Subscribes a tag so that Cicode functions can be called when a tag's value changes. The subscription checks each poll period whether the tag has changed value and if it has, the specified callback function is called. This avoids continuously polling a tag value to monitor changes. To add a function callback to the subscription, use the optional parameter in this command or the SubscriptionAddCallback function.
tagsubscribe.returns: Integer representing the subscription handle that can be used to read values, hook to events or unsubscribe. If unsuccessful, -1 is returned and an error is set. Even though a subscription handle is returned immediately, it can't be used to get attributes until the subscription has been confirmed as this is an asynchronous Cicode function call. The typical Cicode error is 423 when a subscription handled is used too soon. We recommend the use of a callback function or the direct use of the tag extension, e.g. <tag>.VT

paramDocs.TagName: String representing the tag or tag element or the equipment and item name (using equipment.item notation) associated with that tag, to subscribe to in the form of "cluster_name.tag_name.element name" or "cluster_name.equipment. item.element name". If the element name is not specified, it will be resolved at runtime as an unqualified tag reference.
paramDocs.PollTime: Optional integer representing the Datasource Poll time in milliseconds (default 250).
paramDocs.ScaleMode: Optional string stating the mode to subscribe. Supported modes are: Raw, Eng, Percent. Default is "Eng".
paramDocs.Deadband: Optional real value specifying the percentage of the variable tag's engineering range that a tag needs to change by for an update to be sent through the system. Default value is -1.0, indicating the deadband specified by the tag definition is to be used.
paramDocs.Callback: Optional string stating the name of a function to call when the value is updated. If an empty string is specified, no handler is registered. Default value is "" (empty string).
paramDocs.Lightweight: This optional boolean argument indicates whether or not subscription updates use a "lightweight" version of the tag value that does not include a quality timestamp or a value timestamp.
paramDocs.NoUpdateForDuplicateValues: This optional boolean argument allows you to specify if the subscription accepts duplicated values. Set this value to 1 to indicate that a duplicated update is not required for values that have already successfully written to the device.

tagunresolve.name: TagUnresolve
tagunresolve.doc: This function is used to decrement a reference count implemented on a tag by TagResolve. This will allow the tag to be evicted if the decrement causes its reference count to reach zero (0).
tagunresolve.returns: The returned integer represents any error that occurs when the unresolve is attempted (0 for no error).

paramDocs.Handle: The tag handle returned from a TagResolve() function call.

tagunsubscribe.name: TagUnsubscribe
tagunsubscribe.doc: Unsubscribes the tag subscription specified by the integer subscription handle that was returned from the TagSubscribe function. This function also removes any callbacks that are associated with the subscription.
tagunsubscribe.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Handle: Integer handle of the subscription to unsubscribe.

tagwrite.name: TagWrite
tagwrite.doc: Writes to an I/O device variable by specifying the variable tag name or the variable tag name and the name of the requested element having read/write access. The variable tag needs to be defined in the Variable Tags database.
tagwrite.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: A string that can be one of the following:
paramDocs.Value: The value to be written to the I/O device variable. The value is specified as a string, however if an integer or real is used the compiler will convert it to a string. The function converts the string into the correct format, and then writes it to the variable.
paramDocs.Offset: Optional offset for an array variable. Default is 0.
paramDocs.Synch: An optional boolean argument that specifies whether the command is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous (non- blocking). If it is specified as synchronous (blocking) the function will wait until the write has completed and returned from the server before further code execution. This parameter is "False", or asynchronous, by default. If you specify this parameter the rest of the parameters need to be explicitly specified, including nOffset which should be set as 0 if the tag is not an array tag.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tagwriteeventque.name: TagWriteEventQue
tagwriteeventque.doc: Opens the tag write event queue. The TagWriteEventQue is a queue of data containing details of tag value changes initiated by the process.
tagwriteeventque.returns: The handle of the tag write event queue, or -1 if the queue cannot be opened.

tagwriteintarray.name: TagWriteIntArray
tagwriteintarray.doc: This function writes an array of integers to a tag. You can write to all elements of an array tag, or write to a subset. Use the Offset parameter to write to the subset (e.g. if you specify a Length of 5 and an Offset of 2, you will write to the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th elements in the tag array).
tagwriteintarray.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: The string can refer to either: the variable tag name, the equipment and item name (using equipment.item notation) associated with that tag, the alarm name and the alarm property name, the tag name and the tag element name. If the element name is not specified, the writing will be performed to the Field VQT element. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag" or "ClusterName.Equipment.Item".
paramDocs.Length: The number of elements written to the tag.
paramDocs.Value: The element you select in the array to be the first. The array contains the values you are writing to the variable tag. See example below. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.Offset: Optional offset inside the variable tag array where you start writing to. Default is 0.
paramDocs.Sync: An optional boolean argument that specifies whether the command is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous (non- blocking). If it is specified as synchronous (blocking) the function will wait until the write has completed and returned from the server before further code execution. This parameter is "False", or asynchronous, by default. If you specify this parameter the rest of the parameters need to be explicitly specified, including nOffset which should be set as 0 if the tag is not an array tag.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tagwriterealarray.name: TagWriteRealArray
tagwriterealarray.doc: This function writes an array of REAL values to a variable tag. You can write to all elements of an array tag, or write to a subset. Use the Offset parameter to write to the subset (e.g. if you specify a Length of 5 and an Offset of 2, you will write to the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th elements in the tag array).
tagwriterealarray.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: The string can refer to either: the variable tag name, the equipment and item name (using equipment.item notation) associated with that tag, the alarm name and the alarm property name, the tag name and the tag element name. If the element name is not specified, the writing will be performed to the Field VQT element. The name of the tag can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag" or "ClusterName.Equipment.Item".
paramDocs.Length: The number of elements written to the tag.
paramDocs.Value: The element you select in the array to be the first. The array contains the values you are writing to the variable tag. See example below.
paramDocs.Offset: Optional offset inside the variable tag array where you start writing to. Default is 0.
paramDocs.Sync: An optional boolean argument that specifies whether the command is synchronous (blocking) or asynchronous (non- blocking). If it is specified as synchronous (blocking) the function will wait until the write has completed and returned from the server before further code execution. This parameter is "False", or asynchronous, by default. If you specify this parameter the rest of the parameters need to be explicitly specified, including nOffset which should be set as 0 if the tag is not an array tag.
paramDocs.ClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Tag resides. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks.

tan.name: Tan
tan.doc: Calculates the trigonometric tangent of an angle.

taskcall.name: TaskCall
taskcall.doc: Calls a Cicode function by specifying the function name and providing an arguments string.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the function to call, as a string.
paramDocs.sArgs;: The arguments to pass to the function, separated by commas (,). Enclose string arguments in quotes "" and use the string escape character (^) around strings enclosed within a string.

taskcluster.name: TaskCluster
taskcluster.doc: Gets the name of the cluster context in which the current task is executing.
taskcluster.returns: The cluster name of the current context or an empty string if the task is executing without a cluster context.

taskgetsignal.name: TaskGetSignal
taskgetsignal.doc: Retrieves a value that indicates the signal that is currently set for a specific task. This function can be used to check the value of the current signal before using TaskSetSignal to apply a new signal.
taskgetsignal.returns: The value of the current signal. (0 (zero) represents normal operation, 1 indicates the task is stopped).

paramDocs.Hnd: The task's handle. To retrieve this use the function TaskHnd().

taskhnd.name: TaskHnd
taskhnd.doc: Gets the task handle of a specific task. You can then use the task handle with other task functions to control the task. If you do not specify a thread name, it will default to that of the current task.
taskhnd.returns: The task handle, identifying the table where all data on the task is stored.

paramDocs.sName: The thread name of the task. The thread name is the name of the function that was passed to the TaskNew() function. For example, if. . .

taskkill.name: TaskKill
taskkill.doc: Kills a task. The Cicode task will be stopped and will not run again.
taskkill.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hTask: The task handle, returned from the TaskNew() or TaskHnd() function. The task handle identifies the table where all data on the associated task is stored.

tasknew.name: TaskNew
tasknew.doc: Creates a new Cicode task and returns the task handle. You pass the sName of the function (that creates the task) as a string, not as the function tag, and pass the arguments for that function in Arg. After the task is created, it runs in parallel to the calling task. The new task will run forever unless it returns from the function or is killed by another task.
tasknew.returns: The task handle, or -1 if the task cannot be successfully created. The task handle identifies the table where data on the associated task is stored.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the function to create the task, as a string.
paramDocs.sArg: The set of arguments to be passed to the function. Individual arguments need to be separated by commas (,). Enclose string arguments in quotes "" and use the string escape character (^) around strings enclosed within a string. If the string in quotes is not enclosed, then the string is only the first tag found. The entire set of arguments need to be enclosed in quotes ("").
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster context to be applied to the new Cicode task. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the task via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "". You may pass "-" as the ClusterName argument to run the requested Cicode task without a cluster context.

tasknewex.name: TaskNewEx
tasknewex.doc: Creates a new Cicode task with an individual subscription rate and returns the task handle. You pass the sName of the function (that creates the task) as a string, not as the function tag, and pass the arguments for that function in Arg. After the task is created, it runs in parallel to the calling task. The new task will run forever with tags updated at the specified time interval unless it returns from the function or is killed by another task.
tasknewex.returns: The task handle, or -1 if the task cannot be successfully created. The task handle identifies the table where data on the associated task is stored.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the function to create the task, as a string.
paramDocs.sArg: The set of arguments to be passed to the function. Individual arguments need to be separated by commas (,). Enclose string arguments in quotes "" and use the string escape character (^) around strings enclosed within a string. If you do not enclose the string in quotes, then the string is only the first tag found. The entire set of arguments need to be enclosed in quotes ("").
paramDocs.SubscriptionRate: The subscription rate for the task, between 0 and 60000 milliseconds, which determines the frequency at which the I/ O Server reads I/O device data in order to provide tags with up-to-date Cicode variables. A value of -1 may be passed which will use the current task's subscription rate or the default value as set by the existing parameter [Code]TimeData which defaults to 250.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster context to be applied to the new Cicode task. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the task via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "". You may pass "-" as the ClusterName argument to run the requested Cicode task without a cluster context.

taskresume.name: TaskResume
taskresume.doc: Resumes a task that was suspended by the TaskSuspend() function. After a task is resumed, it runs on the next time-slice.
taskresume.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hTask: The task handle, returned from the TaskNew() or TaskHnd() function. The task handle identifies the table where all data on the associated task is stored.

tasksetsignal.name: TaskSetSignal
tasksetsignal.doc: Manually applies a signal to a specified task.
tasksetsignal.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Hnd: The task's handle. To retrieve this use the function TaskHnd().
paramDocs.nSignal: Allows you to signal a specified task. Set to 0 (zero) for normal operation, 1 to stop the task or any other number that represents a defined signal.

tasksuspend.name: TaskSuspend
tasksuspend.doc: Suspends a task. The task will stop running and will start again only when TaskResume() is called.
tasksuspend.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hTask: The task handle, returned from the TaskNew() or TaskHnd() function. The task handle identifies the table where all data on the associated task is stored.

testrandomwave.name: TestRandomWave
testrandomwave.doc: Generates a random wave. The height of the wave is restricted by minimum and maximum values. You can offset the starting point of the wave, for example, to display multiple waves at the same AN. You can use this function to generate test input.
testrandomwave.returns: The value of the random wave.

paramDocs.Period: The number of seconds required to generate one cycle of the wave. If no period is entered, the period has a default of 60.
paramDocs.Low: The lowest value of the wave. If no low value is entered, this value has a default of 0.
paramDocs.High: The highest value of the wave. If no high value is entered, this value has a default of 100.
paramDocs.Offset: The offset in seconds, to generate the wave. If no offset is entered, the offset has a default of 0.

testsawwave.name: TestSawWave
testsawwave.doc: Generates a saw wave. The height of the wave is restricted by minimum and maximum values. You can offset the starting point of the wave, for example, to display multiple waves at the same AN. You can use this function to generate test input.
testsawwave.returns: The value of the saw wave.

paramDocs.Period: The number of seconds required to generate one cycle of the wave. If no period is entered, the period has a default of 60.
paramDocs.Low: The lowest value of the wave. If no low value is entered, this value has a default of 0.
paramDocs.High: The highest value of the wave. If no high value is entered, this value has a default of 100.
paramDocs.Offset: The offset in seconds, to generate the wave. If no offset is entered, the offset has a default of 0.

testsinwave.name: TestSinWave
testsinwave.doc: Generates a sine wave. The height of the wave is restricted by minimum and maximum values. You can offset the starting point of the wave, for example, to display multiple waves at the same AN. You can use this function to generate test input.
testsinwave.returns: The value of the sine wave.

paramDocs.Period: The number of seconds required to generate one cycle of the wave. If no period is entered, the period has a default of 60.
paramDocs.Low: The lowest value of the wave. If no low value is entered, this value has a default of 0.
paramDocs.High: The highest value of the wave. If no high value is entered, this value has a default of 100.
paramDocs.Offset: The offset in seconds, to generate the wave. If no offset is entered, the offset has a default of 0.

testsquarewave.name: TestSquareWave
testsquarewave.doc: Generates a square wave. The height of the wave is restricted by minimum and maximum values. You can offset the starting point of the wave, for example, to display multiple waves at the same AN. You can use this function to generate test input.
testsquarewave.returns: The value of the square wave.

paramDocs.Period: The number of seconds required to generate one cycle of the wave. If no period is entered, the period has a default of 60.
paramDocs.Low: The lowest value of the wave. If no low value is entered, this value has a default of 0.
paramDocs.High: The highest value of the wave. If no high value is entered, this value has a default of 100.
paramDocs.Offset: The offset in seconds, to generate the wave. If no offset is entered, the offset has a default of 0.

testtriangwave.name: TestTriangWave
testtriangwave.doc: Generates a triangular wave. The height of the wave is restricted by minimum and maximum values. You can offset the starting point of the wave, for example, to display multiple waves at the same AN. You can use this function to generate test input.
testtriangwave.returns: The value of the triangular wave.

paramDocs.Period: The number of seconds required to generate one cycle of the wave. If no period is entered, the period has a default of 60.
paramDocs.Low: The lowest value of the wave. If no low value is entered, this value has a default of 0.
paramDocs.High: The highest value of the wave. If no high value is entered, this value has a default of 100.
paramDocs.Offset: The offset in seconds, to generate the wave. If no offset is entered, the offset has a default of 0.

time.name: Time
time.doc: Gets the current time in string format.

timecurrent.name: TimeCurrent
timecurrent.doc: Gets the current system time/date in time/date variable format. Please be aware that Plant SCADA stores time as the number of seconds since 01/01/1970. You can convert this value into usable date and time variables by using the various Date and Time functions.

timehour.name: TimeHour
timehour.doc: Gets the hour value from a time/date variable.

timeinfo.name: TimeInfo
timeinfo.doc: Returns the time format currently used on the Plant SCADA Server.
timeinfo.returns: Depending on the nInfo argument passed to the function, a string containing:

paramDocs.nInfo: Determines the contents of the string returned by the TimeInfo() function. Valid values and resulting strings are:

timeinttotimestamp.name: TimeIntToTimestamp
timeinttotimestamp.doc: Converts a time INTEGER which is represented as a number of seconds since 01/01/1970 to a TIMESTAMP.
timeinttotimestamp.returns: A TIMESTAMP variable or INVALID_TIMESTAMP if invalid.

paramDocs.Millesecond: The number of milliseconds since last second (optional).

timemidnight.name: TimeMidNight
timemidnight.doc: Returns the number of seconds between midnight on January 1, 1970, and the midnight immediately prior to the specified time/date. This function is useful for performing calculations with the time and date.

timemin.name: TimeMin
timemin.doc: Gets the minutes value from a time/date variable.

timesec.name: TimeSec
timesec.doc: Gets the seconds value from a time/date variable.

timeset.name: TimeSet
timeset.doc: Sets the new system time. You can set the time only on the computer which this function is called.
timeset.returns: The error status of the set

paramDocs.Time: The time/date variable to which the new time is set. Sets the time on this computer only.

timestampadd.name: TimestampAdd
timestampadd.doc: Adds an offset to a TIMESTAMP variable.
timestampadd.returns: The TIMESTAMP variable, or INVALID_TIMESTAMP if invalid.

paramDocs.Timestamp: The timestamp to which Offset will be added
paramDocs.Offset: The offset to add, expressed in units of the part parameter

timestampcreate.name: TimestampCreate
timestampcreate.doc: Returns a TIMESTAMP variable created from the parts.
timestampcreate.returns: The composed TIMESTAMP variable, or INVALID_TIMESTAMP if invalid

paramDocs.Timestamp: The timestamp from which the part will be extracted.

timestampcurrent.name: TimestampCurrent
timestampcurrent.doc: Return the current system date and time as a TIMESTAMP variable.
timestampcurrent.returns: A TIMESTAMP variable containing the current system date and time.

timestampdifference.name: TimestampDifference
timestampdifference.doc: Returns the difference between two TIMESTAMP variables as a number of milliseconds.
timestampdifference.returns: The time period between Timestamp1 and Timestamp2. The value is equal or greater than zero. If error, returns 0 with an error code.

paramDocs.Part: The type of time units being used for the result:
paramDocs.bCumulative: Defines how to pass results which values are greater than their time units (see example below).

timestampformat.name: TimestampFormat
timestampformat.doc: Format a TIMESTAMP variable into a string.
timestampformat.returns: A string containing the converted time/date, or an empty string if invalid.

paramDocs.Format: The format of the string is the same as .NET Framework DateTime format. Specifically be reminded that the format is case sensitive. For example 'MM' is the zero padded month number, whereas 'mm' is the zero padded current minute within the hour. Therefore no Year, Day or Seconds will be displayed if they are specified in uppercase as: YYYY, DD, SS. The correct display will only occur when they are specified in lowercase as: yyyy, dd, ss.

timestampgetpart.name: TimestampGetPart
timestampgetpart.doc: Returns one part (year, month, day, etc) of the TIMESTAMP variable.
timestampgetpart.returns: The required part of the TIMESTAMP variable.

paramDocs.Timestamp: The timestamp from which the part will be extracted.

timestampsub.name: TimestampSub
timestampsub.doc: Subtracts an offset from a TIMESTAMP variable.
timestampsub.returns: The TIMESTAMP variable, or INVALID_TIMESTAMP if invalid.

paramDocs.Timestamp: The timestamp to which Offset will be subtracted
paramDocs.Offset: The offset to subtract, expressed in units of the part parameter

timestamptostr.name: TimestampToStr
timestamptostr.doc: Converts a TIMESTAMP variable into a string.
timestamptostr.returns: A string containing the converted time/date or period variable, or an empty string if invalid.

paramDocs.Format: The format number determines which of date/time patterns are used for formatting returned string. Date/time patterns are defined in regional settings on a particular computer and can vary depend on national or individual preferences. The possible format numbers together with examples based on en-US regional settings are listed below:

timestamptotimeint.name: TimestampToTimeInt
timestamptotimeint.doc: Converts a TIMESTAMP variable into a time INTEGER which is represented as a number of seconds since 01/01/1970.
timestamptotimeint.returns: Time as a number of seconds since 01/01/1970 in UTC or local time depending on the last input parameter,-1 if invalid.

timetooledate.name: TimeToOLEDate
timetooledate.doc: Converts a Plant SCADA time/date value to an OLE DATE value (this should be stored in a REAL).

paramDocs.Local: 1 - The return value is output as Local time.

timetostr.name: TimeToStr
timetostr.doc: Converts a time/date variable into a string. Use this function for calculating time differences or run times, and so on. Set Format to 6 to convert time periods that are in milliseconds, such as the times that are returned from the SysTime() and SysTimeDelta() functions.
timetostr.returns: A string containing the converted time/date or period variable, or an empty string if invalid.

timeutcoffset.name: TimeUTCOffset
timeutcoffset.doc: Determines the local time bias from UTC that was in force at a specified time. For example, US Pacific Standard Time is -8 hrs from UTC, so -28800 would be returned (-8 hours x 60 minutes x 60 seconds). However, if the specified time occurred during daylight saving, the returned value would be -7 hours (or -25200 seconds).
timeutcoffset.returns: The local time bias in seconds.

toggle.name: Toggle
toggle.doc: Toggles a digital tag on or off. If the variable tag is ON (1), this function will turn it OFF. If the variable tag is OFF (0), this function will turn it ON.
toggle.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

tracemsg.name: TraceMsg
tracemsg.doc: Displays a message in the Kernel and Debugger debug windows.
tracemsg.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

trenddspcursorcomment.name: TrendDspCursorComment
trenddspcursorcomment.doc: Displays the Trend Comment for the currently selected pen on the displayed trend graph.
trenddspcursorcomment.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the trend.

trenddspcursorscale.name: TrendDspCursorScale
trenddspcursorscale.doc: Displays a scale value for the current pen in the current pen font.
trenddspcursorscale.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the trend.
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of full scale to display for the current pen, as an integer.

trenddspcursortag.name: TrendDspCursorTag
trenddspcursortag.doc: Displays the trend tag name of the current pen in the pen font.
trenddspcursortag.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the trend.
paramDocs.Mode: An optional argument used to specify whether the trend tag name is displayed with a cluster prefix. Set:

trenddspcursortime.name: TrendDspCursorTime
trenddspcursortime.doc: Displays the cursor time of the current pen in the current pen font.
trenddspcursortime.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN number of the trend.

trenddspcursorvalue.name: TrendDspCursorValue
trenddspcursorvalue.doc: Display the cursor value of the current pen in the current pen font.
trenddspcursorvalue.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the trend.

trendgetan.name: TrendGetAn
trendgetan.doc: Gets the AN number of the trend beneath the current mouse position.
trendgetan.returns: The AN of the trend, or 0 (zero) if the mouse is not positioned over a valid trend.

trendpopup.name: TrendPopUp
trendpopup.doc: Displays a pop-up trend with the specified trend pens. You need to create the trend page with the graphic builder and set the pen names to blank.
trendpopup.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the trend page (drawn with the Graphics Builder).
paramDocs.sTag1: The First trend tag to display on the page.
paramDocs.sTag2..sTag8: The trend tags to display on the page.

trendrun.name: TrendRun
trendrun.doc: Initializes the cursor and rubber-band features on a trend page. This function is included as a Cicode Object on all new trend pages. Only use this function when configuring a trend template that requires this functionality.
trendrun.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

trendsetdate.name: TrendSetDate
trendsetdate.doc: Sets the end date for all pens on a trend. Samples taken after this date will not be displayed. You can enter the date in the Value argument, or leave the Value blank - a form is then displayed in run time for the operator to enter an end date.
trendsetdate.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the trend.
paramDocs.Value: The new date, as a string. Samples taken after date will not be displayed. This argument is optional.

trendsetscale.name: TrendSetScale
trendsetscale.doc: Sets the scale of the current pen or of all pens on a trend. You can enter a scale in the Value argument, or leave the Value blank. A form is then displayed in run time for the operator to enter a value for the scale.
trendsetscale.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the trend.
paramDocs.Value: An optional value for the scale, as a string.

trendsetspan.name: TrendSetSpan
trendsetspan.doc: Sets the span time of the trend. The span time is the time period covered in the trend window. You can enter a span time in the Value argument, or leave the Value blank - a form is then displayed in run time for the operator to enter a value for the span time.
trendsetspan.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the trend.
paramDocs.Value: An optional value for the span time, as a string.

trendsettime.name: TrendSetTime
trendsettime.doc: Sets the end time for all the pens on a trend. Samples taken after this time will not be displayed. You can enter an end time in the Value argument, or leave the Value blank - a form is then displayed in run time for the operator to enter a value for the end time.
trendsettime.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the trend.
paramDocs.Value: An optional value for the end time, as a string. Samples taken after this time will not be displayed.

trendsettimebase.name: TrendSetTimebase
trendsettimebase.doc: Sets a new sampling period for a trend. You can enter a sampling period in the Value argument, or leave the Value blank. A form is then displayed in run time for the operator to enter a value for the sampling period.
trendsettimebase.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the trend.
paramDocs.Value: An optional value for the sampling period, as a string.

trendwin.name: TrendWin
trendwin.doc: Displays a trend page (in a new window) with the specified trend pens. You need to create the trend page with the graphic builder and set the pen names to blank. You then display that page by calling this function and pass the required trend tags. The function will create a new window with the specified window mode.
trendwin.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPage: The name of the trend page (drawn with the Graphics Builder).
paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.sTag1: The firs trend tag to display on the page.
paramDocs.sTag2..sTag8: The trend tags to display on the page.

trendzoom.name: TrendZoom
trendzoom.doc: "Zooms" a specified trend in either one or both axes. Set the zoom values (TimeZoom and/or ScaleZoom) to greater than one to "zoom in" or to less than one to "zoom out".
trendzoom.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.SourceAN: The AN on which the source trend is located.
paramDocs.TimeZoom: The scale by which the Time axis will be changed (as a real number).
paramDocs.ScaleZoom: The scale by which the Scale axis will be changed (as a real number).
paramDocs.DestAn: The AN on which the destination or target trend is located. If you do not enter a DestAn, it is set to the same AN as SourceAn.

trnaddhistory.name: TrnAddHistory
trnaddhistory.doc: Adds an old (backed up) trend history file to the trend system so that its data can be used. When you back-up a trend file, change its extension so that it indicates the age of the file's trend data (for example, the month and year).
trnaddhistory.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.FileName: The file name and directory path of an old history file. The old file does not need to reside in the same directory as existing active trends to be restored.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Trend Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trnbrowseclose.name: TrnBrowseClose
trnbrowseclose.doc: The TrnBrowseClose function terminates an active data browse session and cleans up all resources associated with the session.
trnbrowseclose.returns: 0 (zero) if the trend browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TrnBrowseOpen call.

trnbrowsefirst.name: TrnBrowseFirst
trnbrowsefirst.doc: The TrnBrowseFirst function places the data browse cursor at the first record.
trnbrowsefirst.returns: 0 (zero) if the trend browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TrnBrowseOpen call.

trnbrowsegetfield.name: TrnBrowseGetField
trnbrowsegetfield.doc: The TrnBrowseGetField function retrieves the value of the specified field from the record the data browse cursor is currently referencing.
trnbrowsegetfield.returns: The value of the specified field as a string. An empty string may or may not be an indication that an error has been detected. This should be checked in this instance to determine if an error has actually occurred.

paramDocs.Session: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TrnBrowseOpen call.
paramDocs.FieldName: The name of the field that references the value to be returned. Supported fields are:

trnbrowsenext.name: TrnBrowseNext
trnbrowsenext.doc: The TrnBrowseNext function moves the data browse cursor forward one record. If you call this function after you have reached the end of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
trnbrowsenext.returns: 0 (zero) if the trend browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TrnBrowseOpen call.

trnbrowsenumrecords.name: TrnBrowseNumRecords
trnbrowsenumrecords.doc: The TrnBrowseNumRecords function returns the number of records that match the filter criteria.
trnbrowsenumrecords.returns: The number of records that have matched the filter criteria. A value of 0 denotes that no records have matched. A value of -1 denotes that the browse session is unable to provide a fixed number. This may be the case if the data being browsed changed during the browse session.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TrnBrowseOpen call.

trnbrowseopen.name: TrnBrowseOpen
trnbrowseopen.doc: The TrnBrowseOpen function initiates a new browse session and returns a handle to the new session that can be used in subsequent data browse function calls.
trnbrowseopen.returns: Returns an integer handle to the browse session. Returns -1 if unsuccessful.

paramDocs.Filter: A filter expression specifying the records to return during the browse. An empty string indicates that all records will be returned. Where a fieldname is not specified in the filter, it is assumed to be tagname. For example, the filter "AAA" is equivalent to "name=AAA".
paramDocs.Fields: Specifies via a comma delimited string the columns to be returned during the browse. An empty string indicates that the server will return all available columns. Supported fields are:
paramDocs.Clusters: An optional parameter that specifies via a comma delimited string the subset of the clusters to browse. An empty string indicates that the connected clusters will be browsed.

trnbrowseprev.name: TrnBrowsePrev
trnbrowseprev.doc: The TrnBrowsePrev function moves the data browse cursor back one record. If you call this function after you have reached the beginning of the records, error 412 is returned (Databrowse session EOF).
trnbrowseprev.returns: 0 (zero) if the trend browse session exists, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.iSession: The handle to a browse session previously returned by a TrnBrowseOpen call.

trnclientinfo.name: TrnClientInfo
trnclientinfo.doc: Gets information about the trend that is being displayed at the AN point.
trnclientinfo.returns: The requested information (as a string) if successful, otherwise a hardware alarm is generated.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN point number at which the trend is displayed.
paramDocs.nType: The type of information you would like returned.
paramDocs.Data: For future enhancements; is currently ignored.
paramDocs.Error: Output Parameter: If the function is successful, the error is set to 0 (zero). If unsuccessful, an error value is set, and a hardware alarm is triggered. Must be a Long type variable.

trncompareplot.name: TrnComparePlot
trncompareplot.doc: Prints two trends, one overlaid on the other. Each trend can have up to four tags configured on it. The significance of this type of plot is that the two trends show different times and display periods. It is possible to compare a trend tag or tags over different time slots. Each trend line is drawn with a different pen style and marker as appropriate. The trend plot includes a comment and a legend, and you can specify the vertical high and low scales.
trncompareplot.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPort: The name of the printer port to which the plot will be printed. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks. For example LPT1:, to print to the local printer, or \\Pserver\canon1 using UNC to print to a network printer.
paramDocs.sTtile: The title of the trend plot.
paramDocs.sComment: The comment that is to display beneath the title of the trend plot. You do not have to enter a comment.
paramDocs.nAN: Sets the display mode. A value of 0 causes the default display mode to be used. Otherwise, the display mode of the specified AN is set.
paramDocs.iMode: The color mode of the printer.
paramDocs.nSamples: The number of data points on the plot.
paramDocs.iTime1: The end point in time (the most recent point) for the first trend.
paramDocs.rPeriod1: The period (in seconds) of the first trend. This can differ from the actual trend period. If you do not enter a period, it defaults to the sample period of Tag1.
paramDocs.iTime2: The end point in time (the most recent point) for the second trend.
paramDocs.rPeriod2: The period (in seconds) of the second trend. This can differ from the actual trend period. If you do not enter a period, it defaults to the sample period of Tag5.
paramDocs.Tag1. . .Tag8: The trend tags for the plot. Tags 1 to 4 needs to be for the first trend, and tags 5 to 8 needs to be for the second.

trndelete.name: TrnDelete
trndelete.doc: Deletes a trend that is displayed on a current page. This trend may have been created by the TrnNew() function or by a trend object.
trndelete.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.

trndelhistory.name: TrnDelHistory
trndelhistory.doc: Removes a trend history file that has been added to the trend system by the TrnAddHistory() function. This function does not delete the file completely, it only disconnects it from the historical trend system.
trndelhistory.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.FileName: The trend history file to disconnect from the historical trend system.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Specifies the name of the cluster in which the Trend Server resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend server via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trnecho.name: TrnEcho
trnecho.doc: Enables and disables the echo of the trend display. Use this function when you need to make many changes to a trend display, so that the display updates only once. You should first disable the trend echo, do all the trend changes, and then enable the echo to show the changes.
trnecho.returns: The current echo mode, otherwise 0 (zero) is returned, and an error code is set. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.nAN: The animation number of the trend.
paramDocs.nMode: The mode of the echo:

trneventgettable.name: TrnEventGetTable
trneventgettable.doc: Stores event trend data in an event table and the associated time stamp in a time table, for a specified trend tag. Data is stored at the specified Period, working backwards from the starting point specified by EventNo. If Period differs from the trend period configured in the Trend Tags database, the values to be stored are calculated from the trend data. Values are either averaged or interpolated.
trneventgettable.returns: The actual number of samples read. The return value is 0 if an error is detected. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code. If EventNo is 0 (zero) then the EventNo will be set to the current event number.

paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag enclosed in quotation marks "" (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.Tag).
paramDocs.EventNo: The starting event number for entries in the trend table.
paramDocs.Period: The time difference between tabulated trend values (in seconds). For example, if you set this period to 30 seconds, Plant SCADA will get the last trend value (sampled at the end of the trend section), then get the trend value that was sampled 30 seconds before that, and so on until it reaches the start time of the trend section.
paramDocs.Length: The number of trend values to store in the trend table, from 1 to the maximum number of items in the table.
paramDocs.Table: The Cicode array in which the trend data is stored. You can enter the name of an array here (see the example). Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.TimeTable: The table of integer values in which the time stamp is stored. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.Mode: The Display Mode parameters allow you to enter a single integer to specify the display options for a trend (for a maximum of eight trends).
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trneventgettablems.name: TrnEventGetTableMS
trneventgettablems.doc: Stores event trend data and time data (including milliseconds) for a specified trend tag. The event trend data is stored in an event table, and the time stamp in time tables. Data is stored at the specified Period, working backwards from the starting point specified by EventNo. If Period differs from the trend period configured in the Trend Tags database, the values to be stored are calculated from the trend data. Values are either averaged or interpolated.
trneventgettablems.returns: The actual number of samples read. The return value is 0 if an error is detected. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag enclosed in quotation marks "" (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.Tag).
paramDocs.EventNo: The starting event number for entries in the trend table.
paramDocs.Period: The time difference between tabulated trend values (in seconds). For example, if you set this period to 30 seconds, Plant SCADA will get the last trend value (sampled at the end of the trend section), then get the trend value that was sampled 30 seconds before that, and so on until it reaches the start time of the trend section.
paramDocs.Length: The number of trend values to store in the trend table, from 1 to the maximum number of items in the table.
paramDocs.Table: The Cicode array in which the trend data is stored. You can enter the name of an array here (see the example). Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.TimeTable: The table of integer values in which the time stamp is stored. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.Mode: The Display Mode parameters allow you to enter a single integer to specify the display options for a trend (for a maximum of eight trends).
paramDocs.MSTimeTable: The table of integer values in which the millisecond component of the time stamp is stored. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trneventsettable.name: TrnEventSetTable
trneventsettable.doc: Sets event trend data and time data for a specified trend tag. The event trend data is set in an event table, and the time stamp in time tables. Data is set at the period specified, working backwards from the starting point specified by EventNo.
trneventsettable.returns: The actual number of samples written. The return value is 0 if an error is detected. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag enclosed in quotation marks "" (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.Tag).
paramDocs.Period: This will be the interval (in seconds) between trend values when they are set (that is, it will be the perceived sampling period for the trend). This period can differ from the actual trend period. Set to 0 (zero) to default to the actual trend period.
paramDocs.Length: The number of trend values in the trend table.
paramDocs.Table: The table of floating-point values in which the trend data is stored. You can enter the name of an array here (see the example). Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.TimeTable: The table of integer values in which the time stamp is stored. If you would like events to stay in correct time-stamp order, sort the values in this table in ascending order. When EventNo is non-zero the values in this table may be zero. This will result in the values of the requested events being overwritten but the time-stamps staying the same. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trneventsettablems.name: TrnEventSetTableMS
trneventsettablems.doc: Sets event trend data and time data (including milliseconds) for a specified trend tag. The event trend data is set in an event table, and the time stamp in time tables. Data is set at the period specified, working backwards from the starting point specified by EventNo.
trneventsettablems.returns: The actual number of samples written. The return value is 0 if an error is detected. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag enclosed in quotation marks "" (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.Tag).
paramDocs.Period: This will be the interval (in seconds) between trend values when they are set (that is it will be the perceived sampling period for the trend). This period can differ from the actual trend period. Set to 0 (zero) to default to the actual trend period.
paramDocs.Length: Number of trend values in the trend table.
paramDocs.Table: Table of floating-point values in which the trend data is stored. You can enter the name of an array here (see example). Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.TimeTable: Table of integer values in which the time stamp is stored. If you would like events to stay in correct time-stamp order, sort the values in this table in ascending order. When EventNo is non-zero the values in this table may be zero. This will result in the values of the requested events being overwritten but the timestamps staying the same. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.MSTimeTable: The table of integer values in which the millisecond component of the time stamp is stored. Must be a Long type variable.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trnexportclip.name: TrnExportClip
trnexportclip.doc: Exports trend data to the Windows Clipboard. The data is set at the specified Time and Period, and listed from earliest to latest. Any gated or invalid data is written as 0.0.
trnexportclip.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Time: The starting time for the data being exported.
paramDocs.Period: The period (in seconds) of the entries being exported. (This period can differ from the actual trend period.)
paramDocs.Length: The length of the data table, that is The number of rows of samples to be exported. for example if you put the length as 12, and you declare two tags to be exported, you get a grid with 12 rows of samples. Each row has values for each of the two tags making a total of 24 samples.
paramDocs.Mode: The format mode to be used:
paramDocs.ClipMode: The format for the data being exported.
paramDocs.sTag1 ... sTag8: The trend tag names for the data being exported.
paramDocs.iDisplayMode1 ... iDisplayMode8: The Display Mode parameters allow you to enter a single integer to specify the display options for a trend (for a maximum of eight trends).

trnexportcsv.name: TrnExportCSV
trnexportcsv.doc: Exports trend data to a file in CSV (Comma Separated Variable) format. The data is set at the specified Time and Period, and listed from earliest to latest. Any gated or invalid data is written as 0.0.
trnexportcsv.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Filename: The name of the destination path and file.
paramDocs.Time: The starting time for the data being exported.
paramDocs.Period: The period (in seconds) of the entries being exported. (This period can differ from the actual trend period.)
paramDocs.Length: The length of the data table, that is, The number of rows of samples to be exported. for example if you put the length as 12, and you declare two tags to be exported, you get a grid with 12 rows of samples. Each row has values for each of the two tags making a total of 24 samples.
paramDocs.Mode: The format mode to be used:
paramDocs.sTag1 ... sTag8: The trend tag names for the data being exported.
paramDocs.iDisplayMode1 ... iDisplayMode8: The Display Mode parameters allow you to enter a single integer to specify the display options for a trend (for a maximum of eight trends).

trnexportdbf.name: TrnExportDBF
trnexportdbf.doc: Exports trend data to a file in dBASE III format. The data is set at the specified Time and Period, and listed from earliest to latest. Any gated or invalid data is written as 0.0.
trnexportdbf.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Filename: The name of the destination path and file.
paramDocs.Time: The starting time for the data being exported.
paramDocs.Period: The period (in seconds) of the entries being exported. (This period can differ from the actual trend period.)
paramDocs.Length: The length of the data table, that is The number of rows of samples to be exported. for example if you put the length as 12, and you declare two tags to be exported, you get a grid with 12 rows of samples. Each row has values for each of the two tags making a total of 24 samples.
paramDocs.Mode: The format mode to be used:
paramDocs.sTag1 ... sTag8: The trend tag names for the data being exported. Tag names longer than 10 characters will be truncated, as the standard DBF field format is 10 characters.
paramDocs.iDisplayMode1 ... iDisplayMode8: The Display Mode parameters allow you to enter a single integer to specify the display options for a trend (for a maximum of eight trends).

trnexportdde.name: TrnExportDDE
trnexportdde.doc: Exports trend data via DDE. The data is set at the specified Time and Period, and listed from earliest to latest. Any gated or invalid data is written as 0.0. Data is stored as a grid, with each row time-stamped. The first column/field is the date, followed by the time, followed by the tags 1 to 8.
trnexportdde.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sApplication: The application name to export the data.
paramDocs.sDocument: The document in the application to export the data.
paramDocs.sTopic: The topic in the application to export the data. Be aware you may have to use a special topic format to make the data export correctly. See your application documentation for details; For example with Excel you need to specify the matrix of rows and columns as "R1C1:R8C50" depending on the size of the data.
paramDocs.Filename: The name of the destination path and file.
paramDocs.Time: The starting time for the data being exported.
paramDocs.Period: The period (in seconds) of the entries being exported. (This period can differ from the actual trend period.)
paramDocs.Length: The length of the data table, that is The number of rows of samples to be exported. for example if you put the length as 12, and you declare two tags to be exported, you get a grid with 12 rows of samples. Each row has values for each of the two tags making a total of 24 samples.
paramDocs.Mode: The format mode to be used:
paramDocs.DDEMode: The format for the data being exported. CSV format allows the application to separate the data into each individual element, however not every application will support this mode. See you applications documentation for details.
paramDocs.sTag1 ... sTag8: The trend tag names for the data being exported. Tag names longer than 10 characters will be truncated, as the standard DBF field format is 10 characters.
paramDocs.iDisplayMode1 ... iDisplayMode8: The Display Mode parameters allow you to enter a single integer to specify the display options for a trend (for a maximum of eight trends).

trnflush.name: TrnFlush
trnflush.doc: Writes acquired trend data to disk without waiting for the trend buffer to be filled. Plant SCADA normally buffers the trend data in memory and only writes to disk when required, to give optimum performance. Because this function reduces the performance of the Trends Server, use it only when necessary.
trnflush.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the logging tag (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.Tag). Set to " * " to flush all trend data.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trngetbufevent.name: TrnGetBufEvent
trngetbufevent.doc: Gets the event number of a trend at an offset for a specified pen. This function only operates on an event-based trend.
trngetbufevent.returns: The event number. If Offset is not within boundaries, 0 (zero) is returned. If AN or Pen is invalid, 0 (zero) is returned and an error code is set.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.
paramDocs.Offset: The trend buffer offset, in samples. The number of samples can range from 0 to the maximum number of samples that can display on the trend - 1.

trngetbuftime.name: TrnGetBufTime
trngetbuftime.doc: Gets the time and date of a trend at an offset for a specified pen. The Offset should be a value between 0 (zero) and the number of samples displayed on the trend.
trngetbuftime.returns: A time/date variable. If Offset is not within boundaries, 0 (zero) is returned. If nAN or Pen is invalid, 0(zero) is returned and an error code is set.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.
paramDocs.Offset: The trend buffer offset, in samples. The number of samples can range from 0 to the maximum number of samples that can display on the trend - 1.

trngetbufvalue.name: TrnGetBufValue
trngetbufvalue.doc: Gets the value of a trend at an offset for a specified pen. The offset should be a value between -1 and the number of samples displayed on the trend.
trngetbufvalue.returns: The trend value. If the actual value is gated or invalid, the standard invalid or gated values are returned (no error is set). You can check this return value using TrnIsValidValue().

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.
paramDocs.Offset: The trend buffer offset, in samples. The number of samples can range from -1 to the maximum number of samples that can display on the trend minus 1.

trngetcluster.name: TrnGetCluster
trngetcluster.doc: Gets the cluster name of a trend graph on a page.
trngetcluster.returns: The name of the cluster the trend graph is associated with.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend graph.

trngetcursorevent.name: TrnGetCursorEvent
trngetcursorevent.doc: Gets the event number of a trend, at the trend cursor position for a specified pen. This function only operates on an event-based trend.
trngetcursorevent.returns: The event number, or 0 (zero) if the trend cursor is disabled.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.

trngetcursormstime.name: TrnGetCursorMSTime
trngetcursormstime.doc: Gets the time (in milliseconds from the previous midnight) at a trend cursor for a specified pen.
trngetcursormstime.returns: The number of milliseconds since the previous midnight. If the trend cursor is disabled, 0 (zero) is returned. If nAN or Pen is invalid, 0 (zero) is returned and an error code is set.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.

trngetcursorpos.name: TrnGetCursorPos
trngetcursorpos.doc: Gets the offset of a trend cursor from its origin, in samples.
trngetcursorpos.returns: The offset of a trend cursor from its origin, in samples, or -1 if the trend cursor is disabled.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.

trngetcursortime.name: TrnGetCursorTime
trngetcursortime.doc: Gets the time and date at a trend cursor for a specified pen.
trngetcursortime.returns: A time/date variable. If the trend cursor is disabled, 0 (zero) is returned. If nAN or Pen is invalid, 0 (zero) is returned and an error code is set.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.

trngetcursorvalue.name: TrnGetCursorValue
trngetcursorvalue.doc: Gets the value at a trend cursor for a specified pen.
trngetcursorvalue.returns: The trend value. If the actual value is gated or invalid, the standard invalid or gated values are returned (no error is set). You can check this return value using TrnIsValidValue().

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.

trngetcursorvaluestr.name: TrnGetCursorValueStr
trngetcursorvaluestr.doc: Gets the value at a trend cursor for a specified pen. The value is returned as a formatted string using the pen's format specification and (optionally) the engineering units.
trngetcursorvaluestr.returns: The trend value (as a string). If trend data is invalid, or an argument passed to the function is invalid "<na>" is returned. If the actual value is gated (not triggered) "<gated>" is returned. If the trend cursor is disabled, an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN where the trend is located.

trngetdefscale.name: TrnGetDefScale
trngetdefscale.doc: Gets the default engineering zero and full scales of a trend tag.
trngetdefscale.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag enclosed in quotation marks "" (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is "ClusterName.Tag").
paramDocs.LoScale: The engineering zero scale. Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.HiScale: The engineering full scale. Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trngetdisplaymode.name: TrnGetDisplayMode
trngetdisplaymode.doc: Returns the display mode of the selected trend pen. The display mode is set using TrnSetDisplayMode.
trngetdisplaymode.returns: An integer representing the trend's display mode:

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trngetevent.name: TrnGetEvent
trngetevent.doc: Gets the event number of the trend at a percentage along the trend, using the current event as the base point. This function only operates on an event-based trend. The first recorded event (the start event) would be event number 1 and the highest number would be the latest event. The event number is stored in a LONG and would eventually wrap around if you have enough events.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of the trend from the starting event, from 0 (the start event) to 100 (the end event).

trngetformat.name: TrnGetFormat
trngetformat.doc: Gets the format of a trend tag being plotted by a specified pen.
trngetformat.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Width: Variable denoting the width of the format.
paramDocs.DecPlaces: Variable denoting the number of decimal places in the format.

trngetgatedvalue.name: TrnGetGatedValue
trngetgatedvalue.doc: Returns the internally stored value for <GATED>. If the internally stored value changes in the future, you will not need to modify your Cicode, as this function will return the correct value.

trngetinvalidvalue.name: TrnGetInvalidValue
trngetinvalidvalue.doc: Returns the internally stored value for <INVALID>. If the internally stored value changes in the future, you will not need to modify your Cicode, as this function will return the correct value.

trngetmode.name: TrnGetMode
trngetmode.doc: Gets the mode (real-time or historical trending) of the trend pen.
trngetmode.returns: The current mode, 0 for real-time or 1 for historical.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trngetmstime.name: TrnGetMSTime
trngetmstime.doc: Gets the time (in milliseconds from the previous midnight) of the trend (plotted by a specified pen) at a percentage along the trend, using the time and date of the right-most sample displayed. The time associated with the right-most sample displayed is known as the end time. The start time is the time of the left-most sample displayed. Percent 0 (zero) will correspond to the end time, and Percent 100 will correspond to the start time
trngetmstime.returns: The number of milliseconds since the previous midnight. Zero (0) is returned if an error is detected.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of the trend from the time and date of the right-most sample displayed (end time), from 0 to 100.

trngetpen.name: TrnGetPen
trngetpen.doc: Gets the trend tag being plotted by a specified pen.
trngetpen.returns: The trend tag (as a string) being plotted by Pen. If nAN or Pen is invalid, an empty string is returned, and an error code is set. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Mode: An optional argument used to specify whether the trend tag name is returned with a cluster prefix. Set:

trngetpencomment.name: TrnGetPenComment
trngetpencomment.doc: Retrieves the comment of a pen.
trngetpencomment.returns: The comment of the pen as a string.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trngetpenfocus.name: TrnGetPenFocus
trngetpenfocus.doc: Gets the number of the pen currently in focus.
trngetpenfocus.returns: The pen currently in focus (between 1 and 8). If nAN is invalid, -1 is returned and an error code is set.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trngetpenno.name: TrnGetPenNo
trngetpenno.doc: Gets the pen number of a pen name. The pens on a trend are either defined in the Page Trends database or set by the TrnSetPen() function.
trngetpenno.returns: The pen number, or 0 (zero) if an error is detected.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag.

trngetperiod.name: TrnGetPeriod
trngetperiod.doc: Gets the current display period of a trend. (To obtain the sampling period, use the TrnInfo function.)
trngetperiod.returns: The current display period of a trend (in seconds), or 0 (zero) if an error code is detected.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trngetscale.name: TrnGetScale
trngetscale.doc: Gets the display scale of the trend tag being plotted by a specified pen.
trngetscale.returns: The scale of the trend tag being plotted by Pen. If nAN or Pen is invalid, 0 (zero) is returned and an error code is set.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of the full scale, from 0 to 100.

trngetscalestr.name: TrnGetScaleStr
trngetscalestr.doc: Gets the scale of the trend tag being plotted by a specified pen. The value is returned as a formatted string using the pen's format specification and (optionally) the engineering units.
trngetscalestr.returns: The scale of the trend tag being plotted by Pen (as a string). If nAN or Pen is invalid, <na> is returned and an error code is set.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of the full scale, from 0 to 100.

trngetspan.name: TrnGetSpan
trngetspan.doc: Gets the span time of a trend (if the span was set by the TrnSetSpan() function). The span time is the total time displayed in the trend window.
trngetspan.returns: The span time, in seconds. 0(zero) is returned if the AN is invalid or if the span was not set by the TrnSetSpan() function.

paramDocs.nAN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trngettable.name: TrnGetTable
trngettable.doc: This function allows you to tabulate values from a specific section of trend. The values in the table (possibly an array variable) are arranged by time.
trngettable.returns: The actual number of samples read. 0(zero) is returned if an error occurs. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag enclosed in quotation marks "" (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.Tag).
paramDocs.Time: The end time and date (long integer) of the desired trend section. Once you have entered the end time and date (Time), period (Period), and number of trend tag values collected (Length), the start time and date will be calculated automatically. For example, if Time = StrToDate("21/07/20") + StrToTime("09:00"), Period = 30, and Length = 60, the start time would be 08:30. In other words, the trend values for the period between 8.30am and 9am (on July 21, 2020) would be tabulated.
paramDocs.Period: The time difference between tabulated trend values (in seconds). For example, if you set this period to 30 seconds, Plant SCADA will get the last trend value (sampled at the end of the trend section), then get the trend value that was sampled 30 seconds before that, and so on until it reaches the start time of the trend section.
paramDocs.Length: The number of trend values to store in the trend table, from 1 to the maximum number of items in the table. This argument has a max of 4000 (in v6). Specifying a length of greater than 4000 results in a return value of 0 and IsError()=274 (INVALID_ARGUMENT). This limit can be configured using the citect.ini parameter [Trend]MaxRequestLength.
paramDocs.Table: Variable containing the Cicode array in which the trend data is stored. You can enter the name of an array here (see the example).
paramDocs.DisplayMode: The Display Mode parameters allow you to enter a single integer to specify the display options for a trend (for a maximum of eight trends).
paramDocs.Milliseconds: This argument allows you to set your sample request time with millisecond precision. After defining the time and date in seconds with the Time argument, you can then use this argument to define the milliseconds component of the time.
paramDocs.sClusterName: Name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trngettime.name: TrnGetTime
trngettime.doc: Gets the time and date of the trend (plotted by a specified pen) at a percentage along the trend, using the time and date of the right-most sample displayed. The time associated with the rightmost sample displayed is known as the end time. The start time is the time of the left-most sample displayed. Percent 0 (zero) will correspond to the end time, and Percent 100 will correspond to the start time.
trngettime.returns: A time/date variable. 0 (zero) is returned if an error is detected.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Percent: The percentage of the trend from the time and date of the right-most sample displayed (end time), from 0 to 100.

trngetunits.name: TrnGetUnits
trngetunits.doc: Gets the data units for the trend tag plotted by a specified Pen.
trngetunits.returns: The data units for the trend tag plotted by Pen, otherwise an empty string is returned, and an error code is set. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trninfo.name: TrnInfo
trninfo.doc: Gets the configured values of a trend tag.
trninfo.returns: The value (as a string), otherwise an empty string is returned, and an error code is set. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.2: Sample Period (to obtain the Display Period, use the TrnGetPeriod function)
paramDocs.6: Current Event Number. Valid only for event type trends
paramDocs.8: The storage method used for the tag. A returned value of 2 represents two byte storage (scaled), 8 represents eight byte storage (floating point).
paramDocs.9: The file period of the tag in seconds. If the file period is set to monthly or yearly, a file period cannot be calculated as months and years vary in length. Therefore, a file period of 0 will be returned for trends with such file periods.
paramDocs.Tag: The name of the trend tag enclosed in quotation marks "" (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.Tag).
paramDocs.nType: The type of information required:
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trnisvalidvalue.name: TrnIsValidValue
trnisvalidvalue.doc: Determines whether a logged trend value is:

trnnew.name: TrnNew
trnnew.doc: Creates a new trend at run time. This function performs the same operation as an entry in the Page Trends database. After the trend is created by the TrnNew() function, all the other trend functions can access and control the trend.
trnnew.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the bottom right-hand corner of the trend is located.
paramDocs.Trend: The trend definition number (as a STRING).
paramDocs.Tag1 . . .Tag8: The trend tags. (These tags cannot be prefixed with cluster name, cluster should be specified with the ClusterName argument).
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which all the trend tags reside. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trends via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trnplot.name: TrnPlot
trnplot.doc: Prints the trend line of one or more trend tags. Each trend line is drawn with a different pen style and marker as appropriate. The trend plot includes a comment and a legend, and you can specify the vertical high and low scales. The Mode defines the color mode of the printer. The default mode is black and white.
trnplot.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPort: The name of the printer port to which the plot will be printed. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks. For example LPT1:, to print to the local printer, or \\Pserver\canon1 using UNC to print to a network printer.
paramDocs.nSamples: The number of data points on the plot.
paramDocs.iTime: For periodic trend or event trends displayed as periodic:
paramDocs.rPeriod: The period (in seconds) of the trend plot. This can differ from the actual trend period.
paramDocs.sTitle: The title of the trend plot.
paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend. If you enter 0 (zero), the display mode will default to 258. (This is the display mode that is passed into TrnGetTable() when it is called internally by TrnPlot().) If you call TrnPlot() from a report, you need to enter 0 (zero) here.
paramDocs.iMode: The color mode of the printer.
paramDocs.sComment: The comment that is to display beneath the title of the trend plot. You may pass an empty string if no comment is required.

trnprint.name: TrnPrint
trnprint.doc: Prints the trend that is displayed on the screen (at nAN) using the current display mode for each trend. You can specify the trend title, the target printer, whether to print in color or black and white, and whether to display the Plot Setup form when the function is called.
trnprint.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPort: The name of the printer port to which the plot will be printed. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks "". For example "LPT1:", to print to the local printer, or "\\Pserver\canon1" using UNC to print to a network printer.
paramDocs.sTitle: The title to print at the top of the trend plot. If you omit the title in sTitle, the page title will be used.
paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend plot is located.
paramDocs.iModeColor: The color mode of the printer.
paramDocs.DisplayForm: Defines whether or not the Plot Setup form will display when the function is called. This form allows you to enter the color mode of the printer, and define the printer setup etc. (See Printing Trend Data for more information on this form.)

trnsamplesconfigured.name: TrnSamplesConfigured
trnsamplesconfigured.doc: Gets the number of samples configured for the currently displayed trend.
trnsamplesconfigured.returns: The number of samples configured for the trend, or 0 (zero) if an error is detected. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend is located.

trnscroll.name: TrnScroll
trnscroll.doc: Scrolls the trend pen by a specified percentage (of span), or number of samples.
trnscroll.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend is located. Set to -1 for all trends on the current page.
paramDocs.Pen: The trend pen number. Set to -1 for all pens.
paramDocs.nScroll: The amount by which the trend will be scrolled. Use nMode to specify whether the trend will be scrolled by percentage or by number of samples.
paramDocs.nMode: The type of scrolling to be performed.

trnselect.name: TrnSelect
trnselect.doc: Sets up a page for a trend. This function allows you to set up a trend before the trend page is displayed. You can therefore use a single trend page to display any trend in the project by selecting the trend first, and then displaying the trend page. The PageTrend() function uses this function to display the standard trend pages.
trnselect.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Window: The window number (returned from the WinNumber function).
paramDocs.Page: The name of the page that displays the trend.
paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend displays, or -3 for the first trend on the page.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster that is associated with any trend tag for this trend graph. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trnsetcursor.name: TrnSetCursor
trnsetcursor.doc: Moves the trend cursor by a specified number of samples. If the trend cursor is disabled, this function enables it. If the cursor is enabled and the number of samples is 0 (zero), the cursor is disabled. If the cursor is moved off the current trend frame, the trend scrolls.
trnsetcursor.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend is located. Set to -1 for all trends on the current page.
paramDocs.Samples: The number of samples to move the cursor.

trnsetcursorpos.name: TrnSetCursorPos
trnsetcursorpos.doc: Moves the trend cursor to a specified x-axis point, offset from the trend cursor origin. If the trend cursor is disabled, this function enables it. If the position is outside of the trend frame, it sets the trend cursor to half of the frame.
trnsetcursorpos.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend is located. Set to -1 for all trends on the current page.
paramDocs.Position: The x-axis point at which to position the trend cursor, offset from the trend cursor origin.

trnsetdisplaymode.name: TrnSetDisplayMode
trnsetdisplaymode.doc: Specifies how raw trend samples are displayed on the screen.
trnsetdisplaymode.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The animation number of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.PenNumber: The pen number of the chosen trend. Specify:
paramDocs.DisplayMode: The Display Mode parameters allow you to enter a single integer to specify the display options for a trend (for a maximum of eight trends).

trnsetevent.name: TrnSetEvent
trnsetevent.doc: Sets the start event of a trend pen. This function only operates on an event-based trend.
trnsetevent.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.
paramDocs.Event: The number of the start event.

trnsetpen.name: TrnSetPen
trnsetpen.doc: Sets the trend tag of a trend pen. The trend pen changes to the specified tag and the trend is refreshed. The trend pen needs to be in the operator's area to be displayed. If outside of the operator's area, data is not displayed. You cannot mix periodic trends and event trends in the same trend window.
trnsetpen.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned. Be aware that if a mixture of periodic and event trends is detected, the return value is 0 (zero), but the hardware alarm #329 is set.
