paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend is located.
paramDocs.Pen: The pen for which the trend tag will be changed.
paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag. If Tag = ! the pen is deleted.

trnsetpenfocus.name: TrnSetPenFocus
trnsetpenfocus.doc: Sets the focus to a specified pen. After the focus is set, the focus pen is used with other trend functions.
trnsetpenfocus.returns: The old pen focus number, or -1 if an error is detected. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trnsetperiod.name: TrnSetPeriod
trnsetperiod.doc: Sets the display period (time base) of a trend. When the period is changed, Plant SCADA reads the historical data to reconstruct the trend data, and refreshes the trend. Every pen has the same display period.
trnsetperiod.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend is located. Set to -1 for every trend on the current page.
paramDocs.Period: The new sampling period (in seconds) of the trend. To set the display period to the sampling period, set this argument to 0 (zero),

trnsetscale.name: TrnSetScale
trnsetscale.doc: Sets a new scale for a trend pen. In the automatic scaling mode, the zero and full scales are automatically generated.
trnsetscale.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend is located. Set to -1 for all trends on the current page.
paramDocs.Scale: The new value of the scale. Scale is ignored if Percent is -2.

trnsetspan.name: TrnSetSpan
trnsetspan.doc: Sets the span time of a trend. The span time is the total time displayed in the trend window. You can set the period to contain fractions of a second. For example, if you set a trend with 240 samples to a span of 10 minutes, then each sample would be 2.5 seconds. Choose a span long enough to provide a sufficient sample rate to capture accurate real time data.
trnsetspan.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN of the chosen trend.

trnsettable.name: TrnSetTable
trnsettable.doc: Writes trend tag data from a table to the trend logging system (starting at the top of the table, and continuing to the bottom). Each value is written with a time and date, as specified by Period. If Period differs from the trend sampling period (defined in the Trend Tags database), the trend's sample values will be calculated (averaged or interpolated) from the tabulated trend data.
trnsettable.returns: The actual number of samples written. The return value is 0 if an error is detected. You can call the IsError() function to get the actual error code.

paramDocs.Tag: The trend tag enclosed in quotation marks "" (can be prefixed by the name of the cluster that is ClusterName.Tag).
paramDocs.Time: The time and date (long integer) to be associated with the first value in the table when it is set. Once you have entered the end time and date (Time), set period (Period), and number of trend tag values to be set (Length), the start time and date will be calculated automatically. For example, if Time = StrToDate("22/07/20") + StrToTime("09:00"), Period = 30, and Length = 60, the start time would be 08:30. In other words, the first value from the table would be set with time 9am, and the last would be set with time 8.30am (on July 22, 2020).
paramDocs.Period: This will be the interval (in seconds) between trend values when they are set (that is it will be the perceived sampling period for the trend). This period can differ from the actual trend period. Set to 0 (zero) to default to the actual trend period.
paramDocs.Length: The number of trend values in the trend table.
paramDocs.Table: Variable containing the table of floating-point values in which the trend data is stored. You can enter the name of an array here (see the example). Must be a Real type variable.
paramDocs.Milliseconds: This argument allows you to set the time of the first sample in the table with millisecond precision. After defining the time and date in seconds with the Time argument, you can then use this argument to define the milliseconds component of the time.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster in which the trend tag resides. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the trend via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "".

trnsettime.name: TrnSetTime
trnsettime.doc: Sets the end time and date of a trend pen.
trnsettime.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.AN: The AN where the trend is located, or:
paramDocs.Time: The end time and date of the trend. Samples taken after this time and date will not be displayed. Set to 0 (zero) to set the trend to the current time (real-time mode).

usercreate.name: UserCreate
usercreate.doc: This function is now deprecated and will be removed in the next release. Use the UserCreateByRole function instead.
usercreate.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the user.
paramDocs.sFullName: The full name of the user.
paramDocs.sType: The generic type of user. The type needs to be defined in the general properties for a user in Plant SCADA Studio's Security activity (see Add a Plant SCADA User).
paramDocs.sRole: The role to which the user will be assigned. The role needs to be defined in Plant SCADA Studio's Security activity (see Roles).

usercreatebyrole.name: UserCreateByRole
usercreatebyrole.doc: This function is not available for a Windows user.
usercreatebyrole.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the user.
paramDocs.sFullName: The full name of the user.
paramDocs.sRole: The role(s) to which the user will be assigned. If required, you can enter multiple roles as a comma separated list. The role(s) you specify need to be defined in Plant SCADA Studio's Security activity (see Roles).

usercreateform.name: UserCreateForm
usercreateform.doc: Not available for a Windows user.
usercreateform.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

userdelete.name: UserDelete
userdelete.doc: Not available for a Windows user.
userdelete.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the user.

usereditform.name: UserEditForm
usereditform.doc: Not available for a Windows user.
usereditform.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

userinfo.name: UserInfo
userinfo.doc: Gets information about the operator who is currently logged-in to the system.
userinfo.returns: The information (as a string). If an error is detected, an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.nType: The type of user information:

userlogin.name: UserLogin
userlogin.doc: Logs a user into the Plant SCADA system, using either Windows integrated security or Plant SCADA security and gives users access to the areas and privileges assigned to them in the Users database, and uses the locale language defined for that user. Only one user can be logged into a computer at any one time. If a user is already logged in when a second user logs in, the first user is replaced by the newly logged on user. When a newly logged in user does not have access to view the current page (as defined by the page's area), the system returns to the home page as specified by the parameter[Page]HomePage, and if unsuccessful that returns to the startup page. When multiple pages are currently displayed, this occurs for each open window.

paramDocs.sUserName: The user's name as defined in the Users database, or the Windows User account name, in plain text.
paramDocs.sPassword: The user's password, as defined in the Users database or Windows account formatted as a secure string.
paramDocs.sLanguage: The specified language needs to be one of the languages defined in the Languages view in Plant SCADA Studio's Setup activity. If the specified language is undefined, the default language is used by the login user, and a message "Undefined language" is shown in the prompt line.

userpassword.name: UserPassword
userpassword.doc: Not available for a Windows user.
userpassword.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the user.
paramDocs.sOldPassword: The password assigned to the user before the UserPassword() function is run.

userpasswordexpirydays.name: UserPasswordExpiryDays
userpasswordexpirydays.doc: Not available for a Windows user.
userpasswordexpirydays.returns: The return value contains either the number of days before password expiry, or one of two exception conditions:

userpasswordform.name: UserPasswordForm
userpasswordform.doc: Not available for a Windows user.
userpasswordform.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

usersetstr.name: UserSetStr
usersetstr.doc: Sets the value of the given field for the given user record in the project configuration (users.dbf ) on the local machine.
usersetstr.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the user who's configuration record we wish to modify.
paramDocs.sField: The name of the field in users.dbf to modify.
paramDocs.sData: The new value of the field.

userupdaterecord.name: UserUpdateRecord
userupdaterecord.doc: Triggers a recompile of the local project configuration, then notifies the running system that user configuration has been modified and needs to be reloaded.
userupdaterecord.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

userverify.name: UserVerify
userverify.doc: Verifies a given user by authenticating the user's credential, verifies the user privileges and areas against those specified in the functions parameters. Successful verification however does not log the user into the Plant SCADA runtime system.
userverify.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the user.
paramDocs.sPassword: The password of the user. The sPassword argument needs to be passed as a secure string.
paramDocs.sAccess: Specifies the required user's viewable areas.
paramDocs.sPrivGlobal: Specifies the required user's global privilege.
paramDocs.sPriv1-8: Specifies the required areas for privileges 1 - 8. That is, sPriv1 contains the areas (1,2,3,4,...,255) where the user has Privilege 1.

variablequality.name: VariableQuality
variablequality.doc: Extracts the quality from a given variable.
variablequality.returns: The QUALITY of the given variable. If Variable is NULL, it returns quality uncertain (0x40).

paramDocs.Variable: The variable from which the quality will be extracted.

variabletimestamp.name: VariableTimestamp
variabletimestamp.doc: Extracts the timestamp from a given variable.
variabletimestamp.returns: A TIMESTAMP of the given variable depending on the type. If Variable is NULL, returns INVALID_TIMESTAMP.

paramDocs.Variable: The variable from which the timestamp will be extracted.
paramDocs.nType: The type of timestamp:

verifyprivilegeform.name: VerifyPrivilegeForm
verifyprivilegeform.doc: Displays a form that allows a single user to enter their credentials. These credentials are checked against a specified set to ensure the user has the required privileges before allowing the operation to proceed.
verifyprivilegeform.returns: The name of the user that met the required privileges, otherwise ""

paramDocs.sOperationDescription: A description of the operation that requires approval.
paramDocs.sLogDevice: The name of a log device if logging is required, otherwise pass an empty string.
paramDocs.sAccess: The required user viewable areas, or pass an empty string for none.
paramDocs.sGlobalPriv: The required global privilege, otherwise pass an empty string.
paramDocs.sPriv1..8: Specifies the required areas for privileges 1 - 8. That is, sPriv1 contains the areas (1,2,3,4,...,255) where the user has Privilege 1. Each argument needs to be either specified or an empty string for none.

verifyprivilegetagwrite.name: VerifyPrivilegeTagWrite
verifyprivilegetagwrite.doc: Displays a form that allows any single user to enter their credentials in order to approve a write of a specific value to a specific tag. These credentials are checked against a specified set to ensure the user has the required privileges before allowing the operation to proceed.
verifyprivilegetagwrite.returns: Name of user that met the required privileges (and therefore the value was written to the specified tag), otherwise ""

paramDocs.sTagName: The name of the tag to which a write needs to be approved.
paramDocs.sValuetoWrite: The value to write to the tag if approval succeeds.
paramDocs.sLogDevice: The name of a log device if logging is required, otherwise pass an empty string.
paramDocs.sAccess: The required user viewable areas, or pass an empty string for none.
paramDocs.sGlobalPriv: The required global privilege, otherwise pass an empty string.
paramDocs.sPriv1..8: Specifies the required areas for privileges 1 - 8. That is, sPriv1 contains the areas (1,2,3,4,...,255) where the user has Privilege 1. Each argument needs to be either specified or an empty string for none.

version.name: Version
version.doc: Gets the version number of the Plant SCADA software in use.
version.returns: The version number as a string.

paramDocs.nType: The type of version:

whoami.name: WhoAmI
whoami.doc: Displays the user name and full name of the user currently logged-in to the system. When the current logged on user is Windows user this function returns the user’s full name in the format of <DomainName>\<UserName>. The names are displayed at the prompt AN.
whoami.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

wincopy.name: WinCopy
wincopy.doc: Copies the graphics image of the active window to the Windows Clipboard. You can paste this Clipboard image into other applications.
wincopy.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.xScale: The x scaling factor for the item being copied. This argument is optional, as a default setting of 1 is used to maintain the current horizontal scaling of the image. The outcome is proportional to 1; for example, 0.5 halves the width of the image.
paramDocs.yScale: The y scaling factor for the item being copied. This argument is optional, as a default setting of 1 is used to maintain the current vertical scaling of the image. The outcome is proportional to 1; for example, 0.5 halves the height of the image.
paramDocs.bSwapBlackWhite: Swaps the colors black and white for the purpose of printing pages with a lot of black content. Use the default value of 1 to swap black and white (optional).
paramDocs.sMap: The file name or path of a text based map file used to specify colors to swap when printing. By default Plant SCADA will look in the bin directory for the map file. The format for the map file is:

winfile.name: WinFile
winfile.doc: Writes the graphics image of the active window to a file. The file is saved in the Plant SCADA compressed .bmp format.
winfile.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sFile: The name of the file to be created. If no path information is specified, the function will try to create the file in the bin directory (the current directory of the runtime process). Write permission is required.
paramDocs.xScale: The x scaling factor for the item being printed. This argument is optional, as a default setting of 1 is used to maintain the horizontal scaling of the image. The outcome is proportional to 1; for example, 0.5 halves the width of the image .
paramDocs.yScale: The y scaling factor for the item being printed. This argument is optional, as a default setting of 1 is used to maintain the current vertical scaling of the image. The outcome is proportional to 1; for example, 0.5 halves the height of the image.
paramDocs.bSwapBlackWhite: Swaps the colors black and white for the purpose of printing pages with a lot of black content. Use the default value of 1 to swap black and white (optional).
paramDocs.sMap: The file name or path of a text based map file used to specify colors to swap when printing. By default Plant SCADAwill look in the bin directory for the map file. The format for the map file is:

winfree.name: WinFree
winfree.doc: Removes the active display window. Be aware that the last window (and any child windows owned by the last window) cannot be removed. You cannot call this function as an exit command or from a Cicode Object.
winfree.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

winfreeex.name: WinFreeEx
winfreeex.doc: Removes the active display window and allows you to pass a Windows handle to the function for closing the window. Note that the last window (and any child windows owned by the last window) cannot be removed. You cannot call this function as an exit command or from a Cicode Object.
winfreeex.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Window: The window number (returned from the WinNumber() function). Note that this is not the same as the window handle, returned from the WndFind() function.

wingetclicked.name: WinGetClicked
wingetclicked.doc: Gets the number of the Plant SCADA window that has most recently been clicked on using the left mouse button.
wingetclicked.returns: The window number of the Plant SCADA window that has most recently been clicked on using the left mouse button. Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle, returned from the WndFind() function.

wingetfirstchild.name: WinGetFirstChild
wingetfirstchild.doc: Gets the window number of the first child of a parent window. This number can be used with other functions to control the window.
wingetfirstchild.returns: The window number associated with the first child of the specified parent window. If a child window does not exist, –1 is returned.

paramDocs.Window: The window number of the parent window.

wingetfocus.name: WinGetFocus
wingetfocus.doc: Gets the number of the Plant SCADA window that has the keyboard focus.
wingetfocus.returns: The window number of the Plant SCADA window that has the keyboard focus. Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle, returned from the WndFind() function.

wingetname.name: WinGetName
wingetname.doc: Gets the name previously associated with a particular window number using WinSetName. An association with a window is removed when the window is free-ed.
wingetname.returns: String name associated with window number iWinNum, otherwise an empty string is returned.

paramDocs.iWinNum: An optional parameter which specifies the window number to lookup for the associated Name. If no number is specified, the name returned is the one associated with the currently selected window number.

wingetnextchild.name: WinGetNextChild
wingetnextchild.doc: Gets the window number of the next child in a child link. This number can be used with other functions to control the window.
wingetnextchild.returns: The window number associated with the next child in the child link. If a window does not exist, –1 is returned.

paramDocs.Window: The window number of the previous child in the child link.

wingetparent.name: WinGetParent
wingetparent.doc: Retrieves the window number of the specified window's parent or root window.
wingetparent.returns: The window number of the parent or root window.

paramDocs.WinNum: An optional parameter which specifies the window number of the child window. If no number is specified, it retrieves the window number of the currently selected window's parent or root window.
paramDocs.GetRoot: An optional parameter which determines whether to get the parent or root window. If false, it will retrieve the immediate parent window number (default). If true, it retrieves the root window number by walking the chain of parent windows.

wingetwndhnd.name: WinGetWndHnd
wingetwndhnd.doc: Gets the window handle for the current window. The window handle may be used by 'C' programs and Plant SCADA Wnd... functions. You may pass the windows handle to a 'C' program by using the DLL functions.
wingetwndhnd.returns: The window handle if successful, otherwise 0 (zero) is returned. Be aware that this is not the same as a Plant SCADA window number returned from the WinNumber() function.

wingoto.name: WinGoto
wingoto.doc: Changes the active window. The specified window is placed in front of all other windows and all keyboard commands will apply to this window. You cannot call this function as an exit command or from a Cicode Object.
wingoto.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Window: The window number (returned from the WinNumber() function). Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle, returned from the WndFind() function.

winmode.name: WinMode
winmode.doc: Sets the display mode of the active Plant SCADA window.
winmode.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

winmove.name: WinMove
winmove.doc: Moves the active window to a new location and sizes the window in a single operation. This is the same as calling the WinPos() and the WinSize() functions. You use PageInfo to get the current window position.
winmove.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Width: The width of the window, in pixels.
paramDocs.Height: The height of the window, in pixels.

winnew.name: WinNew
winnew.doc: Opens a new display window, with a specified page displayed. The window can later be destroyed with the WinFree() function.
winnew.returns: The window number of the window, or -1 if the window cannot be opened. Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle returned from the WndFind() function.

paramDocs.Page: The name or page number of the page to display (in quotation marks ""). Can be prefixed by the name of a host cluster, that is "ClusterName.Page". This will take precedence over the use of the ClusterName parameter if the two differ.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster that will accommodate the page at runtime. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the page via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "". If the Page parameter is prefixed with the name of a cluster, this parameter will not be used.

winnewat.name: WinNewAt
winnewat.doc: Opens a new display window at a specified location, with a selected page displayed. The window can later be removed with the WinFree() function.
winnewat.returns: The window number of the window, or -1 if the window cannot be opened. Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle returned from the WndFind() function.

paramDocs.Page: The name or page number of the page to display (in quotation marks ""). Can be prefixed by the name of a host cluster, that is "ClusterName.Page". This will take precedence over the use of the sClusterName parameter if the two differ.
paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster that will accommodate the page at runtime. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the page via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "". If the Page parameter is prefixed with the name of a cluster, this parameter will not be used.

winnewpinat.name: WinNewPinAt
winnewpinat.doc: Allows for windows to be "pinned" at specified locations within a main window or within other pinned windows. This function opens a new display window at a specified location, relative to the current active window, with a selected page displayed. The window can later be removed with the WinFree() function.
winnewpinat.returns: The window number of the window, or -1 if the window cannot be opened. Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle returned from the WndFind() function.

paramDocs.Page: The name or page number of the page to display (in quotation marks ""). Can be prefixed by the name of a host cluster, that is "ClusterName.Page". This will take precedence over the use of the ClusterName parameter if the two differ.
paramDocs.X: The x pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.Y: The y pixel coordinate of the top left corner of the window.
paramDocs.Width: The pixel width of the window, scaled relative to the current active window.
paramDocs.Height: The pixel height of the window, scaled relative to the current active window.
paramDocs.sClusterName: The name of the cluster that will accommodate the page at runtime. This is optional if you have one cluster or are resolving the page via the current cluster context. The argument is enclosed in quotation marks "". If the Page parameter is prefixed with the name of a cluster, this parameter will not be used.

winnext.name: WinNext
winnext.doc: Makes the next window (in order of creation) active.
winnext.returns: The window number of the window, or -1 if there is no next window. Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle returned from the WndFind() function.

winnumber.name: WinNumber
winnumber.doc: Gets the window number of the active Plant SCADA window. This number can be used with other functions to control the window.
winnumber.returns: Window Number associated with the Name provided. If no Name is specified then the active window number is returned. If there isn't a valid window number associated with the name provided then -1 is returned.

paramDocs.sName: String name previously associated with a window number using WinSetName().

winpos.name: WinPos
winpos.doc: Moves the active window to a new location. You use PageInfo() to get the current window position.
winpos.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

winprev.name: WinPrev
winprev.doc: Makes the previous window (in order of creation) active.
winprev.returns: The window number of the window, or -1 if there is no next window. Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle returned from the WndFind() function.

winprint.name: WinPrint
winprint.doc: Sends the graphics image of the active window to a printer.
winprint.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPort: The name of the printer port to which the window will be printed. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks "". For example "LPT1:", to print to the local printer, or "\\Pserver\canon1" using UNC to print to a network printer. sPort may not contain spaces.
paramDocs.xScale: The x scaling factor for the print. The default value of 0 (zero) automatically scales the print to fit the page. A value of 1 is used to maintain the current horizontal scaling of the image. The outcome is proportional to 1; for example, 0.5 halves the width of the image (optional).
paramDocs.yScale: The y scaling factor for the print. The default value of 0 (zero) automatically scales the print to fit the page. A value of 1 is used to maintain the current horizontal scaling of the image. The outcome is proportional to 1; for example, 0.5 halves the width of the image (optional).
paramDocs.bSwapBlackWhite: Swaps the colors black and white for the purpose of printing pages with a lot of black content. Use the default value of 1 to swap black and white (optional).
paramDocs.sMap: The file name or path of a text based map file used to specify colors to swap when printing. By default Plant SCADA will look in the bin directory for the map file. The format for the map file is:

winprintfile.name: WinPrintFile
winprintfile.doc: Prints a file to the system printer. The file needs to be saved with the WinFile() function.
winprintfile.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sPort: The name of the printer port to which the window will be printed. This name needs to be enclosed within quotation marks "". For example "LPT1:", to print to the local printer, or "\\Pserver\canon1" using UNC to print to a network printer. sPort may not contain spaces
paramDocs.xScale: The x scaling factor for the print. The default value of 0 (zero) automatically scales the print to fit the page. A value of 1 is used to maintain the current horizontal scaling of the image. The outcome is proportional to 1; for example, 0.5 halves the width of the image (optional).
paramDocs.yScale: The y scaling factor for the print. The default value 0 (zero) automatically scales the print to fit the page. A value of 1 is used to maintain the current horizontal scaling of the image. The outcome is proportional to 1; for example, 0.5 halves the width of the image (optional).
paramDocs.bSwapBlackWhite: Swaps the colors black and white for the purpose of printing pages with a lot of black content. Use the default value of 1 to swap black and white (optional).
paramDocs.fromColor: The hex RGB color value (0xRRGGBB) to change into toColor. The default value of -1 results in no color change (optional).
paramDocs.toColor: The hex RGB color value (0xRRGGBB) into which fromColor is changed. The default value of -1 results in no color change (optional).

winselect.name: WinSelect
winselect.doc: Selects a window to make active. This function only affects the output of Cicode functions. It does not change the screen focus of the windows, or move a background window to the foreground.

paramDocs.Window: The window number to select. Be aware that this is not the same as the window handle returned from the WndFind() function.

winsetname.name: WinSetName
winsetname.doc: Associates a name with a particular window by its window number. An association with a window is removed when the window is free.
winsetname.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: String name to associate with window number iWinNum.
paramDocs.iWinNum: An optional parameter which specifies the window number with which to associate Name. If no number is specified the name is associated with the currently selected window number.

winsize.name: WinSize
winsize.doc: Sizes the active window. The origin of the window does not move.
winsize.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.Mode: Specifies if the size refers to the viewable area or the total window.

winstyle.name: WinStyle
winstyle.doc: Switches on and off scrolling and scrollbar features for existing windows.
winstyle.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

wintitle.name: WinTitle
wintitle.doc: Sets the title of the active window.
wintitle.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sTitle: The new title for the window.

wndfind.name: WndFind
wndfind.doc: Gets the Windows handle of any window of any application, so that the window can be manipulated. The window handle is not the same as the Plant SCADA window number and cannot be used with functions that expect the Plant SCADA window number (the Win... functions).
wndfind.returns: The window handle. Be aware that this is not the same as a Plant SCADA window number returned from the WinNumber() function.

wndgetfileprofile.name: WndGetFileProfile
wndgetfileprofile.doc: Gets a profile string from any .ini file.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the variable.

wndhelp.name: WndHelp
wndhelp.doc: Invokes the Windows Help application (WinHlp32.EXE) to display a specific topic from a specific help file.
wndhelp.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.1: Displays the help topic identified by the context string/number in the Data field. The context string/number needs to be defined in the [MAP] section of the help's .HPJ file.
paramDocs.2: Closes the Help application. Enter an empty string for the Data argument.
paramDocs.3: Displays the help contents topic defined by the CONTENTS option in the [OPTIONS] section of the .HPJ file.
paramDocs.4: Displays the contents topic of the designated How to Use Help file. The context string/number (specified in the Data field) needs to be defined in the [MAP] section of the .HPJ file.
paramDocs.5: Changes the current help contents topic to match the context string/number specified in the Data field. This topic is used instead of the one defined by the CONTENTS option in the [OPTIONS] section of the .HPJ file. This will affect Command 3 (see above). The context string/number needs to be defined in the [MAP] section of the help's .HPJ file, and the help file needs to already be open. The change will last only until the help file is closed.
paramDocs.8: Displays, in a pop-up window, the help topic identified by the context string/number in the Data field. The context string/number needs to be defined in the [MAP] section of the .HPJ file.
paramDocs.9: Tests that the correct help file is displayed. If the correct help file is currently displayed, this command merely makes the help the active window. If the incorrect help file is displayed, WinHelp opens the correct file, and displays the help contents topic defined by the CONTENTS option in the [OPTIONS] section of the .HPJ file.
paramDocs.11: Displays the Plant SCADA Help Topics with either the Contents, the Index, or the Find tab selected, depending on which one was last used. Enter an empty string for the Data argument.
paramDocs.257: Searches the help index for your keyword (as specified in the Data field) and displays the first topic in the index with an identical match. If there is no match, displays the index with your keyword already entered. To display the index without passing a keyword, enter an empty string for the Data argument.
paramDocs.258: Executes the Help macro string specified in the Data field. Help needs to be running and the help file needs to be open, or the message is ignored.
paramDocs.260: Displays, in a pop-up window, the help topic identified by the context string/number in the Data field.
paramDocs.261: Searches the help index for your keyword (as specified in the Data field) and displays the first topic in the index with an identical match. If there is no match, displays the index with your keyword already entered. To display the index without passing a keyword, enter an empty string for the Data argument.
paramDocs.Data: The context string/number or keyword of the help topic that is requested.

wndinfo.name: WndInfo
wndinfo.doc: Gets information on the window system (such as the width and height of the various elements displayed by Windows). WndInfo() can also return flags that indicate whether the current version of the Windows operating system is a debugging version, whether a mouse is present, or whether the functions of the left and right mouse buttons have been exchanged.

paramDocs.iType: The system measurement to be retrieved. Measurements are in pixels. The system measurement needs to be one of the following values:

wndmonitorinfo.name: WndMonitorInfo
wndmonitorinfo.doc: Returns information about a particular monitor.
wndmonitorinfo.returns: Requested information about the selected monitor.

paramDocs.iMonitor: Monitor Number 1 to n, where n is the number of monitors returned from WndInfo(80). Using 0 will return the value for the virtual screen. Using an unsupported monitor number (0 or n) will return -1 for all values.
paramDocs.iType: Type The monitor measurement to be retrieved:

wndmonitorinfoex.name: WndMonitorInfoEx
wndmonitorinfoex.doc: Returns information about a particular monitor using the screen name of the screen profile.
wndmonitorinfoex.returns: Requested information about the selected monitor.

paramDocs.iType: Type The monitor measurement to be retrieved:

wndputfileprofile.name: WndPutFileProfile
wndputfileprofile.doc: Puts a profile string into any .INI file.
wndputfileprofile.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.sName: The name of the variable.

wndshow.name: WndShow
wndshow.doc: Sets the display mode of any window of any application.
wndshow.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hWnd: The Windows handle of the window (returned from the WndFind() function). Be aware that this is not the same as a Plant SCADA window number returned from the WinNumber() function.
paramDocs.nMode: The window mode:

wndviewer.name: WndViewer
wndviewer.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.1: Displays a Viewer topic (specified in the Data field) in the main Viewer window.
paramDocs.2: Displays a Viewer topic (specified in the Data field) in a pop-up window.
paramDocs.sViewerFile: The Multimedia Viewer file to display.
paramDocs.Data: The context string of the Multimedia Viewer topic.

xmlclose.name: XMLClose
xmlclose.doc: Use this function to delete an XML document in memory.
xmlclose.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.

xmlcreate.name: XMLCreate
xmlcreate.doc: Use this function to create a new XML document in memory.
xmlcreate.returns: Handle of XML document, or returns -1 on error

paramDocs.sRootElement: Root element of the XML document.
paramDocs.sNamespace: Optional. Namespace URI of root element.

xmlgetattribute.name: XMLGetAttribute
xmlgetattribute.doc: Retrieves the attribute value of the node from an XML document in memory.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlgetattributecount.name: XMLGetAttributeCount
xmlgetattributecount.doc: Gets number of attribute of specified XML node.
xmlgetattributecount.returns: Number of attribute of specified node.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlgetattributename.name: XMLGetAttributeName
xmlgetattributename.doc: Gets name of specified XML Node’s attribute by using attribute index.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlgetattributevalue.name: XMLGetAttributeValue
xmlgetattributevalue.doc: Gets the value of the specified XML node's attribute by using attribute index.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlgetchild.name: XMLGetChild
xmlgetchild.doc: Retrieves the child node for the specified parent node in XML document in memory.
xmlgetchild.returns: Handle of child node, or -1 on error

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document the parent node belongs to. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the parent node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlgetchildcount.name: XMLGetChildCount
xmlgetchildcount.doc: Retrieves the total number of child nodes for the specified parent node in an XML document in memory.
xmlgetchildcount.returns: Number of child nodes, or -1 on error

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document the parent node belongs to. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the parent node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlgetparent.name: XMLGetParent
xmlgetparent.doc: Gets the parent of specified node. If specified node is the root node in the tree, the parent is the document node.
xmlgetparent.returns: Handle of parent node, or error will be returned.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlgetroot.name: XMLGetRoot
xmlgetroot.doc: Gets the root element of the specified XML document.
xmlgetroot.returns: Handle of root element, or-1 on error.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.

xmlnodeaddchild.name: XMLNodeAddChild
xmlnodeaddchild.doc: Creates an element node with the specified Name and Namespace and appends the node to the end of the list of child nodes of specified parent node in the XML document.
xmlnodeaddchild.returns: Handle of the newly created node, or -1 on error.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document the parent node belongs to. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the parent node.e.g. <shapes>, <polygons>, <polygon>. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.
paramDocs.sName: The qualified name of the new element node.
paramDocs.sNamespace: Optional parameter. The namespace URI of the new node. For example, <shapes xmlns="http://mycompany.com/shapes/v1">.

xmlnodefind.name: XMLNodeFind
xmlnodefind.doc: Use this function to select the first XML node that matches the XPath expression.
xmlnodefind.returns: Handle of the first XML node that matches the XPath expression, or BAD HANDLE on error.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.

xmlnodegetname.name: XMLNodeGetName
xmlnodegetname.doc: Gets the name of the specified node.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlnodegetvalue.name: XMLNodeGetValue
xmlnodegetvalue.doc: Gets the value of the specified node.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlnoderemove.name: XMLNodeRemove
xmlnoderemove.doc: Removes the specified XML node from its parent and XML document.
xmlnoderemove.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.

xmlnodesetvalue.name: XMLNodeSetValue
xmlnodesetvalue.doc: Sets the value of the specified node.
xmlnodesetvalue.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document the parent node belongs to. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent, XMLNodeFind.

xmlopen.name: XMLOpen
xmlopen.doc: Reads an XML file from disk to create XML document.
xmlopen.returns: Handle of the XML document, or -1 on error.

xmlsave.name: XMLSave
xmlsave.doc: Use this function to save XML document on disk.
xmlsave.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.sQuery: Absolute path of the disk file that XML document is written to.

xmlsetattribute.name: XMLSetAttribute
xmlsetattribute.doc: Use this function to set the value of specified attribute of the node in the XML document. If the attribute does not exist, it will be created.
xmlsetattribute.returns: 0 (zero) if successful, otherwise an error code is returned.

paramDocs.hDoc: Handle of the XML document. Returned by XMLCreate or XMLOpen.
paramDocs.hNode: Handle of the node. Returned by XMLGetRoot, XMLGetChild, XMLGetParent or XMLNodeFind.
paramDocs.sName: The name of the attribute.
